papers.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
papers.abstract: Let C_h be the closure of the nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficients of modulus at most h. With the nonzero real roots included, the closure is connected at every height; without them, connectedness becomes arithmetic. We prove that C_h is connected exactly when h=q(q-1) is a pronic number 2, 6, 12, 20, ..., and has at least five components otherwise. At height two this confirms a twenty-year-old numerical observation of Shmerkin and Solomyak on double zeros of power series: apart from 1/2 they form the interval $[1/ρ,1)=C_2\cap(0,1)$, with $ρ$ the tribonacci constant. Disconnection is almost always infinite. For (p-1)^2<h<=p^2-3, $h\neq p(p-1)$, infinitely many components with nonempty interior accumulate at $\pm p$ and $\pm 1/p$, and when h<p(p-1) these four points are themselves components. Next to each square q^2>=16, at least two of the three heights q^2-2, q^2-1, q^2 have infinitely many components accumulating at a common point of (1/(q+1),1/q). Explicit series give infinitely many components at every nonpronic height below 167 other than 1, 3, 4, 9, 25, 63 and 81, and in general at most sqrt(X)+1 nonpronic heights h<=X can have finitely many components, although C_h is a Peano compactum at every height. The proofs compare values and derivatives of all admissible power series near a real double zero; the comparison sets are open and closed in the whole core, so components separated near the axis cannot reconnect elsewhere. On the real axis, the double zeros at heights 1, 3, 4, 7 form sets with infinitely many components; at height one this proves a conjecture of Shmerkin and Solomyak and one of Solomyak on the connectedness locus for pairs of affine maps.

papers.title: Online Graph Coloring: Competitive Ratios Separating Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms
papers.abstract: We study online coloring, focusing on the competitive ratio. The best previously known results were (1) a lower bound of $Ω(n / \log^2 n)$ for both deterministic and randomized algorithms by Halldórsson and Szegedy (1994), (2) an upper bound of $O(n / \log n)$ for randomized algorithms by Halldórsson (1997), and (3) an upper bound of $O(n / \log \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms by Kawarabayashi, Yoneda, and Yoneda (2025). In this paper, we improve these results as follows: 1. A new lower bound of $Ω(n / \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms. 2. A new upper bound of $O(n (\log \log n)^2 / \log^2 n)$ for randomized algorithms. 3. A new upper bound of $O(n / (\log \log n)^{2-\varepsilon})$ for deterministic algorithms for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. For randomized algorithms, we nearly close the gap between the lower and upper bounds; the remaining gap is only $O((\log \log n)^2)$. We establish the asymptotic separation between randomized and deterministic online graph coloring. Against an oblivious adversary, a polynomial-time randomized algorithm achieves a competitive ratio asymptotically smaller than any deterministic algorithm can guarantee, even with unlimited computation.

papers.title: Gradient Estimates for Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations with Solution-Dependent Coefficients
papers.abstract: We study a conormal boundary value problem for a class of singular-degenerate quasilinear elliptic equations in divergence form in bounded domains. The leading terms are measurable in the spatial variable and depend nonlinearly on both the solution and its gradient. The singularity or degeneracy is governed by a power of the distance to the domain boundary, with exponent greater than negative one. In particular, the corresponding weights need not belong to the Muckenhoupt $A_2$ class. Assuming that the weighted mean oscillations of the leading terms in the spatial variable are sufficiently small on small balls and that the domains have Lipschitz boundaries with sufficiently small Lipschitz constants, we establish global weighted $W^{1,p}$-estimates for weak solutions with bounded weighted mean oscillation. Our results extend recent estimates for equations whose leading terms are independent of the solution itself.

papers.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. This establishes a Bergman analogue of the local rigidity results for Szegő logarithmic flatness obtained by Lu--Tian (Duke Math. J., 2004) and, more recently, Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026).

papers.title: Annular Counterexamples and Skew-Shape Block Identities
papers.abstract: We establish four connected results on weighted order ideals, cluster coefficients, and block-statistic enumerators. First, we give a counterexample to Theorem 14 of Kang, Lee and Lim (European Journal of Combinatorics, 2026): in the rank-two annular cluster model, a single bridging-lamination coefficient row produces $1+q^2$, contradicting the asserted unimodality. We identify the unsupported initial case in their published induction. Second, we refute their log-concavity Conjecture 1: the same gap example violates log-concavity, and a further single-curve computation gives the full-support polynomial $1+2q+7q^2+10q^3+9q^4+4q^5+q^6$, which also fails log-concavity. Third, we establish the skew-shape block-statistic identity proposed in Kahane's Conjecture 4.4 (arXiv:2607.11225v1) for arbitrary finite skew Young diagrams, under an explicitly specified root-exclusion convention. Its proof combines commuting tableau-transfer matrices, a connected-block inverse kernel, and finite polynomial differential equations; the corresponding mathematical statements have Lean 4/Mathlib formalizations. Fourth, we derive a bivariate block refinement whose coefficients are nonnegative after shifting the order parameter by one and, when necessary, multiplying by a monomial in the weight parameter. We specify the correction to the printed root convention, confirmed by Kahane in correspondence, and the geometric sign and specialization conventions clarified by the relevant authors for the annular examples.

papers.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
papers.abstract: We find \emph{exotic} connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the higher rank group $G=G_2'$ that are neither $ι$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichmüller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call \emph{$α$-bundles} and \emph{$β$-bundles}, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $α$ and $β$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $β$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_β$-Anosov and $α$-bundles are $P_α$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $σ\in \{α, β\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_σ)$-manifold ${\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $ρ:π_1S\rightarrow G_2'$ associated to a $σ$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $ρ$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $π_1({\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $ρ$ in the space of $P_σ$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_σ$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic.

papers.title: Zeros of Katz's p-adic Eisenstein series E2
papers.abstract: For every prime $p\geq5$, the zeros of Katz's $p$-adic Eisenstein series $E_2$ on elliptic curves with good ordinary reduction have exactly $\lfloor p/12\rfloor+1$ distinct $j$-invariants. We prove that all these invariants lie in finite unramified extensions of $\mathbf{Q}_p$. Their reductions are given by a classical formula involving the supersingular polynomial, and each nonelliptic residue class contains a unique simple zero. For the Legendre family, hypergeometric congruences determine the polynomial of the lifted invariants modulo every power of $p$. We also study isogenies between the zeros. Each $p$-power isogeny class contains at most one zero $j$-invariant, and any two distinct isogenous zero invariants are algebraic over $\mathbf{Q}$. At a fixed cyclic degree, the nonelliptic isogenies give points in a finite divisor over $\mathbf{Q}$ on the corresponding modular curve. Its degree bounds their number and their fields of definition, and excludes several small degrees. The only zeros with complex multiplication have $j=0$ or $1728$. Whether a non-CM zero can have an algebraic $j$-invariant remains open.

papers.title: The expected number of holes of the planar Wiener sausage
papers.abstract: ```text Let $β_1^T(r)$ be the number of holes, that is, the first Betti number, of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ of a planar Brownian motion run up to time $T$. We prove that $\mathbb{E}[β_1^T(r)]$ is of order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ as $T\to\infty$, for each fixed $r>0$, which completes the lower bound obtained in a companion paper from a law for the inradii of the cavities of the path. We also identify which parts of the complement of the path contribute at leading order. At unit time and radius $\varepsilon$, the holes lying in the unbounded component of the complement have expected number $O(\varepsilon^{-2+θ_0})$ for an absolute $θ_0>0$, whereas the additional holes created when a cavity fragments under erosion have expected number of exact order $\varepsilon^{-2}(\log(1/\varepsilon))^{-2}$. In particular the one-pocket constant of the lower bound is strictly improved. The upper bound is obtained by pricing the contact configurations that pin near-critical pockets along the two independent arms of the path from a deterministic time, each arm contributing one factor $1/\log(1/\varepsilon)$. The outer estimate combines a stratified form of this first-moment bound with a packing argument near the frontier of the path, and the splitting lower bound forces a dumbbell-shaped cavity by a local construction followed by two logarithmic avoidance probabilities. The upper bound and the two structural estimates use no limit theorem for the shapes of cavities; the shape law enters only through the lower bound of the companion paper. ```

papers.title: Dynamic linear equations in the presence of small perturbations of an interface
papers.abstract: We consider solutions to the initial boundary value problems for both heat and wave equations in two dimensions. In this paper, we aim to advance the development of high-order terms in the asymptotic expansions of current boundary perturbations caused by small perturbations of the shape of a $C^2$-boundary inhomogeneity. Our derivations are rigorously derived by the field expansion (FE) method (formal derivation) and proved by layer potential techniques. It extends those already derived for small-volume inhomogeneities to develop efficient algorithms for determining certain properties of the shape of an inhomogeneity based on boundary measurements.

papers.title: Automatic Continuity for projective clone homomorphisms
papers.abstract: We show that every projective clone homomorphism from a closed function clone containing the automorphism group of a countable homogeneous Ramsey structure $Δ$ in a finite relational language is uniformly continuous. This answers, for such structures, open questions previously raised by Barto, Bodirsky, Marimon, Pongrácz, and the second author in several papers (Bodirsky, Pinsker, Pongrácz, J. Symb. Log. 2021; Barto, Pinsker, SIAM J. Comput. 2020; Marimon, Pinsker, arXiv:2512.01086). Consequently, the polymorphism clone of a first-order reduct $Γ$ of $Δ$ admits a projective clone homomorphism if and only if $Γ$ primitively positively interprets all finite structures; in other words, this ability of $Γ$ is characterised by the absence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, a purely algebraic condition.sence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, i.e., a purely algebraic condition.

papers.title: The distribution of small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
papers.abstract: Let $0<γ_1\leq γ_2\leq \cdots$ be the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros $ρ_n$ of the Riemann zeta function in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity. Selberg proved unconditionally that there exists $λ_0<1$ such that a positive proportion of the zeros $ρ_n$ satisfy $γ_{n+1}-γ_n\leq 2πλ_0/\log γ_n$. Simonič, Trudgian and Turnage-Butterbaugh were the first to obtain an explicit value in Selberg's theorem, showing that $λ_0=1- 10^{-3\cdot 10^{13}}$ is admissible. This was considerably improved by Zhao who showed that $λ_0= 1-2.36\cdot 10^{-6}$ is admissible. In this paper, we use a different approach, based on an unconditional variant of Montgomery's pair correlation method, to obtain a substantial improvement of these results, showing unconditionally that $λ_0=0.7892<4/5$ is admissible.

papers.title: A fourth-order dimensionally split exponential time differencing scheme with real and distinct pole rational approximation for non-linear reaction-diffusion systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel fourth-order, L-stable exponential time differencing (ETD) Runge-Kutta type scheme incorporating a dimensional splitting integrating factor method for the numerical solution of nonlinear reaction-diffusion systems. The method, ETDRK4RDP-IF, is obtained by approximating the matrix exponential operators in the classical dimensionally split ETDRK-IF scheme with an accurate fourth-order, L-acceptable rational function with real and distinct poles. The L-acceptability of the rational approximation guarantees effective damping of spurious oscillations arising from nonsmooth initial and/or boundary data and further eliminates complex arithmetic in the solution of the associated linear systems, thereby enhancing computational efficiency and making the scheme well-suited for parallel implementation in low-level programming languages such as Fortran and C++. Numerical experiments confirm the fourth-order accuracy for a range of reaction-diffusion problems with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, and demonstrate that it outperforms existing standard ETD methods in serial and parallel implementations, yielding CPU time reductions of up to a factor of 20.

papers.title: Divisor Folding and Finite-Group Trace Obstructions
papers.abstract: For a symmetric integer frequency set of size $n$ with Fourier floor $K$, we study a positive trace weighted by the reciprocal of the regularized Fourier multiplier. If restriction to frequencies divisible by $p$ leaves $n/p+O(K^2)$ frequencies, then for $n\ge K^4$ and $p\ll n/K^3$ the original trace differs by $O(n)$ from $p$ times the core trace at the inherited regularization. The transfer reaches cores of size $\asymp K^3$ and preserves vanishing triple density with diverging normalized triple count. We construct exactly regular finite abelian spectra at these scales for which the linear core trace bound fails by a power. The examples use unions of classical semiprimitive cyclotomic classes and also give obstructions in both reflection parities in odd characteristic. Finally, we bound the overlap of lifts of a core by its smallest positive Fourier height and the symmetry of the lifts. These bounds exclude balanced lifts of the binary examples in a range of cyclic extensions and quantify the asymmetry required in odd prime split extensions.

papers.title: Non-local phase transition models for partial singularities
papers.abstract: We study $Γ$-convergence, under appropriate scalings, of the energy functionals \[ F_\varepsilon(u) := [u]_{H^s(Q)}^2 + \int_{Q} W_\varepsilon(u)\,dx, \] where $s \in (0,1)$, $[\cdot]_{H^s(Q)}$ denotes the $H^s$-seminorm in $Q\subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$, and $W_\varepsilon$ is a multi-well potential featuring infinitely many equally spaced wells together with additional intermediate wells whose height vanishes at a prescribed rate. Depending on this rate, different limiting behaviors emerge, ranging from classical models to new intermediate regimes.

papers.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit family of real $m\times n$ restricted isometries with $m\to\infty$, $m/n\to 0$, $δ_k\to 0$, and $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$. We combine Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph with the property that every small subset spans few edges. We select this vertex set using an incidence geometric result due to Zahl. The proof only uses the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix despite the conventional wisdom that such proof techniques exhibit a barrier of $m^{1/2}$. We prove that this barrier is actually $m^{2/3}$, and we show that our particular construction exhibits the same barrier.

papers.title: A note on the intractability of enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression
papers.abstract: We show that, given a Horn expression and a family of inclusion-wise maximal satisfiable subsets of its clauses, deciding whether there exists another maximal satisfiable subset is NP-complete. As a consequence, unless P=NP, there is no output-polynomial time algorithm enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression.

papers.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
papers.abstract: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. The same pair determines the principal eigenvalue whose sign governs persistence, so early prevalence can inform the threshold even when the individual rates remain uncertain. We prove global weak well-posedness and quantitative parameter stability for the SIS system and use the resulting observation-map estimates to establish Bayesian well-posedness. For an initial infection of size $\varepsilon$, we derive a uniform second-order expansion that describes how the separate rates enter prevalence. Incidence depends explicitly on transmission at leading order. When the noise standard deviation is proportional to $\varepsilon$, we prove $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence in Hellinger distance of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits for both prevalence alone and joint prevalence and incidence data. We bound the principal eigenvalue using the growth rate of the infected $L^2$ norm between two times. This rate gives a lower bound for the full nonlinear system, and the upper bound separates spatial transients from nonlinear saturation. Uniform spectral estimates and bounds on infection size and measurement error give sufficient conditions for persistence and extinction. We also bound the error in posterior persistence probabilities under forward and eigenvalue approximation, accounting for posterior mass near the threshold. Numerical examples illustrate threshold inference and the predicted \(O(\varepsilon)\) convergence of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits in Hellinger distance.

papers.title: Newton non-degenerate holomorphic foliations and their separatrices
papers.abstract: In this paper we study germs of holomorphic foliations in the complex plane that are Newton non-degenerate. This is an algebraic condition attached to the Newton polygon of the foliation, analogous to the one defined by Kouchnirenko for analytic curves and, more generally, hypersurfaces. As in this case, the condition of Newton non-degeneracy for foliations can be identified through the comparison of two numerical invariants: the Newton number - a computation involving simple geometric data of the Newton polygon - and the Milnor number. The Newton number is never greater than the Milnor number, and the foliation is Newton non-degenerate if and only if they are equal. The assumption that a foliation is Newton non-degenerate imposes conditions on its set of separatrices. We prove that, under this hypothesis, the foliation has no weak separatrices and, hence, all its separatrices are analytic. We also give a description of the set of separatrices of a Newton non-degenerate foliation, which is sufficient to characterize the foliation as Newton non-degenerate when it is of generalized curve type. This allows us to prove that the property of being Newton non-degenerate is topologically invariant for foliations of generalized curve type.

papers.title: Progression-free sets in class $2$ and arbitrary finite groups
papers.abstract: We study progression-free sets in arbitrary finite groups. We transfer sharp upper bounds from abelian groups to nilpotent groups of class $2$, and from nilpotent groups to arbitrary groups. Combining a recent result of Raghavan with the author's theorem on large subgroups of class $2$ gives \[ r_3(G) \, \leq \, C \, |G|\exp\left( -c\frac{(\log|G|)^{1/6}}{(\log\log|G|)^{1/3}}\right) \] for every finite group as $|G|\to\infty$. This improves the estimates obtained by using the abelian subgroup supplied by Pyber's theorem.

papers.title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance
papers.abstract: Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second. Every observation influences the estimate in two roles, through its own evaluation when it is held out and through the models it helps fit when it trains. The random splits determine its weight in each role. From this representation, we prove an exact finite-sample identity for the variance of the cross-validated estimate. For a given splitting scheme with a common training set size, the variance is a function of these weights, with constants of the model, the metric, and the population. It covers metrics averaged over observations, such as mean squared error, and over case--control pairs, such as the AUC. The identity shows which schemes to use. The variance decomposes into sampling variance, which depends only on the training size, and variance due to the random fold splitting, which arises when the weights change from one draw of the splits to the next. K-fold cross-validation, whose weights are equal across observations by design, is therefore variance optimal at first order; Monte Carlo and bootstrap cross-validation are not. The first-order variance of K-fold does not depend on K, and under reasonable conditions on the model leave-one-out has the smallest variance of any K-fold scheme. For the AUC the same holds for leave-pair-out, which evaluates every case--control pair. Finally, we show the cross-validated estimate is asymptotically normal with the identity's full variance. Together, these results provide a general theoretical foundation for inference on cross-validated performance and establish principles for selecting variance-optimal cross-validation designs.

papers.title: Measuring Kaplan--Meier Overestimation Under Competing Risks: Event Ordering, Quantification, and Exact Inference
papers.abstract: Competing risks arise when individuals may experience multiple mutually exclusive event types. Competing events are frequently treated as censoring and analysed using Kaplan--Meier (KM) methods, which overestimate real-world event risks. While the existence of KM overestimation is well known, its determinants, magnitude, and inferential properties remain poorly characterised. We develop a nonparametric framework that treats competing risks overestimation as a statistical quantity in its own right. We show that competing event frequency alone is insufficient to characterise KM overestimation and develop an event ordering theory describing how temporal event allocation influences overestimation. Based on these results, we derive a closed-form Total Overestimation Diagnostic (TOD) that quantifies total KM overestimation directly from routine survival analysis output. We establish exact error equivalence results for both cause-specific and total overestimation. In particular, Product Limit Error Equivalence shows that inference for TOD reduces exactly to ordinary overall survival estimation. Simulation experiments validate the theoretical results and show that independent censoring primarily affects precision rather than overestimation magnitude. Across six benchmark competing risks datasets, cause-specific overestimation is characterised by both total overestimation and temporal event allocation. These results provide a practical framework for assessing competing risks relevance and determining when cumulative incidence methods should be preferred to naïve KM risks. The proposed framework transforms competing risks overestimation from a qualitative warning into a measurable quantity that can be routinely quantified, interpreted, and incorporated into reporting practice.

papers.title: Shifted Lagrangian structures and syzygies on Calabi--Yau varieties
papers.abstract: In \cite{FMR25}, Fantechi--Miró-Roig show how to construct new Lagrangian subspaces of the moduli of simple perfect sheaves on a K3 surface from a given one. We reinterpret their construction using the tools and flexibility of derived algebraic geometry. This allows us to generalize from K3 surfaces to (possibly singular) Calabi--Yau schemes of arbitrary dimensions.

papers.title: Regularity of minimisers for the $p$-distance functional
papers.abstract: We consider regularity of minimisers of the $p$-distance functional $\mathcal{F}[u]=\int_Ω\mathrm{dist}(Du,K)^p \mathrm{d}x$ where $K \subset \mathbb{R}^{N \times n}$ is a compact set. We distinguish the scalar and vectorial cases, and consider geometric conditions on $K$ where regularity can be improved.

papers.title: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
papers.abstract: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a computation of the transverse Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple computation of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even cohomology. This is then applied to the classification of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$. Moreover, we study the action of multiplication by the principal orbit on V-shaped symplectic cohomology and prove that if the compactification $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D})$ is positively monotone, then this class induces a periodic structure on symplectic cohomology, reducing the problem of computing an infinite-dimensional group to a finite-dimensional repeating portion. We combine the index computations and this periodic structure to compute the symplectic cohomology of various Milnor fibers of surface singularities, the rational homology balls $B_{p,1}$ as well as complements of star-shaped configurations of rational curves in K3 surfaces, which includes the Milnor fibers of the exceptional unimodal singularities.

papers.title: Phase transitions in the hard-wall large deviations for the Gaussian free field
papers.abstract: We study the probability that the Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\ge3$, stays above a level $-h_N$ throughout the lattice $N$-blow-up of a bounded Lipschitz domain, when $h_N$ is close to the entropic-repulsion height $\sqrt{4g_0\log N}$. Two mechanisms compete: a collective upward displacement of the field, whose cost is governed by capacity, and the suppression of the remaining local violations, whose cost is their expected number, both of which are of order $N^{d-2}/\log N$ exactly in the window $h_N(β)^2=g_0(4\log N+\log\log N+2β)$. We obtain a sharp asymptotic rate expressed through a variational problem combining a Dirichlet energy with an exponential potential inside this critical window. Outside this window we obtain the asymptotics at the appropriate moving speeds: capacity alone governs the cost as $β\to-\infty$, and the expected number of violations as $β\to+\infty$. As an application, we derive lower-deviation bounds for the cover level of a macroscopic body by random interlacements, which determine the order of decay at the transition.

papers.title: Nonparametric Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Mixtures of Logistic Regressions
papers.abstract: Mixtures of logistic regressions provide a flexible framework for modeling binary responses, extending standard logistic regression to accommodate unobserved heterogeneity while retaining an interpretable regression structure. In this paper, we study such models with an unspecified mixing distribution. We analyze a sieve nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) and derive nonasymptotic bounds on the estimation error of the resulting mixture regression function under both fixed and random designs. Our results reveal an explicit tradeoff between statistical estimation error and the approximation error induced by the sieve radius, from which we derive convergence rates under several tail conditions on the mixing distribution. For computation, we propose a finite-particle algorithm that approximates the sieve NPMLE by optimizing the locations and weights of a finitely supported mixing distribution. The method offers numerical advantages over existing algorithms and comes with rigorous convergence guarantees. For any fixed dataset, we establish global convergence of the likelihood to the restricted NPMLE value when the number of particles exceeds a finite threshold. When the true mixing distribution is finitely supported, we further establish uniform global convergence guarantees and derive error bounds that separate algorithmic and statistical errors. Our analysis also yields a denoising bound for the mixing distribution and an identifiability result that complements existing results in the literature.

papers.title: Sharp regularity results for variational integrals asymptotic to the $p$-Dirichlet integral
papers.abstract: We consider the regularity for minimisers of $\int_ΩF(Du) \mathrm{d}x$ where $F(z) \approx |z|^p$ in suitable senses at infinity. Depending on the strength of this asymptotic condition, we discuss various regularity results, and by means of counterexamples we show they are sharp. An effort is made to obtain results without assuming unnecessary regularity of $F$ while covering the full range $1<p<\infty$.

papers.title: Linear-size graphs at every strict dismantling level
papers.abstract: Dismantling reduces a graph to one vertex by successive deletions. At level zero, a vertex is eligible if one of its neighbours is adjacent to all its other neighbours. At level $k\geq1$, its neighbours must induce a graph dismantlable at level $k-1$. A graph has strict level $k$ if it admits a reduction at level $k$ and none at level $k-1$. For every $k\geq1$, we construct a graph of strict level $k$ with $3k+8$ vertices. Each step adds three vertices: the neighbours of one induce the preceding graph, and the other two provide the adjacencies used to rule out other first deletions at the lower level. A second construction gives a graph of order $4k+4$ at strict level $k$. Together the two families give the upper bound $\min\{4k+4,3k+8\}$ on the least order at strict level $k$.

papers.title: Analytic and optimized approximations to the median of the gamma distribution
papers.abstract: The median $ν_Γ(α)$ of the gamma distribution has no closed form, but its behavior at both ends is known: it is asymptotic to $2^{-1/α}e^{-γ}$ (with $γ$ being the Euler-Mascheroni constant) as the shape parameter $α\to 0$, and approaches $α- 1/3$ as $α\to \infty$. We write approximations as interpolations $(1 - g)ν_0 + gν_\infty$ between two elementary-function bounds or approximations, each exact in one limit, with an interpolator $g(α)$ going from 0 to 1, and compare three such forms: a first one between previously proven bounds, a second ending in an approximation from the beta median that is exact at $α= 1$ but does not quite approach $α- 1/3$ as $α\to \infty$, and a third one, between bounds proved here, that corrects the large-$α$ end of the second. For each form, the ideal interpolator's slope at 0, approach to 1, and value at $α= 1$ are derived in closed form. Rational interpolators with every coefficient set in closed form from these properties, with no numerical fitting, reach a worst relative error of 0.0011 over all $α> 0$, with absolute error below 0.0002. Fitting some of these or other coefficients numerically to minimize the worst absolute-or-relative error then trades accuracy against complexity: the Pareto frontier reaches 0.000087 with two fitted constants and 0.000041 with five, and from two on uses degree-4 rationals of the second form with no $α^2$ term in the numerator. The proofs that the end functions of the first and third forms are bounds are machine-checked in Lean 4.

papers.title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
papers.abstract: Branch-and-Bound (B&B) and $A^*$ are popular exact search methods originating from Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence, respectively. Although the two methods share fundamental search principles, their different ways of exploring the search space can lead to substantially different computational performance. We investigate these differences using the Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP) as an exemplary problem setting. We first establish the relationships between mixed-integer linear programming, state-action, and timed Petri-net representations. Since B&B and $A^*$ admit numerous algorithmic enhancements, we focus on relatively basic implementations. This allows us to examine the fundamental differences between the methods rather than compare the performance of state-of-the-art solvers. By using the same lower bound and best-first node selection, we isolate the effects of the search mechanisms, particularly the identification of equivalent states reached through different scheduling decision sequences. Experiments on 480 benchmark RCPSP instances show that graph-based $A^*$ substantially outperforms the B&B variants considered. With additional pruning rules, $A^*$ proves optimality for all 480 instances, compared with 445 for best-first B&B under the same time and memory limits. Depth-first B&B uses less memory and can find feasible solutions even when the search does not finish within the time limit. Stronger linear programming relaxations reduce the search space but introduce considerable computational overhead. Our findings highlight the importance of duplicate-state detection and clarify the computational trade-offs between the search approaches. These insights can help researchers select an appropriate method and identify opportunities to incorporate effective mechanisms from one approach into the other.

papers.title: Cotangent-lift inference of stochastic microbial dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the parameter estimation for the stochastic logistic and Lotka--Volterra diffusions from discrete, irregularly spaced observations corrupted by measurement noise, a setting typical of microbiome time series. For the logistic equation, the growth rate acts as a time change and does not enter the stationary law, so it can be identified only from the temporal structure of the data. We prove that the maximum-likelihood estimator of the Euler scheme, with the observations taken as the states, coincides with the regression of log-increments on abundances used in the literature, and we characterise what this estimator cannot see under measurement noise: for the linearised dynamics, the law of consecutive pairs of observations is invariant along an explicit one-parameter family of relaxation rates and noise levels, and the regression converges to a limit set by the noise. Treating the true abundances as latent, we compute the likelihood with a Gaussian moment filter and show that measurement noise is precisely what couples the filter states across samples. The exact gradient is then the backward recursion of the discrete cotangent lift, whose cost, two to three likelihood evaluations, does not depend on the number of parameters, and we give the covector map of each filter step in closed form. In simulations, the latent estimator recovers the relaxation times, noise levels and interaction strengths that the regression biases, while larger communities require prior information on the interactions. In gut microbiome time series it attributes most of the variability of a dominant genus to measurement noise and estimates its relaxation time at about $64$ hours, with a large standard error.

papers.title: On the stable birational type of Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We show that, given a very general cubic threefold $X$, any smooth cubic threefold stably birational to $X$ must be isomorphic to $X$. The method applies as well to other Fano 3-folds, like the sextic double solid, and the quartic threefold. We also discuss the higher-dimensional case.

papers.title: Scott spectra of distributive continuous lattices
papers.abstract: Let \(L\) be a distributive continuous lattice. We prove that the hull--kernel topology on \(\Spec(L)\) is the Scott topology of the inclusion order if and only if \(σ(L^{\op})=\upsilon(L^{\op})\). The necessary implication and the algebraic case are known. We prove sufficiency for arbitrary distributive continuous lattices, thereby obtaining the spectrum characterization requested by Lawson and Mislove. The proof embeds \(L\) into a continuous lattice that is both a frame and a coframe, and transfers the Scott topology of the spectrum along the induced map of spectra.

papers.title: Stationary integral cycles asymptotic to a pair of transverse oriented $n$-planes at infinity
papers.abstract: Let $P, Q$ be two oriented transverse $n$-planes in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, $n\geq 2$, which satisfy the equality in the Lawlor--Nance angle criterion. We prove that any stationary integral $n$-cycle in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ with $[P]+[Q]$ being the tangent cone at infinity, in both the current and varifold senses, is a translation of $[P]+[Q]$ or of a Lawlor neck.

papers.title: Regularity of $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic functions with applications to stable minimal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We show that the derivative of a $Q$-valued $C^1$ function on an $n$-dimensional domain that is locally harmonic on its regular set is locally Dirichlet minimising, and that its branch set coincides with that of its derivative. As a consequence, we get that a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is $C^{1,α}$ and that its branch set is countably $(n-2)$-rectifiable when $n\geq 3$ and discrete when $n=2$. Our methods are directly applicable to the regularity theory of stable minimal hypersurfaces. We show that a multi-valued Lipschitz function whose graph is a two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal $n$-dimensional hypersurface with locally $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-finite singular set, and whose Lipschitz constant is sufficiently small is in fact multi-valued $C^{1,α}$. As a consequence, we obtain optimal regularity conclusions for a branched sheeting theorem of Bellettini for singular immersions. When $n=2$, we obtain stronger conclusions and show that locally about a branch point, a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is the real part of a Dirichlet minimiser which is itself obtained from a finite number of holomorphic functions via classical branching, thus giving a full series expansion for the function near the branch point. Furthermore, we prove that the class of branched, two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities is compact under varifold convergence.

papers.title: Bi-Hamiltonian structure and conserved quantities of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell system
papers.abstract:
We study the Hamiltonian and bi-Hamiltonian structure of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell (YON) system, an integrable model of long wave-short wave interaction depending on two real parameters $α$ and $β$, which reduces to the Yajima-Oikawa system for $α=0$ and to the Newell system for $β=0$. For $α
eq0$, a constant shift of the long wave maps the YON system into the Newell system, for which two nonlocal Hamiltonian operators are known. We show that, for $α
eq0$, the system admits no local Hamiltonian operator homogeneous in its natural grading and polynomial in $β$. A nonlocal gauge transformation built on the potential of the long wave makes the first of the known operators local for a single value of its parameter: the transformed system is Hamiltonian, for every $α
eq0$ and every $β$, with respect to a local, non-degenerate Poisson operator, which is the Lie-Poisson structure of the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ current algebra. From a recursion operator advancing the hierarchy by two steps, given in explicit weakly nonlocal form, we construct a second, weakly nonlocal Hamiltonian structure, whose nonlocal tail is generated by the three autonomous Lie point symmetries of the system, and prove that both structures are compatible. Since the recursion operator admits no square root and the first structure has no Casimirs, the Lenard-Magri chain splits into two families, seeded by the two simplest conserved quantities. Every flow of both families is local, and all the corresponding Hamiltonians are in involution. As by-products, we relate the Lie point symmetries of the system to its conserved quantities via Noether's theorem, and obtain the conserved densities in closed form by asymptotic diagonalisation of the Lax pair.

papers.title: Scattering thresholds for the NLS equation with polynomially decaying damping
papers.abstract: We study the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a linear damping of strength $a(1+t)^{-θ}$, where $a>0$ and $θ\ge0$, in the whole energy-subcritical range. For $θ>0$, the time-averaged damping vanishes, so that the scattering theory developed in our previous work does not apply. We show that the long-time dynamics is governed by the time integrability of an effective coupling, which decays faster than any power when $θ<1$, polynomially when $θ=1$, and not at all when $θ>1$. In the mass-subcritical case, all solutions are global. They scatter when $θ<1$ and, for $θ=1$, above an explicit exponent depending on $a$. On the other hand, no non-trivial solution is asymptotically free below a second explicit exponent when $θ=1$, and below the short-range exponent $1+2/N$ when $θ>1$. In the mass-critical case, solutions are global below the ground state. Moreover, for $θ\le1$, every solution which survives until its decaying mass becomes subcritical is global and scatters. In the intercritical case, we prove small data scattering and, for $θ\le1$, a dichotomy between scattering and grow-up of the gradient. Finally, in the scale-invariant case $θ=1$, we analyze the range between the two thresholds. We reduce the equation exactly to a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a decaying repulsive harmonic potential, and we construct approximate solitary waves with an integrable error. This leads to a conjecture, supported by numerical simulations, on the sharpness of the scattering threshold.

papers.title: Canonical Volumes of Threefolds with Positive Geometric Genus
papers.abstract: We prove that a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus has canonical volume at least $1/30$, with strict inequality when its Euler characteristic is positive. We describe the equality cases as canonical hypersurfaces of degree $28$ in $\mathbb P(1,3,4,5,14)$. These canonical models and their smooth projective resolutions are simply connected. Their coarse moduli space is irreducible and rational of dimension $103$, with finite quotient singularities; all admissible $\mathbb Q$-Gorenstein deformations are unobstructed and arise by varying the equation.

papers.title: The strongly local part of nonlinear Dirichlet structures and its energy measures
papers.abstract: This paper substantially extends the results of Sasaya (2026, JFA): we propose a framework for nonlinear generalizations of regular Dirichlet forms and prove that each energy in this framework has a largest strongly local part. We also prove the existence and uniqueness of canonical energy measures of this part, which satisfy convexity and locality properties and, under additional assumptions, certain chain rules in one variable. In particular, our framework requires neither $p$-homogeneity nor strong locality. Moreover, under a Ball--Carlen--Lieb-type upper bound, we prove more detailed chain rules for the directional derivatives of these energy measures. Our framework is applicable both to $p$-energy forms on fractals and to a class of symmetric nonlinear Dirichlet forms in the sense of Cipriani and Grillo~\cite{CG2003}, including those of Orlicz--Sobolev and variable-exponent Sobolev type.

papers.title: Long-time behaviour of solutions for equations with randomness
papers.abstract: We discuss results on the mixing properties of solutions for discrete and continuous time equations, drived by stationary bounded random forces, obtained during the last three years in a number or our joint papers. To facilitate applications of these results to specific equations with randomness, the results are edited and properly re-arranged.

papers.title: On operators with infinitely many spectral components
papers.abstract: For a unital complex Banach algebra $\mathscr A$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ be the set of all elements whose spectrum has at least $n$ connected components, and let $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)=\bigcap_{n\in\mathbb N}\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$. We prove that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)\neq\varnothing$ if and only if $\mathscr A$ contains a sequence of non-zero pairwise orthogonal idempotents, and that the number of components of a spectrum is always finite, $\aleph_0$ or $\mathfrak c$. This allows us to extend the spectral depth $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ to a cardinal-valued invariant with values in $\mathbb N\cup\{\aleph_0,\mathfrak c\}$. We show that $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\mathfrak c$ precisely when $\mathscr A$ contains a dyadic family of idempotents indexed by the full binary tree. In that case, some element has spectrum homeomorphic to the Cantor space $\mathbf 2^{\mathbb N}$. The supremum defining $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ is attained when the spectral classes of $\mathscr A$ are dense and when $\mathscr A$ is commutative, but not in general. We construct a unital complex Banach algebra with $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\aleph_0$ and $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)=\varnothing$. If $Δ$ is the character space of a commutative $\mathscr A$ and $π_0(Δ)$ is the space of all components of $Δ$, then $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\card\bigl(π_0(Δ)\bigr)$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is finite, $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\aleph_0$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is infinite and scattered, and $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\mathfrak c$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is not scattered. We also prove that the spectral depth is additive with respect to finite direct sums and that the spectral classes are invariant under injective holomorphic functions.

papers.title: Cost controllability and predictive control of input-constrained monotone systems on Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: Cost controllability, relating controllability and a performance measure like the stage cost in model predictive control (MPC), is a key tool in the stability and suboptimality analysis of closed-loop systems. We establish cost controllability for maximal monotone control systems subject to input constraints, a class encompassing finite- and infinite-dimensional port-Hamiltonian systems with colocated input and output. To this end, we employ a recently proposed saturated feedback to derive state-dependent bounds on the closed-loop cost. Our main result is that cost controllability holds globally with semiglobal exponential rate. We first establish this result in continuous time and then extend it to sampled-data systems. Whereas a qualitative detectability-like property is sufficient for asymptotic convergence of the controller, cost controllability requires quantitative rates. We provide two verifiable conditions ensuring cost controllability with explicit exponential rates: coercivity of the sum of system operator and output injection, and exponential detectability of the linear part. Moreover, under the coercivity condition, the resulting MPC scheme without terminal conditions renders the equilibrium globally asymptotically stable with semiglobal exponential rate already for prediction horizon two. We illustrate our results by a nonlinear finite-dimensional system, a semilinear heat equation and a nonlinearly damped wave equation.

papers.title: Phragmén-Lindelöf theorems for parabolic equations of p-laplacian-type
papers.abstract: We consider rigidity properties of ancient solutions to parabolic equations of $p$-Laplacian-type. We start with the degenerate range $p>2$. First, a solution which is bounded above in an intrinsic backward paraboloid is either bounded in an entire half-space, or grows in space at least like a power with a sharp, explicit exponent. This relies on the expansion of positivity and on the Comparison Principle. Then, we turn to the growth in time. Positivity in the paraboloid alone yields no upper rate: we present explicit self-similar solutions, positive in the paraboloid, with $u(0,-T)\simeq T^β$ for every $β\le0$ and every $β\ge1$. For solutions bounded below in the paraboloid, we prove a dichotomy for the infimum of $u(\cdot,-T)$ on a ball whose radius is a fixed fraction of that of the paraboloid at time $-T$: either it is of order $T$ along a sequence of times, or it grows sublinearly, like $T^ζ$ with $ζ<1$ explicit. In the second case, a Harnack-type argument shows that the supremum on the same ball grows at most linearly. Then, we carry out the same program in the singular, supercritical range $\frac{2N}{N+1}<p<2$, where the picture is similar but several roles are reversed. In space, the iteration via the Comparison Principle can only be started from a point lying above an explicit slope, and explicit solutions show that nothing better than a cone bound can be expected below it. The self-similar profiles are unique but only local, and positivity in the paraboloid is compatible with every exponent $β\le1$ and with no exponent in $(1,\frac1{2-p})$. In time, the dichotomy is replaced by an a priori linear bound for the infimum. Similarities and differences between the two ranges are collected at the end of the work.

papers.title: Pseudoconformal characterizations of scattering in weighted Sobolev spaces for non-scaling-invariant mass-subcritical NLS
papers.abstract: We consider mass-subcritical nonlinear Schrödinger equations with finitely many power-type nonlinearities and initial data in weighted Sobolev spaces. In the short-range regime, we prove a pseudoconformal characterization of scattering in the weighted energy space $Σ$. We also establish a fractional counterpart in $Σ^s$, $s\in(0,1)$, formulated in terms of the boundedness of the order-$s$ pseudoconformal operator. Our results include equations with combined nonlinearities, for which no distinguished scaling symmetry is available. As an application of the fractional theory, we prove small-data scattering in $Σ^s$, $s\in(0,1]$. The arguments rely on the lens transformation, harmonic-oscillator Strichartz estimates, and fractional harmonic Sobolev estimates.

papers.title: On the topology of some linear systems of hyperelliptic curves in Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.abstract: Following a program suggested by Dolgachev and Libgober in 1981, we study the topology of the locus of smooth sections of linear systems of hyperelliptic curves on Hirzebruch surfaces. Our primary interest is the computation of various flavors of ``enriched monodromy representations''. Within this class of examples, we find that a variety of behaviors occur - in some situations the enriched monodromy faithfully captures the fundamental group, and in others it does not. Our arguments mainly leverage algebro-geometric techniques to compute cohomological obstructions to families of embeddings.

papers.title: Tolerance complexes of chordal graphs and squarefree symbolic powers
papers.abstract: For a simplicial complex $K$ and an integer $t\ge0$, the $t$-tolerance complex $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ consists of the sets that become faces of $K$ after deleting at most $t$ of their elements. Kim and Lew conjectured that if $K$ is $d$-Leray, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(η(d+1,t+1)-1)$-Leray (the Leray conjecture), and that if $K$ is $d$-collapsible, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(η(d+1,t+1)-1)$-collapsible (the collapsibility conjecture), where $η$ is the Erdős--Gallai number. We prove the collapsibility conjecture for $d=1$ when $t\le3$ or $\dim K\le4$, and for all $t$ when $K$ is the clique complex of a subtree graph of a spider, a class of chordal graphs containing all interval and split graphs; in particular, it holds for nerves of finite families of intervals. For every $d$, we prove both conjectures when $K$ has at most $d+1$ facets, when $K$ has nonzero homology in its top dimension, and when the Stanley--Reisner ideal of $K$ is squarefree stable. The Stanley--Reisner ideal of $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is the $(t+1)$-st squarefree symbolic power of that of $K$, so the Leray conjecture becomes a regularity bound. Using this, we prove the Leray conjecture for flag complexes when $t\le3$, and for all $t$ for independence complexes of bipartite and chordal graphs, and we show that it is preserved under joins. We also construct chordal graphs $H$ for which the Leray number of $\mathcal{T}_t(\mathrm{Cl}(H))$ exceeds its Helly dimension by an arbitrarily large amount, and others for which it depends on the field. Finally, we reduce the case $t=1$ of the Leray bound for $d$-collapsible complexes to a question on intersections of links.

papers.title: Parabolic semiinfinite sheaves on affine flag varieties
papers.abstract: We study sheaves on affine flag varieties of reductive algebraic groups in parabolic semiinfinite settings, generalizing some constructions and results from the work of Gaitsgory and of Achar, Dhillon, and the first author (for the case of the Borel subgroup) and of Dhillon and Lysenko (for characteristic-$0$ coefficients and a particular case of parabolic semiinfinite condition). In particular we define perverse t-structures and Raskin equivalences in this context, and study an analogue of the Gaitsgory sheaf. In future work, these $\infty$-categories will be related to representation-theoretic $\infty$-categories associated with the Langlands dual group.

papers.title: From Distribution of Extremes With Degradation to the Stress Redundancy Principle
papers.abstract: How a degradation source affects the statistics of the first among many identical independent stochastic particles to successfully reach a narrow target remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impact of degradation on the distributions of first-passage times and exit locations by exploiting the time-dependent fluxes associated with the corresponding Fokker-Planck equation. We also compute the escape probability by solving a mixed boundary value problem. In the large initial population $N_0$ limit, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean first passage time associated with the fastest particle, revealing how the killing field modifies the classical $1/\log(N_0)$ scaling. However, when considering the population size at the time of the first exit, we obtain a specific dependency with respect to degradation, a phenomenon that we call the stress redundancy principle. For a degradation field restricted to a narrow subregion, we use an optimal control approach to derive the optimal trajectory where the fastest escape particles will be concentrated: interestingly, we report here that the optimal trajectories avoid the degradation area depending on killing intensity. Finally, we obtain analytical expressions for the distribution of first exit points along a narrow absorbing arc in two-dimensional regular domains. In addition, for a killing subregion tangent to the target boundary, our computations reveal how geometrical parameters influence the exit distribution. In summary, a killing source can significantly affect the statistics of the fastest diffusing particles, relevant for defining cellular and molecular time scales.

papers.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
papers.abstract: Kühnel and Lassmann constructed a neighborly triangulation of the three-torus on 15 vertices, and Lutz conjectured that it is vertex-minimal. The standard lower-bound arguments exclude at most twelve vertices but do not decide the 13- and 14-vertex cases. We exclude the 13-vertex case. Our proof uses the Novik--Swartz $g_2$-inequality and a simplicial-complement reduction to a nine-vertex model of the punctured three-torus. By analyzing fundamental groups of small simplicial complexes and applying Alexander duality in a vertex link, we obtain a contradiction from the deficiency of $\Z^3$.

papers.title: Independent Families Under Determinacy-Like Hypotheses
papers.abstract: We generalize the notion of an independent family on $ω$ to $\mathcal{J}$-independent families on an arbitrary cardinal $κ$ and then show that under determinacy-like hypotheses that there can be no such families for reasonable $\mathcal{J}$. This is quite atypical as all other generalizations of the kinds of combinatorial families coming from the theory of cardinal characteristics follow a very different pattern, which will also be explained; in this sense independent families seem particularly special. The base theory assumed throughout is $\textsf{ZF + }$All infinite sets are Dedekind infinite.

papers.title: The Symplectic Nature of Noncentral Reducible Stratum in SU(2) Character Variety
papers.abstract: Let \(Σ_g\) be a closed oriented surface of genus \(g\geq2\). The purpose of this paper is to use an explicit example, the representation of the surface group $π_1(Σ_g)$ into $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, to investigate the deformation space of the representation variety at a type of singular points, reducible but noncentral representations, and explore the geometric structure of the corresponding stratum in the representation variety and the character variety. In particular, the reduced tangent quadratic cone determines the symplectic structure at the reducible noncentral stratum of the character variety. Such a symplectic structure fits in the ambient character variety $χ\big(π_1(Σ_g),\mathrm{SU}(2)\big)$, where the top stratum of smooth points admits the Narasimhan-Atiyah-Bott-Goldman symplectic structure.

papers.title: Shape Perturbation of the Galerkin Boundary Element Dirichlet-to-Neumann Matrix on Moving Polygons
papers.abstract: For nonlocal interface evolution problems such as the Mullins-Sekerka flow, certain parametric schemes discretize only the interface and approximate the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map by boundary elements. Their error analysis requires bounds on how this discrete operator changes as the polygon moves. In that analysis, the polygons are only Lipschitz and close to a smooth curve only in a Lipschitz norm, the perturbations are controlled only in the energy norm, and the kernels are singular on the diagonal. We study the symmetric Galerkin boundary element matrix on the polygons in a Lipschitz neighborhood of a smooth reference curve. Its first variation, tested against discrete Neumann solutions, is bounded by the energy norm of the perturbation alone. The second-order remainder of the associated mass form is bounded by the product of the energy norm and the Lipschitz norm of the perturbation, so that only one of the two factors needs a uniform bound. On the interpolating polygon, the matrix is consistent with the continuous operator without the logarithmic loss that a pointwise comparison of the kernels would suggest, and its shape derivative is consistent with that of the continuous operator. All bounds are uniform in the mesh size and depend only on the constants of the reference curve.

papers.title: Splitting module-finite extensions over singular local rings
papers.abstract: We study when a module-finite extension of a singular local ring splits as a module over the base. On a Gorenstein curve of positive residue characteristic, weak normality forces splitting for every extension of finite projective dimension. In residue characteristic two the converse holds when two is zero or a nonzerodivisor. A missing square root in the prescribed base gives an explicit nonsplit extension of generic rank four. We obtain a second curve criterion by gluing retractions on the branches and determine all evaluation ideals for coordinate crossings and for \(x^2=y^2u z_1\cdots z_s\) in odd characteristic. For cubic extensions we prove a presentation theorem with arbitrarily many relations. It applies on the blow-up of an ideal generated by a regular sequence of length three, and on the blow-up of a three-dimensional local ring with a quadric tangent cone. A family of matrices satisfying the criterion exists over every residue field in the regular-sequence case.

papers.title: Generalized Cramér-Rao Inequalities Associated with $(h,τ)$-Divergence and $(h,τ)$-Exponential Family
papers.abstract: The Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and exponential family have laid the foundation for information geometry and have been widely generalized. Using Eguchi's theory, the Fisher information metric can be derived from the KL divergence. Based on this metric, Amari and Nagaoka established an information-geometric proof of the classical Cramér-Rao (CR) inequality for finite-support models. Among the various generalizations of the KL divergence, this paper focuses on the $(h,τ)$-divergence and establishes the associated CR inequality, referred to as the $(h,τ)$-CR inequality, using information geometry. We also provide a proof of this inequality based on the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, thereby extending its applicability to models with more general support sets. Under suitable regularity conditions, equality holds in the classical CR inequality if and only if the underlying family is exponential. However, for the $(h,τ)$-CR inequality, this property does not generally extend to the $(h,τ)$-exponential family. We therefore establish an attainable CR inequality for this family. This new inequality extends the attainment result of the classical CR inequality by the sufficient statistic of the exponential family to the $(h,τ)$-exponential family.

papers.title: Smoothed Least-Absolute Conditional Multidimensional Scaling via Iteratively Reweighted Majorization
papers.abstract: Conditional multidimensional scaling combines latent coordinates with observed covariates to fit pairwise dissimilarities. We develop a smoothed l1 formulation using the shifted Charbonnier loss. We prove residualwise sharpness of the quadratic loss majorizer, monotonicity, compact containment, and stationarity of noncollapsed accumulation points. A uniform additive bound quantifies approximation to exact least-absolute conditional stress. The experiments use paired contamination, separately calibrated loss parameters, combined-configuration recovery, and direct checks of the theorem's inequalities.

papers.title: Numerical analysis of coupled flow, deformation and frictional contact mechanics in a fractured porous medium
papers.abstract: This paper studies the numerical approximation of a mathematical model of coupled flow and viscoelastic deformation in a fractured porous medium including fracture contact mechanics. We consider a mixed-dimensional model, where the fracture is modeled as a co-dimension one object within the porous medium. This model couples Darcy flow in the matrix and fracture, linear viscoelasticity of the matrix and frictional contact mechanics of the fracture surfaces; the contact conditions include normal compliance and a Coulomb friction law. We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme for this problem, using conformal finite elements in space and the implicit Euler method in time. Existence and uniqueness of the discrete solution is established, and stability and a priori error estimates are derived. A numerical experiment is performed in which numerical error estimates are computed and compared to the theoretical results.

papers.title: Ramification of torsion packets on curves with good-reduction Jacobians
papers.abstract: Let $p\ge5$ be a prime number, $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Write $R=W(k)$ for the ring of Witt vectors over $k$, and $K$ for the field of fractions of $R$. Let $X$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over $K$ of genus greater than one. Write $J$ for the Jacobian variety of $X$. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{K}$ of $K$. In the present paper, we prove that if $J$ has good reduction over $R$, then every point $x\in X(\overline{K})$ such that $[σx-x]$ is torsion for each $σ\in \operatorname{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ is $K$-rational.

papers.title: Pareto Front Tracing in Higher Dimensions Using Numerical Integration
papers.abstract: We propose a numerical integration approach for tracing the Pareto front of unconstrained continuous multi-objective optimization problems. By stating optimality conditions for weighted sum scalarizations, we derive parametric equations for Pareto critical points, parameterized by the weights. Sensitivity analysis with respect to the weights yields a system of partial differential equations (PDEs). We prove local existence and uniqueness of solutions and derive conditions under which a solution extends to the entire weight space and yields Pareto optimal solutions. A tracing strategy for the resulting PDE system is developed that uses numerical integration along individual weight coordinates using Runge--Kutta methods. We provide an error analysis considering inexact initial solutions, perturbations of the right-hand sides, and numerical integration errors. We investigate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the tracing strategy on convex quadratic problems and WFG examples, where the latter demonstrate the applicability to problems with Pareto fronts consisting of convex and non-convex parts. Comparisons with repeated weighted sum scalarizations and a predictor--corrector method illustrate the computational benefits of the proposed strategy.

papers.title: Asymptotic Robustness of HDG Schemes for the Convection-Diffusion Equation
papers.abstract: The convection-diffusion problem has been studied extensively as an important model for convection-dominated problems. The problem becomes more challenging when the convecting velocity is no longer Lipschitz and merely has Sobolev regularity. In this paper, we use Boyer's extension of the DiPerna--Lions theory for the transport equation to study the vanishing diffusion limit of discretizations of the convection-diffusion equation with Sobolev velocity. In the case of flux-adapted boundary conditions, we prove that a continuous Galerkin discretization converges strongly to the renormalized solution of the transport equation as the diffusion coefficient and mesh size go to zero, without requiring any relationship between them. We refer to this unconditional strong convergence as asymptotic robustness. In the case of Dirichlet boundary conditions, we use the renormalization theory and barrier arguments to prove that a piecewise constant hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin scheme is asymptotically robust, while the continuous Galerkin scheme may fail to converge. Our results indicate that the asymptotic robustness of schemes for the convection-diffusion problem depends on the realization of the boundary conditions as opposed to internal layers.

papers.title: Characterizing Fixed-Treewidth Planar Graphs
papers.abstract: We give the first inductive characterization of planar graphs of treewidth $k$ for each $k \geq 3$. Our definition generalizes the well-known inductive definition of planar $3$-trees and the recent definition of so-called planar quasi-$4$-trees [Förster, 2024]. As a key step, which may be of independent interest, we show that every planar triangulation $G$ of treewidth $k$ admits a tree decomposition of width $k$ where each adhesion set induces a cycle in $G$. As an application of planar quasi-$4$-trees, we show that planar graphs of treewidth at most $4$ have vertex arboricity at most $2$. That is, the vertex-set of every planar graph of treewidth at most $4$ can be partitioned into two sets that each induce a forest.

papers.title: Bounding and Approximating Kostka Numbers
papers.abstract: Kostka numbers, the coefficients of Schur polynomials, count semistandard Young tableaux of prescribed shape and weight. We give a deterministic algorithm for approximating Kostka numbers within a simply exponential factor in the number of variables and the size of the partition. Our approach combines Gurvits capacity bounds for log-concave polynomials with an algorithm for approximating the Gurvits capacity of a Schur polynomial. For a Schur polynomial in $n$ variables indexed by $λ$, we show that the logarithm of the capacity associated with any nonzero coefficient can be approximated to additive error $ε$ in time polynomial in $n$, $|λ|$, and $\log(1/ε)$. The analysis establishes an explicit bounded optimization region and efficient approximate first-order oracles, and handles boundary weights through a factorization into smaller Schur polynomials.

papers.title: Poisson boundaries of lattices in locally compact groups
papers.abstract: For a random walk on a general locally compact group we provide a discretization procedure transforming the walk to one on a lattice of the group, preserving the Poisson boundary and some finiteness of moments.

papers.title: A New Computational Model for the Spin-Free Sum-of-Squares Energy Bounds of Electronic Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: Optimizing spin-free sum-of-squares (SOS) energy bounds for electronic Hamiltonians leads to semidefinite programs whose expanded size grows rapidly with the orbital dimension. We derive an exact reformulation of an established spin-free SOS model as a convex quadratic problem over a single symmetric matrix constrained between zero and the identity. Explicit recovery maps connect feasible quadratic-program iterates to certificates in the original SOS formulation, and identify the Frank--Wolfe gap with the separation between recovered primal and dual objectives. We implement the quadratic action through GPU-accelerated Coulomb contractions and solve the reformulated problem using a cached implementation of fully corrective Frank--Wolfe, referred to here as the dimension-reduced simplicial method (DRSM) that caches operator products and optimizes convex-combination weights in a small corrective quadratic program. Numerical experiments cover 65 FCIDUMP models, molecular geometries, and regular hydrogen rings, including original-coordinate recovery checks on nine instances and comparisons with FISTA and a boundary-point SDP solver. On eight H100 GPUs, a cold-start calculation for C$_{720}$ with 10,080 spatial orbitals reaches a freshly recomputed Frank--Wolfe gap of $8.82\times10^{-9}$ hartree in 5.02 hours. Full-space hydrogen-ring calculations reach 10,000 orbitals, with cyclic reduction providing further computational savings. These results show how exact reformulation, data structure exploitation and reuse of Coulomb actions make optimization of the selected large-scale SOS relaxation practical.

papers.title: Reconstructing Numerical Semigroups from Circulant Spectral Dimensions
papers.abstract: The polynomial algebra generated by the spectral moments of a family of circulant graphs consists of all eventually polynomial sequences in the graph order; as an unfiltered algebra, it therefore carries little information about the jumps. We show that its natural power-sum weight filtration retains substantially finer arithmetic data. For a finite jump set $S$ with $\gcd(S)=1$ and $M=\max S$, the relevant invariant is the numerical semigroup $Σ_S=\langle M,M-s,M+s:s\in S\rangle$, which arises from the lengths of closed walks winding around the cycle. We prove that the eventual global filtered dimension is $MD+\lfloor D/2\rfloor+1-M(M+1)-g(Σ_S)$. Restricting graph orders to $n\equiv a\pmod q$, for $q\mid M$, replaces the genus term by the number of gaps of $Σ_S$ in the class $-a\pmod q$; the class $a=0$ gives the genus of the quotient semigroup $Σ_S/q$. These formulas yield an inverse reconstruction theorem: the unrestricted dimensions determine $M$, and the dimensions in all classes modulo $M$ at one common stable degree determine the Apéry set and hence $Σ_S$. We give effective thresholds, exact examples, and a finite-rank algorithm valid in every degree. Reconstruction of the semigroup need not identify the original jump set.

papers.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
papers.abstract: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

papers.title: Rectifiable measures in Ahlfors regular spaces: endpoint constructions
papers.abstract: A theorem of Balka and Keleti implies that on any complete separable metric space $\mathbb{X}$, every locally finite Borel measure $μ$ of packing dimension strictly less than $m$ is "Euclidean-like" insofar as there exist Lipschitz maps $f_i:E_i\subset\mathbb{R}^m\rightarrow\mathbb{X}$ such that $μ(\mathbb{X}\setminus\bigcup_1^\infty f_i(E_i))=0$. An ongoing challenge in geometric measure theory is to understand when this property, called $m$-rectifiability, holds for measures of packing dimension $m$. Towards this goal, we prove that every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q\geq m$ supports $m$-rectifiable doubling measures of packing dimension $m$. The proof of existence of such measures is new even when $\mathbb{X}=\mathbb{R}^n$ and $n>m$. More generally, on every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q>m-1$, we construct $m$-rectifiable, purely $(m-1)$-unrectifiable measures with any prescribed exact Hausdorff and packing dimensions $0\leq s_H\leq s_P\leq q$ with $m-1\leq s_P\leq m$, which are doubling when $s_H>0$. This verifies a conjecture of Badger and Schul. The design of the measures relies on metric cubes with variable scaling, in which the ratio of consecutive side lengths tends to infinity but jumps only on a sparse set of generations, together with Badger and Schul's square packing construction of Lipschitz maps.

papers.title: Examples of homological mirror symmetry via Zariski descent
papers.abstract: This paper considers a general setting in which the Fukaya category of an exact symplectic manifold may be decomposed as a fiber product of Fukaya categories of smaller pieces. We establish a property of Fukaya categories that is mirror to Zariski descent of coherent sheaves. This fits into a natural strategy to prove homological mirror symmetry by a local-to-global analysis. The examples we consider in detail are open Riemann surfaces and exact log Calabi-Yau surfaces, and we provide proofs of homological mirror symmetry in these cases.

papers.title: Noetherian connected braided Hopf algebras are affine
papers.abstract: The well-known Wu--Zhang question asks whether every Noetherian Hopf algebra over a field is affine (finitely generated as an algebra). In this paper, we extend this fundamental problem to the braided setting within the monoidal category ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ of left Yetter--Drinfel'd modules over a Hopf algebra $H$. By developing term-rewriting methods based on reduction orderings and prime-word factorizations in free prebraided algebras, we establish explicit expansions for YD-triangular comultiplications. We prove that if $(\mathbb{K}\langle X \rangle, ε)$ is an augmented free algebra in ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ and $I \subseteq \ker ε$ is an ideal invariant under a YD-triangular comultiplication, then every $I$-reducible letter---and consequently every non-empty word in $\langle X \rangle$---can be expressed modulo $I$ as a linear combination of products of $I$-irreducible letters strictly smaller with respect to the reduction order. As a primary consequence, we prove that any right Noetherian connected prebraided Hopf algebra $B$ in ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ is affine, generated by the image of a finite set $X_{I}$ of $I$-irreducible letters. As an application, we show that the braided component $B = A^{\mathrm{co}\,π}$ of a right Noetherian Radford biproduct $A = B \sharp H$ is affine whenever $A_{(0)} \subseteq \jmath(H)$, reducing the affineness of $A$ entirely to that of $H$.

papers.title: Whittaker supermodules for the Takiff superalgebra \mathfrak{osp}(1|2)
papers.abstract: In this article, we classify all simple Whittaker supermodules over the Takiff Lie superalgebra \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)\otimes\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)\), associated with Whittaker characters defined on the even part of its positive nilpotent subalgebra.

papers.title: Anosov representations from cyclic Higgs bundles
papers.abstract: For every complex simple Lie group G (not of type $E_8$) we construct the minimal Slodowy slice, which is a half-dimensional slice in the character variety of a closed surface group into G, containing the composition of Fuchsian representations with the minimal representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ in G and invariant under the mapping class group action. This slice is defined via cyclic Higgs bundles, and we show that when G is not of type $E_8$, the corresponding representations are Anosov, so in particular discrete and faithful, and dominate some Fuchsian representation. For each of these Higgs bundles, we consider the equivariant harmonic map to the symmetric space, and we show it is an embedding and a quasi-isometric embedding with regard to the induced metric. From the cyclicity of these Higgs bundles we are also able to construct an auxiliary harmonic map to a pseudoriemannian symmetric space $G/G^σ$ which is also an embedding.
