Consequently, a non-expansive bijection of $B_X$ onto itself that fails to be an isometry must map some point of $S_X$ into the open unit ball, so the plasticity of $B_X$ reduces to showing that non-expansive bijections preserve norm 1. The proof shows that $F$ is Fréchet differentiable at $0$ with a surjective linear isometry $T$ as its derivative, and then proves $T^{-1}F=\mathrm{id}$ using a quantitative rigidity lemma for non-expansive self-maps $H$ of $B_X$ satisfying $\|a+H(a)\|=2$ for $a\in S_X$; the latter relies on the Baillon-Bruck rate of asymptotic regularity for Krasnosel'skii-Mann iterations. As a corollary, the identity is extremal in the set of non-expansive self-maps of $B_X$ for every Banach space $X$, which together with a result of Bargetz, Dymond and Pirk shows that all surjective isometries of $B_X$ are extremal, answering a question of theirs, including the case of $L^1[0,1]$.

papers.title: Axis-parallel square packing with an exact formula for optimal packing of seven squares
papers.abstract: How large a square is needed to hold axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths? We give exact formulas for the optimal side through seven squares, with explicit constructions and geometric lower-bound proofs. For every $n\ge6$, the optimum for $n$ squares is a sum of at most $n-3$ of the prescribed side lengths. This bound is sharp on an open set of side lengths and yields the optimal Euclidean Lipschitz constant $\sqrt{n-3}$ of the optimum as a function of the $n$ side lengths.

papers.title: Local Tate duality for syntomic cohomology in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a local field of characteristic $p>0$. We show that syntomic cohomology over $k$, with coefficients, and defined using Dodd's theory of $F$-gauges, satisfies local Tate duality. We also prove that syntomic cohomology over the ring of integers of $k$, again with coefficients, is Lagrangian with respect to the duality pairing. Finally, we show that, for $p>2$, these results recover Shatz's duality and Milne's orthogonality results for the cohomology of finite flat group schemes of $p$-power order over $k$.

papers.title: Nonproduct Minimal Submanifolds with Cylindrical Tangent Cones
papers.abstract: This article constructs, via perturbation methods, infinite-dimensional families of non-product minimal submanifolds which have singular sets locally modeled on cylindrical tangent cones. This answers a question raised by Leon Simon in the 1980s, and generalizes work Caffarelli-Hardt-Simon, who treated the case of isolated singularities. This setting requires substantially more work, however, since the natural obstruction space for the problem is infinite dimensional and the map which is meant to compensate for this obstruction using deformations of the singular set exhibits a loss of regularity. This necessitates working in the category of tame Frechet spaces and using the Nash-Moser Implicit Function Theorem.

papers.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
papers.abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties. We also study the probability that a family of $N$ i.i.d.\ Gaussian points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is in convex position and show that a sharp threshold occurs around the value $N=\exp(d/2e)$.

papers.title: A Projection Anderson Acceleration Algorithm for Non-quasi-monotone Variational Inequalities with Hölder Continuous Terms
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a Projection Anderson Acceleration (PAA) algorithm for variational inequality (VI) problems, where the underlying function is expressed as a finite sum of Hölder continuous functions and satisfies the $σ$-star strongly monotone condition that includes the star strong monotonicity with $σ= 1$ as a special case. In the absence of quasi-monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity, we establish the evaluation complexity of the PAA algorithm for finding an approximate solution. Specifically, for the star strongly monotone VI problems, the PAA algorithm needs at most $O (\log (ε^{-1}) ε^{2 (\underlineα - 1)})$ evaluations of the function and projection for finding an $ε$-approximate solution, where $\underlineα \in (0, 1]$ is the smallest exponent of H{ö}lder continuity of the component functions. We illustrate our theoretical results by numerical examples of non-quasi-monotone complementarity problems and non-monotone semilinear elliptic equations with non-Lipschitz terms.

papers.title: Khovanov and knot Floer homology of fibered positive links
papers.abstract: For fibered positive links, we compute the reduced and unreduced Khovanov homology in homological grading two over both $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{F}_2$, and the knot Floer homology in the penultimate Alexander grading. Our Khovanov calculations, combined with the result of Przytycki-Sazdanović, prove that every nontrivial semi-adequate knot has 2-torsion in its unreduced Khovanov homology. This establishes Shumakovitch's conjecture for semi-adequate knots, which include all nontrivial positive knots. The proofs involve induction using the skein exact sequences, with the Hopf link as the base case.

papers.title: Optimum solution to a boundary-value problem for an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$ via measure of noncompactness
papers.abstract: We propose a new class of cyclic (noncyclic) operator type condensing mappings and establish conditions that guarantee the existence of best proximity points (pairs) using measure of noncom-pactness. The results obtained are further applied to investigate the optimum solution of an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$.

papers.title: The generator problem for C*-algebras with comparison
papers.abstract: We show that certain classes of unital, simple, separable C*-algebras with comparison are singly generated, including tracially AF algebras and monotracial crossed products of actions on the Cantor space. In particular, we show that simple, separable, tracially AF algebras have generator rank one.

papers.title: Almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum
papers.abstract: Haemers' conjecture for the generalized spectrum asserts that almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum, that is, for almost all graphs $G$, every graph with the same spectrum as $G$ whose complement has the same spectrum as the complement of $G$ is isomorphic to $G$. We prove this conjecture by showing that the random graph $G(n,1/2)$ is determined by its generalized spectrum with probability tending to one. The proof combines a local theory of the denominators of the rational orthogonal matrices that relate generalized cospectral graphs, Fourier analysis of random symmetric matrices over finite rings, Seidel switching, inverse Littlewood--Offord theory over finite fields, rank estimates for random symmetric matrices modulo primes, and a study of the rational factors of the characteristic polynomial of a random symmetric $\pm1$ matrix with zero diagonal.

papers.title: Riemann functions for almost primes and their counting errors
papers.abstract: The real-axis jump of the prime-zeta function gives an integral form of Gram's series for Riemann's $R$-function. Applying the same operation to the almost-prime Dirichlet series defines functions $R_k$, with $R_1=R$. We prove absolute convergence, recover the classical fixed-order Selberg-Delange expansion, and identify the complementary Perron contribution to the exact count. A convergent incomplete-gamma endpoint expansion, together with the remaining lower cut, gives an exact representation of $R_k$, with explicit formulas for ranks one through four and a coefficient recurrence for every fixed rank. We then study the errors $R_k-N_k$. Under the Riemann hypothesis, their normalized mean-square zero spectra retain multiplicities; with simple zeros, the leading oscillations agree for every fixed $k$. An additional weighted logarithmic-gap moment gives a second-order spectrum and a positive constant in the $(\log\log X)^{-2}$ mean-square cancellation rate for consecutive values of $k$. The global spectral passages are justified by a uniform finite contour and a Gaussian-Laplace block estimate.

papers.title: Eigenvalues of the Hessian in Deep Learning: The Origin of Symmetry and Its Breaking
papers.abstract: Hessian spectra at trained models in deep learning exhibit a persistent pattern: eigenvalues organize into distinct clusters, including a large bulk near zero and a few isolated outliers. This paper shows that a natural account of these spectral phenomena emerges when the original setting is understood as a departure from a nearby, otherwise hidden, highly symmetric reference. Modifications, including changes to the architecture, data distribution, or parameter metric, expose a nearby reference configuration whose Hessian exhibits rich invariances-ones not accounted for by weight symmetries. There, symmetry enables a precise description of the spectra, forcing high-dimensional kernels and eigenvalues of large multiplicity. Returning to the original configuration breaks the Hessian symmetry and thereby produces the observed hierarchy of clusters and outliers. The framework is developed in some generality, with a detailed analysis of three-layer ReLU networks and applications to convolutional, graph, and transformer models, as well as to the NTK. The same mechanism is further shown to yield analogous spectral structures in layerwise Hessians and the Gauss-Newton matrix.

papers.title: Analytic multiplier ideals of toric plurisubharmonic functions on a toric complex space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study analytic multiplier ideal sheaves of toric plurisubharmonic functions on normal affine toric complex analytic spaces equipped with torus-invariant rational divisors, assuming that a positive integer multiple of the log canonical divisor is Cartier. We describe these sheaves in terms of Newton convex bodies and show that they are globally generated by finitely many meromorphic monomials. Our results generalize the description of An and the formulas of Howald and Blickle for monomial ideals, and recover the descriptions of Rashkovskii and Guenancia on affine space. We also extend this description to weights obtained by subtracting positive rational multiples of monomial ideal weights.

papers.title: Banded Totally Positive Matrices and Positive Bidiagonal Factorizations: Existence, Stability, and Toeplitz Orthogonality
papers.abstract: A positive bidiagonal factorization of a banded totally positive matrix expresses it as a product of unit lower and upper bidiagonal factors with positive off-diagonal entries and a positive diagonal matrix. In finite dimension such factorizations always exist, with parameter domains defined by polynomial inequalities. In the semi-infinite case, existence is equivalent to convergence of explicit positive series. Every bounded banded totally positive matrix is an operator-norm limit of matrices admitting these factorizations, through perturbations confined to a fixed initial block. Necessary and sufficient criteria characterize analytic dependence of prescribed factors on perturbations. With fixed initial entries, a relative entrywise criterion allows unbounded factors with different growth rates. For uniformly positive bounded factors with variable initial entries, the criterion involves every pair of factors on each triangular side and the signed triangular inverses. The dimensions of the local factorization families are determined. Normalized LDU factors depend analytically at every interior point of the factorization class. For banded totally positive Toeplitz matrices, a stable positive bidiagonal factorization exists if and only if the symbol polynomial has distinct roots. Root formulas give two polynomial vector families with mixed-type multiple orthogonality for a rectangular matrix of positive measures. One factorization simultaneously attains the smallest possible first off-diagonal entries of both normalization matrices. The weighted linear forms are independent of the factorization. Their Chebyshev expansions yield asymptotic zero spacing inside the support and convergence of normalized kernels to the sine kernel after rescaling by the local zero density.

papers.title: Special Loci in the Moduli of Curves
papers.abstract: We introduce new techniques to study mixed-characteristic special loci in moduli spaces and give several applications, focusing in particular on the moduli space $\mathsf{M}_g$ of curves. These applications include Zariski density results for split Jacobians, non-density results for supersingular loci, and lifting results for algebraic cycles, all under appropriate numerical conditions. Our methods generalize to more-or-less arbitrary moduli spaces mapping to Hodge-type Shimura varieties (and even some settings beyond the Shimura case), and relate to questions raised by Oort and de Jong.

papers.title: An exact compress-with-another threshold in a binary automaton family
papers.abstract: For a state $q$ in a synchronizing automaton, let $μ(q)$ be the minimum length of a word merging $q$ with another initial state. Szykuła asked whether $μ(q)=O(n)$ for strongly connected synchronizing automata and described a binary family attributed to Dżyga, with $n=3p$ states and a conjectured threshold $4n/3$. We specify the boundary transitions omitted from the published piecewise definition and prove that the resulting automata $\mathcal A_p$ satisfy $μ(q_0)=4p=4n/3$ for all $p\geq3$. A shortest word merging $q_0$ with another state is $(ba)^p(ab)^p$. We also construct a reset word of length $3p^2+4p-1$. Consequently, any uniform linear upper bound for $μ(q)$ on binary strongly connected synchronizing automata with corank-one letters has leading constant at least $4/3$.

papers.title: A New insight into the Ambrosio--Reshetnyak approach to Sobolev maps
papers.abstract: Given $p \in (1,\infty)$, let $\operatorname{X}=(\operatorname{X},ρ,μ)$ be a metric measure space such that $(\operatorname{X},\operatorname{d})$ is complete, the measure $μ$ is uniformly locally doubling and $\operatorname{X}$ supports a weak local $(1,p)$-Poincaré inequality. Let $(\operatorname{Y},\operatorname{d},\underline{y})$ be a complete pointed metric space. We prove that the equivalence class (modulo coincidence $μ$-a.e.) of a Borel map $u:\operatorname{X} \to \operatorname{Y}$ with a separable range belongs to the Ambrosio--Reshetnyak--Sobolev class $W_{p}^{1}(\operatorname{X},\operatorname{Y})$ if and only if $h \circ u$ belongs to the Sobolev space $W_{p}^{1}(\operatorname{X})$ for every $1$-Lipschitz function $h:\operatorname{Y} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $h(\underline{y})=0$.

papers.title: The Benson--Etingof--Ostrik conjecture for finite tensor categories
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic admits a symmetric tensor functor to a higher Verlinde category. This was conjectured for arbitrary symmetric tensor categories of moderate growth by Benson, Etingof and Ostrik. The proof uses higher Frobenius functors, introduced by the authors in [CF1]. The main effort is directed towards a proof of a conjecture from [CF1] about thick tensor ideals in the representation category of elementary abelian $p$-groups, which implies that the higher Frobenius functors are symmetric monoidal. In fact, we prove a refinement of the latter conjecture that relates tensoring with restricted Steinberg modules to an iterated generalised cohomology of modules of elementary abelian $p$-groups.

papers.title: Mirror symmetry for gCICY threefolds (I): a $[3,-1]$ block and a non-Gorenstein toric phase
papers.abstract: We construct and analyze a mirror family for the generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau threefold $X_+=[\mathbb{P}^1\,|\,3\ {-1};\ \mathbb{P}^4\,|\,2\ 3]$, with $(h^{1,1},h^{2,1})=(2,46)$. We introduce auxiliary variables to obtain a toric GIT presentation with two chambers. The first gives $X_+$, while the second gives a Calabi-Yau threefold $X_-$ related to $X_+$ by a flop of 16 disjoint $(-1,-1)$-curves. The threefold $X_-$ is a nef complete intersection in a non-Gorenstein toric $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano eightfold. Then the Hori-Vafa equations give a 2-parameter Laurent family, and we construct a smooth projective crepant model $Y$ of its general member with mirrored Hodge numbers. The rank-6 Picard-Fuchs system of $Y$ has two maximally unipotent boundary points, whose indicial algebras are isomorphic to the even cohomology rings $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_+,\mathbb{C})$ and $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_-,\mathbb{C})$. We also show that the predicted genus-zero BPS numbers of the first two vertical degrees agree with direct counts of lines and conics on the genus-one fibration $X_-\to\mathbb{P}^2$.

papers.title: Pellarin's Identity, Carlitz Period, and Anderson Generating Functions over Arbitrary Curves
papers.abstract: We establish three results for a rank-one Drinfeld module over the coefficient ring of a smooth, projective, geometrically connected curve over $ \mathbb F_q$, with a closed point at infinity of arbitrary degree. First, a Tate-algebra unit exists in the module of special functions precisely when this module is free of rank one, that is, when the period lattice is isomorphic to the module of regular differentials; this proves the Gazda--Maurischat conjecture. Second, under the unit-anchor normalization for an isogeny to a principal-period target, a strictly normalized shtuka product and one characteristic residue give the fundamental period; the same defect equation gives the logarithm residue formula. Third, finite étale torsion traces over the field of definition identify the first Frobenius twist of the normalized shtuka differential and express Pellarin's $ \mathcal L(1)$-series at a fundamental period. The source period lattice need not be free.

papers.title: Semi-stable models, local heights and quadratic Chabauty for $X_0(N)^*$
papers.abstract: Quadratic Chabauty computations for $X_0(N)^*$ are complicated by local height contributions at primes of bad reduction. For squarefree $N$, we explain a strategy for constructing a global $p$-adic height for which all the contributions at the primes of bad reduction vanish. As our first main result, we show that such a $p$-adic height exists for all squarefree levels $N>714$. In order to do this, we first give an explicit description of the minimal regular model of $X_0(N)^*$ at primes of bad reduction, and show this model is semi-stable. Each component of this model gives rise to a linear condition which ensures that the contribution at that component vanishes. Using embeddings of quadratic orders into quaternion algebras, we obtain an upper bound for the number of these conditions; when the genus of $X_0(N)^*$ is greater than one more than this bound, there is enough freedom to choose a suitable correspondence, simplifying quadratic Chabauty computations. As an application, we determine the rational points on several curves $X_0(N)^*$ for which this was not done before.

papers.title: On Boston's Unramified Conjecture for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ and McLeman's $(3,3)$-Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $A$ be a complete Noetherian commutative local ring with finite residue field of characteristic $p$. Let $G_{\mathbf{Q}}$ be the absolute Galois group of the rational number field and fix an inertia subgroup $I_p\subset G_{\mathbf{Q}}$ at $p$. We prove that every continuous odd representation $ρ:G_{\mathbf{Q}}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(A)$, unramified outside finitely many primes and with finite $ρ(I_p)$, has finite image if $p>3$ or $A$ has positive characteristic. For $p=3$, the conclusion also holds when the local representation at $3$ is reducible, or the local residual semisimplification has no mod-$3$ cyclotomic self-twist. In particular, this proves the two-dimensional odd case of Boston's unramified Fontaine--Mazur conjecture over $\mathbf{Q}$ for every odd $p$. Furthermore, we deduce finiteness results for conjugate self-dual representations of pro-$p$ Galois groups over imaginary quadratic fields under a ramification condition, and for representations of their unramified pro-$p$ groups of generator rank at most two. As an application, we resolve the sufficiency direction of McLeman's $(3,3)$-conjecture on $p$-class field towers for $p>3$. Namely, we prove that if $K$ is an imaginary quadratic field with $p$-class rank two and the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(K_{\varnothing}(p)/K)$ of the maximal unramified $p$-extension of $K$ has Zassenhaus type $(3,3)$, then the $p$-class field tower of $K$ is finite. For $p=3$, we also rule out infinite towers for ten of the thirteen fourth Zassenhaus quotients classified by Ahlqvist and Pink.

papers.title: A Formalism for Merging Power Series in Solving Multinomial Equations: Master Series and Master Numbers
papers.abstract: It is shown that all solutions of the canonical equation y^a = 1 + a*x*y^b with arbitrary complex exponents a, b (case m = 1) and of its limiting cases - the binomial root y = (1 + a*x)^(1/a) at b = 0, the exponential y = e^x at a = 0, b = 0, and the Lambert equation y = e^(x*y^b) at a = 0 - as well as the logarithms of these solutions (case m = 0), are expressed by a single power master series M(m; a; b; x) = m + x + ((m - a + 2b)/2!) x^2 + ((m - a + 3b)(m - 2a + 3b)/3!) x^3 + ... For multivalued solutions beyond the radius of convergence, a geometric criterion for selecting the conjugate series (the same master series, but with a different set of parameters M(m; a'; b'; x')) is proposed, ensuring branch continuity on the complex plane. This representation of power series in terms of master numbers not only allows one to compute coefficients in degenerate cases where the gamma-function representation loses meaning, but also provides a transparent analytical algorithm for the merge operation on master series. The method is illustrated on problems in gas dynamics and plasma physics, where it is demonstrated that physically realizable states require the application of conjugate series beyond the radius of convergence of the basic expansion.

papers.title: A Proof of the Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture for $E$-infinite algebras
papers.abstract: For any finite-dimensional algebra $A$ over an algebraically closed field, we prove that if $A$ is $E$-infinite, then the Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture holds for $A$. In fact, we show that if there is a rational ray outside the $τ$-tilting fan of $A$, then $A$ admits an infinite family of $θ$-stable bricks of dimension $d$, for some positive integer $d$ and weight $θ$. To show our main result, from any $τ$-regular component of $A$ with no dense orbit, we obtain a brick component that also has no dense orbit and whose points in general position are $θ$-stable modules for a given weight $θ$. As an important consequence, we conclude that $A$ is stably-discrete (also called multiplicity-free) if and only if $A$ is $E$-finite. Moreover, we prove that Demonet's (lattice point) Conjecture implies the stable Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture. For $E$-infinite algebras, our results settle several open conjectures. Together with our earlier work and recent developments, this leads to important reductions in the study of some challenging open problems.

papers.title: Mechanism-Aware Ensemble Conditioning for Data-Limited Emulation of Extreme Events
papers.abstract: Extreme events in chaotic systems are difficult to learn from short trajectories because they are controlled by finite-time instabilities rather than by frequently observed bulk dynamics. We propose a mechanism-aware conditioning plug-in framework that turns a nudged ensemble of an imperfect model into a non-intrusive sensor of the local instability geometry. In the small-noise regime, the ensemble covariance has the same finite-time deformation kernels that govern local instability, providing a Jacobian-free proxy for local amplifications around a trajectory. A small Feature-Wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) network injects the ensemble geometry into an otherwise unchanged backbone without modifying the low-fidelity model simulator. We demonstrate this interface in two settings: a Transformer-style residual-attention corrector for a controlled low-dimensional chaotic system and a probabilistic recurrent STORN corrector for topographic two-layer quasi-geostrophic (QG) flow. In the low-dimensional benchmark, leading ensemble-covariance directions identify transient instabilities that are also detected by Optimally Time-Dependent (OTD) modes. FiLM conditioning improves 99th-percentile exceedance-frequency errors over an otherwise identical unconditioned Transformer. In QG, an ensemble-conditioned FiLM-STORN model substantially improves long-horizon rare-event statistics in the data-limited regime, including density-tail errors, exceedance frequencies, and spatial exceedance-area distributions relative to an unconditioned STORN trained on the same data. On averaged high-threshold exceedance diagnostics, it also outperforms the unconditioned baseline STORN trained with 20 times more expensive trajectory data. These results show that local instability geometry is not merely interpretable post hoc, but an actionable conditioning signal for data-efficient rare-event emulation.

papers.title: Feedback Stabilization for Sampled Linear Systems with Control-linear Noise
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider linear stochastic systems with control-linear noise and periodically sampled measurements. We address the problem of feedback stabilization in the mean-square sense. The main contribution of the paper is to provide a necessary and sufficient condition for feedback stabilization. In particular, we relate feedback stabilizability of the stochastic system to the existence of a fixed point of a Riccati-type algebraic equation and, further, to the existence of a solution to an infinite-horizon optimal control problem.

papers.title: One internal stabilization is enough for resolving self-referential tubes
papers.abstract: This paper shows that one internal stabilization is enough to resolve all the self-referential tubes on an embedding. As an application, this paper gives a complete isotopy classification for embedded surfaces with a common geometric dual in orientable $S^2$-bundle over a surface, provided that the embedded surfaces have greater genus than the base surface of the bundle.

papers.title: Partial factorization and reflexivity of operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable infinite dimensional Hilbert space and $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ the algebra of all bounded linear operators on $\mathcal{H}$. A subalgebra $\mathfrak{A}$ in $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ has the left (resp.\ right) partial factorization property if for any invertible operator $S\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$, there exists an isometry (resp.\ a co-isometry) $U\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ such that $U^*S, S^{-1}U\in\mathfrak{A}$. We show that if $\mathfrak{A}$ is weak operator topology closed with the left (resp.\ right) partial factorization property, then $\mathfrak{A}$ is the nest algebra associated with its invariant subspace lattice. In particular, if $\mathfrak{A}$ is transitive, then $\mathfrak{A}=\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$. This gives a positive answer to Question 6.3 raised by B.V.R. Bhat and M. Kumar in \emph{Publ. Res. Inst. Math. Sci.} \textbf{60}(2024), 507--537.

papers.title: On normal forms and first integrals of planar maps at elliptic fixed points
papers.abstract: We study real-analytic planar maps, that admit a real-analytic first integral with a non-degenerate extremum, in a neighbourhood of an elliptic fixed point. We prove that, if the map preserves an analytic area form, it is real-analytically and symplectically conjugate to a twist map, both in the resonant and in the non-resonant case. Using an example, we show that without the area-preservation assumption the conclusion fails. We then prove that a second, continuous, first integral is either a function of the first one or forces the map to be periodic, in which case the map is analytically (and, when area-preserving, symplectically) conjugate to its linear part. We illustrate our results, we study the McMillan map, and a planar map obtained from the Adler--Yamilov Yang--Baxter map.

papers.title: A Weak Topology on Metric Spaces
papers.abstract: We use metric functionals to construct a topology on metric spaces that induces $d$-weak convergence. We show that this topology is invariant under surjective isometries and characterize its convergence in terms of weak metrics. We prove that the topology is $T_1$ on every metric space. For normed linear spaces, we further show that it is Hausdorff and coarser than the classical weak topology. Finally, we construct a sequence in $C[0,1]$ that is unbounded in the sup-norm yet converges $d$-weakly, thereby correcting an assertion in an earlier work.

papers.title: Proof of the singularity conjecture for discrete subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: Let $μ$ be a finitely supported probability measure on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ whose support generates a Zariski-dense discrete subgroup. We prove that its stationary probability measure on $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{R})$ is singular with respect to the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$-invariant probability measure. The proof compares winding variances on finite covers of a closed hyperbolic surface and uses a topological obstruction.

papers.title: Bernoulli flow for Erdős-Rényi graphs
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the adjacency matrix $A$ of the Erdős-Rényi graph $\mathbb G(N,p)$ in the regime $Np \gg (\log N)^2$. We establish optimal isotropic delocalization for the bulk eigenvectors $\boldsymbol u$, meaning that $\langle \boldsymbol v, \boldsymbol u\rangle^2 \leq \frac{C \log N}{N}$ with very high probability for any deterministic normalized $\boldsymbol v$. In addition, we prove local spectral universality in the bulk by showing that the local spectral statistics coincide with those of the GOE. The main tool of our proof is a local law for the resolvent of $A$, down to optimal spectral scales and with optimal error bounds. Its proof relies on a new approach to local laws that we call the Bernoulli flow. It is a characteristic flow method in which the usual Brownian process is replaced by a Bernoulli process, where each edge of the graph forms an independent Markov process that jumps at unit rate from closed to open. The spectral parameter flows according to a suitably constructed matrix-valued Bernoulli characteristic flow.

papers.title: Interaction between nonlinear diffusion and mean curvature of a surface with initial discontinuities
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problems for a class of nonlinear diffusion equations where each initial data is given by a characteristic function of an open set $Ω$ in the whole Euclidean space. If the boundary $\partialΩ$ is of class $C^2$ in a neighborhood of a point $x$ on it, then we extract the mean curvature of $\partialΩ$ at $x$ from the initial diffusion at $x$. This corresponds to the author's previous result for the two-phase linear diffusion equation. Applications to some overdetermined problems for nonlinear diffusion equations are given.

papers.title: Local-to-Global Isometries in Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces: Thompson and Hilbert Geometries of JB-Cones
papers.abstract: We introduce standard-norm generalized gyrovector spaces: generalized gyrovector spaces whose norm-value line has the ordinary real operations and whose fixed scalar maps are continuous. We prove that every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of two such spaces extends uniquely to a global bijective gyrometric isometry. The proof combines gyromidpoints, point reflections, continuation of local isometry germs, and monodromy; joint continuity of scalar multiplication is derived, rather than assumed. The class includes all nonzero real normed spaces and standardized Möbius, Einstein, and proper-velocity models, and is stable under finite and countable $\ell^p$-products. We also obtain bounded mapping-space examples and, under natural continuity assumptions, standard-norm function-space GGVs $C(K,G)$ for compact $K$. These yield non-Hilbertian and hybrid examples. For every unital JB-algebra, the positive invertible cone carries a one-parameter family of standard-norm GGV structures whose gyrometrics are conjugate to Thompson's metric by power maps. The projective positive cone has a parallel family, based on the variation norm modulo the unit, conjugate to Hilbert's projective metric. The projective structures are contractible. Together with global JB-cone isometry classifications, the abstract theorem yields local-to-global extension and classification results for Thompson and Hilbert geometries. Full-rank density matrices and normalized state spaces of finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebras, including the Albert algebra, give concrete projective examples.

papers.title: Cutoff for q-deformed classical card shuffles in the type A Iwahori--Hecke algebra
papers.abstract: We study the mixing behavior of three q-deformed card shuffles on $\mathcal{H}_q(S_n)$: the short systematic scan introduced in \cite{DiaconisRam2000}, the $q$--deformed random--to--random shuffle introduced in \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, and the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle, whose $q=1$ counterpart was studied in \cite{ArfaeeNestoridi}. The first two chains were diagonalized in \cite{DiaconisRam2000} and \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, respectively. Here, we diagonalize the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle and use the spectra of the three chains to study their mixing behavior. For fixed $q>1$, we prove that all three exhibit total variation and $\ell^2$ cutoff. For the short systematic scan, these improve both the upper and lower bounds of Diaconis and Ram \cite{DiaconisRam2000}.

papers.title: A non-trivially non-trivial automorphism at an inaccessible cardinal
papers.abstract: We show that, relative to the existence of an inaccessible cardinal, it is consistent that for an inaccessible cardinal $κ$, there is a non-trivial automorphism of $\mathcal{P}(κ)/\mathrm{fin}$ whose restriction to $\mathcal{P}(β)/\mathrm{fin}$ is induced by a bijection on $β$ for every $β<κ$. This answers questions posed by Larson--McKenney, Shelah--Steprāns, and Veličković.

papers.title: Adaptive stabilization of a leaderless bearing-constrained formation with disturbances
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of regulating and maintaining a target formation characterized by a set of bidirectional bearing constraints under disturbances. The agents in the formation are modeled by single integrators with deterministic bounded continuous disturbances of which both actual function and upper bound are unavailable for the control design. Due to the time-varying disturbances, the target formation is time-varying. We propose displacement/bearing-only based adaptive sliding mode control laws to uniformly asymptotically stabilize the time-varying target formation and reject the matched disturbances, and provide sufficient conditions to prevent possible collisions. A time-dependent adaptive design method is provided to convert the displacement-based control law to a bearing-only one. In addition, to alleviate chattering phenomena from sliding mode control, smooth adaptive control laws are introduced to guarantee uniform global boundedness of the desired formation. Finally, simulation results are given to support the analysis.

papers.title: An AFLT-type generalization of the $q$-Baker--Forrester ex-conjecture
papers.abstract: The Habsieger--Kadell $q$-Morris constant term identity, which is equivalent to the famous $q$-Selberg integral, has been generalized in numerous ways since the 1980s. Among these, there are two important generalizations: (i) the $q$-Baker--Forrester ex-conjecture, which was conjectured by Baker and Forrester in 1998 and proved by Károlyi, Nagy, Petrov and Volkov in 2015; (ii) the AFLT-type $q$-Morris identity (equivalently, the AFLT-type $q$-Selberg integral), which was obtained by Albion, Rains and Warnaar in 2021, as a $q$-analog of the result of Alba, Fateev, Litvinov and Tarnopolskiy (AFLT). In this paper, by the Gessel--Xin method and the Macdonald polynomials with prescribed symmetry, we unify these two generalizations.

papers.title: Override and Update in Restriction Categories
papers.abstract: We study the override and update operators on partial functions from the perspective of restriction categories. We propose a definition of override restriction categories, in which both of the operators in question exist. We prove a number of results concerning these operators and their relationship to the structure of the ambient restriction category, as well as relating them to the existing literature on the override and update operators. We provide various examples of override restriction categories and in particular show that every classical restriction category is an override restriction category.

papers.title: Binary Multiple-Node-Erasure-Correcting Codes over Complete Graphs: Constructions, q-Ary Metric Balls, and Duality
papers.abstract: Codes over graphs store symbols on edges of a complete undirected graph on $n$ vertices with a self-loop at each vertex; erasing a node removes all its incident edges. Extending Yohananov, Efron, and Yaakobi's construction, we obtain binary codes correcting any three node erasures at infinitely many prime lengths $n$, unconditionally, with redundancy $3n-2$, one bit above the graph Singleton bound. The earlier construction has the same redundancy but requires $2$ to be primitive modulo $n$, which is not known for infinitely many primes. We give a deterministic decoder for these triple-node codes using $O(n^2)$ binary operations and construct Singleton-optimal binary triple-node codes at $n=6,8,10,12$. When $2$ is primitive modulo an odd prime $n$, we extend their double- and triple-node codes to binary codes correcting $ρ$ node erasures with redundancy $ρn-(ρ-1)$ for $2\leqρ\leq(n+1)/2$, saving $ρ-1$ bits over the binary symmetric rank-metric construction when $ρ<(n+1)/2$. Over every finite field of size $q$, the node weight of a word is the least number of vertices whose erasure removes its support. We give exact formulas for ball volumes in this node metric and prove that, for fixed $q,t$, the radius-$t$ volume is asymptotic to $\binom nt q^{tn-\binom t2}$ as $n\to\infty$. We obtain existence and covering bounds; for fixed $q,ρ$, we show that linear $ρ$-node-erasure-correcting codes exist with redundancy at most $ρ\log_q n+O_{q,ρ}(1)$ above the graph Singleton bound. Finally, reformulating Yohananov and Yaakobi's criterion, we show that a linear code over any finite field is Singleton-optimal for $ρ$ node erasures if and only if its dual is Singleton-optimal for erasures of the coordinates inside any $n-ρ$ vertices.

papers.title: Effective Joint Equidistribution of Subspaces of Bounded Height in Rigid Adelic Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove effective joint equidistribution for subspaces of fixed dimension in a fixed rigid adelic space over a number field. The joint distribution records the rescaled height, the archimedean position, and the shapes of the subspace and its quotient. More generally, we obtain counting estimates for regions in which the height bound may depend on the position and both shapes. Under a Hölder-type bound for the measure of boundary layers, the estimates have explicit power-saving error terms. We apply these results to counting problems involving slopes, freeness, and semistability, and to Diophantine approximation with prescribed shapes.

papers.title: Thin-Shell implies small-ball deviation via Gaussian tilts
papers.abstract: We show that uniform thin-shell estimates for isotropic log-concave measures $μ$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ yield precise and explicit deviation estimates for the Euclidean norm $|X|$ below the expectation, improving the square-root dependence of Klartag-Lehec to a quadratic one (which is best possible, up to numeric constants). Using the recent Chen-Klartag sharp variance bound, we deduce: $$ μ\left(|X|\le \sqrt{n}-s\right) \le \exp\left\{ -\frac{s^2}{4} \left(1+O\left(\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\right) \right\} \qquad \forall\, s\in(0,\sqrt{n}). $$ In particular, this yields a new and transparent proof that Thin-Shell implies Slicing (by passing through small-ball estimates). Our method is based on using central Gaussian tilts, recently introduced by Brazitikos, which may be thought of as a deterministic version of Eldan's stochastic localization. An anisotropic variant (when $μ$ has general covariance structure) of these deviation estimates is also obtained.

papers.title: Impulse Response Estimation via Laguerre-Fourier Expansion
papers.abstract: The empirical transfer function estimate (ETFE) is a widely used method for system identification of linear time-invariant (LTI) systems in engineering disciplines such as acoustics, audio engineering, seismography, and tomography. However, ETFE suffers from numerical limitations when the excitation signal is band-limited or vanishes at certain frequencies, which is a common physical constraint of the excitation in practice. In such cases, division in the frequency domain becomes heavily ill-conditioned, and small measurement disturbances or numerical inaccuracies can degrade the solution. This paper presents L-ETFE, a generalization of ETFE based on Laguerre-Fourier expansions that addresses these limitations. After a suitable transformation, the method can yield a well-conditioned circulant problem even when the original ETFE system is ill-conditioned. Solving this problem via classical ETFE yields the discrete Laguerre-Fourier coefficients of the system's transfer function. The desired impulse response (IR) of the system-to-be-identified can then be recovered by a subsequent transformation pipeline. We derive novel and efficient algorithms for performing these transformations and analyse the conditioning of the transformed problem, explicitly characterizing its dependence on the input and a parameter used in the Laguerre-Fourier expansion. We evaluate the method on two simulated discrete-time LTI systems of varying complexity. The experiments demonstrate accurate IR recovery for spectral-zero and band-limited excitation, where standard ETFE fails.

papers.title: Square root crystals and the square root of $B(\infty)$
papers.abstract: We introduce a general monoidal category of $\mathbf{N}$-root crystals and then study the special case of square root $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-crystals. The latter objects include Yu's crystals on semistandard set-valued tableaux. Prior work of the first author, Tong, and Yu showed that regular square root $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-crystals can be a useful tool for proving Grothendieck positivity results. The objects studied here go beyond the regular case and allow us to construct a square root analog of the direct limit crystal $B(\infty)$. We give several descriptions of our square root of $B(\infty)$, using marginally large tableaux, the Lusztig or PBW parameterization, and the Nakashima--Zelevinsky polyhedral model. We show that this crystal has a simple character formula, exhibits a nontrivial Demazure filtration, and recovers Yu's semistandard set-valued tableau crystals after taking appropriate tensor products. We also investigate a number of differences between square root crystals and classical crystal constructions.

papers.title: Multiway Partition is FPT for Connectivity Functions
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be a set of $n$ elements, $f\colon2^E\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ be submodular, $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in E$ be distinct, and $k\in\mathbb N$. The Submodular Multiway Partition problem asks whether $E$ has a partition $(P_1,\ldots,P_r)$ with $t_i\in P_i$ for all $i$ and $\sum_i f(P_i)\le k$. We prove that this problem can be solved in $r^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$ time whenever $f$ is posimodular. This covers monotone submodular functions, matroid rank functions, and nonnegative combinations of monotone and symmetric submodular functions. When $f$ is a connectivity function, we remove the dependence on the number of terminals and obtain a $k^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$-time algorithm. The proof is entirely elementary, and is arguably the simplest proof that Edge Multiway Cut is fixed-parameter tractable. As a new consequence, our main result immediately implies that Hypergraph Multiway Partition is fixed-parameter tractable.

papers.title: 3-Neighbor bootstrap percolation on two-dimensional grids
papers.abstract: In the $3$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process, a vertex becomes (and remains) infected if at least three of its neighbors are infected. We say that an initial configuration of infected vertices percolates if eventually all vertices are infected. We exactly determine the size of the minimum percolating set for the $3$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process on all remaining open cases for rectangular grid graphs $P_m\square P_n$. This extends earlier work of Dukes, Noel, and Romer.

papers.title: From Triangular Array Progression to Near-Log-Concave State Transitions
papers.abstract: The paper introduces near-log-concave random variables and the state-transitions of a family of Markov chains derived from an algorithmic integer sequence progression. We propose a combinatorial rule that generates an asymmetric triangular array whose $n$-th row sums to $2^{n}$ for all $n \geq 0$, where every row is the degree sequence of a multigraph without loops. The structure hosts infinitely many zero-free unimodal near-log-concave sequences whose log-concavity deviation converges to $\log(4/3)$ under logarithmic scaling. From a probabilistic perspective, the construct defines a sequence of near-log-concave probability mass functions, from which, a structural decoupling of moments emerges: the mean diverges while the variance asymptotically converges to a steady-state limit. We study the Shannon entropy dynamics of the triangular array, and generate infinitely many right-stochastic matrices via coordinate transformations over the Tychonoff cube. Our specific framework indicates a broader methodology for modelling asymmetric stochastic systems, where distributions propagate as non-dispersive discrete wave packets, advancing indefinitely without flattening.

papers.title: Fixed-time stabilization of systems with nilpotent matrices in the presence of large unknown delays
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study state-feedback fixed-time stabilization of continuous-time perturbed linear systems with nilpotent matrices in the presence of unknown large constant input/measurement delays with known bounds. By using an additional artificial delay, we design a feedback that for a precisely known linear system with a nilpotent matrix drives the state to zero in fixed time (which is larger than the bound of the unknown delay) and achieves input-to-state stability with a large exponential decay rate in the presence of additive disturbances and small system matrix perturbations and nonlinearities. For perturbed single integrators, fixed-time stabilization is achieved in the case of fast-varying unknown measurement delays with known bounds. The results are extended to discrete-time systems. Numerical simulations illustrate the efficiency of the results.

papers.title: Tiling a triangle into a prime number of congruent triangles
papers.abstract: We prove that if a triangle is cut into $N$ congruent triangles and $N$ is prime, then $N=2$, $N=3$, or $N\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and every such $N$ occurs. In particular, if $N > 3$ then $N$ is not a prime congruent to $3$ modulo $4$. All the proofs in this paper have been formalized in Lean. The argument divides into cases according to possible shapes of the tiled triangle. Let $α,β,γ$ be the angles of the tile. Prior to this posting, there remained several open shapes. The two most difficult shapes were $(2α,β,α+β)$, the {\em triquadratic} shape, and $(β,β,3α)$, the {\em isosceles-$β$} shape, in which $3α+2β= π$ and $α$ is not a rational multiple of $π$. A previous version of this paper relied on incorrect proofs of those cases, which have been retracted, and are replaced here by correct proofs. For each of those two shapes the number of tiles has the form $N = j^2 N_0$, where $N_0 > 1$ is determined by the shape of the tile and $j$ is a positive integer; so $N$ is prime, or even squarefree, only if $j = 1$. We prove by geometric reasoning that neither shape admits a tiling with $j = 1$, which shows that for both shapes $N$ is never prime, and indeed never squarefree. The shape $(β,β,3α+β)$ (where $3α+ 3β= π$) has been settled by Bonfioli. In this paper, we settle the remaining cases, by number-theoretic arguments based on the area equation. Those proofs rule out $N$ prime, but not $N$ squarefree, and we give examples to show that tilings with squarefree $N$ do sometimes exist.

papers.title: Sonic-supersonic jet flows from a straight two-dimensional nozzle with van der Waals equation of state
papers.abstract: This article concerns sonic-supersonic jet flows issuing from a two-dimensional straight nozzle described by the steady compressible Euler system under the van der Waals equation of state. The flow state is prescribed at the nozzle exit, while the surrounding medium is assumed to be either a vacuum or a static atmosphere with lower pressure. When the flow reaches the sonic state at the nozzle exit, the governing equations become degenerate hyperbolic and the resulting jet flow problem can be formulated as a degenerate free boundary problem. The analysis is further complicated by singular behavior near the endpoints of the nozzle exit. By employing characteristic decompositions and suitable a priori estimates, we establish the global existence of locally Lipschitz continuous sonic-supersonic jet flows expanding into a vacuum. Moreover, in the presence of a static atmosphere with pressure lower than that at the nozzle exit, we prove the local existence of sonic-supersonic jet flows near the nozzle exit.

papers.title: Standard modules and Dold--Kan correspondences for generalized Reedy categories
papers.abstract: We develop a representation-theoretic approach to generalized Reedy categories through a systematic study of standard modules. For a broad class of these categories, we provide a uniform, computable framework that reduces abstract Hom-spaces between standard modules to elementary linear algebra and graph theory via incidence matrices and morphism fibers. As a primary application, we establish a uniform extension of the Dold--Kan correspondence for certain categories arising from rooted trees, and obtain an orthogonal decomposition for finite spiders, including the category of finite sets and partial injections. Crucially, this machinery unifies and provides a single conceptual framework for several classical, seemingly disparate results across algebraic topology and representation theory, including Kuhn's decomposition theorem for vector spaces and the Thévenaz--Webb semisimplicity theorem for Mackey functors.

papers.title: Compact Coefficient Formulae for Logarithmic Tangent and Hyperbolic Integrals
papers.abstract: We develop compact coefficient-extraction formulae for several families of hyperbolic, logarithmic tangent, and Malmsten-type integrals whose values are finite linear combinations of odd zeta values and even Dirichlet beta values. The principal advantage of these formulae is that coefficients previously encoded by recursive arrays or nested finite sums are replaced by a single coefficient of an explicit elementary expression. This makes the coefficients easier to compute, keeps the dependence on the parameters visible, and reveals structural features---such as vanishing ranges, extremal coefficients, and sign patterns---without hidden cancellations. For shifted hyperbolic integrals with numerator $\sinh((2k+1)x)$, the coefficients are expressed through Chebyshev--arcsine extractions. The same mechanism yields Laurent coefficient formulae for logarithmic tangent integrals and leads to direct proofs of simple initial and terminal coefficients, including a parity-free terminal identity. For $m,n\geq1$, $m\geq n$, and $m+n$ even, we prove \[ \int_0^\infty\frac{\tanh^{m+1}x}{x^{n+1}}\,dx = (-1)^{(m-n)/2} \sum_{p=\lceil n/2\rceil}^{(m+n)/2} \binom{2p}{n} (2^{2p+1}-1) \frac{ζ(2p+1)}{π^{2p}} [u^{m+n-2p}](u\cot u)^{m+1}. \] \[\int_0^\infty \frac{\tanh^m x}{x^n\cosh x}\,dx = (-1)^{(m-n)/2} \sum_{p=\lceil n/2\rceil}^{(m+n)/2} 2^{2p}\binom{2p-1}{n-1} \frac{β(2p)}{π^{2p-1}} [u^{m+n-2p}] \frac{u}{\sin u}(u\cot u)^m \] In the diagonal zeta case, the formula gives the family $\int_0^\infty(\tanh x/x)^N\,dx$ in a direct, non-recursive form and makes the disappearance of the initial zeta values immediate.

papers.title: The quantum double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct the quantum double $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$. We describe the algebraic structure of $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ by generators and relations. Moreover, we give the comultiplication $Δ$, the counit $\varepsilon$ and the antipode $S$, respectively. Finally, we classify all irreducible representations of $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ when $p=2$.

papers.title: Spectral Characterisation of Covariance Existence in Markov-Switching Affine Recurrences
papers.abstract: This paper provides a finite-dimensional spectral characterisation of covariance existence for finite-state Markov-switching affine recurrences of the form \[ Z_{n+1}=A_{Θ_{n+1}}Z_n+ζ_{n+1}. \] While strict stationarity is typically governed by negativity of the top Lyapunov exponent of the random matrix products, this does not ensure finite variances, covariances, or Pearson correlations. We show that these second-order properties are governed instead by a Markov-switching Kronecker operator. Writing \(T_{ji}:=p_{ij}(A_j\otimes A_j)\) and denoting its spectral radius by \(ρ(T)\), we prove that, under a natural Perron-excitation condition on the innovation covariance, \(ρ(T)<1\) is necessary and sufficient for the stationary solution to be square-integrable. When this condition holds, the regime-weighted second moments solve a finite-dimensional linear system, yielding the covariance matrix explicitly. Thus, the mean-square spectral condition becomes an exact covariance-existence criterion for the stationary law. Examples illustrate the separation: the top Lyapunov exponent may be negative while the second-order spectral radius exceeds one, so strict stationarity can persist even when finite second moments, and hence population covariances and Pearson correlations, do not exist.

papers.title: Trefftz DG Approximation of the T-Matrix for Scattering by Periodic Layered Structures
papers.abstract: We study the scattering of time-harmonic electromagnetic waves by periodic layered gratings, modelled by the 2D Helmholtz equation. The periodic obstacle may include penetrable and impenetrable regions, and consists of a finite number of stacked layers. The boundary value problem is formulated on a single periodic cell using quasi-periodic boundary conditions. The radiation condition in the vertical directions is imposed through Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) operators. To efficiently treat multilayer configurations, we adopt a formulation based on the T-matrix method. The global scattering problem is decomposed into boundary value problems posed on individual layers. On the layer boundaries, the field is expressed in terms of quasi-periodic modal expansions, and the layer T-matrix describes the map between incoming and outgoing wave modes. Each local T-matrix is approximated numerically using a plane-wave based Trefftz Discontinuous Galerkin (TDG) method, which provides an efficient discretization of the layer scattering response. The T-matrix technique leads to linear computational complexity in the number of layers in the grating.

papers.title: Existence of the Lyapunov exponent for $S$-unimodal maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that for any $S$-unimodal map $T$ on $[0,1]$ with a non-flat critical point the Lyapunov exponent exists for Lebesgue almost every point and is equal to a constant $λ_T$. Moreover, $λ_T=0$ if and only if $T$ admits neither an absolutely continuous $T$-invariant probability measure with positive entropy nor a strictly stable periodic orbit. Consequently, if an $S$-unimodal map with a non-flat critical point is infinitely renormalizable or non-statistical then for Lebesgue almost every $x\in [0,1]$ the Lyapunov exponent along the orbit of $x$ exists and is equal to $0$. A key ingredient is the following result of independent interest. If an $S$-unimodal map with a non-flat critical point has no periodic attractor then for Lebesgue almost every $x\in [0,1]$ the lower Lyapunov exponent along the orbit of $x$ is non-negative. This shows that, in the absence of periodic attractors, exponential contraction cannot occur along the orbit of Lebesgue almost every point.

papers.title: Adaptive Reparametrized Time for Score-Based Diffusion Sampling
papers.abstract: We study timestep allocation for score-based diffusion sampling, where a learned reverse-time dynamics is discretized on a finite grid. Uniform and hand-crafted schedules are standard choices, but they rely on fixed prescriptions and can therefore be suboptimal. To address this limitation, we propose Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART), a continuous-time control formulation that learns a time change by treating the speed of the sampling clock as the control, so that a uniform grid on the learned clock induces adaptive timesteps in the original diffusion time. Based on a leading-order Euler error surrogate, ART provides a principled objective for allocating timesteps along the sampling trajectory. To solve this deterministic control problem, we introduce ART-RL, an auxiliary randomized formulation with Gaussian policies that turns schedule learning into a continuous-time reinforcement learning problem. We prove that the randomized ART-RL formulation is equivalent to ART at the optimizer level, in the sense that its optimal Gaussian policy recovers the optimal ART time-warping rate through its mean. We further establish policy evaluation and policy improvement characterizations and derive trajectory-based moment identities that yield implementable actor--critic updates for learning the schedule. Across experiments ranging from controlled low-dimensional settings to image generation, ART-RL can be plugged into existing diffusion samplers by changing only the timestep grid, consistently improving sample quality over strong baseline schedules at matched budgets while leaving the rest of the sampling pipeline unchanged. The learned schedules also exhibit broad generalization, transferring without retraining across sampling budgets, datasets, solvers, pipelines, and representation spaces.

papers.title: GAIA: Geometry-Adaptive Operator Learning for Forward and Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Operator learning for partial differential equations (PDEs) on arbitrary geometries builds fast neural surrogates for large-scale simulation. While recent geometry-adaptive neural operators have made substantial progress, they are mainly designed for forward problems in which inputs and outputs share the same spatial domain. This limits their applicability for boundary value problems (BVPs) and inverse problems, where inputs and outputs may live on different domains. We introduce the Geometry-Adaptive Integral Autoencoder (GAIA), an operator learning model that encodes the domain boundary and the interior field distribution into geometry tokens, and conditions integral transform layers on these tokens via cross-attention, allowing the kernel to adapt locally to geometric features. This yields an architecture capable of learning solution operators for forward and inverse problems on arbitrary domains, solving each in a single pass at inference without per-domain optimization, iterative refinement, or graph construction. We evaluate GAIA on seven 2D and 3D benchmarks, four of which are new or substantially extended benchmarks for inverse problems and BVP: electrical impedance tomography, optical tomography, 3D Darcy flow on varying geometries, and a modified setting of the Poisson BVP on mechanical components benchmark (MCB). GAIA sets new state-of-the-art results on every inverse and BVP task, reducing median relative $L^2$ error by 64% on airfoil flow reconstruction and 22% on EIT relative to the next best amortized method, and outperforming all baselines on every shape category of MCB. On other forward problems, GAIA is competitive with specialized solvers while maintaining stable accuracy across point resolutions on which transformer-based baselines degrade.

papers.title: Plancherel Identities for unbounded subsets of $\mathbb R^d$
papers.abstract: We investigate spectral pairs associated with unbounded subsets of $\mathbb R^d$ that are periodic with respect to full-rank lattices. We establish a characterization of such spectral pairs in terms of the spectrality of an associated bounded fundamental component. More precisely, we prove that the Fourier transform defines an isometric isomorphism onto an $L^2$ space with an explicitly determined absolutely continuous pair measure, supported on a union of translates of a dual-lattice fundamental domain, if and only if the bounded component admits an orthogonal basis of exponential functions with frequencies in the dual lattice. In particular, the Plancherel identity alone is sufficient to characterize these spectral pairs. As an application, when the bounded component tiles $\br^d$ by a lattice, we obtain an equivalence between certain translational tiling properties of unbounded periodic sets and the existence of the corresponding Plancherel identities. We also examine periodicity properties of sets that tile by finite translation sets, highlighting distinctions between the one-dimensional and higher-dimensional settings.

papers.title: The parental parsimony problem on binary, tree-child phylogenetic networks
papers.abstract: Phylogenetic reconstruction is one of the major challenges in computational biology. Among existing reconstruction methods for phylogenetic networks, an important subtask emerges in extending a leaf-labelling on a phylogenetic network to determine a most parsimonious tree inside the network. There exist different variants of this subtask depending on the biological model assumptions for which distinct evolutionary phenomena are captured by the network. In this article we assume that next to hybridization or recombination events, also allopolyploidy or incomplete lineage sorting are present. Then, finding the most parsimonious tree inside the network is called the parental parsimony score problem (PPS), a NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem. We provide the first constant-factor approximation for the PPS on arbitrary but fixed leaf labels and a class of networks on which the PPS remains NP-hard, namely binary, semi-simplex, tree-child phylogenetic networks. Furthermore, we introduce a novel exact solution algorithm for the PPS on binary, tree-child phylogenetic networks and analyze its performance on simulated data.

papers.title: The $M/M_D/c$ queue with dependent servers: A canonical Markovian extension of $M/M/c$
papers.abstract: The classical $M/M/c$ queue is the canonical Markovian model for a single-node queue with Poisson arrivals and homogeneous independent servers. We identify its natural counterpart when the servers are dependent. For homogeneous Markovian labelled service-completion mechanisms (retaining the identities of the completing servers), consistency under restriction to subsets of busy servers is equivalent to an independent Poisson shock representation, yielding homogeneous Marshall--Olkin multivariate exponential residual-service laws. This characterization identifies the $M/M_D/c$ queue as the canonical Markovian extension of $M/M/c$ to dependent homogeneous servers, with a Markovian queue-length process. For heterogeneous servers, augmenting boundary states with busy-server identities yields a Markovian queue-state process, as in the classical independent-server setting. For arbitrary $c$ and fixed idle-set assignment, we derive an explicit matrix-analytic stationary solution and departure and customer-delay laws. Waiting time conditional on delay is exponential, and the stationary sojourn distribution has a phase-type representation with at most $c+1$ phases. A three-server comparison with identical bivariate residual-service laws demonstrates how higher-order dependence can change waiting-time behavior.

papers.title: Well-posedness of the weakly singular Burton-Miller equation for Helmholtz transmission problems
papers.abstract: Although various boundary integral formulations are available for the Helmholtz transmission problem, the weakly singular Burton--Miller equation is promising because it possesses favorable properties for numerical computation. This paper rigorously shows that the weakly singular Burton--Miller equation is well-posed. We establish bounded invertibility on $C(Γ)\times C(Γ)$ for $C^2$ boundaries by proving injectivity and applying the Fredholm alternative. For the prescribed analytic incident field, the integral equation further yields $u\in C^{1,β}(Γ)$ and $q\in C^{0,β}(Γ)$, for $0<β<1$. We also provide a proof that its fictitious eigenvalues are associated with an exterior Dirichlet problem and an interior impedance problem.

papers.title: Agentic Symbolic Search: Approximating Solutions of PDEs Beyond Hand-crafted Expressions, Meshes, and Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Numerical methods and neural networks have transformed our understanding of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs), yet discovering mathematical representations that explain their dynamics remains largely an expert task. We introduce Agentic Symbolic Search (ASYS), in which coding agents construct and refine explicit approximations from a known PDE and supplied mathematical knowledge. ASYS couples evolutionary search over differentiable symbolic programs with gradient-based fitting, using the governing equation to evaluate candidates and guide their revision. For a singular generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda profile, ASYS infers a missing decay term that sets how fast the field approaches its singular-time limit, and builds a basis that fits the profile to a median error of $3.90\times10^{-5}\%$. For Fujita blow-up, separating diffusion from reaction and deriving a local response lowers the supplied formula's error from 55.5% to 0.0879%. For Allen-Cahn interfaces, a 14-parameter construction yields a mode-coupling law confirmed by independent simulations. These studies show how agentic search develops mathematical starting points into accurate, analyzable approximations.

papers.title: List coloring uncrowded hypergraphs at the shattering threshold
papers.abstract: A foundational theorem of Ajtai, Komlós, Pintz, Spencer, and Szemerédi asserts that every $n$-vertex $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph (i.e., with girth at least $5$) of maximum degree at most $Δ$ contains an independent set of size $cn(\logΔ/Δ)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. Improving an earlier bound of Frieze and Mubayi, Iliopoulos showed that every such hypergraph has list chromatic number at most $(1+o(1))(k-1)(Δ/\logΔ)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$. Determining the optimal leading constant in this bound remains a major open problem. A natural target, suggested by the coupon-collector heuristic, is $(k-1)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, which also corresponds to the shattering threshold for coloring sparse random hypergraphs. Our main result shows that this target is attained: for every integer $k\ge2$, every $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph of maximum degree at most $Δ$ satisfies: $$χ_\ell(\mathcal{H})\le(1+o(1))\Big((k-1)\fracΔ{\logΔ}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}.$$ In particular, this confirms a 2019 conjecture of Molloy for uncrowded hypergraphs. Building on this result, we prove that every $k$-uniform linear hypergraph of maximum degree at most $Δ$ has chromatic number at most $(c_k+o(1))(Δ/\logΔ)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, where $c_k\to1$ as $k\to\infty$, thereby proving a conjecture of Verstraëte and Wilson on the independence number of linear hypergraphs in the stronger form of colorings. Our techniques also yield a palette sparsification theorem for uncrowded hypergraphs, partially answering a question of Casselgren and Eriksson.

papers.title: Resolution of Vinzant's Conjecture on Phase Retrieval Injectivity
papers.abstract: Let $A\in\mathbb C^{N\times M}$ with $N=4M-5$ has independent standard complex Gaussian entries. We prove that the probability that the phase retrieval map generated by $A$ is injective is strictly smaller than $1$, and is $O(M^{-1})$ as $M\to \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Cynthia Vinzant, which was later restated by Afonso S. Bandeira in \cite{bandeira2026randomstrasse101}. The main result of this paper was obtained using generative AI, in particular GPT6-Astra, GPT 5.6-sol, and the Rethlas system.

papers.title: The inradius law for the cavities of planar Brownian motion, with applications to the Wiener sausage
papers.abstract: ```text Let $K_1=B[0,1]$ be the trace of a planar Brownian motion, and let $N_{\mathrm{in}}(η)$ be the number of its cavities, the bounded components of $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus K_1$, whose inradius exceeds $η$. We prove that, almost surely and in $L^p$ for every $p\in[1,2]$, $η^2(\log(1/η))^2 N_{\mathrm{in}}(η)\to c_{\mathrm{in}}=\fracπ{2}\int G^2 d\mathcal{L}\in(0,\frac12]$, where $G$ is the ratio of the inradius of a shape to the square root of its area and $\mathcal{L}$ is Werner's limiting shape law. The inradius, and not the area by which the cavities have been counted classically, decides survival under thickening: a cavity contains a hole of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ if and only if its inradius exceeds $r$. Through Brownian scaling, the number $β_1^T(r)$ of holes of the sausage of radius $r$ of $B[0,T]$, the Betti curve of its degree-one persistent homology, is bounded below at the scale $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$, with the identified constant $4c_{\mathrm{in}}$ in expectation and with any smaller constant with probability tending to one. A matching upper bound cannot follow from any general bound in terms of perimeter, area, diameter or length; we prove that it is equivalent to a first-moment estimate for near-critical pockets, the holes at level $η$ on which the distance to the trace is at most $2η$. That estimate is proved in a companion paper, so that the expected number of holes is of exact order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$. ```

papers.title: Asymptotic Theory for Sample Canonical Direction Alignment in High-Dimensional Spiked CCA
papers.abstract: This paper studies the asymptotic behavior of sample canonical directions in a finite-rank spiked high-dimensional canonical correlation analysis model under a Gaussian population assumption. Under the asymptotic regime in which the dimensions of the two data blocks grow proportionally with the sample size, sample canonical directions are generally not consistent estimators of their population counterparts, even when the corresponding sample canonical correlations separate from the bulk spectrum. To quantify directional recovery, we investigate the squared alignment between a sample canonical direction and its associated population direction. For a supercritical simple population spike, we establish an explicit nonzero deterministic limit for the squared alignment. In contrast, for population non-spikes, we show that the alignment with the corresponding population signal directions vanishes asymptotically. Thus, the same phase transition that governs eigenvalue separation also marks a transition in directional recovery. For a supercritical simple spike, we further prove a central limit theorem for its fluctuations around the deterministic limit, with an explicit asymptotic variance expressed through deterministic limits of resolvent trace functionals. To make the theoretical quantities computable from data, we further construct plug-in estimators for both the deterministic alignment limit and the asymptotic variance by inverting the deterministic outlier eigenvalue map, and prove their consistency. Numerical simulations and a real-data illustration support the theoretical results and demonstrate how the proposed estimators assess the recovery quality of sample canonical directions.

papers.title: Temporal Cliques Admit Linear Spanners
papers.abstract: A temporal graph is a graph in which every edge carries a non-empty set of time labels, and it is temporally connected if for every two vertices $u$ and $v$, there exists a $u$-$v$-path with non-decreasing time labels. A spanner is a subset of its edges preserving temporal connectivity. Unlike static graphs, temporally connected graphs need not admit sparse spanners; nonetheless, minimizing spanner size is a central and widely studied problem. A particularly intriguing question is whether temporal cliques admit spanners of linear size. Despite considerable effort over the past years, the best known upper bound remained $O(n \log n)$. We finally resolve this question, proving that every temporal clique on $n$ vertices admits a spanner of size $7n$. Moreover, such a spanner can be computed in polynomial time.

papers.title: A Noetherian Hopf algebra is affine iff its Hopf coradical is affine
papers.abstract: Let $\K$ be an arbitrary field. Extending the structural frameworks established in \cite{JZ2025-2}, this paper introduces novel techniques utilizing mirror reduction orders, prime words, and the generalized lifting methodology. We establish a definitive necessary and sufficient criterion for the affineness of Noetherian Hopf algebras, thereby providing a significant advancement toward resolving the long-standing Wu--Zhang question \cite{WZ2003}. Specifically, we prove that a left or right Noetherian Hopf algebra over $\K$ is affine if and only if its Hopf coradical is affine. This characterization fundamentally reduces the verification to the first filtration step, yielding a criterion that is structurally transparent and highly operational. To establish necessity, we provide an essential intrinsic result demonstrating that the Hopf coradical of an affine Hopf algebra inherits the property of being affine. Furthermore, as direct applications of this equivalence, we prove that a left or right Noetherian Hopf algebra $H$ is affine provided that its coradical $H_{(0)}$ forms a subalgebra (the dual Chevalley property), its coradical $H_{(0)}$ is cocommutative, or its Hopf coradical $H_{[0]}$ is commutative.

papers.title: Inequivalence of the various notions of completeness for Cartan geometries
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the three standard notions of completeness for Cartan geometries are not actually equivalent, modernizing and extending results due to Yeaton Clifton. In an effort to rectify the folklore on the topic, we also provide detailed explanations of how specious proofs in the literature that would claim that these types of completeness are equivalent break down. In the affine case, we construct geodesically complete homogeneous examples with an inextensible exponential curve for each connected Lie group of dimension at least 2, as well as an infinite-dimensional family of examples whose exponential curves are defined for all time but whose overlying frame bundle is not complete as a metric space with respect to a natural metric for the Cartan connection.

papers.title: Spectral inequalities for weighted $p$-Laplacians via Talenti symmetrization
papers.abstract: We consider the weighted $p$-Laplacian associated with a measure $μ$ having a continuous positive density with respect to the Lebesgue measure on an open convex subset $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$. We prove that Talenti's weighted Pólya--Szegő inequality---originally established for Lipschitz functions on $X$---extends to the weighted Sobolev space of functions vanishing on the relative boundary of an open set $Ω\subset X$, defined as the closure of Lipschitz functions supported away from it. This yields Faber--Krahn-type inequalities for the first $(p,q)$-eigenvalue of the weighted Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian. We present several examples fitting this abstract framework, in which the isoperimetric sets are balls, half-spaces, or complements of balls.

papers.title: Revisiting Eigenvalue-Only Divide-and-Conquer Tridiagonal Eigensolver from Algorithmic Perspective
papers.abstract: Divide-and-conquer (D&C) is the natural parallel strategy for symmetric tridiagonal eigenvalue decomposition, yet eigenvalue-only solvers fall back to serial QR algorithm because the quadratic transform state each merge carries exhausts memory at scale. In this paper, we demonstrate that each merge stage in D&C needs only two boundary rows, the first and last rows of a node's eigenvector block, and these close into a recurrence whose parent rows follow from its children's and local merge data alone, so the state is carried up the tree with nothing replayed and persistent memory drops from quadratic to linear. Because this state keeps no replay workspace, adapting the schedule to each merge's post-deflation active rank is a scheduling choice, so both CPU and GPU spend finer-grained parallelism only where substantial secular work survives. We evaluate optimized CPU and GPU implementations, with complexity and correctness analysis, against QR, bisection, and D&C routines in standard libraries.

papers.title: Maximum Probability of Independence in Transitive Matroids
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid on a finite ground set $E$, and suppose that the automorphism group of $M$ acts transitively on $E$. We show the following: if $X_1,\ldots,X_K$ are sampled independently from a distribution $p$ on $E$, then the probability that the samples are distinct and that $\{X_1,\ldots,X_K\}$ is an independent set in $M$ is quasi-concave in $p$ and maximized when $p$ is uniform. For $2\le K\le\rank(M)$, we characterize all maximizers by uniform total mass on the parallel classes and, in particular, show that the maximizer is unique and has global quadratic stability when $M$ is simple.
