To address this, we use tools from dynamical systems and operator theory to express the gradient flow of a general class of stochastic differential equations as a composition of linear operators, allowing us to relate collapse to low-rank biases in generative models. In variational inference and flow-matching tasks, we show that this bias can manifest in two different mechanisms: i) where collapsed models are stable fixed points of the gradient flow, or ii) in sequential feature learning, where smaller modes take progressively longer to be learned, producing an effective collapse for a fixed training budget. Together these findings point to a trade-off between feature learning and collapse, suggesting an operator view as a step towards a unified framework for understanding the learning dynamics of dynamical systems-based generative models.

papers.title: The strong cylinder conjecture over prime fields
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be prime and let $S\subseteq\mathbb F_p^3$ have $p^2$ points, with every affine plane meeting $S$ in a multiple of $p$ points. We give a self-contained argument that $S$ is a union of $p$ parallel lines.

papers.title: Super-positivity via Dirichlet theta functions
papers.abstract: Let $χ$ be a quadratic Dirichlet character and let $Λ(χ, s)$ be its associated completed $L$-function. The super-positivity property, introduced by Yun--Zhang (2017), asserts that $Λ^{(m)} \left( \frac{1}{2}, χ\right) \geq 0$ for all $m \geq 0$. We show that a certain positivity property of its Dirichlet theta function $θ(t, χ)$, namely that $θ(t, χ)>0$ for all $t \geq 1$, implies the super-positivity property for $χ$. We then investigate a refined form of the above property: we conjecture that the sequence $\{ Λ^{(2m)}\left(\frac{1}{2}, χ\right )\}_{ m \geq 0}$ is always eventually increasing and has at most one turning point, and we prove these assertions again when $θ(t, χ)>0$ for $t \geq 1$.

papers.title: On semigroups of order-decreasing partial isometries: presentations and ranks of certain ideals
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{DP}_{n}^{-}$ denote the monoid of all order-decreasing partial isometries on a chain with $n$ elements, and let $\mathcal{ODP}_{n}^{-}$ denote the submonoid of $\mathcal{DP}_{n}^{-}$ consisting of all order-preserving partial isometries. In this paper, for each $1\leq r\leq n$, we determine minimal generating sets of the ideals $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}(n,r) =\{ α\in \mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n} : \lvert \im(α) \rvert \leq r \}$ of $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n}$ and $\mathcal{DP}^{-}(n,r) =\{ α\in \mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n} : \lvert \im(α) \rvert \leq r \}$ of $\mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n}$, thereby determining their ranks. Furthermore, we give presentations for the monoids $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n}$ and $\mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n}$.

papers.title: Controllability with and without Dissipation - a Port-Hamiltonian Approach
papers.abstract: A port-Hamiltonian system with energy dissipation can be modelled by connecting a larger, non-dissipative system with a so-called closure relation. We study whether approximative controllability of the dissipative system is characterised by the same property of the larger system. The answer is negative in general, but positive for sufficiently well-structured systems - this is our main result. As a simple illustration, we show how approximate controllability of a wave equation implies approximate controllability of a heat equation.

papers.title: On necessary conditions for feedback stabilizability when the control space is a fiber bundle
papers.abstract: Within control theory, a question of great interest is to understand when a stabilizing feedback exists. Building upon Krasnosel'skiĭ and co-workers, necessary conditions for the existence of a continuous stabilizing feedback have been pioneered by Brockett and Coron, providing so-called adversarial and homological conditions, respectively. Kvalheim recently generalized their conditions from equilibria to compact attractors and---in line with earlier work by Coron---showed that when a control system can be identified with a vector bundle, the homology condition is stronger, that is, the homology condition implies the adversary condition. Kvalheim also showed that this comparison breaks when extending the case of vector bundles to fiber bundles. In this work, we propose and characterize an appropriate adversarial condition for control systems represented by fiber bundles. The homology condition, on the other hand, is already well-defined, showcasing its general applicability. With the generalized conditions at hand, we show that by appropriately relaxing the regularity of the feedback under consideration, that is, by allowing for mild discontinuities, the homology condition implies the adversarial condition for fiber bundles. Thereby, in this work, we extend these earlier comparative results.

papers.title: Ride-time inequalities for the event-based formulation of the dial-a-ride problem
papers.abstract: The paper investigates the model structure of the event-based mixed-integer programming formulation of the Dial-a-Ride Problem. We find that the design of events allows introducing new valid inequalities on the ride times. Time progression is modelled using Big M constraints which lead to a weak LP relaxation and deteriorate the solution process. The newly introduced valid inequalities deal with this issue and allow reducing the computation times by up to 99% for benchmark instances (a-X* instances) in comparison to the state-of-the-art event-based model formulation. To evaluate the potential of the new valid inequalities, we increase the time windows on the benchmark set by another 15 minutes and evaluate the model on the same instances with a time-related objective function where the Big-M-influenced time variables directly occur in the objective function. Even for the large time windows only two instances could not be solved to optimality within two hours (final gaps of at most 0.8%). With the time-oriented objective the largest average computation time with our valid inequalities was 74 seconds.

papers.title: Almost complex structures on triple blow-ups
papers.abstract: We show that for certain smooth 4-manifolds, almost complex structures on its triple blow-up induce all its spin$^c$ structures with a non-negative-dimensional Seiberg-Witten moduli space. Since this includes all basic classes, our result provides an approximation to the simple type conjecture. Moreover, we expand a result by Dieter Kotschick showing that every finitely presented group is the fundamental group of an almost complex 4-manifold. We show that it can furthermore be chosen to have every even integer as the virtual dimension of the Seiberg-Witten moduli space of a spin$^c$ structure.

papers.title: Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields
papers.abstract: We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields. For this class, we establish commutator and second-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formulas with cubic remainders in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$, controlled by the second moment and uniform in the number of particles. The proofs rely on finite-particle realizations, which preserve the bracket and jointly determine the nonlocal field. We also obtain uniform estimates for smooth bounded kernels and a Leibniz rule for the action of polynomial fields on polynomial observables. Examples from collective dynamics show that the vanishing of the spatial bracket at a fixed law is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation. They concern symmetries, aggregation-dependent rotation, synchronization, the transmission of a turn along a hierarchy, effective three-body interactions and occupancy-dependent circulation.

papers.title: Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey
papers.abstract: Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schrödinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.

papers.title: Permutons
papers.abstract: Permutons are limit structures for large permutations. Intrinsically, a permuton is a familiar mathematical object: a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals. The compact space of permutons completes the set of permutations of all sizes under a natural topology; each permuton is not only a limit of permutations but also a generator of random permutations. Since their (relatively recent) discovery as a tool for understanding the behavior of large (possibly random) permutations, permutons have proved remarkably fruitful, with dozens of fascinating connections to combinatorics and probability. We review the fundamentals of permutons, sometimes providing new, shorter proofs, and give an account of some of their myriad applications. The survey concludes with a long list of open problems. An extensive -- but not comprehensive -- bibliography is appended.

papers.title: Branched real projective structures on surfaces, cyclic Higgs Bundles and Anosov representations
papers.abstract: We use the theory of $3$-cyclic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$-Higgs bundles to study real branched projective structures on compact surfaces recently introduced by the authors. After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities. In the final part of the paper, using different methods, we prove that every Anosov surface group representation into $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ is either Hitchin or belongs to the Barbot component. As a by-product, we obtain that some of the representations associated with the branched structures constructed above are not Anosov.

papers.title: Operational Interpretation of Controllability Allocation Scores via Randomized Interventions
papers.abstract: Controllability allocation scores (CASs) assign weights to virtual input channels without specifying how interventions should be implemented. This paper provides an operational interpretation through randomized finite-duration interventions with prescribed, possibly candidate-dependent waveforms. Selection probabilities are fixed before a mean-output target is specified, while waveform amplitudes are optimized after the target is revealed. We derive the unique minimum expected-energy amplitude policy and formulate volumetric and weighted average-energy allocation criteria. We also establish a finite-trial mean-output error bound and show that waveform-based weighted AE-CAS minimizes an upper bound on the target-averaged mean-square error. We establish uniform convergence of normalized waveform-response Gramians and show that accumulation points of optimal allocations solve the limiting problem. With uniform timing, equal positive waveform efficiencies recover the original CAS in the short-duration limit, whereas unequal efficiencies yield waveform-weighted limits. Under the former conditions, the limiting error bound is proportional to the original weighted AE-CAS objective. For common waveforms, we further establish an exact finite-duration correspondence with the original full-state V-CAS under uniform timing.

papers.title: A Computational Brainsphere Model for the Simulation of Alzheimer's Disease
papers.abstract: Nowadays, there are different medical imaging techniques to collect data about the progression of Alzhei\-mer's disease in a patient's brain. These data describe different phenomena which are still not understood from a biological point of view. How can these data sets be combined in a mathematical model to simulate the evolution of such a neurodegenerative disease in a computer? In this snapshot, we present one possible approach to address this task with the help of graph theory and partial differential equations.

papers.title: Good colorings of doubled triangles and a conjecture of Schwartz
papers.abstract: A good coloring of a sphere triangulation is a black-and-white coloring of its faces such that, at every vertex, the numbers of black and white faces differ by a multiple of~$3$. Good colorings correspond to proper vertex $4$-colorings. For a good coloring with fold count $\mathrm{f}$ (the number of black-white edges) on a triangulation with $F$ faces, R.~E.~Schwartz introduced the Eisenstein isoperimetric ratio $η=\mathrm{f}^2/F$. For triangulations with degree sequence $6,\dots,6,2,2,2$, he proved that $η\ge3$ and conjectured that every such triangulation has a good coloring with $η$ below a universal constant. These triangulations are indexed by the nonzero Eisenstein integers~$β$. We study the family $\T(n)$ given by $β=n$, a positive integer, which consists of the doubled equilateral triangles of side~$n$. We prove that every good coloring of $\T(n)$ has at least $3n$ folds, so $η\ge9/2$, and that this bound is attained for every~$n$. Thus the minimum of $η$ on this family is exactly $9/2$, and Schwartz's conjecture holds for it. We also prove that subdividing a good coloring of $\T(β)$ gives a good coloring of $\T(nβ)$ with the same value of $η$. Consequently, Schwartz's conjecture holds in general if and only if it holds for primitive Eisenstein integers.

papers.title: Equality in the direction bound over prime fields
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be prime. We prove that a noncollinear set of $2m+1\le p$ points in $\AG(2,p)$ determines exactly $m+2$ directions if and only if, up to an affine transformation, it consists of the origin and a coset of a multiplicative subgroup of order $m$ on each coordinate axis. Thus equality is possible precisely when $m\mid p-1$. This extends the Lovász--Schrijver classification for $2m+1=p$.

papers.title: Low-rank Low Precision Training of Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: Training Gaussian processes (GPs) at large scale is computationally challenging because evaluating the log-marginal likelihood and its gradients involves large, dense kernel matrices. We develop a scalable low-rank GP training approach that combines AnchorNet landmark selection with a fully independent training conditional (FITC) correction. The resulting objective and its analytic gradients can be evaluated using low-rank factors, diagonal quantities, and small dense matrices, without forming the full kernel matrix or its derivatives. The complete training procedure is implemented in single precision and evaluated on nine large-scale regression datasets. Across these problems, the method reaches the reference predictive accuracy while substantially reducing training time, although the required approximation rank varies across datasets. We also study the numerical behavior of the full-kernel predictive solve and show that single precision can become limiting for ill-conditioned problems. Finally, we investigate further reducing selected matrix operations to fp16 or TF32. These lower-precision variants provide only modest additional speedups and can become unreliable when the reduced system is poorly conditioned.

papers.title: Smooth asymptotically Self-similar blow up for the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$
papers.abstract: We construct blow up solutions to the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$. More precisely, we construct the solutions $(ψ,n)$ defined for $t\in[0,T)$, blowing up at $t=T$ and taking the form \begin{align} ψ(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{T-t}P\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)e^{i(T-t)^{-1/3}}, n(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{3(T-t)^{4/3}}N\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right) \end{align} in the region $|x|\ll 1$. Here $(P,N)$ is the solution to a specified ODE system related to Zakharov system. The solutions we construct are smooth for $0\leq t<T$. Moreover, there exist $n_0,n_1\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^3\backslash\{0\})$ with bounded support such that for any $r>0$, $(ψ,n,\partial_t n)$ converge to $(0,n_0,n_1)$ in $C^{\infty}(|x|>r)$. We correct the profile $(P,N)$ and obtain a sequence of approximate solutions that coincide in the region $|x|\gtrsim 1$ with higher and higher accuracy. Then we apply perturbative analysis to construct solutions with arbitrarily high finite regularity. The fixed point argument in this procedure actually yields that these solutions are the same for $t$ sufficiently close to $T$, which combined with the persistence of high regularity gives the existence of smooth asymptotically self-similar blow up solutions.

papers.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
papers.abstract: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $φ^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.

papers.title: Adding minimal fresh subsets to $\aleph_ω$
papers.abstract: Assuming the existence of a measurable cardinal, we produce generic extensions $V_1\subsetneq V_2$ of the universe with the same cardinals, cofinalities, and bounded subsets of $\aleph_ω$, such that $V_2$ is generated over $V_1$ by a cofinal $ω$-sequence in $\aleph_ω$, and $V_2$ is a minimal generic extension over $V_1$, i.e., every set of ordinals in $V_2\setminus V_1$ generates $V_2$ over $V_1$.

papers.title: Uniqueness of positive solutions of mixed Laplacian and fractional Laplacian in $\mathbb R$
papers.abstract: We establish the uniqueness and nondegeneracy for positive finite-energy solutions of the following one-dimensional mixed Schrödinger equation \begin{equation} -Q'' + (-Δ)^s Q + Q = |Q|^p Q \quad \text{in } \mathbb R, \end{equation} where $0<s<1$ and $p>0$. For every $0<s<1, p>0$, we obtain the corresponding results for positive solutions whose linearized operators have Morse index equal to one. We extend the nodal analysis developed by Frank-Lenzmann-Silvestre to the mixed operator establishing the monotonicity of the quotient of a hypothetical nontrivial even kernel element by $-Q'$. We then combine this monotonicity with oscillation estimates to prove nondegeneracy, and uniqueness follows by continuation. Moreover, for every $1/2\le s<1,p>0$, both uniqueness and nondegeneracy hold for positive solutions. Our novelty is to use the properties of Green kernel of the mixed operator to derive the upper bound and lower bound on the maximum of each solution. This peak estimate allows us to prove uniqueness by direct comparison and to establish nondegeneracy.

papers.title: Spectral conditions for the existence of $\{K_2,\{C_k\}\}$-factor in $t$-tough graphs
papers.abstract: For $t>0$, a graph $G$ is called $t$-tough if $|S|\geq t\,c(G-S)$ for every $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $c(G-S)\geq2$, where $c(G-S)$ denotes the number of components of $G-S$. Toughness is closely related to the existence of Hamiltonian cycles and factors in graphs. Chvátal [Discrete Math. 5 (1973) 215--228] conjectured that there exists a constant $t_0>0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph of order at least three is Hamiltonian. Bauer, Broersma and Veldman [Discrete Appl. Math. 99 (2000) 317--321] constructed $(9/4-\varepsilon)$-tough graphs without a Hamiltonian path for arbitrarily small $\varepsilon>0$. For the weaker requirement of a $2$-factor, Enomoto et al. [J. Graph Theory 9 (1985) 87--95] proved that every $2$-tough graph of order at least three has a $2$-factor and that the toughness threshold $2$ is best possible. A graph $G$ is said to have a $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor if and only if $G$ contains a spanning subgraph consisting of components that are either cycles or single edges. A $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor can be viewed as a combination of a $1$-factor and a $2$-factor, motivating the study of such factors in tough graphs. In this paper, we establish sharp sufficient conditions in terms of the adjacency spectral radius, the distance spectral radius, and the distance signless Laplacian spectral radius for a $t$-tough graph to have a $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor.

papers.title: Quasipositive and almost positive sectional curvature on finite quotients of Wallach spaces
papers.abstract: We construct nonnegatively curved metrics on the cyclic and full permutation quotients of the Wallach flag manifolds in dimensions $6$, $12$, and $24$. The metrics are quasipositively curved in all three dimensions and almost positively curved in dimensions $12$ and $24$. The cyclic quotients are orientable with fundamental group $C_3$, and their further full permutation quotients have fundamental group $S_3$; none admits any metric of everywhere positive sectional curvature. For the almost-positive metrics we describe every zero-curvature plane and prove that the zero-point loci have Hausdorff dimensions exactly $11$ and $23$, respectively. A one-step deformation has, in each dimension, an explicit zero locus with nonempty interior. Further nested deformations reduce it to a measure-zero set while leaving a common codimension-one stratum. The argument combines normal forms for horizontal commuting planes with quaternionic rank conditions and a dimension estimate for commuting compressions of skew-symmetric operators. We also determine the possible degrees of arbitrary free finite quotients of the three flag covers and derive order bounds for fundamental groups when the Euler characteristic is nonzero. We have used ChatGPT-6-astra for mathematical exploration and verified and rewritten all the results.

papers.title: Parametric spatio-temporal reduced-order modelling via Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and Gaussian Process Regression
papers.abstract: We present SPOD-GPR, a non-intrusive, parametric, spatio-temporal reduced-order model (ROM) that combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD), Spectral POD (SPOD), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). A parametric POD first projects the high-dimensional state onto a low-dimensional subspace. The reduced trajectories are then divided into windowed sections, transformed into the frequency domain, and truncated to the most energetic frequencies. SPOD is then performed independently at each retained frequency, yielding temporally coherent modes and coefficients. The parametric dependence of the POD and SPOD bases is modelled by GPR on a local chart of the Grassmann manifold after Procrustes alignment. The SPOD modal coefficients are learned both as explicit functions of the parameters and through a parameter-conditioned autoregressive model that allows for temporal extrapolation beyond the training window. Gaussian processes are sampled jointly and pathwise via Matheron conditioning, ensuring that each predictive realization carries uncertainty quantification consistent with the posterior distribution. The method is tested on four parametric examples where the parameter values and the prediction horizon lie outside the training data: the two-dimensional anisotropic Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equation in a time-periodic and a travelling-wave regime, each parametrised by one of its two coefficients; flow past a cylinder parametrised by the Reynolds number; and flow past an elliptic obstacle parametrised by its semi-axes. In all cases, SPOD-GPR reduces the normalised mean absolute error compared to a POD-GPR baseline, and improves the calibration of the predictive uncertainty, especially in the fluid flow cases, where POD-GPR is severely overconfident. This opens the way to spectral, uncertainty-aware reduced-order models for many-query and real-time applications, such as digital twins.

papers.title: A Finite-Lag Markov Chain Model for Coarse-Graining Linear SDEs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze a finite-lag Markov chain approximation for coarse-grained linear stochastic differential equations. The chain uses the limiting conditional transition law of the resolved variables to advance on a prescribed time grid. Its stability and statistical properties are studied, with particular attention to the role of the lag time. The chain preserves the exact equilibrium distribution and matches the autocovariance at the chosen lag, while errors at subsequent times are quantified. For a slow-fast system, the analysis relates lag selection to scale separation and dynamical accuracy. A continuous embedding of the chain enables a unified comparison with some existing continuous-time Markovian effective models based on the temporal statistics they preserve. Numerical examples illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: A Poisson-bracket operator for Hamiltonian separability: intrinsic geometry and exact defects
papers.abstract: Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional. For Hamiltonians with a cyclic angle, the linearised operator divided by the squared rotor frequency is an angle derivative of the Melnikov integrand, so that the defect integrated along a homoclinic orbit decides the first-order splitting of the separatrix. Closed-form defects are obtained for the polar-nodal normal forms of satellite theory and, through a covariance of the operator on level sets, for Kerr geodesics. Used for coordinate selection, the defect singles out the separating focal distance of the Euler two-centre problem as its unique nondegenerate minimum, and for axisymmetric potentials it shows that the prescriptions of Sanders and Vasiliev are two weightings of the same Stäckel residual. The residual selector and Binney's shell-orbit fit improve both actions over the median prescription for 48 and 50 of 50 orbits in a flattened logarithmic potential, whereas the operator selector lowers the 90th-percentile action spread of 50 orbits in a Miyamoto-Nagai potential from 2.90% to 0.91%.

papers.title: Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups
papers.abstract: In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up. We prove that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent, then the Mal'cev completions of $Γ$ and $Λ$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Equivalently, using Y. Shalom's result we prove that two infinite countable torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent if and only if $Γ$ and $Λ$ are quasi-isometric if and only if the Mal'cev Completions of $Γ$ and $Λ$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Moreover, we discuss some applications of our main theorem to lifting of quasi-isometric embedding from $Γ$ to $Λ$ to a homo-morphism between their Mal'cev completions, and betti numbers of nilpotent groups.

papers.title: Superlinear regularity of Frobenius powers on a normal hypersurface
papers.abstract: We give answers to four questions on linear bounds for Frobenius powers. Let $\mathfrak m$ denote the homogeneous maximal ideal. We construct a height-two prime $I$ in a geometrically normal four-dimensional graded hypersurface $R$ of characteristic two such that, for every power $q\geq16$ of four, the Loewy length of $H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R/I^{[q]})$ is at least $q^{3/2}/8-1$. Thus no fixed integer $C$ gives annihilation by $\mathfrak m^{Cq}$ for all $q$, as required by the Hochster--Huneke condition $(\mathrm{LC})$. The same construction gives superlinear lower bounds for the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity in Katzman's question, for the exponents of the embedded primary components in the question of Smith and Swanson, and for the degree in the least variable in Katzman's Gröbner basis conjecture. The bounds follow from the degree of the kernel line bundle of a multiplication pencil associated to a family of plane quartics.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction for Multi-Step Forecasting: Conditional Coverage and Sharp Score Calibration Rates
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification in prediction is a central problem in statistics and machine learning. Conformal prediction provides a flexible approach to constructing prediction sets with valid marginal coverage under exchangeability. In this paper, we investigate conformal prediction for both one-step and multi-step forecasting from a single stationary time series, addressing temporal dependence and the additional challenges of joint prediction across multiple horizons. We propose a kernel-based framework, called Time series Residual Analysis for Calibration with Kernels (TRACK), for estimating conditional quantiles of residual scores and constructing prediction sets from rolling-window forecasters. The framework accommodates heterogeneous uncertainty across horizons and accounts for dependence induced by rolling estimation, while allowing predictor memory and forecast horizons to grow with the sample size. Our finite-sample bounds quantify how temporal dependence and overlapping score windows affect calibration and coverage. We further derive bounds for conditional quantile estimation and pointwise conditional coverage discrepancy. The guarantees extend to more general predictors that admit an accurate rolling-window approximation. We also derive matching minimax bounds over classes of known score maps, clarifying how overlapping score windows affect calibration accuracy. Experimental results from simulations and applications to wind energy generation and bike sharing demand show that our methods improve regional conditional coverage while maintaining competitive interval widths.

papers.title: Anomalous regularity and scaling limit by rough transport noise for stochastic 2D fluid models on the torus
papers.abstract: We consider the stochastic 2D Euler and mSQG equations on the torus, with $L^2$ initial data and driven by rough Kraichnan transport noise, for which we construct weak solutions enjoying anomalous regularity and dissipation properties. Moreover, we show that weak solutions in this regularity class are pathwise unique, thus establishing probabilistically strong well-posedness. We further obtain the scaling limit from these equations to the deterministic Navier--Stokes/mSQG equations, with respect to positive Sobolev norms. The proofs rest on the analysis of energy spectrum of the vorticity and on a uniform weighted discrete Poincaré inequality on the lattice, the latter being crucial for making the positive norms accessible.

papers.title: Online Digital Twins: Data Assimilation and Control
papers.abstract: The online assimilation of data and the application of controls are essential ingredients of the digital twin paradigm. In this paper, we formalize the online interaction between the physical process and its virtual digital representation in the setting of continuously arriving data from the physical process and a receding horizon virtual planning process, which provides the control for the physical process. Our mathematical formulation relies on a mean field representation of the data assimilation process as well as a mean field Pontryagin minimum principle for the optimal control problem. Such mean field formulations are computationally attractive because they allow for simultaneous implementation in terms of Hamiltonian interacting particle systems. A more detailed discussion is included for the ensemble Kalman-Bucy filter in combination with affine approximations of the receding horizon control laws. This paper sets out the mathematical framework, while a computational study is left for future research.

papers.title: Pairwise correlation bounds for the random-cluster model with cluster weight at most one
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative bounds on pairwise edge correlations for the random-cluster model with cluster weight $q\in[0,1]$ on arbitrary finite connected graphs. We give two explicit bounds that retain the dependence on the activities of the two specified edges and hold uniformly over the activities of all remaining edges. We also obtain a refinement of one of these bounds using connectivity information from the graph with the two specified edges removed. These results sharpen the bound obtained by a direct application of Lorentzian polynomial theory. At $q=0$, the model is supported on connected spanning subgraphs. In particular, for the uniform probability measure on these subgraphs, the joint inclusion probability of two distinct edges is at most $10/9$ times the product of their marginal inclusion probabilities.

papers.title: Optimal last-iterate rates for the projected decentralized stochastic subgradient method
papers.abstract: We study the projected decentralized stochastic subgradient (PDSG) method for minimizing the average of convex, possibly nonsmooth local objectives over a common closed convex constraint set and a fixed connected undirected network. We focus on the finite-time expected suboptimality of the last local iterate generated at each node, which is the actual output locally available without time averaging or network averaging. Under the standard stepsizes $α_t=α/\sqrt{t}$ and $α_t=2/(μt)$, we establish $\mathcal{O}(\log T/\sqrt{T})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\log T/T)$ last-local-iterate rates for PDSG when each local objective is convex and the aggregate objective is strongly convex, respectively. To eliminate the logarithmic loss, we introduce a general horizon-dependent stepsize framework, termed cooldown stepsize, that combines a base stepsize with segmentwise scaling over a multistage partition and includes the dyadic construction (Jain et al, SIAM J. Optim., 2021) as a special case. For adapting to decentralized settings, we propose a long-range variation condition to make the stepsize schedule compatible with network contraction. Under this cooldown stepsize, we obtain $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ and $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ last-local-iterate rates for PDSG in both problem classes, matching the optimal centralized dependence on $T$. Experiments on a lower-bound instance and constrained hinge-loss problems illustrate the predicted terminal behavior of local iterates and the control of consensus error under the cooldown stepsize.

papers.title: Forelli--Rudin Type Operators in Infinite Dimensions, I
papers.abstract: We introduce Forelli-Rudin type operators on the open unit ball of $\ell^2$. The weighted $L^p$-$L^q$ boundedness of these operators are completely characterized for all $p,q\in[1,\infty]\times [1,\infty]$, and every Schatten class between the weighted $L^2$ spaces are also completely characterized. Meanwhile, we derive trace formulas for corresponding operators, which cannot be obtained from their finite-dimensional counterparts by formally replacing the dimension parameter with infinity. These results are not only infinite-dimensional extensions of those obtained by Cheng, Fang, Wang, and the second author (2017), Zhao and Zhou (2022), and Ding (2022). They also reveal new phenomena that are unique to infinite dimensions and arise from the geometric and measure theoretic differences between finite- and infinite-dimensional spaces. The key ingredient of our proofs is that we also establish the Forelli-Rudin type estimates in infinite dimensions, which may shew some night on the function theory in the infinite-dimensional unit ball.

papers.title: An invariant higher index pairing under Morita equivalence for proper étale groupoids
papers.abstract: For suitable proper étale groupoids, we study a part of the higher index that is invariant under Morita equivalence. We capture this part by a pairing between cyclic homology classes associated with isotropy groups and cyclic cohomology classes of the groupoid convolution algebra. We show that the pushforward is compatible with the maps induced by essential equivalences. This gives a numerical invariant depending only on the Morita equivalence class of the groupoid. In the case of a finite group action, we relate the resulting pairing to the equivariant index and to the Atiyah-Bott fixed-point formula.

papers.title: An Analytic Evaluation of Euler Sharp Sums
papers.abstract: We give a direct analytic evaluation of the Euler sharp sums $ζ^\sharp(2,\{1\}^{d-3},\overline{2})$ for all even integers $d\ge4$, expressing them in terms of ordinary multiple zeta values of depth at most two. The proof reduces these sharp sums to a harmonic-number series and evaluates it using a generating-function identity, thereby proving the even-depth case of a conjecture of Xu and Zhao.

papers.title: Five-Entropic Matroids Are Quinary
papers.abstract: A finite matroid is representable over a field if its elements can be assigned vectors over that field such that the rank of every subset equals the dimension of the span of its vectors. For an integer q >= 2, a matroid is q-entropic if there exists a random vector indexed by its ground set, with each coordinate taking values in a common q-element alphabet, such that the entropy of every marginal subvector equals the rank of the corresponding subset multiplied by log q. It remains open to determine for which values of q every q-entropic matroid is representable over a field. For q=2 and q=3, representability over F_q has long been known. More recently, it was established that every 4-entropic matroid is representable over F_4 and that the 6-entropic matroids are precisely the regular matroids, that is, those representable over every field. We settle the previously unresolved five-symbol case, proving that a finite matroid is 5-entropic if and only if it is representable over F_5. For the nontrivial implication, we use Matúš's equivalence between entropic and partition representations. We show that a degree-five partition representation induces, on each embedded U_{2,4}-minor, an F_5-linear representation after coordinatewise relabeling, with a rescaling class independent of the chosen linearization. Using the foundation presentation of Baker and Lorscheid, we verify the compatibility relations among these local classes and thereby obtain a global F_5-representation.

papers.title: Khintchine's limit theorem for monotone convolutions
papers.abstract: We prove that every weak limit of monotone convolution powers is monotonically infinitely divisible. In contrast, we prove that every probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ can occur as a weak limit of monotone convolutions of an infinitesimal triangular array. We also discuss similar limit theorems for multiplicative monotone convolution on the unit circle.

papers.title: Curve theory in $S^2\times S^2$ with applications to ruled surfaces in $S^3$
papers.abstract: The Riemannian product $S^2\times S^2$ of two unit spheres admits several important geometric interpretations. It can be identified both with the complex quadric $Q^2$ and with the space $\mathcal{L}(S^3)$ of oriented geodesics in the unit $3$-sphere $S^3$. In this paper, we first develop a unified framework for the geometry of curves in $S^2\times S^2$. We introduce projection-regular curves in $S^2\times S^2$ and their curvature data, and prove a congruence theorem for these curves. As an application of this framework, regarding $S^2\times S^2$ as the complex quadric $Q^2$, we classify Kähler magnetic geodesics associated with the product Kähler--Einstein structure. For closed generic projection-regular curves, we establish a sharp Fenchel-type inequality. We then identify $S^2\times S^2$ with the space $\mathcal{L}(S^3)$ of oriented geodesics in the unit $3$-sphere $S^3$ and apply our curve theory to ruled surfaces in $S^3$. In particular, we prove that every nonsingular closed generic projection-regular ruled surface attaining equality in the Fenchel-type inequality is an embedded torus.

papers.title: On the Instance-Specific Sharp Rates for Constrained Least Squares Estimators in the Sequence Model
papers.abstract: We develop a general methodology based on the Feature Space Decomposition framework for establishing explicit, instance-specific sharp rates for the expected estimation error of convex-constrained least squares estimators in the sequence model, without requiring estimates of localized Gaussian mean widths. We apply this methodology to $\ell_q$ ellipsoids, $\ell_1$ balls, and $kB_1^N\cap B_\infty^N$, obtaining matching upper and lower bounds in the nondegenerate regime. Our methodology also extends beyond Gaussian noise to symmetric noise distributions satisfying a Poincaré inequality. We also provide an elementary proof of the instance-specific sharp rate for isotonic regression for any well-specified signal and any noise level. Combining this result with Han's asymptotic reduction, we further obtain explicit instance-specific sharp convergence rates in probability for isotonic regression in Gaussian linear regression under general signal-dependent asymptotics conditions.

papers.title: BMO Vorticity Strong Ill-Posedness for the 2d Incompressible Euler Equation
papers.abstract: For the two dimensional incompressible Euler equation, Yudovich, and independently Serfati, extended the classical existence and uniqueness class to include vorticity with mild singularity. This class is sometimes called the generalized Yudovich class. Then, Vishik extended the uniqueness class to include vorticity in BMO, allowing for stronger singularities than the generalized Yudovich class. In this work, we prove strong ill-posedness of vorticity in BMO.

papers.title: A Bearing-rate-free Implementation of a Scalar Estimator for Bearing-only Target Localization and Circumnavigation
papers.abstract: This paper studies the problem of guiding an agent to localize and circumnavigate a stationary target at a prescribed radius using bearing measurements. Direct implementation of a classical scalar signed-distance estimator requires explicit evaluation of bearing rate signals that can be difficult to obtain in practice. To eliminate this dependence, we propose a bearing-rate-free (BRF) realization of the scalar estimator that recovers the signed-distance estimate algebraically, without numerical differentiation or a separate filter for estimating the bearing rate. We prove, under consistent initialization, that the proposed BRF realization inherits the guarantees previously established for the classical realization, including exponential convergence of both the target estimation error and radial tracking error, as well as the agent-target collision avoidance. Simulations show that, with noise-free bearings, the BRF realization achieves numerical accuracy comparable to that of an exact-bearing-rate benchmark and, at the higher noise levels tested, exhibits smaller radial tracking oscillations than the backward difference implementation of the classical estimator.

papers.title: Rigidity and existence of profiled expansive solutions of the $N$-body problem with homogeneous potentials
papers.abstract: We study expansive solutions of the $N$-body problem with homogeneous potentials of degree $-p$, where $p>0$. We establish asymptotic rigidity for arbitrary solutions with admissible profiles. For general admissible profiles and $0<p<2$, we obtain convergent power-log expansions whose exponents are governed by the leading profiles. In the hyperbolic case, we derive a more explicit analytic representation for all $p>0$, extending Chazy's Newtonian result. Together with the author's recent results [Wu, 2026], this yields a bijective parametrization of hyperbolic solutions near infinity by their asymptotic velocities and offsets. We also establish the existence of free-time minimizing solutions with arbitrary prescribed initial configurations and admissible asymptotic profiles for $0<p<2$, covering the hyperbolic, parabolic and hyperbolic-parabolic regimes. In the hyperbolic case, the result extends to all $p>0$, including possibly collisional initial configurations in the strong-force regime $p \ge 2$. Furthermore, we prove that when $p \neq 2$, every solution with an admissible asymptotic profile is eventually a free-time minimizer.

papers.title: Extreme amenability and failure of the Lévy property for the trace-class special unitary group
papers.abstract: We prove that the trace-class special unitary group, equipped with the trace-norm topology, is extremely amenable but is not a Lévy group, answering questions posed by Pestov. The failure of the Lévy property follows from a uniform non-concentration estimate for every nontrivial compact subgroup. Extreme amenability is established through a transverse spectral-gap estimate and trace-norm duality, yielding asymptotic invariance of Lipschitz observables under each fixed finite-dimensional special unitary subgroup. A limiting argument then gives fixed points for continuous actions on arbitrary compact Hausdorff spaces. We also formulate an abstract criterion for extreme amenability based on asymptotic quadratic invariance along a dense chain of compact subgroups. Neither argument uses concentration results for other Schatten exponents.

papers.title: Lower bound of the Calabi functional and non-Archimedean K-energy
papers.abstract: We prove Donaldson's conjecture which describes the infimum of the Calabi functional by the normalized non-Archimedean K-energy. The proof makes use of proximal equation for the K-energy. To obtain approximate smooth solutions, a continuity path of prescribed scalar curvature equation is coupled with a version of Chen's $\e$-subgeodesic. It does not require a global smooth solution to the Calabi flow.

papers.title: Gersten resolutions for logarithmic forms
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth variety over a field $k$ of characteristic 0. We show that (two versions of) the Zariski sheaves of regular $k$-linear logarithmic differential forms on $X$ (in the most naïve sense, i.e. sums of products of logarithmic differentials) have Gersten property (and therefore coincide). It turns out that the values of these sheaves are free abelian groups. As a consequence, for any integer $n>0$, these sheaves modulo $n$ also have Gersten property. The proof is an elementary application of the Voevodsky's $(-1)$-machinery and consists of assembling several well-known results.

papers.title: Infinitude of integral Hitchin representations of Coxeter polygons
papers.abstract: We prove that there are infinitely many Hitchin $\operatorname{SL}^\pm(3, \mathbb Z)$-representations of a Coxeter $n$-gon($n \geq 9$) group whose boundary parameters are fixed. We construct infinitely many Hitchin $\operatorname{SL}^\pm(3, \mathbb Z)$-representations of a specific Coxeter $6$-gon or $8$-gon corresponding to positive integral points of a generalized Markoff equation.

papers.title: Smooth limits of compact Kahler manifolds with vanishing first Chern class
papers.abstract: Let $π\colon X\toΔ$ be a proper holomorphic submersion from a smooth complex manifold onto the unit disc. Suppose that for every $t\inΔ^*$ the fiber $X_t$ is a compact Kahler manifold whose real first Chern class vanishes. We prove that the central fiber X_0 belongs to Fujiki's class $\cC$, that is, X_0 is bimeromorphic to a compact Kahler manifold.

papers.title: Proof of the QNEC, without assumptions and under a weight
papers.abstract: We complete a proof of the quantum null energy condition (QNEC) in the mathematical framework of Half-Sided Translations and Modular Inclusions (HST/HSMI) removing an assumption that applied to previous proofs. Here we establish a theorem, which when translated to a physical setting implies that the relative entropy comparing the state of fields outside a stationary black hole with a Hartle-Hawking (HH) state is always a convex function of the horizon cut. Previous proofs only applied when a purification with finite null energy was available. We also obtain a QNEC generalization in which the HH Hilbert space is replaced with one based on a weight which is plausibly of relevance to evaporating black holes in flat space.

papers.title: Conical Singularities of Toda Solutions with One Finite-Energy Component and Classification on the Punctured Plane
papers.abstract: We study Toda systems associated with arbitrary complex simple Lie algebras. For solutions on a punctured disc, we prove that finite energy of at least one component near the puncture forces every component to have a conical singularity there. On the punctured plane, we give a geometric formulation and proof of the Lin--Nie--Wei classification of solutions with prescribed cone exponents at the origin and finite total energy in at least one component. We express the parameter space as the complex centralizer of the monodromy modulo a maximal compact subgroup. We also recover the formulas of Karmakar--Lin--Nie--Wei for the cone exponents at infinity and the total energies of the components.

papers.title: CRAFT-GBM: Selecting Best Features for Gradient-Boosted Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Feature subsampling is used to accelerate gradient-boosted trees, yet standard approaches fix the feature count in advance and largely ignore the split-gain evidence accumulated during training. We introduce CRAFT-GBM (Confidence-Ranked Adaptive Feature Tracking), a native LightGBM extension that uses this evidence to adapt which---and, by default, how many---features are searched each boosting round. CRAFT-GBM transforms root-split gains into bounded observations and constructs joint time-uniform bounds valid under adaptive, non-stationary training histories. In its default endogenous mode, after initialization, CRAFT-GBM retains exactly the features that cannot yet be ruled out as best, letting the selected feature-set size $K_t$ emerge from training history rather than a pre-specified fraction. With probability at least $1-δ$, every feature with the largest expected gain is retained jointly across all rounds after initialization. When a feature fraction $f$ is specified instead, CRAFT-GBM ranks features by their interval point estimates and provides an approximate top-$K$ guarantee for feature budget $K_f$. We implement CRAFT-GBM within LightGBM while preserving its native feature-bundling representation, and evaluate it across 14 public and synthetic dataset families and four noise-augmented settings. In the fully endogenous setting, CRAFT-GBM reduces per-fit training time by 39.74\% with 1.04\% lower test loss in the geometric mean across all 18 RQ1 experiments. Under pre-specified feature fraction $f$, Exogenous CRAFT-GBM also yields aggregate training-time reductions up to 13.52 percentage points larger than random feature subsampling, with no increase in aggregate test loss relative to full-feature LightGBM. Accumulated training evidence can thus support adaptive feature search with statistical guarantees while retaining the practical advantages of native gradient boosting.

papers.title: Properties of Public Announcements as Operators: Commutativity, Monotonicity, Idempotence, Fixed Points, and Stabilization
papers.abstract: For each formula $\varphi$, we introduce the public announcement operator $U_\varphi$, which maps every model to its updated model under the public announcement of $\varphi$. We then study its algebraic and dynamic properties with a particular focus on commutativity, monotonicity, idempotence, fixed points, and stabilization. Among many results, we show the following. First, monotonicity of $U_\varphi$ is characterized by a family of preservation conditions and equivalence to an existential formula. Second, there exists a formula that achieves every nonzero ordinal as a stabilization rank---the first stage at which a model stabilizes---of some model. Finally and unexpectedly, extinction of every model under iterated announcements of $\varphi$ is equivalent to common unknowability, being always informative when true, and a fixed point view of the Moore sentence. Over S5, those are further equivalent to common unbelievability and being always informative. Other results include characterizations of commutativity and strong commutativity, idempotence as success, properties of fixed points, and finite and $ω$-stabilization. For analysis, we use PAL (state elimination) and BPAL (arrow elimination), clarifying their subtle differences.

papers.title: Normalized solutions for Schrödinger-Maxwell equation with Sobolev critical and mass subcritical perturbation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Schrödinger-Maxwell equation with critical growth and mass subcritical perturbation \begin{align*} \begin{cases} \displaystyle - Δu+λu+ \left(|x|^{-1}\ast| u|^2\right) u =|u|^{4}u +|u|^{p-2}u\quad\quad \text{in} \ \mathbb{ R}^3, \displaystyle \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|u|^2dx=a^2, \end{cases} \end{align*} where $a>0$ is prescribed, $3<p<\frac{10}{3}$, $\ast$ denotes the convolution and $λ\in \mathbb{R}$ appears as a Lagrange multiplier. When the nonlocal convolution term is absent, the above equation can be reduced to the Schrödinger equation. In this case, the previous works showed that it admits a local minimizer (ground-state) and a mountain-pass type solution. By contrast, we surprisingly find that the above equation has no solutions with negative energy provided $a>0$ is sufficiently small. More precisely, we rigorously prove that the above equation possesses a mountain-pass type solution with positive energy for sufficiently small $a>0$, which reveals an essential difference in solution structure between the Schrödinger-Maxwell equation and the classical Schrödinger equation in the parameter range $3<p<\frac{10}{3}$. The main difficulty encountered in this work is the loss of compactness arising from the Sobolev critical term. Furthermore, we explore the dynamical properties of the corresponding time-dependent problem and establish the strong instability of its standing wave solutions. It is worth pointing out that this work refines and extends the existing literature by covering the unexplored parameter regime $p\in(3,\frac{10}{3})$.

papers.title: On the Global Convergence of Stochastic Adam for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: The Adam optimizer is widely used to train neural networks with highly nonlinear and nonconvex objective functions. Remarkably, Adam often drives the empirical training loss nearly to zero. This phenomenon has been partially explained by neural tangent kernel (NTK) analyses of gradient descent (GD) and stochastic gradient descent (SGD). However, analyzing Adam presents additional challenges. Its first-moment momentum couples stochastic gradients across iterations, while its adaptive second-moment preconditioner depends on the same stochastic gradient used in the update. In this paper, we establish linear convergence guarantees for Adam in training sufficiently wide two-layer neural networks with either full-batch or minibatch gradients. For full-batch Adam, we construct a Lyapunov function to control the effect of historical momentum. For minibatch Adam, our analysis builds on an exact virtual-iterate representation, a conditional analysis of the dependence between stochastic gradients and adaptive preconditioners, and uniform concentration bounds for the second-moment estimates. We prove geometric decay of the empirical loss for full-batch Adam and geometric decay in restricted expectation on a high-probability event for minibatch Adam. Beyond regression, we extend our convergence analysis to physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for solving the Poisson equation, where differential operators and separate sampling of interior and boundary points introduce additional challenges. We establish analogous global convergence guarantees for both deterministic and stochastic Adam under explicit conditions on network width and Adam's parameters, characterizing the effects of minibatch size on convergence. These results help bridge the gap between Adam's empirical success and its theoretical understanding, providing sharper convergence guarantees for PINNs than existing analyses.

papers.title: Invariant operations on vector fields on the line are Lie polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that all $W_1$-equivariant multilinear operations on the Witt Lie algebra $W_1$ are Lie polynomials. We study this question in terms of Wronskian Lie brackets and Novikov products, which are abstractions of the Lie bracket $[a,b]:=ab'-ba'$ and the nonassociative product $a\circ b=ab'$ one can define on a commutative differential algebra. In terms of these notions, our main result asserts that the operad of Wronskian Lie algebras is isomorphic to the operad of equivariant multilinear operations on~$W_1$; we also prove a parallel result for the operad of Novikov algebras, characterizing it as the operad of affine equivariant multilinear operations on $W_1$. Two immediate consequences of our work are a characterization of Lie polynomials in free Novikov algebras and a computation of the degree zero homology of the operadic twisting of the Novikov operad. Finally, while it is known that over a field of zero characteristic, a Novikov algebra embeds into its differential envelope, we show that the same is not necessarily true for Wronskian Lie algebras.

papers.title: Presentations of inverse Artin monoids of type $D_n$ via cluster mutations
papers.abstract: Let $D_n^\varepsilon$ denote the Dynkin diagram of type $D_{n+1}$ with the endpoint $\varepsilon$ of its long branch frozen, and let $\mathcal{M}(D_n^\varepsilon)$ be the mutation class of any orientation of this diagram under mutations at mutable vertices. For each $Γ\in\mathcal{M}(D_n^\varepsilon)$, we define an inverse monoid $M_Γ$ by generators and relations determined by $Γ$. We prove that $M_Γ\cong M_{μ_k(Γ)}$ for every mutable vertex $k$. Consequently, every quiver in this mutation class yields a presentation of the inverse Artin monoid of type $D_n$. Our argument establishes mutation invariance for the presentations of inverse Artin monoids of both types $A_n^\varepsilon$ and $D_n^\varepsilon$.

papers.title: An iterated-logarithm price of anytime validity for log-optimal e-processes
papers.abstract: Log-optimal e-variables at fixed horizons, also called numéraires, have been conjectured to ``almost'' form an e-process for exponential-family null hypotheses. A related open question is whether an e-process can attain the optimal e-power at every horizon up to a bounded loss. Given a final horizon, we study the minimax regret of e-processes relative to the numéraires at all times up to it. For the Gaussian location null and the composite alternative of Gaussian distributions with a smaller variance and an unknown location, we show that the minimax regret in the worst case over the location grows like the iterated logarithm of the final horizon. A single e-process attains this rate at every horizon. This growth answers the question negatively. It also refutes the conjecture if ``almost'' means a regret bounded uniformly over horizons. For this Gaussian location problem, we thus exhibit the frontier precisely: the minimax regret is bounded if and only if the alternatives have at least the variance of the null.

papers.title: Distribution-Free Symmetry Detection in Multi-Reference Alignment at Low SNR
papers.abstract: Symmetry can reveal the structure of a signal, but detecting it becomes difficult when observations are noisy and randomly transformed. We study how to infer symmetry directly from multi-reference alignment data with additive isotropic Gaussian noise of known variance, without aligning the observations or knowing how the transformations were sampled. For cyclic symmetry, we identify a simple statistical signature that yields tests with exact finite-sample error guarantees. We demonstrate their performance even at very low signal-to-noise ratios. Dihedral symmetry presents a deeper challenge: we show that, for some signals, invariant moments below a sharp order threshold cannot distinguish reflectional from purely rotational symmetry. For generic signals, however, this distinction emerges much earlier. We use these insights to develop tests for dihedral symmetry with asymptotic error control under explicit nondegeneracy conditions. Together, the results clarify what we can learn about symmetry from noisy, unaligned data and suggest a path toward symmetry inference in cryo-EM.

papers.title: A Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem for marked graphs
papers.abstract: The classical Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem characterizes graphs with least eigenvalue at least $-2$ in terms of generalized line graphs, exceptional graphs, and root systems. In this paper, we establish a marked graph extension of this theorem. For a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices and a binary vector $\mathbf{b}\in\{0,1\}^n$, we completely characterize all marked graphs $\mathbf{G}=(G,\mathbf{b})$ such that $λ_{\min}(A(G)+\mathbf{b}\mathbf{b}^\top-J_n)\ge -2$, where $J_n$ denotes the all-ones matrix of order $n$. Using representations by finite root systems, we show that every irreducible marked graph satisfying the above inequality is represented by either the root system $B_n$ or the exceptional root system $E_8$. This leads to a complete structural characterization in terms of irreducible marked graphs, namely induced subgraphs of extended generalized line graphs, the marked graph $(2K_1,\mathbf{0})$, and exceptional graphs with all vertices marked. In the special case $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{j}$, our characterization reduces to the original Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem. The root system $B_n$ and extended generalized line graphs play the roles occupied by $D_n$ and generalized line graphs in the classical theory. We further apply the characterization to graphs whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $1$, showing that every $-2$-markable graph satisfies this spectral condition.

papers.title: Schur multiplier exponents of finite $p$-groups: bounds and critical-class phenomena
papers.abstract: The Schur exponent conjecture is a long-standing conjecture in group theory, which asserts that $\operatorname{exp}(\mathrm{M}(G))\mid\operatorname{exp}(G)$ for every finite group $G$, where $\mathrm{M}(G)$ denotes the Schur multiplier of $G$. In this article, we prove that the Schur exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups $G$ of nilpotency class at most $2p-2$ when $p$ is an odd prime. Our approach is to establish upper bounds on the exponent of $γ_{s+1}(G)$ for $s\in\mathbb{N}$. Using this approach, we further establish exponent bounds for Schur multipliers, nonabelian exterior squares, and tensor squares of $G$ of arbitrary nilpotency class, improving some existing bounds. Moreover, we show that Moravec's Bogomolov multiplier exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$. Havas conjectured that, for every prime $p>3$, there exists a finite $p$-group of exponent $p$ and nilpotency class $2p-1$ for which the Schur exponent conjecture fails. We show that the Schur exponent conjecture still holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$ generated by at most three elements. For four-generator groups of exponent $p$ and class at most $2p-1$, we prove that $\mathrm{M}(G)\cong C_{p^2}^{\,b}\times C_p^{\,a}$ for some $a\ge0$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$.

papers.title: Doubly-Efficient Private Information Retrieval from Modular Forms
papers.abstract: We present new information-theoretic protocols for $s$-server, doubly-efficient private information retrieval (PIR) in sublinear server time and one extra bit of space on the servers, for every constant $s \geq 2$. On an $n$-bit database, each of the $s$ PIR servers first builds and stores a preprocessing data structure consisting of $n+1$ bits (which is unique to each server, and after which the server may discard the original database). Then, each server answers a PIR query in time $T_s(n)$, by reading at most $T_s$ bits of its data structure and sending them to the user. In the two server setting ($s=2$), our PIR protocols achieve $T_2 = n^{0.82}$, matching the server time of the state-of-the-art schemes of Henzinger and Ragavan (EUROCRYPT 2026) while shrinking their storage from $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ to $n+1$ bits. With $s \geq 3$ servers, our PIR protocols retain the $n+1$ bits of storage and additionally improve on the server time of all prior information-theoretic $s$-server schemes with $n^{1+o(1)}$ storage: for example, achieving $T_3 = n^{0.74}$ and $T_{10} = n^{0.61}$ (previously $n^{0.79}$ and $n^{0.75}$). Asymptotically, as the server count $s$ grows, we shrink the number of servers required to achieve a given server-work exponent from $s^{3.9}$ to $s$. Our results draw inspiration from matching-vector techniques (Efremenko, STOC 2009), which we generalize to handle degree-two computations in the exponent. Using this generalization, we build doubly-efficient PIR from the new intermediate abstraction of Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions. Then, we construct such Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions via a connection to modular forms and complex analysis: if a Fourier-sparse cone-delta function does not exist, then there exists a modular form which has too many roots, contradicting the valence formula.

papers.title: An operator theoretical approach to weak solvability of a porous medium equation with Neumann boundary condition
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the Neumann problem for the porous medium equation, \[ u_t - Δa(u) = f \quad \mbox{in}\ Ω\times (0, T), \qquad \nabla a(u) \cdot ν=0 \quad \mbox{on}\ \partial Ω\times (0, T), \qquad u(\cdot, 0) = u_0 \quad \mbox{in}\ Ω\] in a smoothly bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ $(N \in \mathbb{N})$, where $T \in (0,\infty)$, $ν$ is the outward unit normal vector to $\partial Ω$, and where $f$ and $u_0$ are given. A typical example in mind is $a(u)=|u|^{p-2}u$ with $p \in [2, \infty)$. The main interest is weak solvability of the problem in the case that $u_0 \in H^1(Ω)^*$, $f \in L^2(0,T; H^1(Ω)^*)$. Under the condition that the mean value of $f(t)$ vanishes for almost all $t \in (0,T)$, existence of weak solutions is established by an application of abstract results from operator theory, for instance, properties of Gâteaux derivative. The key of the proof lies in the approximate equation \[ [(\varepsilon I - Δ)^{-1} u_\varepsilon]_t + a(u_\varepsilon) = (\varepsilon I - Δ)^{-1} f, \quad \varepsilon \in (0,1), \] where the map $\varepsilon I - Δ$ from $H^1(Ω)$ onto its dual space is regarded as the Riesz isomorphism of $H^1(Ω)$ equipped with an appropriate topology.

papers.title: Compact branch sets and injectivity of proper branched coverings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that a proper continuous open discrete map from the open unit ball $B^n$ onto a domain in $\R^n$ with $n\geq5$ is a homeomorphism whenever its branch set is compact. This answers Vuorinen's question affirmatively in every dimension $n\ge5.$ In dimension four, we also show that, under the additional assumption of quasiregularity, the map is a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Together with the three-dimensional theorem of Kauranen, Luisto and Tengvall, these results answer the quasiregular question posed as Problem~7.66 in the collections of Barth--Brannan--Hayman and Hayman--Lingham in every dimension $n\ge3$.

papers.title: AI and Mathematical Work on Mastodon: Attention, Topics, and Target-Specific Evaluations
papers.abstract: How does a mathematical community discuss AI on a federated social platform? We study 24,920 public posts from January--September 2026 by 272 accounts in a fixed roster of 1,002 Mastodon accounts whose profiles indicate mathematical research or study. LLM-assisted extraction identifies 1,191 AI-for-mathematics posts by 101 accounts. Their share of all posts rises from 1.1\% in January to 11.5\% in September, with contributing accounts increasing from 10 to 59. We represent discussion through linked target--aspect--stance triples, separating what is discussed from the property assessed and the author's evaluation. From July to September, capability and usefulness decline as a share of related discussion, while social and institutional concerns increase; changing contributors account for much of the latter shift. Among 38 accounts evaluating both technical quality or utility and communication, credit, or verification procedures, the procedural negative-component fraction is 19.4 percentage points higher on average (95\% account-bootstrap interval: 3.8--35.1). Matching targets within posts gives a similar direction. Repeated extraction varies substantially at the level of individual triples, although replacing the repeated sample preserves the aggregate contrast. Around OpenAI's October 6 mathematics release, related-post share rises from 9.6\% to 13.6\%, and contributing accounts increase from 13 to 28. Post-release discussion includes appreciation of the results' potential mathematical value and applications alongside criticism of promotion centered on result counts, limited methodological disclosure, and verification arrangements.

papers.title: On evolution of mean curvature and minimal areas in general codimension for inverse problems
papers.abstract: Many seemingly standard formulas for the evolution of the mean curvature vector in higher codimension assume only normal variations, which are ill-suited for analyzing the evolution of submanifolds- with-boundary whose boundaries may not be moving orthogonally at each time. Such situations arise when one considers inverse problems for minimal areas, for example, where such boundaries are confined to a larger ambient boundary. In this note, we provide coordinate-free identities for use in such problems, including higher order derivatives of mean curvature. We translate these identities to some of the existing inverse problem literature in codimension one. We also hope readers may find the computational framework helpful in other situations arising in geometric analysis.

papers.title: Zero-cycles on quotients of multiple double covers and their products
papers.abstract: We prove the 0-cycle form of the generalized Bloch conjecture for smooth projective models of subgroup quotients of multiple double covers of projective space, with smooth branch hypersurfaces and reduced simple normal crossings branch divisor. Our integral character criterion yields, in every dimension at least four, simply connected varieties of general type with 0-cycle Chow group \(\mathbb{Z}\), canonical volume four, and no birational product decomposition. We also determine optimal integral supports for componentwise product quotients and character decompositions of degree zero Chow groups. Within this covering class, we classify the minimum volume models and compute their pluricanonical map degrees.

papers.title: Multiplicativity of the Serre Spectral Sequence in Homotopy Type Theory
papers.abstract: Working in homotopy type theory, we define relative homotopy groups and give three equivalent definitions of the product on these groups. Using this product, we establish the multiplicativity of the cohomological Serre spectral sequence. We show a connection between the homotopy product and the cup-product in cohomology, which leads to the classically familiar description of the starting page of the spectral sequence as a tensor product of graded rings. As applications, we compute cohomology rings of several classifying spaces and loop spaces of spheres.

papers.title: When Should AI Overturn a Human Decision? Controversy at the 2026 World Cup and a $\sqrt{2/π}$ Solution
papers.abstract: We study how to combine a human binary call (a referee's offside or onside decision) with an AI numerical measurement (VAR's estimate of an attacker's position relative to the offside line). We derive an explicit maximum-likelihood rule that determines when the referee's call should stand and when a conflicting VAR measurement should overturn it. Our model treats the true offside margin as fixed and unknown and assumes independent additive Gaussian errors in the human's perception and the AI measurement. When both errors have zero means and known standard deviations $σ_H$ and $σ_{AI}$, respectively, the reversal threshold is $\sqrt{2/π}\,σ^2_{AI}/σ_H$. An onside call is overturned precisely when VAR's measured offside margin exceeds this threshold---not merely because VAR places the attacker beyond the offside line. We also derive the rule when either source has a systematic bias. We prove that the maximum-likelihood estimate of the true margin exists and is unique, while the final binary decision requires only a threshold comparison, without computing that estimate numerically. We illustrate the rule through numerical examples and show how to estimate the error parameters from calibration data. The same analysis applies beyond soccer to binary classification problems in which a human call and an AI measurement satisfy the stated model. This paper is intended for educational purposes: we aim to illustrate how undergraduate students and advanced high school students familiar with basic probability and calculus can investigate research questions in AI and its applications.

papers.title: On the free-boundary incompressible porous media equations with surface tension
papers.abstract: We study the free-boundary incompressible porous media equations with surface tension in dimension $1+d$. For fixed positive surface tension, we establish local well-posedness for arbitrary initial interfaces in $H^{s+1}$ and density perturbations in $H^s$, with $s>(d+3)/2$. When $s>(d+5)/2$, we justify the local vanishing-surface-tension limit for stable interfaces and sufficiently small density perturbations. In a finite-depth strip over $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a flat bottom and fixed positive surface tension, we prove global well-posedness and uniform anisotropic energy bounds for small compatible perturbations of an equilibrium with strictly stable stratification, under a horizontal low-frequency condition.

papers.title: The minimum forcing number of graphs and involutory weighted adjacency matrices
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with a perfect matching. The minimum forcing number $f(G)$ of $G$ is the smallest size of a matching in $G$ that is contained in exactly one perfect matching. For the $d$-hypercube $Q_d$ ($d\geq 2$) Diwan (2019) determined $f(Q_d)=2^{d-2}$ by using a linear algebraic method, and Mohammadian (2022) generalized this method and showed that $f(G\square K_2)=n/2$ when a bipartite graph $G$ admits order $n$ and an involutory weighted adjacency matrix over a field $\mathbb F$, where $\square$ denotes the Cartesian product. In this paper, we further prove that if $\operatorname{char}\mathbb{F}\neq 2$, then $\frac{n}{2}\le f(G\mathbin{\square} P_k)\le \frac{n}{2}\lceil\frac{k}{2}\rceil$ for every $k\ge 2$, where $P_k$ is the $k$-vertex path; this recovers Mohammadian's result when $k=2$, and the lower bound is attained for $k=3$. Moreover, we extend this method to non-bipartite graphs. Recursively constructing the adjacency matrix of the folded hypercube $FQ_n$ over the binary field $\mathbb F_2$, we prove that $f(FQ_n\mathbin{\square} K_2)=2^{n-1}$ for every even $n$. Combined with Mohammadian's result for odd $n$, this establishes the same formula for all $n\geq 1$.

papers.title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
papers.abstract: We study the learning of homogenized constitutive laws for inelastic heterogeneous materials, aiming to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations with surrogates that generalize across loading histories and microstructures. We focus on the recurrent neural operator framework, motivated by the explicit form of homogenized Kelvin--Voigt linear viscoelasticity. In this framework, internal variables enable a Markovian approximation of loading-history dependence, and neural operators represent the microstructure-dependent constitutive response. For periodic Kelvin--Voigt viscoelasticity, we prove a universal approximation theorem showing that the model can approximate the homogenized constitutive law to any prescribed accuracy, uniformly in time and over a wide set of admissible strain trajectories and microstructural property fields, in two and three dimensions. This comprises a significant extension of the existing, somewhat limited, one-dimensional theory that uses explicit solutions for piecewise constant materials. Instead, in two and three dimensions, we adopt a more versatile approximation based on the spectral representation of the memory kernel that arises from homogenization. This also enables us to give an explicit bound on the internal-variable dimension, sufficient for approximation, exhibiting logarithmic growth in the inverse relative stress error and in material contrast.
