Building on this, we analyze a nonsmooth trust-region method based on an $L^r$-trust region for $r > 0.5 q$ and prove its convergence to first-order stationary points.

papers.title: A stochastic gradient algorithm for non-separable optimization with convergence guarantee
papers.abstract: We study smooth parameterized non-separable objectives of the form $\mathcal L(θ)=F(Y(θ))$, where a global operator couples the outputs of all training samples. We analyze two stochastic gradient constructions within this output-space framework: the ideal per-batch gradient $G$, obtained by row sampling of the full output gradient, and a cached surrogate $H$ for parameterized updates in which full-data quantities are expensive to evaluate. For uniformly sampled batches, the ideal estimator has a deterministic batch-size scaling and a second moment controlled by the full output gradient. Using this structure, we establish local high-probability confinement and convergence for fixed positive step sizes on a prescribed parameter neighborhood under a power-type gradient inequality, with linear and polynomial regimes determined by its exponent. For the cached surrogate, a Lyapunov function couples the objective gap with the cache error and yields analogous local results on the corresponding non-exit event. The theory includes explicit path-length, confinement, and rate bounds; numerical experiments illustrate finite-budget decay trends and the effects of global output-gradient sampling, batch restriction, and cache tracking.

papers.title: An optimal local theory for reaction-diffusion equations driven by non-trace-class noise
papers.abstract: We study local well-posedness for a class of stochastic reaction-diffusion equations driven by multiplicative, possibly colored, noise. The interaction between rough stochastic forcing and polynomial nonlinearities naturally leads to solutions with low spatial regularity, making the treatment of the nonlinear terms delicate. Our main contribution is a general local existence and uniqueness theory for SPDEs with rough noise and highly irregular initial data. The framework also yields new results in standard noise regimes, including trace-class noise and space-time white noise. We identify the critical initial-data spaces for a wide range of nonlinearities, and we establish instantaneous parabolic regularization, general blow-up criteria, and sufficient conditions for positivity preservation. We apply the abstract theory to several prototypical models, including the stochastic Allen-Cahn, Burgers, Fisher-KPP, and coupled Gray-Scott equations. Finally, in the one-dimensional space-time white-noise setting, we combine our local theory with existing global a priori results in a highly singular regime.

papers.title: Sequential testing of conditionally constrained hypotheses
papers.abstract: We characterise e-processes for testing non-parametric hypotheses that require the conditional mean of a finite-dimensional statistic to lie in a prescribed convex set. Our main result is a complete-class theorem: every such e-process is pointwise dominated by a predictable product of affine one-step e-variables. Consequently, restricting to test supermartingales entails no loss: at any rejection threshold, the dominating process rejects no later on any observation path. We further show that a minimal complete class exists and consists of predictable products of maximal affine one-step e-variables. These results extend previous complete-class results from single-step constrained testing and bounded one-dimensional conditional mean testing to a broader conditional sequential setting.

papers.title: Weighted Recursions for Hurwitz Class Numbers
papers.abstract: We establish new recursions for Hurwitz class numbers with polynomial weights. In contrast to previous recursions, our results decouple class numbers of even and odd discriminants. Our main tool is the vector-valued holomorphic projection operator applied to mock modular forms. We invoke representation theory to connect the relevant spaces of vector-valued modular forms to spaces of classical new and old forms. We thereby leverage the vanishing of spaces of vector-valued cusp forms not available in the scalar case.

papers.title: Transversal unfoldings of derived foliations
papers.abstract: We study when a derived foliation along the fibres of a smooth morphism extends transversally to the total space. We classify strict unfoldings by basic Lie derivations, retaining the automorphisms arising from central isotropy. We define an intrinsic space of unfoldings and prove its agreement with the strict classification when the relative cotangent complex is a vector bundle in degree zero. A counterexample shows that the strict construction is not invariant under equivalent presentations. For two-term cotangent complexes, we describe cotangent extensions and their integrability conditions, and obtain cohomological existence criteria for strict unfoldings in explicit families. On smooth representable leaf spaces, descended unfoldings correspond to integrable Ehresmann connections.

papers.title: Delta-pulse solution in Zener viscoelastic model
papers.abstract: We derive an exact integral representation of the response to an impulsive boundary excitation in a semi-infinite, homogeneous, linear viscoelastic medium governed by the Zener model. Starting from the Bromwich integral, we analytically invert the relevant Laplace transforms and express the response in terms of modified Bessel functions of the first kind and Macdonald functions of half-integer order. The representation reduces to the known Maxwell solution in the appropriate limit. As an independent computational approach, we characterize the saddle points of the phase function and construct the associated steepest-descent path (SDP). Its branches satisfy a sixth-degree polynomial equation in the imaginary part of the complex variable, which is cubic in its square. Numerical comparisons for several model parameters confirm the agreement of the two methods. The integral representation reveals the structure of the response, whereas the SDP approach requires no closed-form inverse Laplace transform and can therefore be applied to more general viscoelastic models.

papers.title: On rational representations and rational group algebra of $\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$
papers.abstract: In this article, we study rational representations of $G=\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$, where $q$ is a prime power. Let $ρ$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then $ρ$ affords the character \[ Ω(χ)=m_{\mathbb{Q}}(χ)\sum_{σ\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(χ)/\mathbb{Q})}χ^σ, \] for some irreducible complex character $χ$ of $G$, where $m_{\mathbb{Q}}(χ)$ denotes the Schur index of $χ$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and conversely, every character of this form is afforded by an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. We obtain a combinatorial description for the counting of inequivalent irreducible $\mathbb{Q}$-representations of $G$ of each distinct degree. Furthermore, we briefly determine the rational character table of $G$ and present a method for constructing an irreducible rational matrix representation $ρ$ of $G$ affording the character $Ω(χ)$, where $χ$ is an irreducible complex character of $G$ arising from parabolic induction. Finally, using the results on the rational representations of $G$, we derive an explicit combinatorial formula, depending only on $q$, for the Wedderburn decomposition of $\mathbb{Q}G$.

papers.title: Ferrofluids: Modeling and Approximation
papers.abstract: Starting from Maxwell's and linear momentum balance equations, we derive a ferrofluid model using the generalized Onsager's principle. Guided by a discrete perturbation estimate, we design and analyze families of Galerkin schemes that converge to sufficiently regular solutions and derive error estimates. Finally, we numerically explore the model with our proposed method.

papers.title: Stacky geometry and logarithmic topology of transversely affine foliations
papers.abstract: We study the linear monodromy of codimension-one transversely affine foliations through multiplicative quotient stacks and logarithmic boundary topology. When the transverse affine structure admits a global presentation on $U$, a choice of multiplicative developing coordinate induces a morphism to $[\mathbb{C}^*/Γ]$, where $Γ\subset\mathbb{C}^*$ is the image of the linear monodromy. We prove that for infinite $Γ$ every strict semi-equivariant holomorphic self-map of $\mathbb{C}^*$ is a monomial, and classify the nonconstant strict semi-equivariant rational self-maps of $\mathbb{P}^1$ for arbitrary $Γ$. For a logarithmic connection along a simple normal crossings divisor, we describe the meridional characters and angular foliations on the boundary fibres of the Kato--Nakayama space, including the topology and closures of their leaves. We also describe the extension of the linear monodromy local system to this space and the effect of local Kummer base change on finite meridional monodromy.

papers.title: An extension of Stein's method incorporating dependence
papers.abstract: We extend Stein's method to include a prescribed dependence with respect to an auxiliary random variable, for conditional laws for which Stein characterizations do exist. This considerably extends the range of applications of Stein's method. The characterization we derive subsumes the case of independent random variables. Using the Malliavin calculus, we illustrate our extension on the example of a conditionally Gaussian/Beta-distributed random variable.

papers.title: Spanning triangulations in random graphs
papers.abstract: In 1991 Bollobás and Frieze found the threshold for the emergence of a spanning triangulation of a triangle in the binomial random graph, up to a logarithmic factor. In this paper, we find the threshold probability for the emergence of a spanning triangulation of a $k$-gon for any $3\leq k\leq n$, up to a constant factor.

papers.title: Abs-Smooth Frank-Wolfe Method: Primal-Dual Analysis, Heavy Ball Momentum, and Inexact Oracles
papers.abstract: We study projection-free optimization for convex objectives that satisfy abs-smoothness, a structural property that captures many non-smooth yet piecewise smooth functions arising, e.g., in modern machine learning models. We develop a unified framework for Abs-Smooth Frank-Wolfe methods, establishing a clean primal-dual analysis that guarantees convergence without requiring classical smoothness assumptions. Our framework extends the available results in two important directions. First, we introduce a heavy ball momentum variant and show that momentum can be incorporated naturally under abs-smoothness while preserving convergence guarantees. Second, we analyze inexact minimization oracles, demonstrating robustness to approximate inner solutions. Moreover, we relax the full convexity assumption and study the case where convexity holds only for the piecewise linear approximations of the objective, further broadening the applicability of conditional gradient methods to a wider class of non-smooth problems.

papers.title: Optimal Diameters of High Multiplicity g-Golomb Rulers
papers.abstract: A set $\cG$ of $n$ integers is called a $g$-Golomb ruler if the difference between any two distinct elements of $\cG$ is repeated at most $g$ times. If $g=1$, these are also called $B_2$-sets, Sidon sets, and Babcock sets. We define $G(g,n)$ to be the minimum diameter of a $g$-Golomb ruler with $n$ marks. In this paper, we prove that for every $ε>0$ and all sufficiently large positive integers $b$, if $g\ge(π/3+ε)b^{3/2}$, then $G(g,g+b)=g+2b-2$. Explicit thresholds are given for $b\le251$. The main technique is through an arithmetic property of the integers that are \emph{not} in a $g$-Golomb ruler, leading us to introduce LM rulers, a class of rulers where every positive integer distance $d$ occurs as a difference at most $d-1$ times. Writing $L(n)$ for the minimum diameter of an $n$-element LM ruler, we prove $L(n)\ge\sqrt{8/9}\,(n-1)^{3/2}$ for every positive integer $n$ and, using a Farey construction, $L(n)\le(π/3+o(1))n^{3/2}$ as $n\to\infty$. We also provide computationally verified optimal LM rulers for every $1\le n\le250$.

papers.title: Size and spectral conditions for a graph with given minimum degree to be $k$-$d$-critical
papers.abstract: A $k$-matching in a graph $G$ is defined as a function $f:E(G) \rightarrow \{0,1,\ldots,k\}$ satisfying $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)} f(e)$ $\leq k$ for each vertex $v\in V(G)$, where $E_G(v)$ denotes the set of edges incident to $v$ in $G$. For $1\leq d\leq k$ and $d \equiv |V(G)|~(\mathrm{mod}~2)$, if for any $ v \in V(G)$, there exists a $k$-matching $f$ such that $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)}f(e)=k-d$ and $\sum_{e\in E_G(u)}f(e)=k \text{ for any } u\in V(G)-\{v\}$, then $G$ is $k$-$d$-critical. A graph $G$ of odd order (resp. even order) is generalized factor-critical (resp. generalized bicritical) if the empty set is the unique set attaining the maximum value in $k$-Berge-Tutte-formula of $G$. In this paper, we provide sharp sufficient conditions in terms of size or spectral radius respectively for a graph $G$ to be $k$-$d$-critical, generalized factor-critical and generalized bicritical with minimum degree.

papers.title: Fast Rates for Offline Contextual Bandits with Forward-KL Regularization under Single-Policy Concentrability
papers.abstract: \emph{Kullback-Leibler} (KL) regularization is ubiquitous in reinforcement learning algorithms in the form of \emph{reverse} or \emph{forward} KL. Recent studies have demonstrated $ε^{-1}$-type fast rates for decision making under reverse KL regularization, in contrast to the standard $ε^{-2}$-type sample complexity. However, for forward-KL-regularized objectives, existing statistical analyses are either not applicable or result in $\tilde{O}(ε^{-2})$ slow rates. We take the first step towards addressing this problem via a streamlined analysis of forward-KL-regularized offline CBs. We give the first $\tilde{O}(ε^{-1})$ upper bounds in tabular and general function approximation settings, both under notions of \emph{single-policy concentrability}. In particular, our convex-analytical pipeline unifies these settings by exploiting the pessimism principle in a novel way and completely bypasses the proof routines in previous works based on the mean value theorem, which might be of independent interest. Moreover, we provide rate-optimal lower bounds, manifesting the tightness of our upper bounds in terms of statistical rates. Our lower bounds also demonstrate that the forward-KL-regularized sample complexity recovers the unregularized slow rate in the low-regularization regime, similarly to the reverse-KL regularization.

papers.title: Minimax Optimal Estimation of Transport-Growth Pairs in Unbalanced Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Unbalanced optimal transport extends classical optimal transport to measures with different total masses, but statistical guarantees for estimation of the transport map and the growth map remain limited. We study unbalanced optimal transport with quadratic cost and Kullback-Leibler marginal penalties and argue that the natural target of estimation is a transport-growth pair. Consequently, we develop two estimators for the transport-growth pair under two setups: a nearest-neighbor estimator for transporting between general densities, and a kernel-based estimator for transporting between smooth densities. We prove that the kernel-based estimator achieves the minimax optimal rate up to a logarithmic factor by deriving a matching lower bound on the minimax risk. Our main technical contribution is a reduction of estimation to a stability bound on the unbalanced optimal transport value. This bound controls the transport map and growth map risks through the duality gap of the true dual potentials for the estimated measures. These results provide a statistical foundation for estimation of the transport-growth pair in unbalanced optimal transport.

papers.title: No Triangulation Without Representation: Generalization in Topological Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Despite an ever-increasing interest in topological deep learning models that target higher-order datasets, there is no consensus on how to evaluate such models. This is exacerbated by the fact that topological objects permit operations, such as structural refinements, that are not appropriate for graph data. In this work, we extend MANTRA, a benchmark dataset containing manifold triangulations, to a larger class of manifolds with more diverse homeomorphism types. We show that, contrary to prior claims, graph neural networks can saturate the benchmark, while higher-order message passing methods lag behind. However, we find that this is contingent on the right representation and feature assignment, emphasizing their importance in baseline models. Hence, we present a novel evaluation protocol based on representational diversity and triangulation refinement. Even when including refinement-like changes in the training data, existing models fail to generalize beyond the combinatorial structure of the data. This points towards a research gap in developing models that understand topological structure independent of scale. Our work thus provides the necessary scaffolding to evaluate future models and enable the development of topology-aware inductive biases.

papers.title: INEUS: Iterative Neural Solver for High-Dimensional PIDEs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce INEUS, a meshfree iterative neural solver for partial integro-differential equations (PIDEs). The method replaces the explicit evaluation of nonlocal jump integrals with single-jump sampling and reformulates PIDE solving as a sequence of recursive regression problems. Like Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), INEUS learns global solutions over the entire space-time domain, yet it offers a more efficient treatment of nonlocal terms and avoids the computationally expensive differentiation of full PIDE residuals. These features make INEUS particularly well suited for high-dimensional PDEs and PIDEs. Supported by a contraction-based convergence proof for linear PIDEs, our numerical experiments show that INEUS delivers accurate and scalable solutions for various high-dimensional linear and nonlinear examples.

papers.title: Self-organized regime switching in null-recurrent dynamics
papers.abstract: Based on discrete observations $X_0,X_Δ,\dots, X_{nΔ}$ for $Δ=n^{-γ}$ with $γ\in [0,1)$ of the null-recurrent dynamic $dX_t = σ(X_t)dW_t$ with a Brownian motion $W$ and $σ(x)=α\mathbb{1}\{x<ρ\} + β\mathbb{1}\{x\geq ρ\}$, we derive rate of convergence and limiting distribution of the profile MLE for $ρ$. This includes low-frequency asymptotics ($γ=0$) for which the observations form a null-recurrent Markov chain. The derived non-standard limit is the argsup over a doubly stochastic drifted Poisson process explicitly involving the local time of oscillating Brownian motion. Its dependence on $ρ$ as well as the unknown volatility levels $α$ and $β$ is shown to be continuous w.r.t. the topology of weak convergence, enabling statistical inference. Whereas this limit is independent of the sampling frequency, the profile MLE's rate of convergence equals $n^{-(1+γ)/2}$ and is proven to be minimax optimal. The surprising idea of the proof of the limit theorem is to relate the long-term behavior of the null-recurrent Markov chain to the infill asymptotics on a fixed time interval. Indeed, in the very special case that $(X_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is started in the true parameter $X_0=ρ_0$, the process $(X_t-ρ_0)_{t\geq 0}$ is shown to possess a desirable distributional self-similarity. On basis of the strong Markov property, the artificial constellation of starting in $ρ_0$ is finally overcome by a coupling argument.

papers.title: Partition-of-Unity Gaussian Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
papers.abstract: Gaussian basis functions provide an efficient and flexible alternative to spline activations in Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs), but their performance is sensitive to the Gaussian scale parameter ε. We introduce the partition-of-unity Gaussian KAN (PU-GKAN), a kernel-based normalization framework that transfers the Shepard partition-of-unity principle to trainable KAN edge functions. Each Gaussian edge basis is normalized by its local sum over fixed centers, preserving the standard edge-based architecture and essentially the same trainable coefficient structure as GKAN. The resulting feature map reproduces constants exactly at the edge level and admits an explicit normalized finite-feature kernel interpretation. Numerical experiments show that PU-GKAN reduces sensitivity to ε, improves validation accuracy for most smooth and moderately non-smooth targets, and provides more stable training behavior. These benefits persist across variations in sample size and number of centers, higher-dimensional architectures, and Matern RBF bases. PU-GKAN also improves physics-informed neural networks for Helmholtz and wave equations, with validation-error reductions of up to 90%. These results establish partition-of-unity normalization as a mathematically grounded and broadly applicable framework for improving the reliability and accuracy of radial basis function KANs.

papers.title: Admissible Lax-Wendroff Flux Reconstruction Method with Automatic Differentiation on Adaptive Curved Meshes for Relativistic Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: The relativistic hydrodynamics (RHD) equations can give rise to solutions which have shocks, contact discontinuities, and other sharp structures, which interact and evolve over time. Capturing these sharp waves effectively requires a mesh with high resolution, making the scheme computationally expensive. In this work, adaptive mesh refinement is used with the high-order Lax-Wendroff flux reconstruction (LWFR) method to solve the system of RHD equations, which is closed with general Synge-type equations of state. To make the scheme Jacobian-free, the idea of automatic differentiation is incorporated for computing the temporal derivatives in the time average flux approximations. The high-order method is blended with an admissible low-order method at the subcell level to control the Gibbs oscillations and maintain the physical admissibility of the solution. Finally, several test cases involving high Lorentz factors, low densities, low pressures, strong shock waves, and other discontinuities are used to demonstrate the robustness, accuracy, and effectiveness of the proposed method. These simulations are performed with AMR using various linear and curved meshes to show the scheme's efficiency and ability to handle complex geometries.

papers.title: Induced fiber topological pressure for random dynamical systems
papers.abstract: We introduce induced fiber topological pressure for random dynamical systems and identify it with two critical exponents and the threshold of classical fiber pressure, allowing infinite fiber topological entropy. We establish an almost-sure fiberwise formula and a variational principle, and identify induced equilibrium states with classical equilibrium states. If the fiber topological entropy is finite and the entropy map is upper semicontinuous, an ergodic induced equilibrium state exists.

papers.title: Towards Optimal Passive Feedback Control of LTI Systems under LQR Performance
papers.abstract: We study state-feedback design for continuous-time LTI systems with a control input and an external input-output pair. Our objective is to determine feedback gains that render the closed-loop system (strictly) passive with respect to the external port while minimizing the standard LQR cost in the disturbance-free case. The resulting constrained optimization problem is intractable due to bilinear matrix inequalities. We analyze the set of passivating gains, showing it is unbounded, possibly nonconvex, path-connected, and contractible. We propose an indirect approach, in which the set of passivating feedback gains is inner-approximated by a compact, convex polytope. A projected gradient flow is employed to compute a gain within this polytope that minimizes the LQR cost. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness of the method.

papers.title: Internal structures in the category of right-preordered groups
papers.abstract: We give explicit axioms for the algebraic theory of the quasivarieties of right-preordered groups and preordered groups. We then look at lattices of effective equivalence relations, which turn out to be similar to the lattices of equivalence relations in the category of groups. Once this is established, we study internal structures in the category of right-preordered groups. We start with some general results and then prove the S-protomodularity of the category of right-preordered groups, when considering the class S of Schreier split epimorphisms. Following this, we investigate further and prove that the category of right-preordered groups turns out to be action representable when we restrict our attention to split epimorphisms in S. Relatively to this class of split epimorphisms, we define the notion of S-precrossed modules, and then of S-crossed modules; that correspond exactly to Schreier internal reflexive graphs and Schreier internal categories, respectively. Lastly, we characterize groupoids among Schreier internal categories and give some examples.

papers.title: Computing Families of Periodic Solutions of the 4- and 6-Body Problems Using an Adaptive Gradient-Free Stochastic Method
papers.abstract: In this paper, we numerically compute planar periodic motions of the 4- and 6-body problems. We consider a 4-body configuration formed by two opposite pairs of bodies and a 6-body configuration formed by two equilateral triangles. More generally, for two regular $k$-gons with masses $1$ and $m_2$ in the respective groups, we derive a system of four second-order differential equations for two radial and two angular variables; for $k=2$, the groups are opposite pairs. With $r_1(0)=1$, the periodicity conditions lead to an overdetermined nonlinear system consisting of eight return equations in five unknowns. We show that, for collision-free solutions, four symmetry conditions at $H=T/2$ imply these eight equations. For prescribed mass ratio and angular advance, we solve the resulting four equations in four unknowns using Newton's method. An adaptive stochastic black-box procedure, which uses only function evaluations, provides initial approximations. The method searches for solutions by sampling in an anisotropic box whose dimensions adapt using information from previous successful iterations. Exact satisfaction of the return conditions gives a motion that repeats up to rotation and relabeling; an angular advance that is a rational multiple of $2π$ then gives a periodic motion. We report numerical examples and check the return residuals of the printed initial conditions using both the reduced equations and independent integrations of the full Cartesian equations.

papers.title: Magnitude homology of real hyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: We define and study the magnitude and magnitude homology of real hyperplane arrangements by regarding their tope graphs as metric spaces. Since magnitude is a refinement of the cardinality, this may be viewed as a natural generalization of the classical problem of counting the chambers of an arrangement. Our central result is a structure theorem asserting that the magnitude and magnitude homology of an arrangement decompose into contributions indexed by its faces. In particular, the magnitude is determined by the intersection lattice of the arrangement. We also observe several interesting phenomena, including a characterization of Boolean arrangements in terms of diagonality and a reciprocity theorem reminiscent of Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity. Finally, based on explicit computations, we conjecture that the magnitude homology of an arrangement is torsion-free and determined by its intersection lattice.

papers.title: Linear Asymptotic Stability of the Smooth 1-Solitons for the Degasperis-Procesi Equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic stability of smooth 1-solitons in the Degasperis-Procesi (DP) equation. Such solutions necessarily exist on a non-zero background, and their spectral and orbital stability has previously been verified by Li, Liu & Wu and by Lafortune & Pelinovsky. Using the complete integrability of the DP equation to establish the strong spectral stability of smooth solitary waves, namely that the origin is the only eigenvalue of the associated linearized operator acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and that, moreover, in appropriate exponentially weighted spaces the non-zero spectrum for the linearized operator admits a spectral gap away from the imaginary axis. This spectral gap result {is then} upgraded to an exponential decay estimate on the semigroup associated with the linearized operator, establishing a linear asymptotic stability result in exponentially weighted spaces. Finally, we outline analytical challenges with extending our result to the nonlinear level.

papers.title: Associated varieties of integral minimal highest weight modules
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex simple Lie algebra and $L(λ)$ be a simple highest weight module of $\mathfrak{g}$ with highest weight $λ-ρ$, where $ρ$ is half the sum of positive roots. A simple $\mathfrak{g}$-module $L_w:=L(-wρ)$ is called integral minimal if the associated variety of its annihilator ideal equals the closure of the unique minimal special nilpotent orbit. In this paper, we find that the associated variety of any integral minimal module $L_w$ is irreducible and equal to the orbital variety corresponding to a minimal-length element in the Kazhdan--Lusztig right cell containing $w$.

papers.title: Negative Avoiding Sequences
papers.abstract: Negative avoiding sequences of span $n$ are periodic sequences of elements from $\mathbb{Z}_k$ for some $k$ with the property that no $n$-tuple occurs more than once in a period and if an $n$-tuple does occur then its negative does not. They are a special type of cut-down de Bruijn sequence with potential position-location applications. We establish a simple upper bound on the period of such a sequence, and refer to sequences meeting this bound as maximal negative avoiding sequences. We then go on to demonstrate the existence of maximal negative avoiding sequences for every $k\geq3$ and every $n\geq2$.

papers.title: Splitting-strategies for arbitrary-order fully mixed finite element discretizations of the Biot equations
papers.abstract: We study the fully-mixed formulation of the Biot equations which is characterized by a symmetric coupling between flow and deformation while each subphysics has internally a saddle point structure. This enables the use of stable mixed finite elements for each subproblem without a strong compatibility condition across the two subphysics. To exploit this flexibility while preserving the conservation structure of both subproblems, we consider fully mixed finite element methods in which the symmetry of the elastic stress tensor is enforced weakly, often referred to as a five-field formulation. The resulting mixed formulation exhibits an overarching saddle-point structure whose stability is determined by suitable inf-sup conditions. Inf-sup stability is established for several families of discrete spaces of arbitrary order, leading to optimal a priori error estimates. Iterative splitting strategies following the classical fixed-stress split with additional tuning are specifically investigated for the fully mixed formulation with proof of convergence and rates depending on the coupling strength. Contrary to previous analyses on coupled problems with a symmetric structure, we theoretically prove the efficacy of negative stabilization, consistent with Schur-complement ideas. Numerical results based on analytical solutions and the classical 2D Mandel problem and a 3D footing problem are presented supporting the theory.

papers.title: Counting subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{o}$ be a compact discrete valuation ring with residue field $\mathbb{F}_q$. We study the cotype zeta function of finite-index subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$ by adapting an approach developed by Voll for more general algebras. For each $\emptyset\neq I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, we express the generating series counting subalgebras whose elementary divisor valuations, listed in decreasing order, have jumps precisely at the positions in $I$ as a finite weighted sum of $\mathfrak{o}$-adic integrals. We compute these integrals in several cases, obtaining explicit formulas for the generating series associated with every singleton set $I$ in arbitrary rank. We also obtain the cotype zeta function of unital subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^4$. As a by-product, we obtain a universal lower bound for the abscissa of convergence of the subalgebra zeta function of any $\mathfrak{o}$-algebra that is free of rank $n$ as an $\mathfrak{o}$-module. We also establish several results concerning the uniformity problem for the subalgebra zeta function of \(\mathfrak{o}^n\). To do so, we study two systems of polynomial equations over the residue field and apply the results to derive the number of irreducible unital subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$ of index $q^e$, for $e\leq n+3$. Finally, we use the decomposition of subalgebras into local factors to obtain the number of unital subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$ of index $q^e$ for $e\leq 9$. For each fixed $n$, these subalgebra counts are universal polynomials in $q$.

papers.title: Poisson cohomology of "book" Poisson structures
papers.abstract: We compute the Poisson cohomology of the linear Poisson structure dual to the n-dimensional "book" Lie algebra, defined by [e_0,e_i]=e_i, [e_i,e_j]=0, for i,j=1,...,n-1.

papers.title: The recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson map, the orthogonal transpose symmetry map, and the computation of $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux
papers.abstract: Recently Watanabe has given an algorithm to compute a bijection, that he calls (quantum) Littlewood-Richardson (LR) map of type AII, between semi-standard Young tableaux of shape a partition with at most $2n$ parts and pairs of tableaux consisting of a symplectic tableau with shape a partition with at most $n$ parts, and a recording tableau of skew-shape given by the two previous shapes. The recording tableaux in that algorithm are shown to be equinumerous to LR-Sundaram tableaux whose injectivity is shown combinatorially while the surjectivity is concluded via representation theory of a quantum symmetric pair of type AII$_{2n-1}$. The algorithm to compute the quantum LR map provides a new branching model for the branching multiplicities from $GL_{2n}(\C)$ to $Sp_{2n}(\C)$. Here, as morally suggested by Watanabe, one provides a combinatorial proof for the surjectivity of the quantum LR map which in turn exhibits the restriction of the LR orthogonal transpose symmetry map to LR-Sundaram tableaux. The surjectivity is exhibited via the iteration of the reverse Schensted column insertion, initialized on a symplectic tableau, ruled by the slack data of a quantum recording tableau, and followed with the inverse reduction map on the bumped symplectic column in each iteration. The explicit inverse reduction map has been recently computed by the author in arXiv:2606.24840v2 for any symplectic column. The inverse of the quantum LR map is used to compute and characterize a family of $\k$- highest weight semi-standard tableaux in the recent proof of the Naito-Sagaki conjecture using the Watanabe's branching rule based on the crystal basis theory for $\imath$quantum groups of type AII$_{2n-1}$. That family of tableaux is generated by quantum recording tableaux with $1$-$0$-slack sequence and shape length $2n$ or $2n-1$ is characterized by certain linear inequalities.

papers.title: Parallel Newton methods for the continuous quadratic knapsack problem: A Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel tale
papers.abstract: The continuous quadratic knapsack (CQK) problem involves minimizing a diagonal convex quadratic function subject to box constraints and a single linear equality constraint. It has numerous applications in resource allocation, multicommodity flow, machine learning, and classical optimization tasks such as Lagrangian relaxation and quasi-Newton updates. In this work, we revisit the semismooth Newton method introduced by Cominetti, Mascarenhas, and Silva. We demonstrate that the method can be significantly improved in two directions. First, for projections onto the simplex or the $\ell_1$-ball, it can incorporate Condat's highly effective initial multiplier guess. Second, it can serve as a flexible foundation for CQK algorithms, allowing for different parallel variants tailored to exploit CPU and GPU computational models. These improvements are implemented in the open-source Julia package \texttt{NewtonCQK.jl}. We present extensive numerical tests comparing this implementation with other state-of-the-art solvers, demonstrating its superior efficiency and scalability.

papers.title: A universal model for the bifurcations of asymptotic values
papers.abstract: We study a universal model for the bifurcation of asymptotic values, based on the notion of tangent-like maps and families thereof. In analogy with polynomials and polynomial-like maps, we prove that every tangent-like map can be associated to a member of the model family. In particular, the filled Julia sets of tangent-like maps are quasiconformally homeomorphic to the ones for the model family. Likewise, the bifurcation locus of a family of tangent-like maps is homeomorphic to the boundary of the {\em Tandelbrot set} $\mathcal T$, the bifurcation locus of the model. Moreover $\mathcal T$ is universal, in the sense that homeomorphic copies of it can be found densely in the activity loci of asymptotic values of any appropriate natural family of finite type meromorphic maps. When applied to the iterates of a transcendental meromorphic map, these results make it possible to build a transcendental renormalization theory, a question that has been open for the last 25 years.

papers.title: Cores and localizations of $(\infty,\infty)$-categories
papers.abstract: We consider $(\infty,d)$-categories in the limit $d\to \infty$ via the core or localization functors that forget or invert higher non-invertible arrows, respectively. We compare the two resulting $(\infty,1)$-categories of $(\infty,\infty)$-categories and exhibit the localization-limit as a reflective localization of the core-limit. Furthermore, we study notions of invertibility that only emerge at $d=\infty$ and give rise to intermediate reflective localizations between the two limits. For example, we characterize coinductive completion and the maps it inverts, and reveal a new separation beyond the one of Henry--Loubaton by showing that even the stronger $ω$-completeness does not suffice to carve out the localization-limit.

papers.title: The permutation automorphism groups of irreducible cyclic codes
papers.abstract: The study of permutation automorphism groups of cyclic codes is a central topic in algebraic coding theory. A cyclic code over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is called irreducible if its check polynomial is irreducible over $\mathbb{F}_q$, and it is non-degenerate if it is not periodic. Such a non-degenerate code is standard if its permutation automorphism group is equal to the group generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius automorphism, and non-standard otherwise. In this paper, we give a complete classification of all non-standard non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes, using the classification of finite simple groups. Our result shows that, apart from a small number of explicit exceptional families and their descendants under certain secondary constructions, every non-degenerate irreducible cyclic code is standard, and up to four explicit exceptions, every nonzero degenerate cyclic code is non-standard. This classification has several consequences. First, it yields a general description of non-standard linear recurring sequence subgroups, extending the earlier work of Brison and Nogueira; secondly, it establishes the Schmidt-White conjecture for all non-standard non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes. Moreover, our results provide strong evidence in support of the conjecture of Berger and Charpin that almost all cyclic codes are standard.

papers.title: Singular spaces for computing the structured distance to singularity
papers.abstract: Finding the distance to singularity for a matrix is a ubiquitous problem in numerical linear algebra, and is elegantly solved by the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem. Its structured variant arises when one considers structured matrices and wants to preserve their structure. This problem is important for several matrix nearness problems that either entirely or partly reduce to a structured distance to singularity problem. In this work, we propose a new method for the structured distance to singularity problem based on singular spaces, that is, linear subspaces consisting of singular matrices. We study the properties of these spaces to guide the construction of the algorithm. In the Tikhonov regularized formulation, the method globally minimizes a certain objective function alternately in its arguments. We show that a restricted family of singular spaces suffices to attain the best possible improvement in a single iteration. In many of the numerical comparisons, the proposed method yields substantial reductions in running time when compared with existing methods, while the computed distances to singularity remain comparable. These gains allow larger problems to be solved within practical running times.

papers.title: Generalized $\mathbb{Z}_p$ toric codes as qudit low-density parity-check codes
papers.abstract: We study two-dimensional translation-invariant CSS stabilizer codes over prime-dimensional qudits on the square lattice under twisted boundary conditions, generalizing the Kitaev $\mathbb{Z}_p$ toric code by augmenting each stabilizer with two additional qudits. Using the Laurent-polynomial formalism, we adapt the Gröbner basis to compute the logical dimension $k$ efficiently, without explicitly constructing large parity-check matrices. We then perform a systematic search over various stabilizer realizations and lattice geometries for $p\in\{3,5,7,11\}$, identifying qudit low-density parity-check codes with the optimal finite-size performance. Representative examples include $[[242,10, \leq 22]]_3$ and $[[120,6, \leq 20]]_{11}$, both achieving $k d^{2}/n \leq 20$. Across the searched regime, the best observed $k d^{2}$ at fixed $n$ increases with $p$, with an empirical relation $k d^{2} = 0.0541 \, n^{2}\ln p + 3.84 \, n$, compatible with a Bravyi--Poulin--Terhal-type tradeoff when the interaction range grows with system size.

papers.title: Pathwise solutions of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by a multiplicative Hermite noise
papers.abstract: We study the viscous Burgers equation on the real line perturbed by a multiplicative noise $σ(u)\dot{Z}_t$, where $Z$ is a Hermite process of order $q\ge1$ and Hurst index $H\in(1/2,1)$; the case $q=1$ is fractional Brownian motion and $q=2$ is the Rosenblatt process. The stochastic term is a Young integral and the equation is solved path by path. A transformation of Doss-Sussmann type reduces it to a parabolic equation with random coefficients and quadratic growth in the gradient, for which we prove a maximum principle and a gradient estimate of Bernstein type on short time windows. We obtain global existence and uniqueness, the pathwise bound $|u(t,x)|\le\|u_0\|_\infty+\|σ\|_\infty|Z_t|$, and a Wong-Zakai type result without correction term. All moments are finite and $\mathbb{E}\exp(λ\sup_x|u(t,x)|^{2/q})<\infty$ for small $λ$. For the Rosenblatt process with $σ\geσ_0>0$, $\mathbb{E}\,e^{λu(t,x)}$ is finite for small $λ$ and infinite for $λσ_0t^H\geθ_H$, an explicit spectral constant, while the left tail is sub-Gaussian. We show that the temporal Hölder exponent $H$ is optimal, identify the limits of the power variations of $t\mapsto u(t,x)$, and deduce consistent estimators of $H$ and of the noise intensity from one path observed at one spatial point. For $q=2$ we relate the pathwise solution to a Skorokhod formulation through the forward/Skorokhod correction formula of Čoupek, Duncan and Pasik-Duncan.

papers.title: Bench-MFG: A Benchmark Suite for Learning in Stationary Mean Field Games
papers.abstract: The rise of Mean Field Games (MFGs) has fostered a growing family of algorithms designed to solve large-scale multi-agent systems. However, the field currently lacks a standardized evaluation protocol, forcing researchers to rely on bespoke, isolated, and often simplistic environments. This fragmentation makes it difficult to assess the robustness, generalization, and failure modes of emerging methods. To address this gap, we propose a comprehensive benchmark suite for MFGs, focusing on the discrete-time, discrete-space, stationary setting. We introduce a taxonomy of problem classes, ranging from no-interaction and monotone games to potential and dynamics-coupled games, and provide prototypical environments for each. Furthermore, we present MF-Garnets, a method for generating random MFG instances to facilitate rigorous statistical testing. We benchmark a variety of learning algorithms across these environments, including a novel population-based approach (MF-PSO). To our knowledge, this is the first benchmark for MFGs.

papers.title: A new product formula for $(z;q)_\infty$, with applications to asymptotics
papers.abstract: We express the $q$-Pochhammer symbol $(z;q)_\infty$ as an infinite product of gamma functions, analogously to how Narukawa expressed the elliptic gamma function as an infinite product of hyperbolic gamma functions. This identity is used to obtain asymptotic expansions when $q$ tends to $1$.

papers.title: Discovering hypergeometric series with harmonic numbers via Wilf-Zeilberger seeds
papers.abstract: By extracting coefficients from Wilf-Zeilberger pairs with respect to auxiliary parameters, we discover many nontrivial hypergeometric series involving harmonic numbers. In particular, we obtain a rapidly convergent series for the depth-two multiple zeta value $ζ(5,3)$, which appears to be the first result of its kind in the literature. We also investigate the Hilbert series attached to a WZ-seed and conjecture that it admits a remarkably simple form, suggesting the presence of an underlying graded-algebra structure associated with WZ-seeds.

papers.title: Induced Cycles of Many Lengths
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph and let $\mathrm{cl}(G)$ be the number of distinct induced cycle lengths in $G$. We show that for $c,t\in \mathbb N$, every graph $G$ that does not contain an induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{t+1}$ or $K_{t,t}$ and satisfies $\mathrm{cl}(G) \le c$ has bounded treewidth. As a consequence, we obtain a polynomial-time algorithm for deciding whether a graph $G$ contains induced cycles of at least three distinct lengths.

papers.title: Size conditions and spectral conditions for generalized factor-critical (bicritical) graphs and $k$-$d$-critical graphs
papers.abstract: Let $\mbox{odd}(G)$ and $i(G)$ denote the number of nontrivial odd components and the number of isolated vertices of a graph $G$, respectively. The $k$-Berge-Tutte-formula of a graph $G$ is defined as: $\mbox{def}_k(G)=\mathop{\text{max}}\limits_{S\subseteq V(G)}\{k\cdot i(G-S)-k|S|\} $ for even $k$; $\mbox{def}_k(G)=\mathop{\mbox{max}}\limits_{S\subseteq V(G)}\{\mbox{odd}(G-S)+k\cdot i(G-S)-k|S|\} $ for odd $k$. A $k$-barrier of a graph $G$ is the subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ that reaches the maximum value in the $k$-Berge-Tutte-formula of $G$. A graph $G$ of odd order (resp. even order) is generalized factor-critical (resp. generalized bicritical) if $\emptyset$ is its only $k$-barrier. Denote by $E_G(v)$ the set of all edges incident to a vertex $v$ in $G$. A $k$-matching of a graph $G$ is a function $f:E(G) \rightarrow \{0,1,...,k\}$ such that $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)} f(e)$ $\leq k$ for every vertex $v\in V(G)$. For $1\leq d\leq k$ and $d \equiv |V(G)|$(mod 2), if for any $ v \in V(G)$, there exists a $k$-matching $f$ such that $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)}f(e)=k-d$ and $\sum_{e\in E_G(u)}f(e)=k \text{ for any } u\in V(G)-\{v\}$. Then $G$ is $k$-$d$-critical. In this paper, we establish tight sufficient conditions in terms of size or spectral radius respectively for a graph $G$ to be generalized factor-critical, generalized bicritical, and $k$-$d$-critical. Furthermore, we prove the equivalence of the existence of four factors (namely, $\{K_2,\{C_t: t\geq 3\}\}$-factor, $\{K_2,\{C_{2t+1}:t\geq 1 \}\}$-factor, fractional perfect matching, perfect $k$-matching with even $k$) in a graph. Thus we also give size conditions and spectral radius conditions for a graph $G-v$ to have one of the four factors for any $v\in V(G)$.

papers.title: Stationary Mean-Field singular control of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
papers.abstract: Motivated by continuous-time optimal inventory management, we study a class of stationary mean-field control problems with singular controls. The dynamics are modeled by a mean-reverting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, and the performance criterion is given by a quadratic long-time average expected cost functional. The mean-field dependence is through the stationary mean of the controlled process itself, which enters the ergodic cost functional. We relate optimal controls for the stationary mean-field control problem to equilibria of an associated stationary mean-field game. In particular, optimal controls induce equilibria of the associated game, while the converse holds true within the class of admissible controls satisfying an additional integrability requirement. Finally, we solve the stationary mean-field game explicitly, thereby obtaining an explicitly characterized optimal reflection policy for the stationary mean-field control problem within this restricted class.

papers.title: Regularity of Lipschitz free boundaries for weak solutions of Alt-Caffarelli type problems
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Serrin problem, we study weak solutions of the generalised Alt-Caffarelli problem $-Δu = f$ in $Ω$, $u = 0$ on $\partialΩ$, $\partial_νu = Q$ on $\partialΩ$. Our main result establishes that if $Ω$ is Lipschitz, then it is actually $C^{\infty}$ (provided that $f$ and $Q$ are smooth). This was known before only for viscosity solutions. As a corollary, we obtain an alternative solution of Serrin's problem in the case of Lipschitz domains. We also discuss the characterisation of the regularity of Lipschitz domains in terms of their Poisson kernel.

papers.title: Some examples of DG-Lie formality transfer
papers.abstract: We give a convenient reformulation, a slight generalization and some applications of the formality transfer theorem for DG-Lie algebras.

papers.title: Control policies for a two-stage queueing system with parallel and single server options
papers.abstract: We study a two-stage queueing system attended by two flexible servers. Once a server begins to interact with a job, it remains attached to its job throughout both stages of service. After completing the first-stage service, the server chooses between two second-stage options. Option 1 sends the server-job pair to a parallel-service station where both servers may operate simultaneously; therefore, the server immediately begins the second-stage service on its job. Option 2 routes the pair to a single-service station that admits at most one server-job pair into service at a time. While we consider the complete range of parameters, the usual reason for choosing Option 2 is that jobs may receive higher-quality (faster and/or lower expected cost) service. If the single-service station is occupied, the pair must wait together until the station becomes available. The decision-making scenario is modeled via a Markov decision process formulation of a clearing system with holding costs at each station. Focusing on cases with a large initial queue, we fully characterize the structural properties of an optimal control policy based on the relationship between the service rates at the downstream stations. A numerical study highlights the significance of understanding the structure of the optimal policy by comparing its performance against several natural heuristic policies.

papers.title: Efficient total facial coloring of combinatorial maps
papers.abstract: Let $1<k\in\mathbb{Z}$. A total coloring of a connected simple regular graph $G$ via color set $]k]_0=\{0,1,\ldots, k\}$ is efficient if each color yields an efficient dominating set, where efficient domination applies to each color class in $V(G)$. An efficient total coloring of $G$ via $[k]_0$ extends to an efficient total facial coloring $c$ of a map $M(G)$ of $G$ if it assigns a vertex-and-edge $k$-color set to the boundary cycle of each face, with the consequently missing color assigned to the face itself, so that the two adjacent faces along each edge are assigned different colors. Focus is set upon planar and toroidal maps. Modifications of $c$ are also treated by removing a perfect dominating set or a 1-factor from $G$.

papers.title: High-order augmented Lagrangian methods and robust multilevel inner solvers
papers.abstract: We analyze high-order augmented Lagrangian methods for convex optimization problems with linear constraints and construct robust multilevel inner solvers. For the high-order proximal point method, we derive energy error estimates under uniform convexity that distinguish the sublinear, linear, and superlinear regimes by comparing the regularization power with the uniform convexity exponent. Through duality, these estimates yield convergence results for the high-order augmented Lagrangian method. The primal subproblems become nearly semicoercive as the penalty parameter decreases. We address this difficulty using multilevel subspace correction methods whose subspaces decompose the constraint kernel. Applications to nonlinear diffusion, Darcy--Forchheimer flow, and the finite neuron method show how the multilevel design accommodates mean, divergence, and boundary constraints. Numerical experiments illustrate the outer convergence regimes and demonstrate parameter-robust behavior of the inner solvers across different meshes.

papers.title: On two conjectures in spectral hypergraph theory
papers.abstract: For a connected uniform hypergraph $H$, we prove two conjectures concerning the algebraic multiplicities of the spectral radius of its adjacency tensor and the zero eigenvalue of its Laplacian tensor. In particular, we establish that the algebraic multiplicity of each of these eigenvalues is equal to the cardinality of the corresponding projective eigenvariety.

papers.title: Global compactness results for fractional $p$-Laplace Hardy Sobolev operator on a bounded domain
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a Struwe type global compactness result for a class of nonlinear critical Hardy-Sobolev exponent problems driven by the fractional $p$-Laplace Hardy-Sobolev operator.

papers.title: Robust Parallel Machine Scheduling: A Comparison of Robustness Measures and Local Search Approaches
papers.abstract: In many real-world scheduling problems, the processing times of tasks are subject to uncertainty. This makes it essential to design schedules that are robust against disruptions. We distinguish between two types of robustness: quality-robust schedules keep a stable objective value under disruptions, while solution-robust schedules keep a stable schedule structure. We study how to generate schedules for the Stochastic Parallel Machine Scheduling Problem (SPMSP) with precedence constraints and release dates that are both quality- and solution-robust. To this end, we compare several robustness measures and local search algorithms that use these measures. We start with an extensive simulation study where we determine the correlation of 13 existing and 6 new robustness measures with both quality and solution robustness. Next, we use the measures with high robustness correlation as the objective in our local search algorithm to find the best way to generate schedules containing both job-machine assignments as well as buffer assignments. We use a new dynamic objective weight within our local search algorithms, which actively changes the objective weights in each iteration. We found that the best way to generate robust schedules is to use robustness measures that model the processing times with normal distribution approximations and to combine job placement and buffer assignment simultaneously.

papers.title: On fractal minimizers and potentials of occupation measures
papers.abstract: We highlight two basic types of variational problems and prove the existence of fractal minimizers through the direct method in the calculus of variations. By design these minimizers are Hölder curves or Hölder parametrizations of surfaces whose images generally have a non-integer Hausdorff dimension. Their origin is deterministic, but their regularity properties are roughly similar to those of typical realizations of stochastic processes. As a key tool and our main technical result, we prove novel continuity and boundedness results for potentials of occupation measures of Gaussian random fields. These results complement well-known results for local times, but hold under much less restrictive assumptions. In an auxiliary section, we generalize earlier results on nonlinear compositions of fractional Sobolev functions with $BV$-functions to higher dimensions.

papers.title: A Benamou-Brenier Proximal Splitting Method for Constrained Unbalanced Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: The dynamic formulation of optimal transport, also known as the Benamou-Brenier formulation, has been extended to the unbalanced case by introducing a source term in the continuity equation. When this source term is penalized based on the Fisher-Rao metric, the resulting model is referred to as the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) setting, and allows for the comparison between any two positive measures without the need for equalized total mass. In recent work, we introduced a constrained variant of this model, in which affine integral equality constraints are imposed along the measure path. In the present paper, we propose a further generalization of this framework, which allows for constraints that apply not just to the density path but also to the momentum and source terms, and incorporates affine inequalities in addition to equality constraints. We prove, under suitable assumptions on the constraints, the well-posedness of the resulting class of convex variational problems. The paper is then primarily devoted to developing an effective numerical pipeline that tackles the corresponding constrained optimization problem based on finite difference discretizations and parallel proximal schemes. Our proposed framework encompasses standard balanced and unbalanced optimal transport, as well as a multitude of natural and practically relevant constraints, and we highlight its versatility via several synthetic and real data examples.

papers.title: Secondary Stiefel-Whitney numbers and corresponding cobordism groups
papers.abstract: For every relation $R$ between Stiefel-Whitney numbers of closed $(n+1)$-manifolds we consider an associated invariant $\varkappa_R$ of null-cobordant $n$-manifolds with a certain additional structure. For $n=2k-1$ and $R = w_{n+1}+v_k^2$ the invariant $\varkappa_R$ equals the Kervaire semi-characteristic. In addition, we construct the cobordism group $Ω_n^R$, which extends the unoriented cobordism group $Ω_n^O$. We show that $\varkappa_R$ is a complete invariant of $R$-cobordism classes of null-cobordant $n$-manifolds. We prove that our invariant $\varkappa_R$ and $R$-cobordism class of manifold are quadratic in the sense of Gusarov-Vassiliev-Podkorytov.

papers.title: Blowup for the multiplicative stochastic heat equation with superlinear drift
papers.abstract: We consider the stochastic heat equation with multiplicative white noise: $\partial_t u =\partial_x^2u + b(u) +σ(u) \dot W$, both on $[0,1]$ and $\mathbb R$. In the case of $[0,1]$ we show that the finite Osgood criterion on $b$ is a necessary and sufficient condition for finite-time blowup, under fairly general conditions on $σ$. In the case of $\mathbb R$ we show instantaneous explosion when we start with initial profile $u_0\equiv 1$. Our work introduces a novel approach that not only extends the work of [12] which dealt with bounded $σ$, but also provides an alternate route to proving such results. A key ingredient is a comparison result which shows that the solution on $\mathbb R$ stays above the corresponding solution on $[0,1]$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions.

papers.title: Absorbed Types and Derivations in Exponential o-Minimal Theories
papers.abstract: I analyze $\mathcal{O}$-weakly immediate and $\mathcal{O}$-residual types in an o-minimal expansion of an ordered field $\mathbb{E}$, where $\mathcal{O}$ is a convex valuation ring. The main result is a characterization of those exponential theories $T$ such that for all $(\mathbb{E}, \mathcal{O})\models T_{\mathrm{convex}}$ the image of any $\mathcal{O}$-weakly immediate type is given by some composition of translations, sign changes and exponential, of some \emph{possibly different} $\mathcal{O}$-weakly immediate type. I call these theories \emph{transserial}, and they encompass simply exponential theories such as $T_{\exp}$ and $T_{an, \exp}$. A consequence of the analysis is that there are no counterexamples to \emph{Tressl's signature-alternative} (cf [15]) in models of transserial theories admitting an Archimedean prime model. The characterization has at its core some arguments that use very few but fundamental properties of the valued differential field of germs at a cut in an o-minimal structure. These are abstracted in some conditions of compatibility between the derivation and the order or the derivation and the valuation, both ultimately stemming from the mean-value-theorem in o-minimal structures. I develop some basic theory around these notions and observe that in the case of few constants (i.e.\ when the valuation ring contains the constants) these notions specialize to notions thoroughly studied in arXiv:1509.02588

papers.title: Symmetric harmoniousness of odd-order groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every group of odd order is symmetric harmonious, i.e., there exists a permutation $g_0,g_1,\dots,g_{\ell-1}$ of the elements of $G$ such that the consecutive products $g_0g_1,g_1g_2,\dots,g_{\ell-1}g_0$ also form a permutation of the elements of $G$ and $g_{\ell-i}=g_i^{-1}$ for all $1\le i\le \ell-1$, where $\ell=|G|$. Consequently, a group is symmetric harmonious if and only if it has odd order. We also characterize symmetric harmonious sequences in terms of complete mappings. As applications we obtain new examples of R*-sequenceable groups, and we show that every split extension of an odd-order group by a harmoniously matched group is both harmonious and \#-harmonious. Together with several new harmoniously matched groups ($D_{12},D_{16},D_{20},D_{24},Q_{16},Q_{24},A_4,S_4$), this yields many non-abelian groups that are both harmonious and \#-harmonious, including infinite families of dihedral and dicyclic groups and all $2$-nilpotent groups with an abelian Sylow $2$-subgroup that is neither cyclic nor elementary abelian and is central in its normalizer.

papers.title: The doubling property of the elliptic measure, for elliptic operators with drifts satisfying an average diverging condition
papers.abstract: We show doubling of the elliptic measure corresponding to the operator with an elliptic principal term and a drift that diverges, on average on Whitney cubes, like the inverse distance to the boundary, with a small constant. Essentially a small Carleson constant assumption on the drift, this generalizes earlier results with the hypothesis of pointwise smallness of such a drift. This relates to recent perturbative results of rough Dirichlet solvability in domains with drifts or potentials that satisfy a Carleson measure condition, which have also been considered earlier by Hofmann-Lewis and Kenig-Pipher. While we work in 1-sided chord arc domains, these results are new even for the half-space. In the process, we also prove Hardy inequalities in such domains with Alhfors-David regular boundary, using a stopping time argument.

papers.title: Effective Resistance in Simplicial Complexes: Generalizations and Properties
papers.abstract: Originally introduced in circuit theory, the notion of effective resistance has been fruitfully exploited in graph theory, where each edge in a graph is understood as a resistor in an electric network. In this context, the effective resistance between two vertices quantifies the total opposition to current flow when a unit current is injected at one vertex and extracted at the other. As such, it encodes rich structural and geometric information about the underlying graph: it satisfies a minimum-energy principle termed Thomson's principle, defines a metric on the vertex set, relates to the topology of the graph through Foster's theorem, and determines the probability of appearance of an edge in a random spanning tree. Generalizations of effective resistance to simplicial complexes have been proposed in several forms, often formulated as matrix products of standard operators associated with the complex. We introduce a novel, basis-independent bilinear form, derived from an algebraic reinterpretation of circuit theory, that extends the classical effective resistance from graphs to simplicial complexes. This bilinear form acts on chains and cochains, and in particular, simplices and cosimplices in a simplicial complex. Our framework subsumes and unifies all existing matrix-based formulations of effective resistance. Moreover, we establish higher-order analogues of several fundamental properties known in the graph case: (i) we extend Thomson's principle to our basis-free framework; (ii) we establish metric properties for the effective resistance and its square root on chains and cycles, recovering the classical graph case; (iii) we provide a generalization of Foster's theorem to simplicial complexes; and (iv) we prove a matrix-tree theorem for higher-dimensional spanning trees, linking effective resistance to the probability of appearance of a simplex in random simplicial spanning trees.

papers.title: Sub-Diffusive Black--Scholes Model and Structure-Preserving Girsanov Transform
papers.abstract: We propose a sub-diffusive Black--Scholes model in which stock prices are governed by stochastic differential equations driven by sub-diffusions. The model captures the periods of low trading activity observed in bear markets, and it contains the classical Black--Scholes model as a special case. The sub-diffusive spot market is arbitrage-free but, in general, incomplete. We study the pricing of European contingent claims in this model. To this end, we establish a structure-preserving Girsanov transform for sub-diffusions. We use it to identify the minimal martingale measure of the model. This measure is the unique equivalent martingale measure under which the discounted stock prices are martingales driven by sub-diffusions with the same law as the original ones. Using this measure, we price every contingent claim in $L^p$ with $p>2$. For each such claim, we construct a replicating strategy that is mean self-financing and minimizes the local risk, and whose value process gives the price process of the claim. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the price of a European call option. We show that this price solves a partial differential equation with a fractional derivative in time, which we call the time-fractional Black--Scholes equation.

papers.title: Proper maps of annuli
papers.abstract: We study proper holomorphic maps of annuli in complex Euclidean spaces, that is, domains with $U(n)$ as the automorphism group. By the Hartogs phenomenon and a result of Forstnerič, such maps are always rational and extend to proper maps of balls. We first prove that a proper map of annuli from $n$ dimensions to $N$ dimensions where $N < \binom{n+1}{2}$ is always an affine embedding. This inequality is sharp as the homogeneous map of degree 2 satisfies $N=\binom{n+1}{2}$. Next we find a necessary and sufficient condition for a map to be homogeneous: A proper map of annuli is homogeneous if and only if its general hyperplane rank, the affine dimension of the image of a general hyperplane, is exactly $N-1$. As a corollary, we obtain a classification of homogeneous proper maps of balls. A homogeneous proper ball map takes all spheres centered at the origin to spheres centered at the origin. We show that if a proper ball map has general hyperplane rank $N-1$ and takes one sphere centered at the origin to a sphere centered at the origin, then it is homogeneous. Another corollary of this result is a complete classification of proper maps of annuli from dimension 2 to dimension 3. Finally, we give a complete normal form of rational proper maps of annuli of degree 2.

papers.title: On a Question of Mirzakhani and Vondrák concerning Sperner Labelings of the Simplex-Lattice Hypergraph
papers.abstract: Mirzakhani and Vondrák asked whether the simplex-lattice hypergraph admits a Sperner-admissible labeling in which every hyperedge receives at most two colors. We answer this question affirmatively by introducing the \emph{dominant labeling}, in which every lattice point is labeled by its unique \emph{dominant index}. In their hybrid model of fair division, this yields preference functions under which at most two players are nearly satisfied. We determine the number of vertices of each color and the number of hyperedges using a given pair of colors; these counts are expressed through the entries of Catalan's triangle. We also characterize the color sets of hyperedges of the other hypergraphs that arise from the edgewise triangulation of the dilations of the standard unit simplex.

papers.title: Linear relations among radicals
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field, fix an algebraic closure $\overline{K}$, and let $G$ be a subgroup of $\overline{K}^\times$. We are able to give a closed formula for the ratio between the degree $[K(G):K]$ and the index $|GK^\times:K^\times|$, provided that the latter is finite. Our formula explains all the $K$-linear relations among radicals, which (beyond the ones stemming from the multiplicative group $GK^\times/K^\times$) are generated by relations among roots of unity and single radicals. Our work builds on results by Rybowicz, which in turn are based on work by Kneser and Schinzel.

papers.title: Emerging consecutive pattern avoidance
papers.abstract: In this note we study the asymptotic popularity, that is, the limit probability to find a given consecutive pattern at a random position in a random permutation in the eighteen classes of permutations avoiding at least two length 3 consecutive patterns. We show that for ten classes, this popularity can be readily deduced from the structure of the permutations. By combining analytical and bijective approaches, we study in detail two more involved cases. The problem remains open for five classes.

papers.title: DualHash: Stochastic Primal-Dual Algorithms for W-Type Regularized Deep Hashing
papers.abstract: Deep hashing encodes high-dimensional image features into compact binary codes, enabling efficient similarity search in large-scale content-based image retrieval, a problem akin to semantic-preserving lossy compression under extreme bit-rate constraints. A fundamental challenge in deep hashing stems from the discrete nature of quantization in generating the codes. W-type regularizations, such as $z\mapsto\||z|-1\|_1$, are widely adopted and empirically effective at pushing network outputs toward binary values. However, existing methods often directly optimize these regularizations without convergence guarantees. While proximal gradient methods offer a promising solution, the coupling between W-type regularizers and neural network outputs results in composite forms that generally lack closed-form proximal solutions. In this paper, using Fenchel duality, we reformulate the nonconvex W-type regularization term through its convex conjugate, yielding a min-max problem with tractable proximal updates. We show that this min-max problem captures the stationarity of the original deep hashing objective up to the quantization error. Building on this problem, we present a stochastic primal-dual hashing algorithm, referred to as DualHash, with oracle complexity guarantees. We derive two algorithm instances: a momentum-based version with $O(\varepsilon^{-4})$ oracle complexity and an improved $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ version using variance reduction, both for $\varepsilon$-KKT points of the min-max problem, which yield near-stationarity guarantees for the original objective. Experiments on three standard datasets demonstrate competitive retrieval accuracy and reduced quantization error, validating the practical value of DualHash for image retrieval problems. Our implementation of DualHash is available at https://github.com/RailLee/DualHash.

papers.title: Generalized Divisors and Canonical Coarsening on Tame Deligne-Mumford Curves
papers.abstract: We study effective generalized divisors on reduced tame Deligne-Mumford curves over $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying $G_1$ and $S_2$. Canonical coarsening maps divisor ideals to coarse canonical lattices. We describe its fibres by exact intervals of equivariant lattices. For flat projective finite-quotient families of geometrically reduced Gorenstein curves over locally Noetherian bases, with finite constant groups and the stated relative-duality and base-change hypotheses, we construct projective invariant-Quot schemes for fixed canonical lattices with finite flat quotients and prescribed quotient representations. A nontrivial marked deformation preserves the coarse ring, normalization, conductor and entire fixed canonical fibre, while a length-four isotypic jet detects its parameter. We compute the full normalization and conductor correction after support restriction on an explicit rank-three chart. As a module, the correction splits into one surface and two line canonical modules, with a common grading shift. The corresponding square-zero algebra extension is nonsplit. The full source-support pair is compared through second order. Exact computational certificates accompany the proofs.

papers.title: DE-Sinc approximation for unilateral rapidly decreasing functions and its computable error bound
papers.abstract: The Sinc approximation is highly effective for functions that decay rapidly at both ends of the real axis. For unilateral rapidly decreasing functions, which decay algebraically as $t\to-\infty$ and exponentially as $t\to\infty$, an appropriate variable transformation is required. Existing single-exponential transformations for this class of functions yield only root-exponential convergence, even when improved transformations are employed. This paper develops a double-exponential (DE)-Sinc approximation based on the transformation $t=2\sinh(\log(\log(1+\exp(π\sinh x))))$, which was previously introduced for numerical integration. The main contribution is a rigorous and computable error bound of order $\operatorname{O}(\exp(-cn/\log n))$ with a constant explicitly expressed in terms of the problem parameters. Under the stated assumptions, the resulting approximation achieves almost exponential convergence and is suitable for computation with guaranteed accuracy. Numerical examples satisfying these assumptions confirm the predicted convergence behavior and the validity of the derived error bound.

papers.title: A reverse entropy power inequality for i.i.d. log-concave random variables
papers.abstract: We show that $h_\infty(X+Y)\leq h_\infty(Z+W)$, where $X, Y$ are independent log-concave random variables, and $Z, W$ are exponential random variables having the same respective $\infty$-Rényi entropies. Analogs for integer-valued monotone log-concave random variables are also obtained. Our main tools are decreasing rearrangement, majorization, and the change of measure.

papers.title: Convergence of optimizers implies eigenvalues filtering at equilibrium
papers.abstract: Ample empirical evidence in deep neural network training suggests that a variety of optimizers tend to find nearly global optima. In this article, we adopt the reversed perspective that convergence to an arbitrary point is assumed rather than proven, focusing on the consequences of this assumption. From this viewpoint, in line with recent advances on the edge-of-stability phenomenon, we argue that different optimizers effectively act as eigenvalue filters determined by their hyperparameters. Specifically, the standard gradient descent method inherently avoids the sharpest minima, whereas Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) algorithms go even further by actively favoring wider basins. Inspired by these insights, we propose two novel algorithms that exhibit enhanced eigenvalue filtering, effectively promoting wider minima. Our theoretical analysis leverages a generalized Hadamard--Perron stable manifold theorem and applies to general semialgebraic $C^2$ functions, without requiring additional non-degeneracy conditions or global Lipschitz bound assumptions. We support our conclusions with numerical experiments on feed-forward neural networks.

papers.title: Computing weighted sheaf cohomology using noncommutative differential modules
papers.abstract: We describe a novel method for computing sheaf cohomology over weighted projective spaces and stacks using exterior algebra and differential module techniques, generalizing an algorithm due to Eisenbud-Fløystad-Schreyer over projective space.

papers.title: The ribbon category of representations of a crossed module
papers.abstract: The theory of representations of a crossed module is a direct generalization of the theory of representations of groups. For a finite group G, the Drinfeld quantum double of the group G is a Hopf algebra that represents a special case of crossed module of finite groups. Here we study how to extend the construction of the Drinfeld quantum double for any other kind of crossed module of finite groups. This leads to a Hopf algebra D(G,H) that presents similarities with a Drinfeld double. We then study simple subalgebras of D(G,H) and give two isomorphisms for the decomposition into a product of simple subalgebras. We then study the category D(G,H)-mod^Fd of finite dimensional modules over D(G,H), which turns out to be isomorphic to the category of finite dimensional representations of finite crossed modules of groups. These categories being monoidal, we also study links between direct sums of simple objects and tensor products of simple objects and give some results for a Clebsch-Gordan formula. We, in this context, present and develop the character theory for representations of crossed modules of finite groups, and detail the proofs. We then study the category itself, which leads to some ribbon invariants.

papers.title: Noise estimation of SDE from a single data trajectory
