Under the additional assumption $\Div\B\le0$, we construct a Green's function and prove pointwise and gradient estimates. For the characteristic distributional identity with a Dirac mass at the pole to hold, we will additionally assume either $\Div\B=0$ or $\B\in L^{n,1}_{	extup{loc}}(Ω)$. Moreover, in the divergence-free case, we obtain a local lower bound for the Green's function, CFMS estimates, doubling of harmonic measure, a comparison principle for nonnegative solutions with zero trace, and a change of pole formula. Finally, we construct, in the upper half-space, an operator of the form $-Δ+\B\cdot
abla$ with $\B$ form-bounded and divergence-free, whose harmonic measure exhibits dimension drop.

papers.title: Positivity and negativity for $h$-bases for $n$
papers.abstract: A set $A$ of integers is an $h$-basis for $n$ if every integer in $[0,n] = \{0,1,2,\ldots,n\}$ belongs to the sumset $hA$, that is, can be represented as the sum of exactly $h$ not necessarily distinct elements of $A$. The classical postage stamp problem asks for the largest integer $n_h(k)$ such that $[0,n_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of nonnegative integers of size $k+1$. We consider the effect of allowing negative elements. Let $n^{\flat}_h(k)$ be the largest integer such that $[0,n^{\flat}_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of integers of size $k+1$ containing at least one negative integer. For $k=2$, we have $n^{\flat}_h(2) < n_h(2)$ if $h$ is odd or $h=4$ and $n^{\flat}_h(2) = n_h(2)$ if $h$ is even and $h \neq 4$. Proofs of these comparison results were autonomously discovered and formally verified in Lean by https://aristotle.harmonic.fun/}{Aristotle}, a formal reasoning agent developed by https://www.harmonic.fun/}{Harmonic}. In this paper we give new proofs of these results.

papers.title: A recurrence in logarithmic Möbius sums with coprimality conditions via Euler-Maclaurin
papers.abstract: We derive a recurrence for logarithmically weighted Möbius sums by combining Möbius inversion with the Euler-Maclaurin summation formula. Consequently, starting from estimates of orders zero, one and two, we obtain polynomial approximations for these sums for every nonnegative integer exponent of $\log$. We then extend these estimates to sums with coprimality conditions via a convolution identity and to sums weighted by the reciprocal of the sum-of-divisors function. We also study the nonnegativity of the latter sums for every positive integer logarithmic order, establishing that they never change sign.

papers.title: Block Sensitivity and Certificate Complexity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions
papers.abstract: We investigate block sensitivity and certificate complexity of monomial rotation-symmetric Boolean functions, obtaining exact formulas and structural classifications for several families. For odd-degree monomial rotation-symmetric functions, the equality $s(f)=n$ established in our earlier work yields $bs(f)=C(f)=n$. For quadratic monomial rotation-symmetric functions, we determine both measures completely and prove that block sensitivity equals certificate complexity. For consecutive quartic monomials, we determine sensitivity, block sensitivity, and certificate complexity in every residue class of the number of variables. Our principal result is an exact global block-sensitivity formula for consecutive monomials of every even degree $d\ge4$. Writing $n=q(d+2)+ρ$, where $0\leρ<d+2$ and $q\ge\max\{2,d/2-1\}$, we prove \[ bs(F_{d,n})=n-\min\left\{\left\lceil\fracρ{2}\right\rceil,d+2-ρ\right\}. \] We also establish the corresponding sensitivity formula by a self-contained argument, yielding arbitrarily large gaps between sensitivity and block sensitivity as the degree varies. For certificate complexity, we obtain exact pointwise formulas for structured run-and-gap configurations and establish additional global equalities, including $C(F_{6,8q+5})=bs(F_{6,8q+5})=8q+2$ for $q\ge2$. Our methods combine cyclic run decomposition, parity arguments, explicit sensitive-block constructions, and constant-subcube certificates. The exact global certificate complexity for arbitrary even degrees remains open.

papers.title: Sensitivity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions via Binary Necklaces
papers.abstract: Rotation symmetric Boolean functions are important structured families in the theory of Boolean functions, where cyclic invariance permits compact algebraic descriptions while retaining nontrivial local behavior. We investigate their sensitivity through binary necklaces and monomial orbit sums. In the necklace quotient of the Boolean cube, ordinary adjacency does not record the number of coordinate flips: we give a directed flip-multiplicity formula involving stabilizers and distance-two near-periods, and derive exact local sensitivity formulas when the number of variables is an odd prime. For monomial rotation symmetric functions we determine sensitivity for all odd degrees and for quadratic orbit sums. For the consecutive-monomial family of every even degree $d\ge4$, we prove a run-cluster inequality and obtain the eventual exact formula $s(F_{d,n})=n-\min\{r,d+2-r\}$, where $n\equiv r\pmod{d+2}$, under the stated length hypothesis. The consecutive quartic case follows explicitly. We also evaluate sensitivity for cyclic run-threshold functions. Our results provide exact combinatorial and complexity-theoretic information about cyclic Boolean functions and clarify how cyclic symmetry governs local sensitivity.

papers.title: Equilibria and Consensus in Mixed Weighted-Average and Weighted-Median Opinion Dynamics: The Consensus-Promoting Role of Weighted-Average Individuals
papers.abstract: How individuals respond to their neighbors' opinions shapes whether a networked group reaches consensus. This paper analyzes synchronous discrete-time opinion dynamics on a fixed influence network, where individuals use either weighted-average (WA) or weighted-median (WM) opinion-aggregation mechanisms with individual-specific inertia coefficients. We characterize equilibria through graph-theoretic conditions on opinion level sets and WA balance equations, proving that every solution converges to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium. We define type-dependent cohesive sets, whose WA members assign all their influence weight to the set and WM members assign at least half. The absence of two disjoint such sets gives a necessary and sufficient graph-theoretic criterion for consensus from any initial condition. Otherwise, an open set of initial conditions leads to persistent dissensus. Converting WM individuals to WA cannot create type-dependent cohesive sets and preserves existing guarantees of consensus from any initial condition. If the conversion eliminates every disjoint pair of these sets, the converted system also guarantees consensus from any initial condition. Four numerical studies examine the locations and proportion of weighted-average individuals, as well as the influence weights, while comparing the consensus criterion with finite-horizon simulation outcomes. In the four network ensembles with 100 individuals, the observed frequency of reaching a prescribed consensus tolerance is nondecreasing with WA proportion at each tested simulation horizon. This trend supports the consensus-promoting role of WA individuals, although individual realizations need not follow it.

papers.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
papers.abstract: We prove cone restriction estimates under half-scale dimensional conditions. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we incorporate the broad restriction estimate of Ou--Wang and a localized multilinear estimate obtained through cyclic bilinear pairing and multilinear Kakeya bounds for local packet energies. For certain ambient and weight dimensions, our estimates are sharp in suitable ranges of $p$, up to an $R^\varepsilon$ loss.

papers.title: Low Lying Zeros of Dedekind Zeta Functions
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n_K$, and let $h(K)$ denote the smallest absolute value of the imaginary part of a non-trivial zero of its Dedekind zeta function $ζ_K$. In 1979, Hoffstein proved the unconditional bound $h(K)\leq 0.87+o(1)$ as $n_K\to\infty$. In a 1990 survey, Odlyzko announced the stronger bound $h(K)\leq 0.54+o(1)$ without proof. No improvement on Hoffstein's bound has since appeared with a published proof. We construct a comparison kernel from a linear combination of three identities and show that Hoffstein's original parameters give $h(K)<0.825$ for sufficiently large $n_K$. We generalise Hoffstein's method via Stechkin's trick and prove $h(K)<0.58$ for all sufficiently large $n_K$, giving the best proved estimate to date. Moreover, $ζ_K$ has at least $c n_K$ non-trivial zeros with imaginary part in $[0,0.58]$, counted with multiplicity, for some $c>0$ and $n_K$ large enough.

papers.title: Finite Root Sums in Symmetrizable Kac-Moody Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra with root system $Φ$. A subset $S\subseteqΦ$ is closed if $α,β\in S$ and $α+β\inΦ$ imply $α+β\in S$. For finite and affine Kac-Moody algebras, this closure property is known to extend from pairs to arbitrary finite sums that are roots. We prove that every closed subset of the root system of any symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra is closed under arbitrary finite sums that are roots. The proof uses real-root strings, a simultaneous separation lemma for positive imaginary roots, and a lemma on when the sum of two positive imaginary roots is again a root. As an application, we extend a necessary condition for wideness of regular subalgebras from finite and affine types to all symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebras: the symmetric closure of the roots associated to a wide regular subalgebra is the entire root system.

papers.title: On Waring-Goldbach problem for two squares and higher powers
papers.abstract: Let $ν_1(n)$ and $ν_2(n)$, respectively, denote the number of representations of the natural number $n$ as the following form \begin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^4+p_4^4+p_5^4+p_6^5+p_7^8, \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^3+p_4^4+p_5^5+p_6^6+p_7^8, \end{equation*} where $p_1,\dots,p_7$ are primes in both above cases. In this paper, it is proved that $ν_1(n)\gg n^{43/40}(\log n)^{-7}$ holds for every sufficiently large integer $n$ subject to $n\equiv1\pmod2$ and $n\equiv\pm1\pmod3$. Moreover, we also establish that $ν_2(n)\gg n^{43/40}(\log n)^{-7}$ holds for every sufficiently large integer $n$ subject to $n\equiv1\pmod2$. These results improve and enhance the earlier work of Andrade [1] and Wang-Tian [17], respectively.

papers.title: The optimal information complexity of VC learning
papers.abstract: Steinke and Zakynthinou(2020) introduces the Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) framework of analyzing the information complexity of learning algorithms based on algorithm-dependent information-theoretic quantities. We study one of these quantities, the evaluated Conditional Mutual Information (eCMI). It has been an interesting question whether the optimal PAC guarantee for VC classes can be recovered from the algorithm-dependent analyses via CMI. And we show that it is possible to recover this guarantee by constructing a learning algorithm whose eCMI is of order O(d) in the realizable case, where d is the VC-dimension of the concept class. Specially, our algorithm is a randomized Majority-of-5 base learners with optimal in-expectation generalization guarantee.

papers.title: Nonlinear lower-tail large deviations at criticality
papers.abstract: We introduce general methods to derive lower tail large deviation principles, for a variety of nonlinear problems of combinatorial interest. These methods are especially effective in "critical" regimes, where the nonlinearities are not sparse enough for Poissonian lower tails (e.g., Janson's inequality does not provide a sharp tail bound), but the situation is not so dense that combinatorial effects dominate (e.g., we cannot directly apply the theory of hypergraph containers or the relative entropy framework of Kozma-Samotij). In particular, these are regimes where one expects interesting phase transitions to occur. Our results have a number of consequences related to subgraphs in random graphs, answering various questions of Warnke and Jenssen-Perkins-Potukuchi-Simkin. For example, consider a random graph $G\sim \mathbb G(n,p)$, and let $L_\triangle(n,p)=\log\Pr[G\text{ is triangle-free}]$. The first-order asymptotics of $L_\triangle(n,p)$ have long been known in all parameter ranges except the critical regime where $p$ has order of magnitude $1/\sqrt n$. We are able to fill this gap: for any fixed $c>0$, we show that $n^{-3/2}L_\triangle(n,c/\sqrt n)$ converges to a limit expressed in terms of a two-parameter variational problem, which has a single phase transition at $c\approx 4.341$. In contrast, we show that there is no such phase transition for the probability that $G$ is $C_{2\ell}$-free, for any fixed even cycle $C_{2\ell}$. We also obtain some applications in combinatorial design theory. Addressing conjectures of Glock-Kühn-Lo-Osthus, Kelly, and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney-Simkin, we obtain new estimates on the number of order-$n$ Steiner triple systems with no Pasch configuration and the number of order-$n$ Latin squares with no $2\times 2$ Latin subsquare (both tight up to a factor of $\exp(o(n^2))$).

papers.title: Distributed Learning of $α$-Potential Functions in Strategic Multi-agent Systems
papers.abstract: We study the problem of computing the tightest \(α\)-potential approximation of a general-sum game over continuous action spaces, within a prescribed class of potential functions and when each player has access only to its own utility function. The difficulty is twofold: the approximation error involves a worst-case search over an infinite set of unilateral deviations, and the required utility information is distributed across players. For a linear-in-parameters potential class, we use an exact finite-tuple reformulation that separates the problem into a global outer search over deviation tuples and distributed convex inner problems. We develop a primal--dual inner oracle tailored to this structure and establish a uniform one-sided accuracy guarantee. This oracle can be combined with global outer search to obtain an end-to-end guarantee on the outer optimization error. We also develop a projected zeroth-order outer method as a computationally lighter alternative for higher-dimensional problems. Numerical experiments illustrate the accuracy--computation tradeoff between the two outer-search methods and show that the proposed optimization framework can improve upon analytical \(α\)-potential constructions.

papers.title: Arbitrary Stage Spectra for Raikov Remainders Along Quotient Towers
papers.abstract: Let $θ$ be an ordinal and let $(N_α)_{α\leqθ}$ be a continuous increasing tower of closed normal subgroups of a Hausdorff topological group $G$, with $N_0=\{e\}$. Write $ρG$ for the Raikov completion of $G$, and put $K_α=\overline{N_α}^{ρG}$ and $H_α=GK_α$. The successive and limit differences of the groups $H_α$ mark the first stages at which points of $ρG$ become old quotient points. For every nonzero ordinal $θ$ and every set $S\subseteq(0,θ]$, there is a Hausdorff pseudocompact Boolean group with a continuous tower of closed normal subgroups such that every member of the tower is pseudocompact and the nonempty strata occur exactly at the stages in $S$. The terminal quotient can simultaneously be chosen isomorphic to $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, and for every $δ<θ$ the successive factor $N_{δ+1}/N_δ$ is compact exactly when $δ+1\notin S$. Thus a tower may have a single nonempty stratum at a limit stage even when every successive factor is compact. For a closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$, let $\widehat q:ρG\toρ(G/N)$ extend the quotient homomorphism and put $K=\overline N^{ρG}$. Over $gN\in G/N$, the fiber in $ρG\setminus G$ is $g(K\setminus N)$, homeomorphic to $ρN\setminus N$, while for $y\in\widehat q(ρG)\setminus(G/N)$ the entire $\widehat q$-fiber lies in $ρG\setminus G$ and is homeomorphic to $ρN$. For precompact kernels this gives a canonical decomposition, and nested quotients give the two-stage identity underlying the transfinite filtration. Further results concern pseudocompact Raikov remainders and include countable Abelian examples.

papers.title: Second-order Wasserstein response for Lévy laws
papers.abstract: Moving an atom and splitting it symmetrically can give the same weak change in a Lévy characteristic, yet produce Wasserstein errors of different orders. We explain this through first- and second-order expansions of the distribution function for infinitely divisible laws with a Gaussian factor. The expansions are uniform over Lipschitz tests and include distributional directions from moving atoms. When the first response is nonzero, analyticity gives the signed second coefficient of the Wasserstein--1 distance. When it vanishes, a finite second displacement moment gives a quadratic response, with a positive coefficient whenever the dispersion is nonzero. For local balanced remeshing, we prove matching bounds in terms of grid-alignment variance and construct a linear program with a controlled optimization gap. We also determine the sharp transition as Gaussian smoothing vanishes. The appendices give proofs, metric speed and length, and multivariate and state-dependent extensions.

papers.title: Conditional Fluctuations of Mean-Field Systems with Stable Common Noise
papers.abstract: We study conditional fluctuations of smooth mean-field systems on a torus with symmetric stable common jumps of index $0<α<1$. A positive-strip estimate makes empirical Poisson acceptance errors negligible at the sampling scale. Given the full Poisson master, the conditional laws converge in probability to a centered Gaussian kernel in a negative Sobolev path space. In dimension one, quantile coupling preserves this limit for microscopic marks with relative tail remainder $O(x^{-ρ})$, where $ρ>\tfracα{2}$. A second-order tail expansion identifies the response when this condition fails: it shifts the conditional Gaussian mean at criticality and, when nonzero, dominates sampling below criticality. We also identify the transition from a stable to a Brownian rank error. In a translation model, rank and clock couplings give the same microscopic laws but different path fluctuations. Rank coupling gives a functional Gaussian limit. Clock coupling admits no diverging additive path normalization at the limiting center.

papers.title: On the quadratic length of plane Cremona maps of degree 4
papers.abstract: Every non-linear plane Cremona map can be decomposed into quadratic maps, and the minimum number of quadratic maps required is called its quadratic length. It is known that plane Cremona maps of degree 3 have quadratic length either 2 or 3. In this paper, we study the quadratic length of plane Cremona maps $\varphi$ of degree 4. Recall that either $\varphi$ is de Jonquières, i.e. it has a base point of multiplicity 3, or it is not de Jonquières. In the latter case, $\varphi$ has quadratic length 2, whereas in the former case we prove that $\varphi$ has quadratic length 3, 4, or 5, and we classify those maps that reach the upper bound.

papers.title: On the hit problem of rank five
papers.abstract: Let $P_q$ be the graded polynomial algebra $\mathbb F_2[x_1,x_2,\ldots ,x_q]$ over the prime field of two elements, $\mathbb F_2$, with the degree of each $x_i$ being 1. We study the {\it hit Peterson problem} of finding a minimal set of generators for $P_q$ as a module over the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra, $\mathcal{A}.$ In this note, we present the minimal sets of $\mathcal{A}$-generators for $P_5$ in the cases where the degree are sufficiently general.

papers.title: A Log-Star Comparison Between Expectation Threshold and Fractional Expectation Threshold
papers.abstract: We proved a log-star comparison between the expectation threshold $q(\mathcal F)$ and the fractional expectation threshold $q_f(\mathcal F)$ for any nontrivial increasing family $\mathcal F$ on a finite ground set $V$ of size $|V|=N$. Specifically, we show that $$q_f(\mathcal F)\le64\log_2^*(N+2)\,q(\mathcal F),$$ where $\log_2^* x$ is the iterated logarithm of base-2. Using similiar methods, one can extend this result to the following stronger form: there exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that \[ q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(l(\mathcal F)),\quad q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)), \] where $l(\mathcal F):=\max\{2,\max_{S\in\min\mathcal F}|S|\}$ and $\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)$ denotes the VC-dimension of $\min\mathcal F$. On October 7, 2026, OpenAI released a result proving the equivalence of fractional and integral thresholds, which supersedes the findings in this note. The authors are keeping this note for historical reference.

papers.title: Anchored Extra-Proximal Methods: Optimal Higher-Order Methods for Monotone Inclusion Problems
papers.abstract: We characterize, up to logarithmic factors, the optimal higher-order oracle complexity of finding approximate solutions to composite monotone inclusion problems, formed by the sum of a smooth single-valued monotone operator and a maximal monotone set-valued operator. We introduce the Anchored Extra-Proximal (AEP) framework, which combines an anchored extrapolation step with an inexact anchored proximal update satisfying a relative-error condition. This framework recovers the composite Fast Extragradient method in the first-order setting and yields natural higher-order extensions through Taylor approximations of the smooth operator at the extrapolated point. For every $p\geq 2$, assuming that the $(p-1)$th derivative of the single-valued operator is $L_p$-Lipschitz continuous and the initial distance to a solution is at most $R$, we combine AEP with a bisection line search to obtain a $p$th-order method that attains a tangent residual of at most $\varepsilon$ in $\widetilde{O}((L_p R^{p}/\varepsilon)^{\frac{2}{3p-1}})$ oracle calls. We complement this result with a worst-case lower bound of $Ω((L_p R^p/\varepsilon)^{\frac{2}{3p-1}})$ for every deterministic algorithm in the $p$th-order oracle model, without imposing any prescribed update structure. For the subclass of smooth nonexpansive fixed-point problems, we further establish a lower bound of $Ω(\min\{R/\varepsilon, {(L_p R^{p}/\varepsilon)}^{\frac{2}{3p-1}}\})$. By choosing between AEP and Halpern iteration, we match this lower bound up to logarithmic factors, thereby also settling the deterministic oracle complexity of smooth nonexpansive fixed-point problems.

papers.title: On the $W^{2,p}$ solvability for mixed boundary value problems
papers.abstract: We establish global $W^{2,p}$ solvability for the Poisson equation with mixed Dirichlet--Neumann boundary conditions in two classes of domains in all dimensions $n\geq 2$. For $C^{1,α}$ domains with a Reifenbeg flat interface, we obtain the optimal range $1<p<4/3$, provided that $α>1-1/p$. For Lipschitz polyhedra with facewise boundary decompositions, we obtain solvability for $p$ close to $1$. In both settings, we establish endpoint $W^{2,1}$ solvability for data in an adapted atomic Hardy space. Applications of the methods to Lamé systems are also discussed.

papers.title: Localization Lengths for Two-Dimensional Random Band Matrices: Exponential Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: We consider $N \times N$ random band matrices $H = (H_{xy})$ with centered complex Gaussian entries, indexed by points $x,y$ on the two-dimensional discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z} / \sqrt{N} \mathbb{Z})^2$. The matrix entries $H_{xy}$ vanish whenever the distance between $x$ and $y$ exceeds a constant multiple of the bandwidth parameter $W$. We prove that, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, if $W\geq(\log N)^{1+\varepsilon}$, then all bulk eigenvectors are delocalized with high probability. Equivalently, this yields a lower bound of order $\exp(W^{1-\varepsilon})$ on the localization length of two-dimensional random band matrices for arbitrarily small constant $\varepsilon>0$, improving the superpolynomial lower bound $W^C$ for every fixed constant $C>0$ established in arXiv:2503.07606. A key ingredient of our proof is a new strategy that closes the resolvent flow analysis using only loop observables of order at most two, without relying on the higher-order loop hierarchy.

papers.title: A global stochastic maximum principle for forward-backward stochastic control systems with quadratic convex generator and unbounded terminal condition
papers.abstract: We establish a global stochastic maximum principle for forward-backward stochastic control systems with an unbounded terminal condition and a generator that has quadratic growth and is convex in $Z$. The control domain need not be convex, and the diffusion coefficient may depend on the control. In this setting, the BMO martingale estimates used for quadratic BSDEs with bounded terminal conditions are no longer directly available. To overcome this difficulty, we work under an equivalent probability measure associated with the optimal trajectory and establish the estimates needed for the variational analysis. In particular, using a representation formula for convex quadratic BSDEs with conditional estimates, we derive estimates for the backward-state perturbations under this fixed measure. These estimates allow us to justify a second-order expansion of the cost functional and obtain the global stochastic maximum principle.

papers.title: Locally Closed Prime Ideals and Isotropy Induction in Kumjian--Pask Algebras over Commutative Rings
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative unital ring and let $Γ$ be a row-finite, strongly aperiodic higher-rank graph with no sources and a nonempty finite vertex set. We determine the prime ideals that occur as annihilators of modules induced from simple isotropy modules. They are parametrised by maximal tails of $Γ$ and prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ for which the fraction field of $R/\mathfrak p$ is obtained by inverting a single element. Under the product description of the prime spectrum, these are precisely its locally closed points. The realisation argument uses a dense periodic orbit in every finite maximal-tail quotient. We also construct an explicit faithful simple module for the Leavitt algebra $L_R(1,2)$ whenever $R$ is a Goldman domain. Consequently, $L_{k[t]_{(t)}}(1,2)$ is primitive although its coefficient ring is not a field. In this example the zero ideal is locally closed but not completely irreducible. We obtain full prime-to-primitive coincidence for coefficient rings with finite spectrum and for semilocal rings of Krull dimension at most one, and transfer the results to split pullback Kumjian--Pask algebras. For pullbacks over an uncountable field, the full primitive spectrum is described without assuming algebraic closedness.

papers.title: Propagation failure in heterogeneous FitzHugh--Nagumo systems via coupled upper and lower solutions
papers.abstract: Traveling waves are fundamental objects in reaction--diffusion systems; however, spatial heterogeneities can distort or inhibit their propagation. Determining whether a given heterogeneity results in propagation failure remains challenging, particularly in systems with coupled components. In this paper, we present explicit constructions of stationary coupled upper and lower solutions tailored to specific heterogeneities for a one-dimensional FitzHugh--Nagumo system. By leveraging the mixed quasimonotone structure of the system, these barriers yield sufficient conditions for the failure of propagation for families of trapped initial conditions. The stationary constructions establish directional signal blocking in FitzHugh--Nagumo neuron models with localized reaction heterogeneities, including light-gated ionic conductances, and with abrupt geometric variations; the resulting stationary barriers persist for sufficiently small recovery diffusion. Additionally, we introduce explicit almost stationary barriers, which provide conditional bounds on the expansion of componentwise threshold regions in homogeneous media.

papers.title: A note on the diameter of graphs of two-dimensional simplex codes
papers.abstract: Let $\Gs(2,q)$ denote the graph induced in the Grassmann graph by the $q$-ary simplex codes of dimension $2$. We determine its diameter for every prime power $q$. The cases $q=2,3$ are elementary, while the diameter for $q=4$ follows from a known description of the distance relation. We prove that the diameter equals $3$ for every $q\ge5$, so that it is $0$ for $q=2$, $2$ for $q=3$, and $3$ for all $q\ge4$. The proof uses the realization of two-dimensional simplex codes as projective lines and a ratio criterion for collinearity of simplex points. A consequence of a theorem of Marshall Hall on finite abelian groups yields a bridge lemma and gives the uniform upper bound $3$. To obtain the matching lower bound for $q\ge5$, we construct an explicit diagonal pair of simplex lines and rule out a common neighbor by two independent arguments, one based on moments and the other on products. For $q\ge7$, we also give an independent counting proof. The case $q=4$ is treated separately. In particular, for $q\ge4$ the simplex-code graph is not isometrically embedded in the ambient Grassmann graph.

papers.title: A Complex Structure on A Rational Homology Six-Sphere with Two-Torsion
papers.abstract: We construct a compact, smooth, simply connected complex threefold. Its second and third integral homology groups are cyclic of order two, and its remaining homology groups agree with those of the six-sphere.

papers.title: Minimax-Optimal Early Stopping for SGD via the Discrepancy Principle
papers.abstract: We study early stopping for stochastic gradient descent with a constant step size applied to noisy linear inverse problems with polynomially decaying spectrum. The iteration is stopped by the discrepancy principle, that is, as soon as its residual reaches the prescribed noise level. For Hölder source conditions below a saturation level determined by the polynomial decay, we prove that the mean-square reconstruction error at the stopping index is bounded by the classical rate, up to an explicit factor involving the step size and the incoherence of the design, and that the expected number of iterations is of the order of the oracle stopping index. The rate is minimax-optimal for deterministic noise whenever the spectrum contains an eigenvalue at the oracle scale and this factor stays bounded. The step size is restricted by a spectrum-weighted incoherence condition. The analysis allows rank-deficient designs and inconsistent observations.

papers.title: Distributed Linear Programming on GPU Clusters at Extreme Scale
papers.abstract: Large linear programs can exceed the memory of a single compute node. Although first-order methods replace sparse factorizations with GPU-suited matrix-vector products, other solver phases can reintroduce a single-node memory limit. We present SHARDLP, a distributed GPU LP solver that keeps the matrix and primal-dual state partitioned from sharded input through solution output. On the Google PDLP benchmark, SHARDLP solves ten of eleven instances, compared with eight in the published CPU PDLP study. On the largest benchmark, eight H200 GPUs solve a 1.185-billion-variable, 6.338-billion-nonzero LP in 9.9 minutes; the published CPU experiment reports 21.06 hours on different hardware. Beyond this benchmark, separately checked multi-node solves reach up to 13.604 billion variables and 40.807 billion nonzeros, while validated executions span up to 76 GPUs across 29 compute nodes. For column-partitioned solves, support-aware communication skips GPUs that store no coefficients for a row; on an LP with 2.76 billion nonzeros, it cuts modelled communication by 92.97% and improves solver time by 1.27x-1.52x. The code for SHARDLP is available at https://github.com/ArnaudDeza/ShardLP.

papers.title: Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the Möbius-Invariant Willmore Flow
papers.abstract: We prove uniqueness of finite-time geometric endpoints for the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in $\mathbb{S}^3$ under uniform quantitative nonumbilicity. The multiplicity-counting varifolds converge, without reparametrization or Möbius renormalization, to a unique integral two-varifold. An intrinsic transport estimate gives quantitative total-variation convergence of the induced area measures on the fixed domain and bounded-Lipschitz Cauchy control of their pushforwards. Together with Allard compactness and rectifiability, this upgrades subsequential compactness to full-trajectory varifold convergence. The limit has generalized Euclidean mean curvature in $L^2$ with the natural endpoint lower-semicontinuity bound. For finite maximal trajectories with initial energy at most $8π$, Jakob's subsequential alternative becomes sequence independent: the limit is zero, or it has unit density and embedded Lipschitz support of genus zero or one. For Hopf-torus trajectories under the same energy bound, nonumbilicity is automatic and the anchored constant-speed profiles converge weakly in $W^{2,2}$ and strongly in $W^{1,2}$ and $C^{1,α}$ for every $α<\frac{1}{2}$. At infinite time, the same method yields a unique limit under an additional finite-dissipation-length condition.

papers.title: On smooth affine surfaces with the cohomology of a smooth curve
papers.abstract: We prove that if a smooth affine complex surface has the same integral mixed Hodge structure as a smooth curve whose compactification is of positive genus, then it admits a smooth morphism to the curve with fibers isomorphic to $\mathbb{A}^1$. In particular, every such surface is the total space of a torsor for a line bundle on the curve. The motivation comes from Jouanolou's trick, to which this result gives a kind of converse in dimension $2$. We also give an example in the case of $\mathbb{P}^1$ which has the same integral mixed Hodge structure as $\mathbb{P}^1$ and simply connected but does not admit a smooth $\mathbb{A}^1$ fibration over $\mathbb{P}^1$.

papers.title: Bounded Harmonic Functions on Products with a Parabolic Factor
papers.abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a connected complete parabolic Riemannian manifold and $N$ is a connected complete stochastically complete Riemannian manifold, then every bounded harmonic function on $M\times N$ is independent of the $M$-variable. Equivalently, pullback by the second projection induces an isometric isomorphism from the space of bounded harmonic functions on $N$ onto that on $M\times N$. In particular, the product of two parabolic manifolds has the bounded Liouville property, thereby answering Problem~16 of Grigor'yan's survey in the affirmative. The key analytic input is a total-variation memory-loss property of the heat kernel on a parabolic manifold. We establish this property by showing that the time-one heat kernel defines an aperiodic Harris recurrent transition kernel and then applying the row-merging theorem of Jamison and Orey.

papers.title: Critical-point-free energy for fractional-Toledo representations
papers.abstract: Let $S_g$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\ge2$. For a reductive representation $ρ:π_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$, let $E_ρ$ be the energy function on Teichmüller space associated to equivariant harmonic maps into $\mathrm{CH}^2$. For every positive integer $d$ with $3\nmid d$, all sufficiently large $h$, and every $g>h$, we construct an irreducible reductive representation \[ ρ_{g,h,d}:π_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1) \] with \[ τ(ρ_{g,h,d})=2h-2-\frac{2d}{3}\notin\mathbb Z, \qquad \mathrm{Crit}(E_{ρ_{g,h,d}})=\varnothing. \] Consequently, the associated branched-minimal-surface forgetful map is not surjective in these nonintegral Toledo components.

papers.title: Sidon sets with $Δ$-separated sumsets in additive number theory
papers.abstract: The set $A$ is a $B_h$-set if every element of the sumset $hA$ has a unique representation as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. A $B_2$-set is also called a Sidon set. A $B_{h,Δ}$-set is a $B_h$-set $A$ whose sumset $hA$ is $Δ$-separated, that is, $|x-x'| \geq Δ$ for all $x,x' \in hA$ with $x\neq x'$. Upper and lower bounds are obtained for the cardinality of the largest $B_{2,Δ}$-sets contained in $\{1,2,\ldots, n\}$, that is, sets $A \subseteq \{1,2,\ldots, n\}$ such that, if $a,b,c,d \in A$ and $\{a,b\} \neq \{c,d\}$, then $|(a+b)-(c+d)| \geq Δ$.

papers.title: Quadratic Stiff Damping and Full-Step Asymptotic Preservation in a Two-Stage Fourth-Order Finite-Volume Method for Cattaneo Relaxation
papers.abstract: We couple a previously analyzed L-stable sequential two-stage fourth-order time formula to a specified fifth-order finite-volume residual for the periodic Goldstein--Taylor/Cattaneo equation in one and two dimensions. The required second time derivative is chosen as the exact derivative along the semi-discrete trajectory, $\mathcal G_h(U)=D\mathcal L_h(U)\mathcal L_h(U)$. For our linear reconstruction and flux, applying the same conservative face operator to $V=\mathcal L_h(U)$ yields this derivative exactly. A central face flux produces a skew-adjoint divergence--gradient pair, allowing a fixed-grid full-step asymptotic-preserving (AP) theorem for the implemented operator; for the specified central-flux discrete heat target, a wave-speed Rusanov flux has the same derivative closure but fails that target. This statement is not a claim about Rusanov-type discretizations in general. Within the previously established L-stable parameter interval, $C_q=5/183$ is the unique fixed coefficient within the admissible family, in the sense of the asymptotic damping exponent, that cancels the leading inverse-stiffness amplification, giving $R(-x)=O(x^{-2})$ rather than the generic $O(x^{-1})$ as $x=Δt/δ\to\infty$. Independent high-precision scalar calculations and the actual two-dimensional finite-volume transverse mode verify the exponent up to $x=10^5$; a mixed slow--fast state shows the resulting flux-error advantage for specified data. This damping statement does not optimize finite-stiffness accuracy or computational efficiency. The AP statements below concern the fixed-grid linear periodic problem with exact stage solutions; no mesh-uniform or nonlinear AP result is claimed.

papers.title: Toward a Unified Statistical Theory of Multi-View Pretraining for Neural Knowledge Graph Learning
papers.abstract: Knowledge graph learning offers a powerful framework for representing and inferring structured knowledge, with broad practical applications. Two obstacles limit current methods: labeled triples are scarce for each entity and relation, which makes expressive models hard to train, and scoring functions are designed ad hoc, which limits their generalizability and leaves them without theoretical grounding. We address both obstacles with a theoretically grounded framework, with end-to-end guarantees, that extends and subsumes existing methods. The framework proceeds in two stages: multi-view unsupervised pretraining that integrates heterogeneous sources of entity side information into a shared representation, followed by supervised learning across multiple relation types. We establish a unified nonasymptotic risk bound that combines the subspace recovery error of pretraining and the sample complexity of the labeled data in a single guarantee, quantifying formally how large-scale unlabeled data from multiple views benefits downstream knowledge prediction. Synthetic experiments validate each component of the theory, and experiments on large-scale real-world knowledge graph benchmarks confirm the effectiveness of our approach.

papers.title: On a twisted Singer conjecture
papers.abstract: According to the Singer conjecture, the $L^2$-Betti numbers of a closed aspherical manifold are expected to vanish outside the middle dimension. In this paper, we study a natural analog of the Singer conjecture concerning the vanishing of twisted $L^2$-Betti numbers outside the lower middle dimension. These invariants can be thought of as $L^2$-Betti numbers of an infinite cyclic cover, depending on a first cohomology class. This is related to a previous conjecture by the author, which connects the twisted $L^2$-Euler characteristic to the Thurston norm, and which we prove for a class of closed arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds.

papers.title: Triple arrays from ovals in finite projective planes
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that whenever a projective plane of odd order n contains an oval, it may be used to construct a triple array with n + 1 rows, n.n columns and n(n + 1) symbols. In particular, for any odd prime power s, we use the projective plane over the field of order s to construct an explicitly given (s + 1) times s.s triple array on s(s + 1) symbols. This is only the third infinite series of triple arrays (up to transposition) to be found. Our construction proves a recent conjecture of Gordeev and Ohman (2025) in the case of odd prime powers.

papers.title: Uniform $L^{\infty}$-Boundedness and Upper Semicontinuity of Global Attractors for Reaction--Diffusion Equations with Neumann Boundary Conditions on Uniform Jones Domains
papers.abstract: We consider a family of semilinear parabolic equations with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions on a family of varying non-smooth domains $\{Ω_μ\}_{μ\in Λ} \subset \mathbb{R}^n $. Assuming only that the domains have uniformly bounded volumes, bounded away from zero, and satisfy a uniform Jones condition, together with the usual structural requirements on the linear and nonlinear terms, we establish the well-posedness of the problem in an appropriate scale of fractional Banach spaces and prove the existence of global attractors. The attractors themselves are shown to be uniformly bounded in $L^{\infty}(Ω_μ)$ by an elementary truncation argument, which uses no property of the domains beyond the weak formulation of the Neumann condition. A Moser--Alikakos bootstrap iteration, in conjunction with the uniform Gronwall lemma and the uniform properties of the Jones extension operator, then yields the stronger statement that bounded sets of $L^{q}(Ω_μ)$ are absorbed, in finite time and uniformly in $μ$, into a fixed ball of $L^{\infty}(Ω_μ)$; this iteration uses only first-order Sobolev embeddings, which is what makes it available on domains where the domain of the elliptic operator is not contained in $H^{2}$. Finally, assuming the volume convergence of the domains, $|Ω_μ\triangle Ω_0| \to 0$, we construct a framework of connecting maps, show that the uniform Jones condition upgrades this convergence in measure to Mosco convergence of the associated bilinear forms, and prove that the family of attractors is upper semicontinuous at $μ= 0$ in $L^2(Ω_μ)$ and hence, by interpolation, in $H^s(Ω_μ)$ for every $s<1$.

papers.title: A polynomial criterion for DP-coloring of uncrowded hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We prove a color-degree criterion for DP-coloring of finite uncrowded hypergraphs of bounded rank. For a $q$-fold cover with edge sizes between $2$ and $r+1$, let $D_\ell$ be the maximum number of forbidden colorings on $(\ell+1)$-edges prescribing a fixed color at a fixed vertex. If $q$ is sufficiently large in terms of $r$, then the cover admits a coloring whenever \[ \sum_{\ell=1}^r\frac{D_\ell}{q^\ell}\leq\log q-20\log\log q. \] For uncrowded $(r+1)$-uniform hypergraphs of maximum degree $Δ$, this gives a DP-chromatic number at most $(1+O_r(\log\logΔ/\logΔ))(rΔ/\logΔ)^{1/r}$.

papers.title: On the Harborth Conjecture. Part I. Quadrilaterals
papers.abstract: Harborth conjecture states that every planar graph has a crossing-free straight-line drawing in which every edge has an integer length. Kleber's strengthening asks for the vertices themselves to have integer coordinates. In this series of papers, we make progress towards settling these conjectures. Kleber's conjecture reduces to local rational-distance statements for special polygons with at most five vertices. The triangle case is known from the results of Almering and Berry. In this paper, we prove the existence of a rational-distance point on an interior integer diagonal in all the cases for non-degenerate and degenerate quadrilaterals. In the upcoming papers, we focus on non-degenerate and degenerate pentagons.

papers.title: Preference-Based Reward Learning under Partial Observability with Inexact Dynamics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study how partial observability and inexact latent-state inference affect reward learning from preferences. To that end, we study preference-based reward learning under partial observability, where the learner forms latent-state estimates using an inexact learned POMDP model, so model error can accumulate over time. For finite log-linear POMDPs, we characterize this error term by establishing the stability of the belief filter to parametric model error under certain mixing conditions, yielding bounds on the belief mismatch in expectation and in high probability. We further extend this stability mechanism beyond the log-linear setting to neural-softmax POMDP models with overparameterized neural networks. We then propagate these errors into trajectory-level feature perturbations and derive finite-sample guarantees for constrained Bradley-Terry reward estimation from preferences. Our results decouple statistical error from an irreducible model-mismatch bias, and clarify when preference-based reward learning remains feasible under partial observability with imperfect dynamics.

papers.title: Generalized Sobolev-Orlicz spaces based on the Riesz fractional gradient as interpolation and potential spaces
papers.abstract: In this work we establish that the recently introduced fractional Sobolev spaces based on the Riesz fractional gradient of Musielak-Orlicz functions by one of the authors, coincide with the space of Bessel potentials of functions on such generalized Orlicz setting. Moreover, we identify them as complex interpolation spaces, and exploiting the well known properties for interpolation of operators we obtain several structural properties for those spaces.

papers.title: Hausdorff operators and fractional Hausdorff operators in the Dunkl setting
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the boundedness properties of the Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator on generalized Dunkl-type Morrey spaces and generalized Dunkl-type Campanato spaces. Furthermore, we introduce the fractional Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator and study its boundedness from $L^p(\mathbb{R}, dμ_α)$ to $L^q(\mathbb{R}, dμ_α)$. We also establish the boundedness of the fractional Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator on generalized Dunkl-type Morrey spaces under suitable conditions. As a consequence of our main results, we derive several applications. Finally, we evaluate the exact norm of the Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator on Dunkl-type Morrey spaces and Dunkl-type Campanato spaces.

papers.title: Discrete Coplanarity Rigidity and Local Mahler Volume Growth Near the Cube
papers.abstract: We study the finite-dimensional isovertex radial stratum of the cube, P(c)=conv{(1+c_q)q : q in Q_n={+/-1}^n}, with c(-q)=c(q), and establish quantitative rigidity and volume-product estimates for n>=3. The first main result identifies the kernel of the linearized facet-coplanarity operator R_n with the homothety direction span{1} and proves that the coplanarity defect is locally equivalent to both the transverse amplitude dist_infty(c,span{1}) and the distance d_GL(P(c),C_n) to the GL(n)-orbit of the cube. After normalizing out the homothety mode onto 1^perp, a key step is a second-order comparison between the linearized vertex-displacement seminorm and its optimization over small linear transformations. The second main result converts transverse radial perturbations c in 1^perp into a linear volume increment. A facetwise concave-envelope construction and an associated pocket functional yield the explicit primal lower bound vol(P(c))-2^n >= 8/(3(n-1))||c||_infty - O(||c||_infty^2) on 1^perp. Combining this with a chamber-independent first-order expansion of the polar volume (whose linear part vanishes on 1^perp with a uniform quadratic remainder) gives a linear lower bound for the Mahler product V_M(P(c))-V_M(C_n) in terms of d_GL(P(c),C_n). In dimension three, an exact chamber analysis on 1^perp yields vol(P(c))=8+(8/3)||c||_infty+O(||c||_infty^2), and the Mahler product has one-sided directional derivative (32/9)||u||_infty along every nonzero ray in 1^perp. In dimension four, a symmetry-orbit classification of the seventy balanced Boolean directions yields six combinatorial types and explicit first-order pocket bounds. We also distinguish the frozen-combinatorics KKT balance from geometric stationarity.

papers.title: Maximum Utility Split Method for Utility Preference Elicitation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a new approach, called maximum utility split (MUS) scheme, which is built on random utility split (RUS) scheme but with a notable difference: one lottery is designed with two fixed outcomes but with varying probability, and the other has a deterministic outcome specifically chosen at the point where the range between the largest and smallest possible utility values is maximized. Consequently, the probability of random lottery is set such that the range of the ambiguity set of utility functions is reduced by half at the point. Under moderate conditions, we show that MUS can successively generate a sequence of such questionnaires and effectively reduce the ambiguity set, eventually converging to the true utility function as the number of questionnaires increases. The main challenge is to effectively identify the point with the largest utility range for a given ambiguity set constructed from preference information. Based on the structure of the ambiguity set, we propose an interval-based algorithm which identifies each certain-outcome lottery by solving a sequence of linear programs. Moreover, to deal with the case where elicitation terminates before the ambiguity set reduces to a singleton, we demonstrate how to figure out a nominal utility function by solving optimization programs. These identify the smallest and largest utility functions under the Kantorovich metric within the ambiguity set, after which we identify a nominal utility function located in the middle of them. Finally, numerical results demonstrate the efficiency of the MUS method and the performance of a robo-advisor system based on MUS-type queries and the nominal utility elicitation. While the main discussions focus on concave utility functions, we also demonstrate how the MUS approach can be extended to accommodate general non-concave utility functions, particularly S-shaped ones.

papers.title: Express Language Modeling
papers.abstract: We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.

papers.title: Proper efficiency results in vector optimisation in real linear-topological spaces based on vectorial penalisation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we are dealing with constrained vector optimisation problems where the objective function acts between real linear-topological spaces. Our aim is to study the relationships between the sets of properly efficient solutions to constrained and unconstrained vector optimisation problems under certain cone convexity assumptions on the objective function using a vectorial penalisation approach.

papers.title: Attention as In-Context Empirical Bayes: A Two-Stage View via Particle Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study minimal attention-only transformers under all-token corruption and show they admit a two-stage empirical Bayes interpretation. A single attention step computes a kernel-weighted posterior mean with respect to the empirical distribution defined by the context. Depth refines this distribution through particle dynamics (Stage 1), while a long-range skip-connection carries the noisy input as a query for posterior inference (Stage 2), revealing distinct statistical roles for depth and attention residuals. The framework isolates a minimal setting in which the context itself induces a depth-dependent energy landscape governing in-context inference. We show that effective denoising can emerge without an explicit noise schedule: a fixed kernel bandwidth and finite integration horizon suffice, yielding a principled depth-noise relationship. We further establish a posterior-mean recovery guarantee for Gaussian priors, showing the empirical estimator converges to the Bayes-optimal predictor under sequential asymptotic conditions. Connecting these dynamics to reverse-diffusion limits, our results provide a statistical interpretation of attention as in-context inference via sample-based posterior estimation, without explicit density modeling.

papers.title: Online Learning on Hidden-Convex Losses via Algorithmic Equivalence: Optimal Regret, Geometric Barrier, and Bandit Feedback
papers.abstract: We study adversarial online learning with hidden-convex losses, i.e., nonconvex losses that become convex after a nonlinear reparameterization. Ghai, Lu and Hazan (2022) proved that, under geometric and smoothness assumptions, online gradient descent (OGD) on such nonconvex losses approximately simulates online mirror descent (OMD) on the underlying convex losses with a suitable regularizer, yielding $\mathcal{O}(T^{2/3})$ regret. They left open whether the optimal $Θ(\sqrt{T})$ regret from online convex optimization can be recovered in this hidden-convex setting. We answer this question affirmatively. More specifically, via a sharper discrete-time algorithmic equivalence argument, we prove that OGD achieves $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T})$ regret under the same assumptions, matching the optimal worst-case rate for adversarial online convex optimization. We also address another open question of Ghai, Lu and Hazan (2022) by clarifying the geometry required for this algorithmic equivalence. We replace the diagonal-Jacobian sufficient condition with a necessary-and-sufficient Hessian compatibility condition, thereby expanding the class of admissible reparameterizations. We complement our tight regret bound with a lower bound showing that OGD suffers $Ω(T)$ regret even with a stepsize of order $1/\sqrt{T}$, for a smooth Hessian incompatible reparameterization between convex domains and an adversarial sequence of hidden-convex losses. Finally, we extend our analysis to one-point bandit feedback and prove a $\mathcal{O}(T^{3/4})$ expected regret bound for bandit OGD with spherical smoothing, matching its classical rate on convex losses.

papers.title: Solving Linear and Integer Programs Faster Using Data
papers.abstract: We study how much a linear program (LP) or an integer program (IP) can be compressed when solved repeatedly over a fixed feasible region with varying objective coefficients. We provide a framework that compresses LP and IP formulations with guarantees on the probability of preserving optimality, using either an uncertainty set for the cost vector or historical samples. Our framework exposes a tunable tradeoff between compression and the probability of recovering an optimal solution. We characterize the minimum dimension of affine reformulations preserving the full optimizer set over a given cost region and provide sample-based learning algorithms with fast-rate guarantees, without requiring a nondegeneracy assumption for LPs. With high confidence over the training data, the learned reformulation preserves the optimizer set for an independent test cost with probability at least $1-ρ-\widetilde{O}(d^\star_ρ/\hat n)$, where $ρ$ bounds the excluded probability mass, $d^\star_ρ$ is the retained region's decision-relevant dimension, and $\hat n$ is the number retained from $n$ training samples. Existing data-driven approaches to LP and IP reduction do not, to our knowledge, learn a single low-dimensional affine reformulation with a prescribed probability of preserving the full optimizer set. Experimental results show substantial improvements over the compared baselines in accuracy, sample efficiency, and computational speed.

papers.title: Breakeven complexity: A new perspective on neural partial differential equation solvers
papers.abstract: Neural surrogate solvers of partial differential equations (PDEs) promise dramatic speedups over numerical methods, especially in scenarios requiring many solves. However, current accuracy-based evaluations do not fully consider two central issues: (1) neural solvers incur substantial up-front costs for data generation, training, and tuning; and (2) classical solvers can also generate low-fidelity solutions at a sufficiently low simulation cost. To explicitly account for these realities and fully incorporate end-to-end costs, we propose an evaluation framework centered on breakeven complexity, a metric that counts the forward solves before a learned solver is cost-effective relative to an error-equivalent traditional solver. To evaluate this measure, we apply scaling laws to determine how much training budget to allocate to data generation and discuss how to achieve smooth error-matching in diverse settings. We evaluate the breakeven complexity of multiple neural PDE solvers on three PDEs on 2D periodic domains from APEBench and a novel benchmark of flows past multiple obstacles generated by the GPU-native PyFR code. Among other findings, our results suggest that neural PDE solvers become more effective as problems get harder in terms of cost, dimension, rollout, physics regime (e.g. higher Reynolds number), etc.

papers.title: Nearest-Neighbor Radii under Dependent Sampling
papers.abstract: Nearest-neighbor methods are fundamental to classical and modern machine learning, yet their geometric properties are typically analyzed under independent sampling. In this paper, we study the nearest-neighbor radii under dependent sampling. We consider strong mixing dependent observations and ask whether dependence changes the scale of nearest-neighbor neighborhoods. We establish distribution-free almost sure convergence under polynomial mixing and sharp non-asymptotic moment bounds under geometric mixing. The moment bounds depend on the local intrinsic dimension rather than the ambient dimension, making the results applicable to high-dimensional data supported on lower-dimensional manifolds. Synthetic experiments and real-world time-series benchmarks illustrate the theory, showing that nearest-neighbor geometry remains informative under dependent sampling.

papers.title: Parameterized Complexity of Stationarity Testing for Piecewise-Affine Functions and Shallow CNN Losses
papers.abstract: We study the parameterized complexity of testing approximate first-order stationarity at a prescribed point for continuous piecewise-affine (PA) functions, a basic task in nonsmooth optimization. PA functions form a canonical model for nonsmooth stationarity testing and capture the local polyhedral geometry that appears in ReLU-type training losses. Recent work of Tian and So (2025) shows that testing approximate stationarity notions for PA functions is computationally intractable in the worst case, and identifies fixed-dimensional tractability as an open direction. We address this direction from the viewpoint of parameterized complexity, with the ambient dimension $d$ as the parameter. In this paper, we give XP algorithms in fixed dimension for the tractable sides, and prove W[1]-hardness for the complementary sides. Moreover, lower bounds under the parameterized $k$-Clique hypothesis rule out deterministic algorithms running in time $ρ(d)s^{o(d)}$ for any computable function $ρ$, where $s$ denotes the total binary encoding length of the instance. As a further consequence, our results yield the corresponding parameterized complexity picture for testing local minimality of continuous PA functions. We also extend our hardness results to a family of shallow ReLU CNN training losses, tested in the trainable weight space. Thus, the same parameterized-complexity picture also appears for simple CNN training losses. Notably, our lower bounds assume that $k$-Clique on $N$-vertex graphs admits no deterministic $ρ(k)N^{o(k)}$-time algorithm for any computable function $ρ$. The recent refutations of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) (OpenAI, 2026) and the stronger fine-grained $k$-Clique hypothesis (Vassilevska Williams and Zamir, 2026) do not contradict this assumption.

papers.title: Understanding Simulated Annealing: from Weak Poincaré Inequalities to a Discrete Optimal Transport Framework
papers.abstract: Simulated annealing follows a path of distributions from an easy initial law to a target. Standard analyses require rapid mixing at every fixed temperature, which can fail for multimodal targets even when annealing succeeds. Motivated by the continuous optimal-transport analysis of annealed Langevin dynamics by Guo, Tao, and Chen (ICLR 2025), we develop a discrete optimal-transport framework for finite-state annealing. The discrete action of the path integrates the minimum electrical energy needed to route the demand $-\partial_sπ_s$ through the chain's transition capacities. Like a path-dependent inverse conductance, it penalizes a bottleneck only when the path must move mass across it. We also introduce weak action, which leaves an $\varepsilon$ amount of this motion unrouted. Up to initialization error, action $\mathcal A$ gives reverse-KL error at most $\mathcal A/(4T)$ after $T$ expected updates, while weak action gives TV error at most $\varepsilon+\sqrt{\mathcal A^{w}_\varepsilon/(8T)}$. Paralleling canonical paths and Poincaré inequalities, we develop flow and spectral bounds, showing that pathwise (weak) Poincaré inequalities imply (weak) action bounds. We also show that a weak Poincaré inequality yields a genuine one after removing a small amount of mass. As a pathwise analogue of chain decomposition, we obtain a componentwise algorithm for mixtures with phase weights supplied at initialization. Applications include mean-field Ising and Potts models and bipartite spin systems. For every fixed $δ>0$, we give a polynomial-time single-site annealing sampler for uniform independent sets in $(d,D)$-biregular bipartite graphs with $D/d\geq1+δ$ and large $D$. To our knowledge, this is the first polynomial-time sampler requiring only a fixed multiplicative degree imbalance, strictly extending the $D\geq7d\log d$ regime of Cannon and Perkins (SODA 2020).

papers.title: Active Learning for Conditional Generative Compressed Sensing
papers.abstract: Generative compressed sensing uses the range of a pretrained generator as a nonlinear model for recovering structured signals from limited measurements. We study a conditional version of this problem for image recovery from subsampled Fourier measurements using prompt-conditioned generative models. Our framework separates two roles of conditioning: the prompt used to design the sampling distribution and the prompt used to define the recovery model. For ReLU and Lipschitz conditional generators, we prove stable recovery bounds showing that prompt-matched Christoffel sampling retains the same Christoffel complexity constant as existing near-optimal generative compressed sensing theory, while prompt mismatch incurs an explicit compatibility penalty. Experiments with Stable Diffusion show that prompts meaningfully reshape Christoffel sampling distributions and influence image recovery. Overall, our results suggest treating prompts as design variables for sensing, approximation, and recovery, opening new directions for the practical use of conditional generative models in compressed sensing, where conditioning, sampling, and optimization must be considered jointly.

papers.title: On $S$-Noetherian Lattices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we define and study $S$-Noetherian lattices as a natural generalization of Noetherian rings. We prove that a ring $R$ is $S$-Noetherian if and only if its ideal lattice, $Id(R)$, is $S_L$-Noetherian. Furthermore, we establish a Cohen-Kaplansky type theorem for $S$-Noetherian lattices, showing that $L$ is $S$-Noetherian if and only if every $S$-prime element of $L$ is $S$-compact. Finally, we introduce the concept of $S$-primary elements - a generalization of primary elements in multiplicative lattices and demonstrate the existence (when every element of $S$ is meet principal, as is the case for the ideal lattice of a ring) and uniqueness of $S$-primary decomposition in $S$-Noetherian lattices.

papers.title: On the construction of almost periodic solutions for the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation $$ \mathrm{i}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{xx}u-V\ast u+\mathrm{i}\vert u\vert^{2}\partial_{x}u=0 $$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}$, depending on some potential $V$. We prove that for `almost all' potentials $V$, this equation admits an almost-periodic solution.

papers.title: Principal Manifold Estimation with Riemannian Templates
papers.abstract: Principal manifold estimation (PME) has been successfully applied to robotics and neuroimaging. However, the existing PME framework does not directly accommodate manifolds with non-Euclidean topology, and its theoretical foundations remain incomplete. In this article, we develop a complete theoretical framework for PME that summarizes high-dimensional point clouds using low-dimensional manifolds with general, potentially non-Euclidean topology. The choice of topology can be informed by topological data analysis. Drawing on the theory of Sobolev spaces on Riemannian manifolds, we establish that the proposed principal manifolds are well-defined, prove convergence of the iterative algorithm used to compute them, and establish the consistency of the finite-sample estimator. We further provide a Bayesian interpretation of PME that connects the framework to recent developments in Gaussian processes on Riemannian manifolds. Examples illustrate how the proposed PME framework can be applied to existing statistical methods, including manifold-valued regression. Numerical experiments illustrate the proposed methodology, its computational implementation, and its theoretical properties.

papers.title: Maximal regularity for a compressible fluid-structure interaction system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We investigate a fluid-structure interaction system in which the dynamics of the fluid is described by the compressible Navier-Stokes equations, while the elastic structure is modeled by a damped plate equation. The fluid evolves in a three-dimensional bounded domain, with the structure occupies a part of its boundary. Instead of standard no-slip boundary conditions, we consider the Navier-slip boundary conditions at the fluid-structure interface as well as at the fixed boundary. We establish the local-in-time existence and uniqueness of strong solutions within $L^{p}-L^{q}$ framework. The existence result is obtained for small time by decoupling the linearized system and employing a cascade strategy combined with the Second Schauder fixed point theorem, whereas the uniqueness is shown by deriving weak regularity properties for the associated linear coupled operator in a Hilbert space setting. It is the first result addressing strong solutions for a compressible fluid interacting with a damped plate under Navier-slip boundary conditions.

papers.title: Mutation of Theta Functions
papers.abstract: We give an account of mutation of theta functions in cluster scattering diagrams, starting with a notion of mutation that is related to, but different from, the notion of mutation defined by Gross, Hacking, Keel, and Kontsevich.This different approach to mutation leads to several applications. Three of the applications simplify the process of computing structure constants for multiplication of theta functions, and these are used in another paper on cluster scattering diagrams of affine type. Notable in these three applications is the appearance of mutation symmetries and dominance regions. The other two applications have to do with pointed reduced bases, a variation on the pointed bases of Fan Qin. We give a characterization of pointed reduced bases analogous to Qin's characterization of pointed bases. All of these applications take place in a version of Gross, Hacking, Keel, and Kontsevich's canonical algebra that can be constructed for an arbitrary exchange matrix.

papers.title: Analogue of the theta group $Γ_θ,$ II
papers.abstract: In this series of papers, we introduce higher level versions of the theta group $Γ_θ.$ In this paper, we treat the theta group of level $5$, $Γ_{θ,5},$ and construct modular forms on $Γ_{θ,5}$. Moreover we compute their multiplier systems. For this purpose, we derive transformation formula of theta function with characteristics.

papers.title: Maximin Robust Bayesian Experimental Design
papers.abstract: We address the brittleness of Bayesian experimental design under model misspecification by formulating the problem as a max--min game between the experimenter and an adversarial nature subject to information-theoretic constraints. We demonstrate that this approach yields a robust objective governed by Sibson's $α$-mutual information~(MI), which identifies the $α$-tilted posterior as the robust belief update and establishes the Rényi divergence as the appropriate measure of conditional information gain. To mitigate the bias and variance of nested Monte Carlo estimators needed to estimate Sibson's $α$-MI, we adopt a PAC-Bayes framework to search over stochastic design policies, yielding rigorous high-probability lower bounds on the robust expected information gain that explicitly control finite-sample error.

papers.title: Estimating Condition Number with Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a fast method for estimating the condition number of sparse matrices using graph neural networks (GNNs). For efficient deployment of GNNs, we introduce a graph feature construction with $\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{nnz} + n)$ complexity, where $\mathrm{nnz}$ is the number of non-zero elements in the matrix and $n$ denotes the matrix dimension. We propose two schemes for estimating the matrix condition number using GNNs; one follows by decomposing the condition number and predicts the relatively more computationally intensive part $\|\mathbf{A}^{-1}\|$, without explicitly forming the inverse, while the other is to predict the whole condition number $κ$. Our approach can be extended to an arbitrary norm. Extensive experiments are conducted for the estimation of the 1-norm and 2-norm condition numbers, which show that our method achieves a significant speedup over the traditional numerical estimation methods. Our software for GNN condition number estimator is made publicly available at https://github.com/inEXASCALE/sparse-kappa.

papers.title: Combinatorial Properties of the Raisonnier Filter
papers.abstract: The Raisonnier filter is a combinatorial object isolated by Jean Raisonnier in order to simplify Shelah's proof that if all $\mathbfΣ^1_3$ sets are Lebesgue-measurable then there is an inner model with an inaccessible cardinal. In this paper, we study the combinatorics of a general version of the Raisonnier filter, with an eye to potential applications in descriptive set theory. We prove various results about the Raisonnier Filter generated by simple sets, and we study the ideals associated to the Raisonnier Filter being rapid and/or unbounded, connecting it to the null-additive and meagre-additive ideals studied by Pawlikowski and Shelah. Among the more interesting results is a converse to Raisonnier's theorem which indicates that Raisonnier's technique is unlikely to lead to similar results for other regularity properties. We also draw some conclusions regarding the Borel and dual Borel Conjectures.

papers.title: Analogue of the theta group $Γ_θ$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce higher level versions of the theta group $Γ_θ.$ In particular, we treat level 3 and 4 versions of the theta group, $Γ_{θ,3}$ and $Γ_{θ,4}$ and prove that $\displaystyle F(τ)=η\left(\frac{τ-1}{3} \right) η\left(\frac{τ+1}{3} \right)$ and $\displaystyle G(τ)=η\left(\frac{τ-1}{4} \right) η\left(\frac{τ+1}{4} \right)$ are modular forms on $Γ_{θ,3}$ and $Γ_{θ,4}$ respectively. Moreover we compute their multiplier systems, $ν_{F}$ and $ν_{G}$.

papers.title: Competition Versus Complexity in Multiple-Selection Prophet Inequalities
papers.abstract: Competition complexity formalizes a compelling intuition: rather than refining the mechanism, how much additional competition is sufficient for a simple mechanism to compete with an optimal one? We begin the study of this question in multi-unit pricing for welfare maximization using prophet inequalities. An online decision-maker observes $m \geq k$ nonnegative values drawn independently from a known distribution, may select up to $k$ of them, and aims to maximize the expected sum of selected values. The benchmark is a prophet who observes a sequence of length $n \geq k$ and selects the $k$ largest values. We focus on the widely adopted class of single-threshold algorithms and fully characterize their $(1-\varepsilon)$-competition complexity. Notably, our results reveal a sharp competition-induced phase transition: in the absence of competition, single-threshold algorithms are fundamentally limited to a $1-1/\sqrt{2kπ}$ fraction of the prophet value, whereas even a $1\%$ multiplicative increase beyond $n$ observations suffices to achieve a $1-\exp(-Θ(k))$ fraction. Another notable result happens when $k=1$: we show that the $(1-\varepsilon)$-competition complexity is exactly $\ln(1/\varepsilon)$, fully resolving an open question by Brustle et al. [Math. Oper. Res. 2024]. Our analysis is based on infinite-dimensional linear programming and duality arguments.

papers.title: Hecke curves in Frobenius strata of moduli space of rank 2 vector bundles
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field with characteristic $2$, and let $X$ be a smooth projective algebraic curve of genus $g \geqslant 2$ over $k$. Let $\mathcal{M}^s_X(2,\mathcal{L})$ be the moduli space of rank $2$ stable vector bundles with determinant $\mathcal{L}$ on $X$. The Frobenius stratification measures the instability of bundles in $\mathcal{M}^s_X(r,\mathcal{L})$ under pullback by the Frobenius map. We show that there exists a Frobenius stratum in $\mathcal{M}^s_X(2,\mathcal{L})$ which is covered by Hecke curves.

papers.title: Phase transitions on periodic orbits in $β$-transformation with a hole at zero
papers.abstract: Given $β\in(1,2]$, let $T_β: [0,1)\to[0,1);~x\mapstoβx\pmod 1$. For $m\in\mathbb N$ let \[ τ_m(β):=\sup\left\{t\in[0,1): K_β(t)\textrm{ contains a periodic orbit of smallest period }m \right\}, \] where $K_β(t)=\{x\in[0,1): T_β^n(x)\notin(0,t)~\forall n\ge 0\}$ is the survivor set of the open dynamical system $(T_β, [0,1), H)$ with a hole $H=(0,t)$. In this paper we give a complete characterization of $τ_m$, and show that $τ_m$ is piecewise continuous with precisely $ψ(m)$ discontinuity points, where $ψ(m)$ is the number of bulbs of period $m$ in the Mandelbrot set. To describe the critical value function $τ_m$ we construct a finite butterfly tree $\mathcal T_m$, from which we are able to determine the discontinuity points and the analytic formula of $τ_m$ based on Farey words and substitution operators. As a by product, we characterize the extremal Lyndon words and extremal Perron words. Since we are working in the symbolic space, our result can be applied to study phase transitions for periodic orbits in topologically expansive Lorenz maps, doubling map with an asymmetric hole, intermediate $β$-transformations, unique expansions in double bases, and so on.

papers.title: Monotone Optimisation with Learned Projections
papers.abstract: Optimisation algorithms typically assume oracle access to objectives and constraints, yet in many applications these functions are available only through data. To recover them, a common approach learns a surrogate for each function and optimises over it, but this can be unnecessarily expensive and may fail to preserve the structure required by the optimisation algorithm. We study this problem for monotone optimisation, a class of non-convex problems which can be solved globally using the Polyblock Outer Approximation (POA) algorithm. Our key observation is that POA does not require the constraint functions themselves, but only a scalar quantity we call the radial inverse. Learning this quantity directly replaces POA's inner bisection loop over a learned constraint with a single radial inverse evaluation. We characterise exactly which maps arise as radial inverses of monotone constraints, and relate their approximation error to perturbations of the feasible set and optimal objective value. Building on these results, we introduce Homogeneous-Monotone Radial Inverse (HM-RI) networks, structured min-max models that enforce the monotonicity and positive-homogeneity of radial inverses by construction. Across synthetic monotone optimisation problems and a cellular transmit-power application, HM-RI improves solution quality over direct constraint surrogates and local optimisation baselines by up to 58.6 percentage points relative to the Oracle reference objective, while achieving a 3.0-4.7x speed-up over bisection-based POA with learned constraint surrogates, with the largest solution-quality gains occurring in data-limited and piecewise-constant settings.

papers.title: All-Pass Function OPF: A Solver-Friendly, Physics-Preserving Approximation of AC OPF
papers.abstract: This paper presents a rational approximation of the AC optimal power flow (AC OPF) problem based on an all-pass approximation of the exponential power flow kernel. The classical AC OPF relies on trigonometric coupling between bus voltage phasors, which yields a nonconvex program with oscillatory derivatives that can slow, or in some cases destabilize, interior-point methods. We replace the trigonometric terms with an all-pass function (APF) approximation whose real and imaginary components act as smooth surrogates for the cosine and sine functions, and we introduce a pre-rotation to shift the argument of the approximation toward its most accurate region, ensuring that the reformulated power flow model preserves physical loss behavior, maintains the symmetry of the classical kernels, and improves the conditioning of the Jacobian and Hessian matrices. The proposed APF OPF formulation remains nonconvex, as in the classical model, but it eliminates trigonometric evaluations and empirically produces larger and more stable Newton steps under standard interior-point solvers.
