Numerical results on more than 25 IEEE and PGLib test systems ranging from 9 to 10{,}000 buses demonstrate that the APF OPF model achieves solutions with accuracy comparable to that of the classical formulation while reducing solver times, indicating a more solver-friendly nonconvex representation of AC OPF. All code, functions, verification scripts, and generated results are publicly available on \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/APF-OPF}{GitHub}, along with a README describing how to run and reproduce the experiments.

papers.title: A Bregman Regularized Proximal Point Method for Solving Equilibrium Problems on Hadamard Manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper we develop a Bregman regularized proximal point algorithm for solving monotone equilibrium problems on Hadamard manifolds. It has been shown that the regularization term induced by a Bregman function is, in general, nonconvex on Hadamard manifolds unless the curvature is zero. Nevertheless, we prove that the proposed Bregman regularization scheme does converge to a solution of the equilibrium problem on Hadamard manifolds in the presence of a strong assumption on the convexity of the set formed by the regularization term. Moreover, we employ a coercivity condition on the Bregman function which is weaker than those typically assumed in the existing literature on Bregman regularization. Numerical experiments on illustrative examples demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our proposed method.

papers.title: Kato's Ramification filtration via de Rham-Witt complex and applications
papers.abstract: Given an $F$-finite regular scheme $X$ of positive characteristic and a simple normal crossing divisor $E$ on $X$, we introduce a filtration on the de Rham--Witt complex $W_mΩ^\bullet_{X\setminus E}$. When $X$ is the spectrum of a henselian discrete valuation ring $A$ with quotient field $K$, this extends the classical filtration on $W_m(K)$ due to Brylinski. We show that Kato's ramification filtration on $H^q_\et(X \setminus E, {\Q}/{\Z}(q-1))$ for $q \ge 1$ admits an explicit description in terms of the above filtration on the de Rham--Witt complex of $X \setminus E$. When $q =1$, this specializes to the results of Kato and Kerz--Saito. As applications, we construct a generalized version of Kato's refined Swan conductor for regular schemes, prove Lefschetz theorems for Kato's ramification filtrations for smooth projective varieties over $F$-finite fields, and prove Lefschetz and vanishing theorems for the Brauer group.

papers.title: Path Types in Algebraic Type Theory
papers.abstract: A new approach to the semantics of identity types in intensional Martin-Löf type theory is proposed, assuming only a category with finite limits and an interval. The specification of \emph{extensional} identity types in the original presentation of natural models paralleled that of the other type formers $Σ$ and $Π$, but the treatment of the \emph{intensional} case there was less uniform. It was later reformulated to an account based on polynomials; here a further improvement in the style of the other type formers is achieved by employing an interval, in order to give a single pullback specification of a model with \emph{path types}. The interval is also used to specify a (Hurewicz) fibration structure on the universe of the model. It is shown that the combination of these two conditions suffices to model the intensional identity rules, assuming only finite limits. The addition of an interval also relates the current treatment to that of cubical type theory.

papers.title: Qualitative properties of positive solutions to mixed local and nonlocal critical problems in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: We consider the following mixed local and non-local critical elliptic equation: \begin{equation*}\label{0.1} \left\{ \begin{array}{lll} -Δu+(-Δ)^su=λh u^{p}+u^{2^*-1}, &\text{in}\,\, \mathbb{R}^n, u>0, &\text {in} \,\, \mathbb{R}^n, \lim\limits_{|x|\to\infty} u(x) = 0, \end{array} \right. \end{equation*} where $n\geqslant4, \,\, p\in (0,2^*-1),\,\, 2^*:=\frac{2n}{n-2}$ and $h$ is a positive function. We first show the existence and regularity results of viscosity solutions to the above critical elliptic equation. More precisely, from \cite{Su-Xu} weak solutions are obtained and we prove they are indeed viscosity solutions and their regularity is: \( u \in C^α(\mathbb{R}^n) \) for $p\in(0,1);$ \( u \in C^{2,β}(\mathbb{R}^n) \) for $p\in [1, 2^*-1).$ Moreover, for $p\in [1, 2^*-1)$, these viscosity solutions are indeed classical ones and we then prove the existence of positive solutions with the qualitative properties such as the decay estimates and the radial symmetry.

papers.title: Modular points and dimensions of Eisenstein deformation spaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we study two-dimensional Eisenstein deformation spaces, focusing on the Zariski density of modular points and the dimensions of their irreducible components. Over $\mathbb{Q}$, under explicit generic hypotheses, we prove that every irreducible component has characteristic zero and dimension $4$, and that modular points are Zariski dense. Over certain abelian totally real fields, we prove a big $R=\mathbb{T}$ theorem for the union of the high-dimensional components. As an arithmetic application, we prove the weight-one Fontaine-Mazur conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$ for $p\geq 5$, with no hypothesis on the residual representation. In a complementary direction, we prove a local-to-global finiteness theorem for pseudo-deformation rings. Combining this with ordinary finiteness and modularity-theoretic inputs, we prove Mazur's dimension conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$ in both the residually reducible and residually irreducible cases, and deduce Emerton's equidimensionality conjecture for the $p$-adic big Hecke algebra for every odd prime.

papers.title: Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers for Nonlinear Matrix Decompositions
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for solving nonlinear matrix decompositions (NMD). Given an input matrix $X \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ and a factorization rank $r \ll \min(m, n)$, NMD seeks matrices $W \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times r}$ and $H \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times n}$ such that $X \approx f(WH)$, where $f$ is an element-wise nonlinear function. We evaluate our method on several representative nonlinear models: the rectified linear unit activation $f(x) = \max(0, x)$, suitable for nonnegative sparse data approximation, the component-wise square $f(x) = x^2$, applicable to probabilistic circuit representation, and the MinMax transform $f(x) = \min(b, \max(a, x))$, relevant for recommender systems. The proposed framework flexibly supports diverse loss functions, including least squares, $\ell_1$ norm, and the Kullback-Leibler divergence, and can be readily extended to other nonlinearities and metrics. We illustrate the applicability, efficiency, and adaptability of the approach on real-world datasets, highlighting its potential for a broad range of applications.

papers.title: Transient rebellions in the Kuramoto oscillator: Morse-Smale structural stability and connection graphs of finite 2-shift type
papers.abstract: The celebrated 1975 Kuramoto model of $N$ identical oscillators with phase angle vector $\boldsymbol{\vartheta}=(\vartheta_1,\ldots,\vartheta_N)$ and all-to-all coupling reads \begin{equation} \label{*} \dot\vartheta_j\,=\tfrac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^N \sin(\vartheta_k-\vartheta_j). \tag{*} \end{equation} Here we have passed to co-rotating coordinates in normalized time scale. The model is highly accessible to rigorous mathematical analysis, and has been studied as a paradigm for effects like total and partial synchronization. Most initial conditions $\boldsymbol{\vartheta}$ lead to total synchronization. The large number of asymptotically $\sim 2^{N-1}$ (circles of) partially synchronized states, however, is unstable. The precise behavior of transitions to synchrony seems to have eluded description. In the present paper, we address this gap. By the gradient structure of (*), the global dynamics decompose into equilibria and heteroclinic orbits between them. Except for the extremes of total instability and total synchrony, all equilibria are 2-cluster solutions: their phase angles $\vartheta_j$ attain only two values, with a phase difference of $π$ between them. Any heteroclinic orbit between 2-cluster equilibria, or towards synchrony, can be realized as a 3-cluster rebellion. Cluster rebellions split the smaller, "slim", minority cluster of the source equilibrium and send the rebellious part to join the bigger, "fat", majority cluster. Heteroclinic transversality identifies the Kuramoto model as a structurally stable Morse-Smale system. In particular, heteroclinic orbits can be concatenated in finite time. The options involved in successive cluster rebellions amount to finite symbol sequences of 2-shift type. We include numerical illustrations, and a comparison with coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators. The paper is dedicated to Professor Yoshiki Kuramoto, with admiration.

papers.title: An L-Stable Sequential Implicit Two-Stage Fourth-Order Time Discretization with Second-Order Stiff Damping
papers.abstract: We construct a fully implicit, sequential two-stage time discretization for stiff systems using physical quantities and their rates of change. Coefficients are determined by direct Taylor matching, and convergence analysis proves fourth-order accuracy at both midpoint and endpoint for fixed smooth systems. Pole and imaginary-axis boundary analysis, together with the maximum modulus principle, characterizes the \(L\)-stable family. Within this family, \(C_q=5/183\) uniquely cancels the leading inverse-power term and gives the full-step amplification factor quadratic stiff decay, while \(C_a=\frac{25-\sqrt{105}}{780}\) yields the highest accuracy. The method combines \(L\)-stability with second-order stiff damping, two-stage fourth-order accuracy, and sequential implicitness. In contrast, fourth-order Gauss--Legendre and symmetric Hermite--Obreshkov schemes are \(A\)-stable rather than \(L\)-stable; their variants must sacrifice per-stage accuracy to improve stiff stability. Among \(L\)-stable methods, two-stage Radau IIA and TR--BDF2 have third- and second-order accuracy, respectively, while SDIRK requires five stages for fourth order. Gauss and Radau stages must be solved in a coupled manner. Stiff ODE and scalar tests verify fourth-order convergence and quadratic stiff decay. Finite-volume tests show fourth-order joint convergence on smooth one-dimensional problems and fast-mode damping in two-dimensional cases. At the same acoustic error threshold, the method uses eight implicit stages, whereas three-stage Radau IIA uses twelve. Finally, the sequential formulation keeps each Newton system at the state dimension, reducing its size, improving efficiency, and facilitating parallel computation.

papers.title: New Obstacles to Multiple Recurrence
papers.abstract: We show that there is a set which is not a set of multiple recurrence despite being a set of recurrence for nil-Bohr sets. This answers Huang, Shao, and Ye's "higher-order" version of Katznelson's Question on Bohr recurrence and topological recurrence in the negative. Equivalently, we construct a set $S$ so that there is a finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ without monochromatic three-term arithmetic progressions with common differences in $S$, but so that $S$ lacks the usual polynomial obstacles to arithmetic progressions. This represents a significant contribution to our understanding of when a restricted van der Waerden theorem or a restricted Szemerédi Theorem holds, an important problem in additive combinatorics and Ramsey theory.

papers.title: Large-Time Analysis of the Langevin Dynamics for Energies Fulfilling Polyak-Łojasiewicz Conditions
papers.abstract: In this work, we take a step towards understanding overdamped Langevin dynamics for the minimization of a general class of objective functions $\mathcal{L}$. We establish well-posedness and regularity of the law $ρ_t$ of the process through novel a priori estimates, and, very importantly, we characterize the large-time behavior of $ρ_t$ under truly minimal assumptions on $\mathcal{L}$. In the case of integrable Gibbs density, the law converges to the normalized Gibbs measure. In the non-integrable case, we prove that the law diffuses. The rate of convergence, in terms of relative Dirichlet energy with respect to the Gibbs measure, is $\mathcal O(1/(σt))$, where $σ$ is the diffusion parameter. Under a Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition on $\mathcal{L}$, we also derive sharp exponential contractivity results toward the set of global minimizers. Combining these results we provide the first systematic convergence analysis of Langevin dynamics under PL conditions in non-integrable Gibbs settings: a first phase of exponential in time contraction toward the set of minimizers and then a large-time exploration over it with rate $\mathcal O(1/(σt))$ in terms of the relative Dirichlet energy.

papers.title: A formula for the edge density $\sqrt{n}$-correction for two-dimensional Coulomb systems
papers.abstract: In connection with recent work on smallest gaps, C. Charlier proves that the 1-point function of a suitable planar Coulomb system $\{z_j\}_1^n$, in the determinantal case with respect to an external potential $Q(z)$, admits the expansion, as $n\to\infty$, $$R_n\bigg(z_0+\frac t {\sqrt{2n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)}}ν(z_0)\bigg)=n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)\frac {\operatorname{erfc} t}2+\sqrt{n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)}\,C(z_0;t)+\mathcal{O}(\log^6 n).$$ Here $t$ is a real parameter, $z_0$ is a regular boundary point of the (connected) Coulomb droplet and $ν(z_0)$ is the outwards unit normal; the coefficient $C(z_0;t)$ has an apriori structure depending on a number of parameters. In this note we identify the parameters and obtain a formula for $C(z_0;t)$ in potential theoretic and geometric terms. Our formula holds for a large class of potentials such that the droplet is connected with smooth boundary. Our derivation uses the well known expectation of fluctuations formula.

papers.title: Vu's conjecture holds for claw-free graphs
papers.abstract: Given a graph $G$, let $Δ_2(G)$ denote the maximum number of neighbors any two distinct vertices of $G$ have in common. Vu (2002) proposed that, provided $Δ_2(G)$ is not too small as a proportion of the maximum degree $Δ(G)$ of $G$, the chromatic number of $G$ should never be too much larger than $Δ_2(G)$. We make a first approach towards Vu's conjecture from a structural graph theoretic point of view. We prove that, in the case where $G$ is claw-free, indeed the chromatic number of $G$ is at most $Δ_2(G)+3$. This is tight, as our bound is met with equality for the line graph of the Petersen graph. Moreover, we can prove this in terms of the more specific parameter that bounds the maximum number of neighbors any two endpoints of some edge of $G$ have in common. Our result may be viewed as a generalization of the classic bound of Vizing (1964) for edge-coloring.

papers.title: Debiased Kernel Estimation of Spot Volatility in the Presence of Infinite Variation Jumps
papers.abstract: Volatility estimation is a central problem in financial econometrics, but becomes particularly challenging when jump activity is high, a phenomenon observed empirically in highly traded financial securities. In this paper, we revisit the problem of spot volatility estimation for an Itô semimartingale with jumps of unbounded variation. We construct truncated kernel-based estimators and debiased variants that extend rate-optimal spot volatility estimation to a wider range of jump activity indices, from the previously available bound $Y<4/3$ to $Y<20/11$. Rate-suboptimal CLTs are also established for $Y>20/11$. Compared with earlier work, our approach achieves smaller asymptotic variances through the use of more general kernels and an optimal choice for the bandwidth convergence rate, and also has broader applicability under more flexible model assumptions. A comprehensive simulation study confirms that our procedures outperform competing methods in finite samples.

papers.title: Density estimation for exponential functionals of subordinators
papers.abstract: Exponential functionals of subordinators play a key role in probability theory and arise in numerous applications, yet explicit density formulas have until now been available only in a limited number of special settings. This paper provides a general remedy. First, we obtain a closed-form representation of the density for the entire class of integer-valued subordinators (compound Poisson processes with positive integer jump sizes) in the form of a rapidly converging series whose coefficients obey a simple recurrence; we further extend the construction to include drift by means of an explicit iterative scheme. Second, we propose a general approximation method for arbitrary driftless subordinators, including cases where the Lévy measure has continuous support. By discretizing the Lévy measure, we generate a sequence of explicit, computable densities that is proved to converge to the true density. Together, these results greatly broaden the theory of exponential functionals, transforming a problem previously tractable only in rare instances into one that is either explicitly solvable or can be systematically approximated for the full class of subordinators. The resulting formulas enable fast and accurate computations for financial modelling, insurance risk assessment, and stochastic simulation, while the approximation procedure provides a robust and stable alternative to existing numerical methods. The unified framework --- linking pantograph equations, $q$-calculus, and Poisson approximation --- also opens avenues for analyzing more general decreasing functionals and drifted subordinators with general Lévy measures.

papers.title: Orthogonality of non-pretentious functions to polynomials over Function Fields
papers.abstract: We prove that non-pretentious multiplicative functions are orthogonal to polynomials over function fields (up to characteristic conditions).

papers.title: Blow-up solutions of parabolic $p$-Laplacian inequalities on locally finite graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study blow up behavior of the semilinear parabolic inequality with $p$-Laplacian operator and nonlinear source $u_t - Δ_p u \geq σ(x, t)Φ(u)$ on a locally finite connected weighted graph $G = (V, E)$. We extend the comparison principle and thereby establish the relationship between the initial value and the existence of blow-up solutions to the problem under different growth rates of $Φ$. We prove that when the growth rate of $Φ$ exceeds linear growth, blow-up solutions exist under appropriate initial conditions.

papers.title: SDEs with critical general distributional drifts: sharp solvability and blow-ups
papers.abstract: We develop weak solution theory of SDEs having general distributional drifts that can introduce local blow-up effects. Our assumption on the drift is closely related to the variational theory of the Kolmogorov backward equation in the standard Hilbert triple $W^{1,2} \hookrightarrow L^2 \hookrightarrow W^{-1,2}$. Under suitable smallness assumption on the drift, one has well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in this Hilbert triple. In turn, by a result of Mazya and Verbitsky, boundedness of the drift term from $W^{1,2}$ to $W^{-1,2}$ is equivalent to a decomposition of the drift in the sum of a form-bounded drift (including, for example, Morrey or Chang--Wilson--Wolff drifts) and a divergence-free distributional drift in the ${\rm BMO}^{-1}$ space of Koch and Tataru; such decomposition is our class of drifts. We apply our results to finite particle systems with strong attracting interactions immersed in a stationary turbulent flow. This includes particle systems of Keller-Segel type. Crucially, in dimensions $d \geq 3$, we cover almost the entire admissible range of attraction strengths, reaching nearly to the blow-up threshold. As a further application of our results for SDEs and of the theory of Bessel processes, we obtain an improved upper bound on the constant in the many-particle Hardy inequality of Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Laptev, and Tidblom.

papers.title: Conserved quantities of distinguished curves on conformal sphere
papers.abstract: We give conserved quantities of two generalizations of conformal circles on the conformal sphere. One generalization concerns curves carrying a distinguished parallel tractor along them, which can be used to construct the conserved quantities. The other is the class of curves satisfying the conformal Mercator equation, the conserved quantities of which are computed using Lagrangian formalism. The two generalizations are not disjoint, and our main result is the relation between their conserved quantities. Explicit examples are also presented.

papers.title: Ultrametric approximation and Gromov--Hausdorff clouds
papers.abstract: We compute the Gromov--Hausdorff distance from a metric space to the class of ultrametric spaces in terms of its ultrametric defect and study when a compact ultrametric space attains this distance. For the product of a compact ultrametric space and a compact connected metric space, we give a criterion for the existence of such an approximation. For every integer $k\geqslant1$, we obtain an exact formula for the distance from a bounded metric space to the class of ultrametric spaces with at most $k$ points and prove that the minimum is attained. We characterize the clouds that contain a path-connected space. For compact $X$, we construct a geodesic of length $\operatorname{diam}\textbf{U}(X)/2$ to a nearest connected compact space.

papers.title: The Maximum Number of Sets for 12 Cards is 14
papers.abstract: We analyze a mathematical property of the popular card game SET. We present a revised geometric and computer-assisted proof that the maximum number of sets for 12 cards is 14 using finite field geometry, combinatorics, and graph theory. We present several computer algorithms for finding or approximating the maximum number of sets. We show a complete computer proof that iterates over all possible board configurations. We use this method to compute the maximum number of sets with 4 properties for a small number of cards, but it is generally too inefficient. With this method, we compute the maximum number of sets for 3 properties for all possible numbers of cards. Finally, we compare this to an existing approximation algorithm for finding maximal sets.

papers.title: Non-collapsed RCD spaces with local bounded covering geometry
papers.abstract: We study non-collapsed $\mathrm{RCD}(-(N-1),N)$ spaces with locally bounded covering geometry. Our first main result generalizes Gromov's almost flat manifold theorem: if the universal cover is non-collapsing and the diameter is sufficiently small, then the space is bi-Holder homeomorphic to an infranilmanifold. In the smooth setting with $\mathrm{Ric} \ge -(N-1)$, this homeomorphism is actually a diffeomorphism. As an application of our arguments, we show that Gromov's almost flat manifold theorem extends to the $\mathrm{RCD}+\mathrm{CBA}$ setting. Our second main result generalizes Fukaya's fibration theorem. Suppose a sequence of non-collapsed $\mathrm{RCD}(-(N-1),N)$ spaces with locally bounded covering geometry converges in the pointed measured Gromov--Hausdorff sense to a smooth manifold of dimension $k < N$. We then construct a topological fiber bundle map from the RCD spaces to the limit manifold. The fibers are infranilmanifolds, and the structure group is affine. Finally, although there exist collapsing Ricci limit spaces with no topological manifold points, we prove that if the sequence additionally satisfies locally bounded covering geometry and the limit space has dimension $k$, then every $k$-regular point is a topological manifold point.

papers.title: Spectral Limits of the Neumann-Poincaré Operator on Degenerating Tori
papers.abstract: We determine the limit of the spectrum of the Neumann-Poincaré operator on circular tori as the torus degenerates. As the central hole closes, the spectrum converges to $[-1/2,0]$ together with a set of positive points, which we characterize as eigenvalues of explicit limiting operators. As the cross-section shrinks, the spectrum converges to $[0,1/2]$.

papers.title: Graph Fourier Neural Kernels: Learning Full PDE Trajectories Across Geometries and Anisotropic Parameter Fields
papers.abstract: High-fidelity simulations of time-dependent nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) are expensive to repeat across families of domains and parameter fields, a cost that recurs in design optimization, uncertainty quantification, and computational medicine. Most neural-operator surrogates require each domain to be mapped onto a common grid or reference shape, and few predict the full time course. We introduce Graph Fourier Neural Kernels (G-FuNK), a neural operator for second-order semilinear PDEs with a diffusive principal part that transfers across geometries and anisotropic diffusion tensors without coordinate maps or diffeomorphisms. A weighted graph and its Laplacian supply a spectral basis that encodes geometry and anisotropy. Shared layers act in this basis, at a cost linear in mesh size after one partial eigendecomposition per geometry, and a neural ODE integrator propagates the learned generator to full spatiotemporal trajectories on unseen domains. Across anisotropic heat flow, stiff reaction-diffusion, FitzHugh-Nagumo, and patient-specific left-atrial electrophysiology on CT-derived surfaces, G-FuNK reproduces held-out trajectories with relative $L^2$ error between 0.046 and 0.160. Its accuracy is comparable to that of a geometry-aware Fourier neural operator on regular domains, and its predictions are unchanged when a rectangular domain is rotated. On left atria, whose venous and valvular openings prevent mapping onto a reference shape, it predicts an 85-ms trajectory in under half a second, against about 5 minutes for finite elements, with a mean activation-time error of 1.73 ms. Accuracy depends on graph construction and is highest when the learned generator is integrated at its training time step.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Quantum State Tomography for Structured Quantum States in One Dimension
papers.abstract: In this paper, we answer this fundamental question affirmatively by using a class of informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (IC-POVMs), including symmetric IC-POVMs (SIC-POVMs) and spherical $t$-designs, focusing on sample complexity while not accounting for the implementation complexity of the measurement settings. For SIC-POVMs and spherical 2-designs, we show that the number of state copies to guarantee bounded recovery error of an MPO state with a constrained least-squares estimator depends on the probability distribution of the MPO under the POVM but scales only linearly with $n$ when the distribution is approximately uniform. For general spherical $t$-designs with a sufficiently large $t$, we prove that only a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is sufficient for a guaranteed recovery of any state represented by an MPO. In addition, we establish a sample complexity lower bound based on the Cramer-Rao bound, showing that, for strictly positive definite MPO states and unbiased estimators, a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is also necessary, although the upper and lower bounds do not yet match in their dependence on the target accuracy. Furthermore, we propose a spectral method and a projected gradient descent (PGD) algorithm to solve the constrained least-squares problem, both equipped with rigorous recovery error guarantees.

papers.title: Lower order terms in the shape of cubic fields
papers.abstract: We demonstrate equidistribution of the lattice shape of cubic fields when ordered by discriminant, giving an estimate in the Eisenstein series spectrum with a lower order main term. The analysis gives a separate discussion of the contributions of reducible and irreducible binary cubic forms, following a method of Shintani. Our work answers a question posed at the American Institute of Math by giving a precise geometric and spectral description of an evident barrier to equidistribution in the lattice shape.

papers.title: The Bruce-Roberts number of holomorphic 1-forms along complex analytic varieties
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the \textit{Bruce--Roberts number} for holomorphic 1-forms relative to complex analytic varieties. Our main result shows that the Bruce--Roberts number of a 1-form $ω$ relative to a complex analytic hypersurface $X$ with an isolated singularity can be expressed in terms of the \textit{Goméz-Mont--Seade--Verjovsky index} of $ω$ along $X$, the \textit{Milnor number} of $ω$ and the \textit{Tjurina number} of $X$. This result allows us to recover known formulas for the Bruce--Roberts number of a holomorphic function along $X$ and to establish connections between this number, the radial index, and the local Euler obstruction of $ω$ along $X$. Moreover, we present applications to both global and local holomorphic foliations in complex dimension two.

papers.title: The non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the forced MHD equations
papers.abstract: We construct two distinct Leray solutions of the three-dimensional forced viscous, resistive magnetohydrodynamic equations in the whole space, with zero initial data and identical forcing. Our construction begins with a periodic axisymmetric unstable MHD mode associated with a rotating column and a nonconstant axial magnetic field. The rotating profile is also centrifugally unstable at zero magnetic field; the construction uses an unstable MHD eigenvalue and does not require magnetic destabilization of a hydrodynamically stable flow. Our spectral construction tracks a prescribed unstable MHD eigenvalue under radial truncation, the addition of small positive viscosity, and toroidal closure. The first two steps use a decomposition into a skew-adjoint principal part and compact feedback at a fixed Fourier frequency. Keeping the viscosity fixed, we bend the column into a compactly supported toroidal profile and obtain a genuine whole-space unstable eigenvalue through convergence of localized Stokes resolvents. A small-dilation limit and an exact rescaling then yield an unstable background in similarity variables. A nonlinear trajectory along its unstable direction produces the second solution. Both solutions are smooth for positive times and satisfy the energy equality. The forcing acts in both the velocity and magnetic equations.

papers.title: Metric Multiview Geometry---a Catalogue in Low Dimensions
papers.abstract: We systematically compile an exhaustive catalogue of multiview varieties and anchored multiview varieties arising from projections of points, lines, and planes in 1, 2, and 3-dimensional projective spaces. We say that two such varieties are ED-equivalent if there is a linear isomorphism between them that preserves ED-critical points. This gives rise to fourteen representatives, at most two of which are equivalent, and we determine various properties---dimension, set-theoretic equations, and multidegrees---for all varieties featured in our catalogue. In the case of points, we also present a complementary study of resectioning varieties and their singular loci. Finally, we propose conjectures for the Euclidean distance degrees of all varieties appearing in our comprehensive compilation.

papers.title: On the (In)Compatibility between Group Fairness and Individual Fairness
papers.abstract: We study the compatibility between utility-optimized statistical parity and individual fairness. While individual fairness seeks to treat similar individuals similarly, optimal statistical parity aims to provide similar treatment to individuals who share relative similarity within their respective sensitive groups. Although both fairness perspectives are desirable, they often conflict in practical applications. Our goal in this work is to analyze the existence of this conflict and its potential solution. In particular, we establish sufficient (sharp) conditions for the compatibility between the optimal (post-processing) statistical parity $L^2$ learning and the ($K$-Lipschitz or $(ε,δ)$) individual fairness requirements. When a conflict arises, we first relax the optimal statistical parity solution to the Pareto frontier, representing the optimal trade-off between $L^2$ error and statistical disparity, and then examine its compatibility with individual fairness. Our analysis identifies regions along the Pareto frontier that satisfy individual fairness constraints. Additionally, we provide individual fairness guarantees for the composition of a trained model with the optimal post-processing step, enabling practitioners to assess the compatibility of post-processed models. This provides practitioners with a principled approach to achieving Pareto-optimal statistical parity while maintaining individual fairness constraints.

papers.title: On the limit of simply connected manifolds with discrete isometric cocompact group actions
papers.abstract: We study the fundamental group of the equivariant Gromov--Hausdorff limit space \[ (M_i, p_i, G_i) \xrightarrow{eGH} (Y, p, G), \] where $\{(M_i,p_i)\}_{i\in\mathbb N}$ is a sequence of complete, connected, and simply connected $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with $\mathrm{Ric}\ge -(n-1)$. Here $G_i\subset \mathrm{Iso}(M_i)$ is a discrete subgroup satisfying $\mathrm{diam}(M_i/G_i)\le D$ for some fixed constant $D>0$. Let $G_0$ denote the identity component of $G$. Then $G_0$ is a nilpotent Lie group. Let $T^k \subseteq G_0$ be the maximal torus. Our main result asserts that the quotient space $Y/T^k$ is simply connected. Moreover, the fundamental group $π_1(Y,p)$ is generated, up to conjugation, by loops contained in $T^k$-orbits. More precisely, each generator can be represented by a loop of the form \begin{equation*} γ= α\cdot β\cdot α^{-1}, \end{equation*} where $α$ is a curve from $p$ to some point $y \in Y$, and $β$ is a loop based at $y$ that lies entirely in the $T^k$-orbit of $y$.

papers.title: An Eilenberg-Watts Theorem and Morita localization for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-categories
papers.abstract: Hilbert modules over a $C^*$-category were first defined by Mitchener, who also proved that they form a $C^*$-category. An Eilenberg-Watts theorem for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-algebras was proved by Blecher. We follow a similar path to prove an Eilenberg-Watts theorem for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-categories and characterize equivalences of categories of Hilbert modules as being given by tensoring with imprimitivity bimodules. We employ our results to prove several equivalences of bicategories of $C^*$-algebras and $C^*$-categories, and to exhibit a Morita localization of the category of locally small $C^*$-categories.

papers.title: Edge universality of sparse Erdős-Rényi digraphs
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal A$ be the adjacency matrix of the Erdős-Rényi directed graph $\mathscr G(N,p)$. We denote the eigenvalues of $\mathcal A$ by $λ_1^{\cal A},...,λ^{\cal A}_N$, and $|λ_1^{\cal A}|=\max_i|λ_i^{\cal A}|$. For $N^{-1+o(1)}\leq p\leq 1/2$, we show that \[ \max_{i=2,3,...,N} \bigg|\frac{λ_i^{\mathcal A}}{\sqrt{Np(1-p)}}\bigg| =1+O(N^{-1/2+o(1)}) \] with very high probability. In addition, we prove that near the unit circle, the local eigenvalue statistics of ${\mathcal A}/\sqrt{Np(1-p)}$ coincide with those of the real Ginibre ensemble. As a by-product, we also show that all non-trivial eigenvectors of $\mathcal A$ are completely delocalized. For Hermitian random matrices, it is known that the edge statistics are sensitive to the sparsity: in the very sparse regime, one needs to remove many noise random variables (which affect both the mean and the fluctuation) to recover the Tracy-Widom distribution. Our results imply that, compared to their analogues in the Hermitian case, the edge statistics of non-Hermitian sparse random matrices are more robust.

papers.title: Doubly Free-Boundary Rail-Yard Dimers and Annular Gaussian Fluctuations
papers.abstract: We study rail-yard dimer models with free boundaries at both ends. The double free-boundary geometry introduces infinitely many reflected Cauchy factors into partition functions and contour formulas for height Laplace observables. For admissible piecewise periodic weights satisfying the stated separation conditions, we prove a Laplace-transform law of large numbers and obtain a limit shape through weak convergence of slope measures. For $β=1$, under the stated regularity and nonexceptional endpoint conditions, we derive a necessary real double-root condition for the frozen boundary. We also prove Gaussian fluctuations of centered height Laplace observables, with covariance determined by an annular reflected-image kernel expressed through theta functions. Finally, we construct an exact growth-diagram sampler for finite reflected truncations and prove that their laws converge in total variation to the full Gibbs measure on every fixed rail-yard graph with finitely many columns as the truncation level tends to infinity.

papers.title: $(G,μ)$-Windows and Deformations of $(G,μ)$-Displays
papers.abstract: Let $k_0$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}_p$, and let $μ$ be a cocharacter of $G_{W(k_0)}$ such that the set of $μ$-weights of $\Lie G$ is a subset of $\{-1,0,1,2,\dots\}$. We prove that the groupoid of adjoint nilpotent $(G,μ)$-displays as in \cite[Definition 1.0.1]{pappas}, \cite{lau2} and \cite[Definition 3.16]{E7} is equivalent to the groupoid of $(G,μ)$-windows, which are the generalizations of windows as in \cite[Definition 5.1]{langer2} and \cite[Definition 3.3.1]{E7}.

papers.title: Ratio of tiling generating functions of semi-hexagons and quartered hexagons with dents
papers.abstract: We consider the tiling generating functions of semi-hexagons and quartered hexagons with dents on their sides. In general, there are no simple product formulas for these generating functions. However, we show that the modification in the regions' width changes the tiling generating functions by only a simple multiplicative factor.

papers.title: Maximal Non-commuting Sets in Certain Unipotent Upper-triangular Linear Groups
papers.abstract: Let $ω(G)$ be the maximum size of a set of pairwise non-commuting elements of a group $G$. We determine $ω(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))$, where $UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q)$ is the group of $4\times 4$ unipotent upper-triangular matrices over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, in terms of a classical invariant of finite geometry: we prove that \[ ω(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3-q+1+ν(q), \] where $ν(q)$ is the largest size of a partial ovoid of the symplectic generalized quadrangle $\mathrm{W}(3,q)$ disjoint from a fixed line. We show that $ν(q)=q^2$ for even $q$ and $ν(q)=μ(q)$ for odd $q$, where $μ(q)$ is the largest size of a partial ovoid of $\mathrm{W}(3,q)$. Consequently $ω(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3+q^2-q+1$ for even $q$, while for odd $q$ we obtain $q^3+2q-1\le ω(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))\le q^3+q^2-2q+2$; the upper bound rests on a self-contained proof of the inequality $μ(q)\le q^2-q+1$. In particular $ω(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))$ is not a polynomial in $q$, not even for large $q$. This corrects Theorem~$A$ of the published version of this paper, where the value $q^3+q+1+ω(\mathcal{M})$ was claimed. We also study the non-commuting structures $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ introduced there: we prove that $ω(\mathcal{M})=q(q-1)$ for even $q$, that $ω(\mathcal{Q})=μ(q)-1$ for all $q$, and that for odd $q$ a non-commuting set in $\mathcal{Q}$ consisting of almost $m$ lines exists only for $m\le 5$. Exact values for small $q$ and a list of open problems and conjectures are included. Consequently for odd $q$ \[ ω(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3-q+2+ω(\mathcal{Q}). \]

papers.title: Trees in Random Sparse Graphs with a Given Degree Sequence
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ be the set of graphs $G(V,\, E)$ with $\left|V\right|=n$, and the degree sequence equal to $D=(d_{1},\, d_{2},\,\dots,\, d_{n})$. In addition, for $\frac{1}{2}<a<1$, we define the set of graphs with an almost given degree sequence $D$ as follows, \[ \mathbb{G}_{a}^{D}:=\cup\,\mathbb{G}^{\bar{D}}, \] where the union is over all degree sequences $\bar{D}$ such that, for $1\leq i\leq n$, we have $\left|d_{i}-\bar{d}_{i}\right|<d_{i}^{a}$. Now, if we chose random graphs $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ and $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{a}}\left(D\right)$ uniformly out of the sets $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ and $\mathbb{G}_{a}^{D}$, respectively, what do they look like? This has been studied when $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ is a dense graph, i.e. $\left|E\right|=Θ(n^{2})$, in the sense of graphons, or when $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ is very sparse, i.e. $d_{n}^{2}=o(\left|E\right|)$. In the case of sparse graphs with an almost given degree sequence, we investigate this question, and give the finite tree subgraph structure of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{a}}\left(D\right)$ under some mild conditions. For the random graph $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ with a given degree sequence, we re-derive the finite tree structure in dense and very sparse cases to give a continuous picture. Moreover, for a pair of vectors $\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)\in\mathbb{Z}^{n_{1}}\times\mathbb{Z}^{n_{2}}$, we let $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{b}}\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$ be the random bipartite graph that is chosen uniformly out of the set $\mathbb{G}^{D_{1},D_{2}}$, where $\mathbb{G}^{D_{1},D_{2}}$ is the set of all bipartite graphs with the degree sequence $\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$. We are able to show the result for $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{b}}\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$ without any further conditions.

papers.title: Triangle Tiling: The case $3α+ 2β= π$
papers.abstract: An $N$-tiling of triangle $ABC$ by triangle $T$ (the ``tile'') is a way of writing $ABC$ as a union of $N$ copies of $T$ overlapping only at their boundaries. Let the tile $T$ have angles $(α,β,γ)$, and sides $(a,b,c)$. This paper takes up the case when $3α+ 2β= π$. Then there are (as was already known) exactly five possible shapes of $ABC$ not similar to $T$: either $ABC$ is isosceles with base angles $α$, $β$, or $α+β$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2α,β,α+β)$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2α, α, 2β)$. We prove that the tile is rational (the ratios of its sides are rational). We then exhibit several families of previously unknown tilings. We also exhibit, for each shape, a Diophantine equation in $N$ and the parameters of the tile that must have a solution whenever there is a tiling of some triangle of that shape. By means of these Diophantine equations, some conclusions about the possible values of $N$ are drawn. We prove, for example, that there is no $N$-tiling with $N$ prime when $3α+ 2β= π$, for three of the five shapes; that question remains open for the shape $(2α,β,α+β)$ and for isosceles triangles with base angles $β$. These equations also imply that for each $N$, there is a finite set of possibilities for the tile $(a,b,c)$ and the triangle $ABC$. (Usually, but not always, there is just one possible tile.) For each of the five shapes, we give a construction method that works under certain sufficient conditions, but there remain values of $N$ that satisfy our necessary conditions and for which we do not know whether a tiling exists. All results have been formalized in Lean.

papers.title: Quadratic Bendixson criterion for delay systems: a numerical implementation
papers.abstract: We present a software implementation (as a Python package) of approximation schemes for verifying frequency inequalities arising from the quadratic Bendixson criterion for systems of delay equations (with a single delay in the linear part). In applications to dissipative nonlinear autonomous systems, such inequalities ensure global stability. The theoretical foundations of this approach were developed in our related work. In particular, it was shown that the transfer operators involved into the frequency inequalities can be represented as integral operators with bounded kernels of the Hardy--Volterra type. Here, we use this representation to construct approximation schemes based on finite-dimensional truncations of the transfer operators. Examples of using the package are provided.

papers.title: A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We present a constrained mixed variational formulation for incremental irreversible thermodynamics. A single augmented action combines a linearized contact-increment penalty, equilibrium and dissipative Fenchel--Young defects, a storage--transport functional, and multipliers enforcing the constitutive increments. Under frozen-coefficient and boundary assumptions, stationarity yields the linearized contact condition, the Tisza relation, the Onsager flux--force law, and the implicit balance equation. An exact-elimination theorem shows that the contact and multiplier fields can be reconstructed algebraically from a solution of the reduced weak balance problem. We also prove off-shell invariance of the equilibrium--storage--multiplier sector under an equilibrium-sector partial Legendre transformation; invariance of the full augmented action is not claimed. For Fourier heat conduction, we derive a weighted drift identity and a per-step energy-drift bound for the energy-representation three-term incremental functional. In one spatial dimension, a small-time-step estimate yields a uniform $H^1$ bound and a discrete $L^2(0,T_f;H^2)$ bound, leading to cumulative $O(δt)$ drift over fixed time intervals. A conservative mixed discontinuous Galerkin (DG0)--Raviart--Thomas (RT0) discretization with fully implicit conductivity $κ(T)=1+T^2$ preserves discrete energy to roundoff. A separate lumped-mass piecewise-linear benchmark reproduces the predicted finite-step drift.

papers.title: Neural Networks with Local Converging Inputs for Solving the 3D Stokes Equations on Unstructured Meshes: Novel Techniques and Advances
papers.abstract: Neural-network surrogates for fluid-flow PDEs usually learn the solution globally, which requires large networks and many high-fidelity training simulations. Neural networks with local converging inputs (NNLCI) instead work locally. They predict the high-fidelity solution at a point from two converging coarse-grid solutions sampled near that point, which keeps the network small, needs little training data, and generalizes across geometries. Here, the two low-fidelity meshes, LF1 and LF2, have on average about 300 and 730 tetrahedra, compared with about 155,000 in the high-fidelity mesh (HF). In this work, we develop an NNLCI framework for three-dimensional Stokes equations on unstructured tetrahedral meshes and introduce two techniques for building local inputs near complex curved boundaries. First, input patches may extend beyond the boundary, with the outside values obtained from a local least-squares fit, so that every high-fidelity point can be predicted, including those next to the wall. Second, the local mesh spacing is estimated from neighboring centroids, which sets the stencil size consistently on unstructured meshes. For pipe flows with one to three bumps, including a circumferentially rotated bump, NNLCI reduces the relative $L^2$ error of the finer low-fidelity solution by $90\%$ to $94\%$, evaluated at all high-fidelity points. Both techniques carry over to other NNLCI problems with smooth solutions on point-cloud discretizations.

papers.title: On the average eccentricity of Eulerian and bipartite Eulerian digraphs
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be an Eulerian digraph of order $n$ and minimum degree $δ$. We prove that the average eccentricity of $D$ satisfies $\avec(D) \leq \frac{3n}{δ+1}$, and that $\avec(D) \leq \frac{2n}δ+2$ if $D$ is bipartite. We show that both bounds are best possible apart from an additive constant and the $δ+1$ versus $δ+2$ gap (resp.\ the $δ$ versus $δ+1$ gap in the bipartite case), where the average eccentricity of the extremal examples shows that $\avec = \frac{3n}{δ+2}-2$ in general and $\avec = \frac{2n}{δ+1}-\frac{5}{2}$ in the bipartite case for $δ\geq 2$. We further conjecture that these values are the true maxima up to an additive constant (for $δ\geq 3$ in the bipartite case).

papers.title: Forward and pullback attraction under worst-case and ergodic exponents in a predator-prey model with bounded random refuge
papers.abstract: We consider a predator-prey system with logistic prey, Holling type II response and a prey refuge fluctuating randomly within a band, driven by a bounded transformation of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. Bounded noise yields a deterministic compact set attracting forward uniformly in the realisation, alongside the random pullback attractor, and we compare the two. The smallest such deterministic set, the minimal uniform attracting set, is the kernel of the control system in which the accessible fraction is any measurable band-valued function, and it meets the coexistence region exactly when the upper worst-case invasion exponent of the predator is positive, whereas the pullback attractor is governed by the ergodic invasion exponent, which decides the predator's fate pathwise. When the predator becomes extinct, the closure of the union of the fibres of the pullback attractor equals the minimal uniform attracting set if and only if the upper worst-case exponent is nonpositive, and otherwise the inclusion is strict and the latter is invariant under no realisation. When the predator persists, the essential closure of the union of the fibres contains, for every frozen environment in which the predator invades, the equilibrium or a periodic orbit of the frozen system, and every state the control system can reach from them. The predator is uniformly persistent when the lower worst-case exponent is positive and almost surely not when it is negative. The ergodic exponent lies below its deterministic counterpart by an amount comparable to the curvature of the response times the variance of the accessible fraction.

papers.title: Weak $λ$-sets and almost-normal Isbell-Mrówka spaces
papers.abstract: We determine the least cardinality of a set of reals that is not a weak $λ$-set, proving that it is $\max\{\mathfrak b,\mathfrak s\}$, where $\mathfrak b$ and $\mathfrak s$ are the bounding and splitting numbers. We prove that if $\mathfrak s<\mathfrak b$, then every first countable weak $λ$-space is a $λ$-space. We also show, relative to the consistency of $\mathsf{ZFC}$, that the existence of a weak $λ$-set that is not a $λ$-set is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}+\mathfrak b=\mathfrak s$. In particular, we show that in the model obtained by adding $ω_2$ Cohen reals over a model of $\mathsf{CH}$, every weak $λ$-set is a $λ$-set. Finally, we construct an almost-normal MAD family under $\mathsf{CH}$ and show that no such family exists under $\mathsf{OCA}_{\mathrm T}+\mathfrak{ap}>ω_1$. Thus, the existence of an almost-normal MAD family is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}$.

papers.title: A uniform lower bound for logarithmic Trudinger-Moser suprema in dimension $N\ge3$
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be the unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge2$, and let $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)$ denote the critical Trudinger-Moser supremum of Calanchi and Ruf for radial functions in the Sobolev space with logarithmic weight $(-\log|x|)^{β(N-1)}$, $0\leβ<1$. We prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)>(2N-\frac25)|B|$ for every $β\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge 3$. This lower bound is uniform in $β$ and lies strictly above the upper bound $|B|\big(1+e^{1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1{N-1}}\big)$ for the concentration level obtained by Carleson-Chang for $β=0$ and, for $β>0$, by Roy for $N=2$ and by Roy and Nguyen for $N\ge 3$. As a consequence, we prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)$ is attained for every $β\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge3$, which was previously known only for $β>0$ small enough. For $N=2$, the existence of extremals for every $β\in [0, 1)$ was recently obtained by de Oliveira.

papers.title: The stochastic phase field crystal equation with conservative space-time white noise: well-posedness, regularity and existence of a density
papers.abstract: We study the phase field crystal equation $\partial_tu=Δ[(1+Δ)^2u+u^3-\varepsilon u]+σ\partial_x\dot W$ on $[0,π]$ with the boundary conditions $\partial_xu=\partial_x^3u=\partial_x^5u=0$ at $x=0,π$, perturbed by a conservative space-time white noise. This sixth order equation is the standard model for crystal growth at atomic length scales and diffusive time scales, and the conservative noise is the form of thermal fluctuations used in the physics literature. We prove that for every initial condition in $H^1$ there exists a unique global mild solution, continuous in space and time, which preserves the mean and whose supremum has finite moments of all orders. We determine its Hölder regularity: away from $t=0$, it is Hölder continuous in time with any exponent smaller than $1/4$, and $C^1$ in space with a spatial derivative which is Hölder continuous with any exponent smaller than $1/2$. Finally, using Malliavin calculus and a localization argument, we prove that for $σ\neq0$ the law of $u(t,x)$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure for every $t>0$ and every $x$. A specific feature of the model is a second neutral mode of the linear operator, besides the constant mode, which requires a separate treatment in the a priori estimates.

papers.title: The Herzog--Schönheim Conjecture for Solvable Groups
papers.abstract: The Herzog--Schönheim conjecture states that if a group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, cosets of subgroups, then two of these subgroups have the same index. We prove the conjecture for all solvable groups, finite or infinite. Sun's bound on unions of cosets, applied in a quotient, is combined with divisibility restrictions on local indices relative to the subgroup generated by the $p$-elements, where $p$ is the largest prime divisor of the order of a minimal counterexample. These restrictions are obtained by counting fixed points in a primitive solvable quotient. This suffices except at the prime $7$, where the counting bound narrowly fails and an additional overlap argument is needed. The proof has been formalized in Lean~4 with mathlib.

papers.title: Frequency shifts: non-soficity, absence of specification and intrinsic ergodicity
papers.abstract: For $p_c\in(0,1)$, the frequency shift $Σ(p_c)\subset\{0,1\}^{\N}$, introduced by Becker and Baraviera, is the closure of the shift orbits of the set of sequences in which a symbol $1$ is followed by $1$ exactly when the density of ones up to that position does not exceed $p_c$. We show that $Σ(p_c)$ is never sofic and never has the (weak) specification property. For $p_c=\frac{k}{k+1}$, with $k\ge1$, we describe $Σ(p_c)$ completely: $Σ(\frac12)$ is the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^m\}_{m\ge1}$, while for $k\ge2$ the shift $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is not transitive, but every invariant probability measure is supported on the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^{km}\}_{m\ge1}$. For every $k \ge 1$, the topological entropy of $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is $\frac{\log2}{k+1}$, and, using the Climenhaga--Thompson criterion, we prove that $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is intrinsically ergodic.

papers.title: Higher-order Sobolev stability and temporal decay estimate for the tropical climate model with small $H^1$ data
papers.abstract: We study the stability and temporal decay of solutions to the two-dimensional tropical climate model with Laplacian dissipation in both velocity equations and no thermal diffusion. For initial data in $H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ ($s \geq 1$) with sufficiently small $H^1$ norm, we establish a unique global solution satisfying uniform $H^s$ bounds and time-integrated estimates for the velocity and temperature. The smallness is independent of $s$, and the higher Sobolev norms of the initial data need not be small. Furthermore, without additional spatial integrability or negative-order regularity of the initial data, we prove that the $\dot H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ norms of the solutions are $o(t^{- s / 2})$ as $t \to \infty$. We also show that this decay rate is sharp: no additional decay factor tending to zero works for all such initial data.

papers.title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
papers.abstract: Given a graph $Γ$ with vertex set $V(Γ)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $Γ$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $Γ\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the \emph{connected zero forcing number} $Z_C(Γ)$. A \emph{connected zero forcing polynomial} of a finite graph $Γ$ is a monic polynomial $Z_C^Γ(x) \;=\; \sum_{k} a_k x^k$, where $a_k$ counts the number of connected zero forcing sets of $Γ$ of size $k$, which we denote by $Z_C(Γ,k)$. In this paper, we find the connected zero forcing polynomial of any finite tree $T$. We then establish sharp lower bounds for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices. We also identify a family of trees, which we call uniform trees, and we prove that for any tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, there exists a uniform tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, whose connected zero forcing polynomial bounds as an upper bound, the connected zero forcing polynomial of the tree coefficient wise. Again for $2\leq p\leq 4$, we establish a sharp upper bound for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices.

papers.title: Holomorphic Isometric Embeddings of the Unit Disk into the Symmetrized Bidisk
papers.abstract: We give a complete characterization of the holomorphic isometric embeddings $F:(\mathbb{D},k\,ds^2)\rightarrow (\mathbb{G}_2,ds^2)$ of the unit disk into the symmetrized bidisk with respect to the Bergman metric up to a scalar constant. We show that the isometric constant $k$ can take only the values $k=1$ and $k=3$. For $k=3$, we prove that $(2z,z^2)$ is the unique isometry up to a reparametrization. For $k=1$, we construct an isometric embedding which intersects the royal variety at a single point and does not admit a holomorphic lift to the bidisk via the symmetrization map. We further show that this isometric embedding is unique up to reparametrizations. Finally, none of the isometries are totally geodesic.

papers.title: Unramified case of Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms
papers.abstract: The Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms asserts that any rationally isotropic nondegenerate quadratic form over a semilocal regular domain with $2$ invertible is isotropic. We prove the Colliot-Thélène conjecture for semilocal regular domains that are geometrically regular over a discrete valuation ring with $2$ invertible. In particular, this includes unramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, where $p\neq 2$.

papers.title: Taylor Formulas for H-structures
papers.abstract: We give a uniform second-order Taylor formula for tensorial Riemannian $H$-structures in Riemannian normal coordinates whose initial frame is $H$-adapted. For a defining multi-tensor $ξ$ with intrinsic torsion $T$, the linear coefficient is $T_q\diamondξ$, and the quadratic coefficient features the covariant derivative of $T$, its iterated diamond action, and curvature. The formula applies componentwise to tensors of arbitrary type and recovers the known $G_2$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(7)$ expansions. We also give the almost Hermitian specialisation and prove that vanishing of the complete second-order torsion contribution forces the intrinsic torsion to vanish at the centre of the coordinates.

papers.title: DMP-Oriented Anisotropic Mesh Adaptation for SUPG Finite Element Methods for Time-Dependent Convection-Diffusion Problems
papers.abstract: We study discrete bound preservation for fully discrete piecewise-linear streamline upwind Petrov--Galerkin (SUPG) finite element approximations of time-dependent convection--diffusion equations on anisotropic triangular meshes. Although the continuous homogeneous-source problem satisfies a parabolic maximum principle, SUPG approximations can exhibit nonphysical undershoots and overshoots. We derive sufficient nodal discrete maximum principle (DMP) conditions that account for the stabilized mass matrix, the combined effects of physical and streamline diffusion, time-step restrictions, and transfer between successive meshes. The analysis identifies a SUPG-effective diffusion tensor and motivates an anisotropic metric aligned with its inverse. We construct a combined metric that retains the effective-tensor geometry while introducing solution-dependent mesh density through recovered Hessian information. The resulting DMP conditions provide a theoretical basis for anisotropic mesh design. Numerical experiments for time-dependent transport problems with isotropic and moderately anisotropic diffusion demonstrate that, under mass-compatible limited SUPG stabilization, the combined metric substantially reduces measured undershoots relative to other methods at matched nominal mesh budgets, although improved bound behavior can carry an accuracy penalty. A controlled tensor--density comparison in the anisotropic transport test supports a contribution from the effective tensor beyond the prescribed mesh density.

papers.title: Improving Analytic Constants via Interpretable AI-Guided Lean Proof Refinement
papers.abstract: AI agents are increasingly capable of discovering new mathematical results, yet their reasoning and generated proofs can be difficult to understand and verify. We introduce an interpretable framework for AI-guided mathematical discovery, focused on improving quantitative bounds on analytic constants. Our key insight is that existing proofs often contain slack in intermediate lemmas, which can be tightened without reconstructing the entire argument. To exploit this structure, we represent proofs as partially-formalized Lean blueprints: human-interpretable dependency graphs of definitions, lemmas, and theorems. An AI agent then iteratively refines the Lean code while preserving the blueprint's dependency structure, allowing local improvements to automatically propagate to a verified final bound. This interpretable structure allows humans to inspect the agent's refinements and understand how local improvements propagate to the final theorem. For Grothendieck's constant ($\mathcal{K}_G$), we obtain $$ \mathcal{K}_G \leq \fracπ{2\log(1+\sqrt{2})} - 10^{-17}, $$ an explicit numerical improvement over Krivine's 1977 bound. For Korenblum's constant ($\mathcal{K}_K$), we obtain $$ \mathcal{K}_K \geq 0.356565, $$ improving Wang's 2025 bound of $0.3554$. Our experiments demonstrate the potential of both partial formalization and iterative agentic refinement for interpretable mathematical discovery.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Robust Blinded Sample Size Re-estimation Based on Nuisance Parameters
papers.abstract: Blinded sample size re-estimation aims to mitigate uncertainty in nuisance parameters at the design stage while preserving the integrity of the trial. It allows the required sample size to be updated without revealing treatment assignments and thereby reduces the risk of an inappropriate sample size. Although numerous procedures have been proposed for different outcome types, a unified framework is still lacking. We therefore develop a general framework for blinded sample size re-estimation based on nuisance parameters. Within this general framework, we develop robust methods to reduce the influence of extreme observations. The proposed framework combines asymptotically linear estimators for the parameter of interest with robust Z-estimators for nuisance parameters, thereby unifying a broad class of existing procedures through different choices of estimating functions. We also propose a general principle for constructing nuisance parameters that can be estimated from blinded data. The proposed framework is supported by asymptotic theory showing that the type I error rate converges to the nominal level under regularity conditions. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method maintains reliable type I error control across a range of settings, including contaminated data and small pilot sample sizes. Compared with existing blinded and unblinded methods, the proposed framework is more flexible and less sensitive to outliers. A clinical trial application illustrates its practical utility.

papers.title: Dominant permutations, positive mixed-variable formulas, and product-splitting equivalence for (double) Schubert polynomials
papers.abstract: We present new positive combinatorial formulas for triple Schubert coefficients in mixed-variable products of double Schubert polynomials, $\mathfrak{S}_u(x;y)\mathfrak{S}_v(x;z)$, expressed in the $\mathfrak{S}_w(x;y)$ basis, in the case where $u$ is dominant. This result complements earlier results where $v$ was assumed dominant. To generalize further, we introduce a relation on permutations that we call ``domination,'' under which dominant permutations dominate all others. When $u$ dominates $w$, we obtain an explicit positive formula for $c^w_{u,v}(y;z)$, which in particular yields positivity when $u$ and $v$ have separated descents. In addition to these new positivity results, we establish a product--splitting equivalence for double Schubert polynomials, relating triple Schubert coefficients to splitting coefficients. This equivalence highlights structural symmetries and provides reduction methods for computing coefficients that are otherwise difficult to access. Taken together, these results extend the range of double Schubert polynomial products for which positivity can be established combinatorially and yield explicit formulas that can be implemented computationally.

papers.title: Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices
papers.abstract: We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.

papers.title: An Introduction to Applied Probability and Stochastic Processes: Open Lecture Notes
papers.abstract: These open lecture notes provide a broad introduction to measure-theoretic probability and stochastic processes, with a focus on applications. Topics include probability spaces, conditional expectation, generating and characteristic functions, Markov chains in discrete and continuous time, convergence of random variables, Brownian motion, stochastic calculus, stochastic differential equations and their connection to partial differential equations, jump diffusions, stochastic control, optimal stopping, and Monte Carlo methods. Most chapters include exercises, and solutions are provided. The notes were written for a two-quarter course for first-year PhD students in applied mathematics, and should also be useful to graduate students in statistics, engineering, economics and finance. The LaTeX source is freely available on GitHub under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license, and readers are encouraged to fork the notes and contribute corrections, improvements, and new material.

papers.title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
papers.abstract: The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.

papers.title: Compact metric spaces as exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces
papers.abstract: The class of compact metric spaces (metric spaces which induce a compact topology), despite being an important class of metric spaces, is not closed under many natural constructions. For instance, infinite metric products of compact metric spaces will often fail to induce a compact topology, while on the other hand, the topological product of any family of compact metric spaces is always a compact topological space, evidencing a discrepancy between topological and metric products. The notion of metric compact Hausdorff space -- compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with a lower semi-continuous metric -- provides a class of spaces which keep track of metric data and topological data separately, thereby forming a complete and cocomplete category, while including all compact metric spaces. Our main contribution is that this inclusion can be characterised via universal property: the compact metric spaces are the exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces with respect to a natural monoidal structure on the respective category.

papers.title: Absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology
papers.abstract: We construct absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology, for real 3-manifolds such that the image of the fixed point set in the quotient is nullhomologous. This allows us to fix the sign of Miyazawa's degree invariant. Our construction uses a mod-two index-theoretic correction term, the Arf invariant.

papers.title: Diophantine definitions of nonsplitting for central simple algebras over global fields
papers.abstract: For every global field and every fixed degree, we prove that the structure constants defining nonsplit central simple algebras form a diophantine set. We formulate a local witness principle separating reliable localization, exact localization, and local detection. Adapted Kummer and Artin--Schreier presentations provide a common construction of witnesses through a uniform radical formula and ramification matching. This gives an independent proof of the non-characteristic case, which also follows from Morrison's nonnorm theorem, and treats the characteristic-degree case by the same method. We recover prime-degree nonnorm definability and give applications to rootless polynomials, anisotropic quadratic forms in all characteristics, and generalized Severi--Brauer varieties.

papers.title: Sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints for composite hypotheses
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints, where multiple independent data sources are observed over time, but only a limited subset can be sampled at each instant. The objective is to identify the anomalous sources while controlling the probabilities of at least one false alarm and at least one missed detection below prescribed levels. An identification policy must jointly determine when to stop sampling, which sources to declare anomalous, and how to allocate observations across sources under the sampling constraints. We seek policies that minimize the expected time to decision to a first-order asymptotic approximation as the error probabilities vanish. The observations from each source follow an unknown density belonging to one of two disjoint sets, corresponding to regular and anomalous behavior. Focusing on a nonparametric framework, which allows greater flexibility in modeling regular and anomalous statistical behavior, we establish general conditions for asymptotic optimality and provide a unified characterization of asymptotically optimal policies for composite hypothesis testing under sampling constraints. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed policies, and the robustness of the nonparametric framework.

papers.title: Positivity Proofs for Third-Order Holonomic Sequences via Differences Scaled by Rational Functions
papers.abstract: We study the positivity of sequences $f$ that satisfy a third-order holonomic recurrence $f(n+3)= P_2(n) f(n+2) + P_1(n) f(n+1) + P_0(n) f(n)$ whose coefficients $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ are rational functions in $\R(x)$. We provide a sufficient condition on $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ for the recurrence to admit a solution all but finitely many terms of which are positive, and whose positivity is robust under small perturbations of the initial values. This sufficient condition is also a necessary condition for a subclass of the recurrences. By developing the proof of this sufficient condition, for another subclass of the recurrences, we show that it is decidable whether all the terms of a given sequence are positive for any initial values outside an exceptional plane. It is common to construct a positivity certificate, which guarantees the positivity of a solution, to show this kind of decidability. In this paper, we construct a new type of positivity certificate via the $S$-scaled difference $f(n+1) - S(n) f(n)$ for a suitable $S \in \R(x)$. This result partially improves the work by Ibrahim and Salvy.

papers.title: Vertex splitting, global rigidity and nondegenerate equilibrium stresses
papers.abstract: We prove Whiteley's conjecture that every nontrivial vertex split of a generically globally rigid graph preserves generic global rigidity in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), for all \(d\geq1\). We give two proofs of the stronger assertion that the split graph is infinitesimally rigid at every generic coincident realisation of the two split vertices. Both proofs use maximum-rank equilibrium stress matrices and then apply the coincident-rigidity criterion of Cruickshank, Jackson and Tanigawa. The second construction also shows that every generically globally rigid graph admits a nondegenerate equilibrium stress of maximum rank at every generic realisation, establishing a conjecture of Jordán and Tanigawa.

papers.title: On the Bendixson criterion for attractors of dynamical systems in metric spaces
papers.abstract: We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S. Muldowney to Banach spaces. First, we give a concise proof of the criterion for general dynamical systems (semiflows, mappings, cocycles) in metric spaces using Čech cohomology. This approach allows for a significant weakening of previously known conditions while simultaneously resolving existing misunderstandings. Second, for compact invariant sets of semiflows that are topologically one-dimensional and possess zero first cohomology (e.g., attracting a superset with zero first cohomology), we prove that any chain recurrent point within the invariant set must be an equilibrium. In the proof, we construct a global strict Lyapunov function using Whitney-Bebutov sections. Third, we generalize and refine R.A. Smith's theorem concerning the finiteness of the set of fixed points for analytic mappings, as well as M.L. Cartwright's theorems on to almost periodic flows.

papers.title: An Optimal First-Order Active-Hull Method for Convex Composite Hölder Smooth Optimization
papers.abstract: We consider the problem (P): ${\min}_{x\in \mathbb{R}^n}\, f(x)+g(x)$ under the Euclidean geometry, where $f$ is convex and $(M,ν)$-Hölder smooth on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and $g$ is proper, closed and convex on $\mathbb{R}^n$, admits a generalized linear minimization oracle (GLMO), and has bounded domain with diameter $D$. An first-order active-hull (AH) method has access to both the first-order oracle (FO) of $f$ and the GLMO of $g$, and outputs a point that lies in the convex hull of all the past GLMO returns. We propose a new first-order AH method for solving (P), which is based on our newly developed ``recentered homotopy smoothing framework''. We show that in the high-dimensional regime, this method achieves the optimal FO and GLMO complexties simultaneously for all $ν\in[0,1]$.

papers.title: Sharp Constants and Maximizers for Weighted Moser--Trudinger Inequalities on the Heisenberg Group
papers.abstract: This article concerns Moser-Trudinger inequalities on the entire Heisenberg group, focusing on sharp constants, maximizers, and applications to subelliptic PDEs. We address several questions on the existence of maximizers in the singular case $0<β<Q$, where the singular weight yields compactness. We first establish an Adimurthi-Druet-type weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality without blow-up analysis and determine its sharp constant. We also prove its equivalence with the critical weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality. For the subcritical inequality of Lam, Lu and Tang \cite{Lam-Lu-Tang-2014}, we obtain two-sided asymptotic bounds near the sharp threshold and prove existence of maximizers in a suitable regime. This inequality also yields insight into borderline Sobolev theory and an asymptotic Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg interpolation-type inequality. We further establish a weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality under inhomogeneous norm constraints and prove its equivalence with the subcritical inequality, thereby characterizing the associated supremum and its maximizers. An improved subcritical weighted inequality is also derived, and its maximization problem is shown to admit a maximizer. Finally, these inequalities are applied to normalized subelliptic equations driven by the $Q$-sub-Laplacian with nonlinearities having singular critical exponential growth at infinity. We prove the existence of nontrivial ground states for every prescribed mass $a>0$, provided the nonlinearity is sufficiently large in a suitable sense depending on $a$.

papers.title: New lower bounds for even and odd values of the partition function
papers.abstract: Let $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ denote the numbers of integers $0\leq n< X$ for which the ordinary partition function $p(n)$ is odd and even, respectively. The Parkin--Shanks conjecture predicts that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ are both asymptotic to $X/2$. Bellaïche and Nicolas proved that $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X} \log \log X$, while Zheng, building on work of Ono and Swaminathan, recently proved that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X}$. We improve both bounds simultaneously by proving $\min\{N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X), N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\}\gg X^{3/4}/(\log X \log \log X)$.

papers.title: Optimal Byzantine-resilient Federated Learning with User-level Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: Real-world deployment of federated learning (FL) requires resilience against adversarial clients and data privacy.
