papers.abstract: One considers quasihomogeneous isolated singularities of hypersurfaces in arbitrary dimensions through the lenses of three apparently quite apart themes: syzygies, singularity invariants, and foliations. In the first of these, one adds to the well-known result of Saito a syzygy-theoretic characterization of a quasihomogeneous singularity affording an effective computational criterion. In the second theme, one explores the Milnor-Tjurina difference number from a commutative algebra viewpoint. Building on the Briancon-Skoda theorem and exponent, we extend previously known inequalities by Dimca and Greuel to arbitrary dimension and provide algebraic formulas involving the syzygy-theoretic part and reduction exponents. In the last theme, one recovers and brings to algebraic light a result of Camacho and Movasati by establishing a couple of characterizations of quasihomogeneous isolated singularities in terms of the generators of the module of invariant vector fields.

papers.title: Bridging Batch and Streaming Estimations to System Identification under Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: System identification in modern engineering systems faces emerging challenges from unanticipated adversarial attacks beyond existing detection mechanisms. In this work, we obtain a provably accurate estimate of the Markov parameter matrix of order $k$ to identify partially observed linear systems, in which the probability $p$ of having an attack at each time is smaller than $0.5$. We show that given the batch data accumulated up to time $T^*$, the $\ell_2$-norm estimator achieves an error with stepwise exponential decay as the attack probability $p$ decreases. Furthermore, low-dimensional attack structures can decouple the exponential decay order from the attack probability $p$, achieving an error decay that scales with $T^*$. We then propose a stochastic projected subgradient descent algorithm on streaming data that produces an estimate at each time $t<T^*$, in which case the expected estimation error proves to be the larger of $\mathcal{O}(k/\sqrt{t})$ and the baseline error of the $\ell_2$-norm estimator at $T^*$. This stochastic approach illustrates how non-smooth estimators can leverage first-order methods despite lacking recursive formulas. Finally, we integrate batch and streaming estimations to recover the Hankel matrix using the appropriate estimates of the Markov parameter matrix, which enables the synthesis of a robust adaptive controller based on the estimated balanced truncated model under adversarial attacks.

papers.title: On the Rate of Gaussian Approximation for Online Linear Regression Problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of Gaussian approximation for the online linear regression task. We derive the corresponding rates for the setting of a constant stepsize and study the explicit dependence of the convergence rate on the problem dimension $d$ and quantities related to the design matrix. When the number of iterations $n$ is known in advance, our results yield a normal approximation rate of order $\sqrt{\log{n}/n}$, provided that the sample size $n$ is large enough.

papers.title: Three-Neighbour Bootstrap Percolation in Thin Three-Dimensional Grids
papers.abstract: We improve the status of the problem of determining minimum-sized percolating sets in $a \times b \times c$ grids under the $3$-neighbour process. Using several new constructions, we show that optimal percolating sets exist whenever $\min(a,b,c) \ge 7$. As an important step toward this, we also show that all grids with $\min(a,b,c) \ge 4$ have a percolating set whose size exactly achieves the lower bound $(ab+ac+bc)/3$ whenever this value is an integer.

papers.title: Faster Linear Algebra Algorithms with Structured Random Matrices
papers.abstract: To achieve the greatest possible speed, practitioners regularly implement randomized algorithms for low-rank approximation and least-squares regression with structured dimension reduction maps. Despite significant research effort, basic questions remain about the design and analysis of randomized linear algebra algorithms that employ structured random matrices. This paper develops a new perspective on structured dimension reduction, based on the oblivious subspace injection (OSI) property. The OSI property is a relatively weak assumption on a random matrix that holds when the matrix preserves the length of vectors on average and, with high probability, does not annihilate any vector in a low-dimensional subspace. With the OSI abstraction, the analysis of a randomized linear algebra algorithm factors into two parts: (i) proving that the algorithm works when implemented with an OSI; and (ii) proving that a given random matrix model has the OSI property. This paper develops both parts of the program. First, it analyzes standard randomized algorithms for low-rank approximation and least-squares regression under the OSI assumption. Second, it identifies many examples of OSIs, including random sparse matrices, randomized trigonometric transforms, and random matrices with tensor product structure. These theoretical results imply faster, near-optimal runtimes for several fundamental linear algebra tasks. The paper also provides guidance on implementation, along with empirical evidence that structured random matrices offer exemplary performance for a range of synthetic problems and contemporary scientific applications.

papers.title: SAGE: A Set-based Adaptive Gradient Estimator
papers.abstract: We introduce a set membership perspective on gradient estimation for black-box scalar functions, in which the gradient is not approximated as a single point estimate but characterised as a member of a set of admissible gradients consistent with available function samples and regularity assumptions. Bounds on gradient uncertainty, obtained from standard multivariate Taylor series results, are used to represent this admissible set through linear inequalities, making gradient uncertainty explicit and directly exploitable. Building on this formulation, we propose an adaptive strategy to refine the admissible gradient set to a desired precision by selectively acquiring new samples only when necessary. The resulting framework naturally accommodates function evaluations affected by noise with finite but a priori unknown bounds, yields the theoretical best attainable precision of the gradient set, and provides the optimal sampling distance from the point of interest to maximise information gain during refinement. Within this framework, we introduce the Set-Based Adaptive Gradient Estimator (SAGE), which extracts an estimate of the true gradient from the admissible set whilst preserving high sample efficiency and robustness to noise. Numerical experiments on large collections of random gradient-query points, as well as in the context of a first-order optimisation method, compared the performance of SAGE against commonly used gradient estimators from the literature. Our results show that SAGE achieved competitive gradient accuracy across noise levels without requiring any a priori noise characterisation. In a first-order optimisation setting, noise-informed competitors can outperform SAGE when such characterisation is available. Nevertheless, SAGE remained broadly competitive, making it particularly attractive in settings where noise characterisation is impractical to obtain.

papers.title: Flexible $3$-valent graphs of arbitrary girth
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a finite connected flexible $3$-valent vertex-transitive graph of girth $\ell$ for every integer $\ell \geq 3$.

papers.title: Optimal Sobolev embeddings for generalized Lorentz-Zygmund spaces
papers.abstract: This work deals with embeddings, of any integer order, for generalized Lorentz-Zygmund-Sobolev spaces on Euclidean domains satisfying minimal regularity assumptions. Explicit rearrangement-invariant, Hölder, Morrey and Campanato optimal target spaces are exhibited.

papers.title: Shrinkers of the area-preserving curve-shortening flow: Classification and saddle-point property
papers.abstract: We consider homothetic evolutions of the area-preserving curve-shortening flow (APCSF), that is, classical curve-shortening flow with an additional non-local forcing term. By using known results on $λ$-curves, we prove the existence of non-circular shrinkers for this flow. In our first main result, we present a full classification of such curves, similar to the well-known Abresch-Langer classification for shrinkers of curve-shortening flow. Finally, we also deduce a saddle-point property for all non-circular (APCSF)-shrinkers analogous to the known saddle-point property of Abresch-Langer curves.

papers.title: The Modified Camassa--Holm Equation with Step-Like Boundary Conditions: A Characterization of Existence
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the modified Camassa-Holm equation \[ u_t+\left((u^2-u_x^2)m\right)_x=0,\quad m:= u-u_{xx}, \quad t>0,\ \ -\infty<x<+\infty \] subject to the step-like initial data: $u(x,0)\to A_1$ as $x\to-\infty$ and $u(x,0)\to A_2$ as $x\to+\infty$, where $0<A_1<A_2$. First, using the Riemann--Hilbert approach, we establish the global solvability of the corresponding problem in the reciprocal $(y,t)$-variables. Then the reconstruction in the original $(x,t)$-variables is obtained under a positivity condition expressed in terms of the solution of the associated Riemann--Hilbert problem.

papers.title: Higher path groupoids and the holonomy of formal power series connections
papers.abstract: Building on ideas of Kohno, we develop a framework for the construction of higher holonomy functors via the transport of formal power series connections. Using these techniques, we obtain functors from the path groupoid, the path 2-groupoid, and the path 3-groupoid of a manifold. We show that the resulting higher holonomy functors can detect non-trivial classes in higher homotopy groups. As an application, we construct a Gray functor from the path 3-groupoid of the configuration space of $m$ points in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n\geqslant 4$ and compute its restriction to 3-tracks with constant boundary when $n=4$.

papers.title: Hodge-Riemann polynomials
papers.abstract: We show that Schur classes of ample vector bundles on smooth projective varieties satisfy Hodge-Riemann relations on $H^{p,q}$ under the assumption that $H^{p-2,q-2}$ vanishes. More generally, we study Hodge-Riemann polynomials, which are partially symmetric polynomials that produce cohomology classes satisfying the Hodge-Riemann property when evaluated at Chern roots of ample vector bundles. In the case of line bundles and in bidegree $(1,1)$, these are precisely the nonzero dually Lorentzian polynomials. We prove various properties of Hodge-Riemann polynomials, confirming predictions and answering questions of Ross and Toma. As an application, we show that the derivative sequence of any product of Schur polynomials is Schur log-concave, confirming conjectures of Ross and Wu.

papers.title: PPO in the Fisher-Rao geometry
papers.abstract: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is widely used in reinforcement learning due to its strong empirical performance, yet it lacks formal guarantees for policy improvement and convergence. PPO's clipped surrogate objective is motivated by a lower bound on linearization of the value function in flat geometry setting. We derive a tighter surrogate objective and introduce Fisher-Rao PPO (FR-PPO) by leveraging the Fisher-Rao (FR) geometry. Our scheme provides strong theoretical guarantees, including monotonic policy improvement. In the direct parametrization setting, we show that FR-PPO achieves sub-linear convergence, and for parametrized policies we further obtain sub-linear convergence up to the compatible function approximation error. Finally, although our primary focus is theoretical, we also demonstrate empirically that FR-PPO can be implemented as a drop-in replacement for PPO and achieves performance comparable to PPO across a range of standard reinforcement learning tasks.

papers.title: The only Class 0 Flower snark is the smallest
papers.abstract: In graph pebbling, pebbles are distributed across the vertices of a graph. A pebbling move consists of removing two pebbles from one vertex and adding one pebble to an adjacent vertex. The pebbling number is the minimum number $t$ such that, regardless of how the $t$ pebbles are initially placed, it is always possible to perform a sequence of moves that results in at least one pebble placed on any specified target vertex. Graphs whose pebbling number is equal to the number of vertices are called Class~$0$ and provide a challenging set of graphs that resist being characterized. In this note, we answer a question recently proposed by the pioneering study on the pebbling number of snark graphs: we prove that the smallest Flower snark $J_3$ is Class~$0$, establishing that $J_3$ in fact is the only Class~$0$ Flower snark. that systematically reduce the space of pebble configurations. Our bound-based approach shows particular promise for diameter $3$ graphs, where the neighborhood structure remains sufficiently constrained to enable effective analysis.

papers.title: Algebraic Zhou valuations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we generalize Zhou valuations, originally defined on complex domains, to the framework of general schemes. We demonstrate that an algebraic version of the Jonsson--Mustaţă conjecture is equivalent to the statement that every Zhou valuation is quasi-monomial. By introducing a mixed version of jumping numbers and Tian functions associated with valuations, we obtain characterizations of a valuation being a Zhou valuation or computing some jumping number using the Tian functions. Furthermore, we establish the correspondence between Zhou valuations in algebraic settings and their counterparts in analytic settings.

papers.title: Smooth atlas stratified spaces, K-Homology Orientations, and Gysin maps, Part 1
papers.abstract: We introduce smooth atlas stratified spaces. We show that this class is closed under cartesian products; consequently, it is possible to define fiber bundles of smooth atlas stratified spaces. We describe the resolution of such a space to a manifold with fibered corners and use this result in order to prove that the class of smooth atlas stratified spaces coincides with that of Thom-Mather stratified spaces. We then consider Witt pseudomanifolds (such as singular complex algebraic varieties) where it is well-known that a bordism invariant signature is available and equal to the Fredholm index of a realization of the signature operator. To each oriented fiber bundle of stratified spaces, with Witt fibers, we assign a class in bivariant KK-theory (with 2 inverted). Kasparov multiplication by this element defines a Gysin map in analytic K-homology and one of our main results is that this Gysin map preserves the analytic signature class of Witt spaces. We prove in fact a more general result: functoriality for fiber bundles in the sense that if one fiber bundle is the composition of two others then the KK-class of the former is the Kasparov product of the classes of the latter. We also discuss this result for other Dirac-type operators satisfying an analytic Witt condition, for example the spin-Dirac operator on a fibration of psc-Witt spin pseudomanifolds. We next define the analytic Gysin map associated to an oriented normally non-singular inclusion of Witt spaces and prove that it also preserves the signature class. Finally, we relate the analytic signature class of a Witt space with the topological Siegel-Sullivan orientation. Specifically we show that if one applies the inverse of the second Adams operation to the Sullivan orientation and complexifies then one obtains our analytic signature class under the natural identification between analytic and topological K-homology.

papers.title: Existence and multiplicity of $L^2$-Normalized solutions for the periodic Schrödinger system of Hamiltonian type
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the following nonlinear Schrödinger system of Hamiltonian type \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{array}{l} -Δu+V(x)u=\partial_v H(x,u,v)+ωv,\ x \in \mathbb{R}^N, \\ -Δv+V(x)v=\partial_u H(x,u,v)+ωu,\ x \in \mathbb{R}^N, \\ \displaystyle\int_{\R^N}|z|^2dx=a^2, \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} where the potential function $V(x)$ is periodic, $z:=(u,v):\R^N\rightarrow \R\times\R$, $ω\in \R$ appears as a Lagrange multiplier, $a>0$ is a prescribed constant. The existence and multiplicity of $L^2$-normalized solutions for the above Schrödinger system are obtained. The proof combines a constrained variational reduction, compactness estimates, and a Ljusternik--Schnirelmann type multiplicity theorem. In addition, a bifurcation result is also given.

papers.title: Global patterns in signed permutations
papers.abstract: Global permutation patterns have recently been shown to characterize important properties of a Coxeter group. Here we study global patterns in the context of signed permutations, with both characterizing and enumerative results. Surprisingly, many properties of signed permutations may be characterized by avoidance of the same set of patterns as the corresponding properties in the symmetric group. We also extend previous enumerative work of Egge, and our work has connections to the Garfinkle--Barbasch--Vogan correspondence, the Erdős--Szekeres theorem, and well-known integer sequences.

papers.title: Phase diagram for intermittent maps
papers.abstract: This paper studies the phase diagram of a fixed Pomeau--Manneville, or intermittent, map under a varying Hölder continuous potential of fixed exponent. Depending on the exponent, there are either one or two thermodynamic phases. The \emph{intermittent} phase is characterized by a unique Gibbs state whose typical orbits alternate irregularly between time intervals spent near the neutral fixed point and chaotic excursions away from it. The stationary phase is characterized by the Dirac mass at the neutral fixed point being the unique Gibbs state. Above a threshold exponent, every potential belongs to the intermittent phase, so the phase diagram is trivial. At or below the threshold, the phase transition locus is a co-dimension 1 topological submanifold separating the two phases, and it coincides with the set of potentials at which the pressure function fails to be real-analytic. This paper also investigates the relationships between the phase transition locus, (persistent) phase transitions in temperature, and ground states. It highlights a connection between phase transitions in temperature and ergodic optimization.

papers.title: A structure and asymptotic preserving scheme for the quasineutral limit of the Vlasov-Poisson system
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a new numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system that is both asymptotically consistent and stable in the quasineutral regime, i.e. when the Debye length $λ$ is small compared to the characteristic spatial scale of the physical domain. Our approach consists in reformulating the Vlasov-Poisson system as a hyperbolic problem by applying a spectral expansion in the basis of Hermite functions in the velocity space and in designing a structure-preserving scheme for the time and spatial variables. Through this Hermite formulation, we establish a convergence result for the electric field toward its quasineutral limit together with explicit error estimates in $λ$. Following this path, we then propose a fully discrete numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system, inspired by the approach in arXiv:2306.14605, and rigorously prove that it is uniformly consistent in the quasineutral limit regime. Finally, we present several numerical simulations to illustrate the behavior of the proposed scheme. These results demonstrate the capability of our method to describe quasineutral plasmas, illustrate its stability and confirm its asymptotic preserving property.

papers.title: Averaging principle for rough slow-fast systems of level 3
papers.abstract: The averaging principle for slow-fast systems of various kind of stochastic (partial) differential equations has been extensively studied. An analogous result was shown for slow-fast systems of rough differential equations driven by random rough paths a few years ago and the study of ``rough slow-fast systems" seems to be gaining momentum now. In all known results, however, the driving rough paths are of level 2. In this paper we formulate rough slow-fast systems driven by random rough paths of level 3 and prove the strong averaging principle of Khas'minskii-type.

papers.title: Equivalence of synchronization states in the Kuramoto flow: a unified framework
papers.abstract: On the fiftieth anniversary of the Kuramoto model, synchronization remains a central paradigm for collective behavior in complex oscillator systems. While phase locking, frequency synchronization, and order-parameter coherence are widely used to characterize synchronization, their precise dynamical relationship has remained unclear, especially in finite-dimensional systems beyond mean-field limits. In this work, we show that, in the fully connected Kuramoto model, full phase locking, phase locking, frequency synchronization, and order-parameter synchronization are dynamically equivalent. Moreover, we demonstrate that the equivalence between phase locking and frequency synchronization is governed by a topology-independent mechanism and persists for generic symmetric coupling structures. These results provide a unified dynamical framework for synchronization and clarify the structural role of the Kuramoto order parameter.

papers.title: Langevin Monte-Carlo Provably Learns Depth Two Neural Nets at Any Size and Data
papers.abstract: In this note we prove that the Langevin Monte Carlo (LMC) algorithm can minimize the population risk of appropriately regularized depth-2 nets with no restrictions on the size of the net and for any choice of training data --- and we give non-asymptotic convergence rates for it. We achieve this via showing that in q-Renyi divergence, the iterates of LMC converge to the Gibbs distribution of certain Frobenius norm regularized losses for these nets --- in both classification and regression settings. The key technicality of the work is two-fold (a) to keep the amount of regularization needed be independent of the size of the net and (b) to obtain convergence rates that scale with just the Poincare constant of the corresponding Gibbs measure. This work synthesizes several recent observations about isoperimetry conditions under which LMC converges and that two-layer neural loss functions can always be regularized by a constant amount such that they satisfy the Villani conditions, and thus their Gibbs measures satisfy a Poincare inequality.

papers.title: On rigid regular graphs and a problem of Babai and Pultr
papers.abstract: A graph is rigid if it only admits the identity endomorphism. We show that for every $d\ge 3$ there exist infinitely many mutually rigid $d$-regular graphs of arbitrary odd girth $g\geq 7$. Moreover, we determine the minimum order of a rigid $d$-regular graph for every $d\ge 3$. This provides strong positive answers to a question of van der Zypen [https://mathoverflow.net/q/296483, https://mathoverflow.net/q/321108]. Further, we use our construction to show that every finite monoid is isomorphic to the endomorphism monoid of a regular graph. This solves a problem of Babai and Pultr [J. Comb. Theory, Ser. B, 1980].

papers.title: Operator level soft edge to bulk transition in $β$-ensembles via canonical systems
papers.abstract: The stochastic Airy and sine operators, which are respectively a random Sturm-Liouville operator and a random Dirac operator, characterize the soft edge and bulk scaling limits of $β$-ensembles. Dirac and Sturm-Liouville operators are distinct operator classes which can both be represented as canonical systems, which gives a unified framework for defining important properties, such as their spectral data. Seeing both as canonical systems, we prove that in a suitable high-energy scaling limit, the Airy operator converges to the sine operator. We prove this convergence in the vague topology of canonical systems' coefficient matrices, and deduce the convergence of the associated Weyl-Titchmarsh functions and spectral measures. Our proof relies on a coupling between the Brownian paths that drive the two operators, under which the convergence holds in probability. This extends the corresponding result at the level of the eigenvalue point processes, proven by Valkó and Virág (2009) by comparison to the Gaussian $β$-ensemble.

papers.title: Fluctuation Correction and Global Solutions for the Stochastic Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto System via Entropy-Based Regularization
papers.abstract: We study a stochastic extension of the n-species Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto (SKT) cross-diffusion system, in which a multiplicative noise term accounts for fluctuation corrections to the mean-field dynamics arising from a finite underlying population. The noise we consider is motivated by, but not rigorously derived from, the particle-system approximation of Chen, Daus, Holzinger, and J"ungel; it only partially respects the entropy (gradient-flow) structure of the deterministic system, which is the main source of the technical difficulties addressed in this paper. For the resulting system of stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), we establish the existence of nonnegative, global, weak martingale solutions, under a detailed-balance condition on the diffusion coefficients and a smallness condition relating the noise intensity to these coefficients. This smallness condition amounts to a sufficiently large population size N (equivalently, small fluctuation strength 1/N): the existence theory thus operates in the perturbative regime around the deterministic mean-field limit, and for fixed coefficients it is always satisfiable once N is large enough.

papers.title: Pluripotential theory and special holonomy: Hodge decompositions and $\partial\bar\partial$ lemmata
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact torsion-free $G_2$ 7-manifold or Calabi-Yau 6-manifold. We prove Hodge decomposition theorems for the $dd^φ$ operators, introduced by Harvey and Lawson, which generalize the $i\partial\bar\partial$ operator used in classical pluripotential theory. We then obtain analogues of the $\partial\bar\partial$ lemma in this context. We formalize this by defining cohomology spaces analogous to Bott-Chern cohomology and we relate them to harmonic forms on $M$. In the $G_2$ case we provide a geometric interpretation of the corresponding cohomology classes in terms of coassociative submanifolds and gerbes: this is analogous to the classical interpretation of Bott-Chern cohomology classes in terms of divisors and holomorphic line bundles.

papers.title: Central simple algebras, Milnor $K$-theory and homogeneous spaces over complete discretely valued fields of dimension 2
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field of dimension $2$. We prove the following statements on the arithmetic of $K$. - The ``period equals index'' property holds for central simple $K$-algebras. - If $K$ has characteristic $0$, for every prime $p$, every class in the Milnor $\mathrm{K}$-theory modulo $p$ is represented by a symbol. - Serre's Conjecture II holds for the field $K$. That is, for every semisimple and simply connected $K$-group $G$, the set $H^1(K,G)$ is trivial.

papers.title: The automorphism groups of Kummer surfaces in characteristic two and their complex analogues
papers.abstract: We calculate the automorphism group of the Kummer surface associated with a curve of genus 2 or the product of two elliptic curves in characteristic two under the assumption that the Kummer surface is a $K3$ surface. Moreover we discuss the complex $K3$ surfaces with the same Picard lattice as these Kummer surfaces. The paper has two appendices.

papers.title: On a generalized Monge-Ampère equation on closed almost Kähler surfaces
papers.abstract: We show the existence and uniqueness of solutions to a generalized Monge-Ampère equation on closed almost Kähler surfaces, where the equation depends only on the underlying almost Kähler structure. As an application, we prove Donaldson's conjecture for tamed almost complex 4-manifolds.

papers.title: Good minimal models with nowhere vanishing holomorphic $1$-forms
papers.abstract: Popa and Schnell show that any holomorphic 1-form on a smooth projective variety of general type has zeros. In this article, we show that a smooth good minimal model has a holomorphic 1-form without zero if and only if it admits an analytic fiber bundle structure over a positive dimensional abelian variety.

papers.title: Pointwise convergence of noncommutative discrete spherical ergodic averages
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish spherical maximal inequalities associated with commuting trace-preserving automorphisms on von Neumann algebras, extending Magyar-Stein-Wainger's discrete spherical maximal inequalities to the noncommutative setting. On a noncommutative probability space, we further prove that, under a strong ergodicity assumption, the corresponding discrete spherical averages converge bilaterally almost uniformly to $τ(x)1$ for every $x\in L_p(\mathcal M)$, $\frac{d}{d-2}<p\leq\infty$, when $d\geq5$.

papers.title: Q-Learning under Finite Model Uncertainty
papers.abstract: We propose a robust Q-learning algorithm for Markov decision processes under model uncertainty when each state--action pair is associated with a finite ambiguity set of candidate transition kernels. This finite-measure framework enables user-designed uncertainty models, including competing fitted models and stress scenarios. {The learner observes successor states and their deterministic rewards from every candidate simulator, without requiring explicit knowledge of the transition probabilities or the reward function.} We establish almost sure convergence of the learned Q-function to the robust optimum, and derive a time-uniform high-probability error certificate that separates an observable empirical Bellman residual from transition-kernel estimation error. We also give quantitative finite-ambiguity approximation results for Wasserstein and parametric uncertainty models on finite state spaces. Numerical examples illustrate the effect of scenario selection and compare the tabular algorithm with robust value iteration.

papers.title: Sharp Finiteness Principles for the boundary values of $C^2$-functions
papers.abstract: Let $Ω$ be an arbitrary domain in ${\bf R}^n$, and let $C^2(Ω)$ be the space of all functions whose partial derivatives of all orders up to two are continuous and bounded on $Ω$. We prove the following Finiteness Principle for the boundary values of $C^2(Ω)$-functions: A function $f$ defined on the boundary of $Ω$ is the trace of a function $F\in C^2(Ω)$ provided there exists $λ>0$ such that, for every set $E$ of at most $N=3\cdot 2^{n-1}$ boundary points, there exists a function $F_E\in C^2(Ω)$ with $\|F_E\|_{C^2(Ω)}\leλ$ whose trace coincides with $f$ on $E$. Moreover, $F$ can be chosen with $\|F\|_{C^2(Ω)}\leγλ$ where $γ$ depends only on $n$. We also refine this principle by showing that it suffices to consider $N$-point sets $E$ with specific geometric ``visibility'' properties relative to $Ω$.

papers.title: Generalized gyrovector spaces revisited
papers.abstract: We revise a proof of a Mazur-Ulam theorem for generalized gyrovector spaces.

papers.title: Scaling limit of the colored ASEP and stochastic six-vertex models
papers.abstract: We consider the colored asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) and stochastic six vertex (S6V) model with fully packed initial conditions; the states of these models can be encoded by 2-parameter height functions. We show under Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling of time, space, and fluctuations that these height functions converge to the Airy sheet. Several corollaries follow. (1) For ASEP and the S6V model under the basic coupling, we consider the 4-parameter height function at position $y$ and time $t$ with a step initial condition at position $x$ and time $s < t$, and prove that under KPZ scaling it converges to the directed landscape. (2) As a consequence, in our paper arXiv:2412.18117, we prove that ASEPs and S6V models under the basic coupling, with multiple general initial data, converge to KPZ fixed points coupled through the directed landscape. (3) We prove that the colored ASEP stationary measures converge to the stationary horizon. (4) We prove a form of decoupling for the colored ASEP height functions, as well as for the stationary two-point function, as broadly predicted by the theory of non-linear fluctuating hydrodynamics. The starting point for our Airy sheet convergence result is an embedding of these colored models into a larger structure -- a color-indexed family of coupled line ensembles with an explicit Gibbs property, i.e., a colored Hall-Littlewood line ensemble. The core of our work then becomes to develop a framework to analyze the edge scaling limit of these ensembles.

papers.title: Mirror Descent-Ascent for mean-field min-max problems
papers.abstract: We study two variants of the mirror descent-ascent (MDA) algorithm for solving min-max problems on the space of measures: simultaneous and alternating. We work under assumptions of convexity-concavity and relative smoothness of the payoff function with respect to a suitable Bregman divergence, defined on the space of measures via flat derivatives. We establish non-asymptotic convergence rates to mixed Nash equilibria, measured in the Nikaidô-Isoda error, proving an $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1/2})$ rate for simultaneous MDA and an improved $\mathcal{O}(N^{-2/3})$ rate for alternating MDA. The main technical contribution is an infinite-dimensional dual space analysis that relates Bregman divergences on measures to dual Bregman divergences on spaces of bounded continuous functions, allowing us to control asymmetric commutator terms created by alternating updates. The results substantially generalize prior analyses restricted to bilinear objectives and also apply to nonlinear convex-concave problems on measure spaces, thereby providing a unified theoretical foundation for MDA in mean-field min-max optimization.

papers.title: Log canonical singularities of plurisubharmonic functions
papers.abstract: A plurisubharmonic weight is \emph{log canonical} if it is at the critical point of turning non-integrable. Given a log canonical plurisubharmonic weight, we show that locally there always exists a log canonical `holomorphic' weight having the same non-integrable locus. The proof uses the theory of quasimonomial valuations developed by Jonsson-Mustaţă and Xu, as well as the minimal model program over complex analytic spaces due to Fujino and Lyu-Murayama. As a consequence, we obtain that the non-integrable locus is seminormal.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Airport Ground Holding Problem under Wasserstein Ambiguity Sets
papers.abstract: We develop a distributionally robust formulation of the single-airport ground holding problem (dr-SAGHP) using a $1$-Wasserstein ambiguity set with an $\ell_1$ transportation metric over the full physical capacity support. We exploit the problem's structural properties to develop an exact dynamic programming separation algorithm within delayed constraint generation (DCG-DP). We also develop K-IL, which combines Kelley's cutting-plane method with an integer L-shaped framework to solve a a restricted-support approximation, rs-dr-SAGHP. Delayed constraint generation with MILP separation (DCG-MILP) serves as the computational baseline. Computational experiments demonstrate substantial runtime reductions for DCG-DP and K-IL relative to this baseline. Airport capacity distributions are constructed using Gaussian process regression based on historical weather and operational data at Denver International Airport from 2021 to 2023. We develop a chronological expanding-window calibration procedure to select the Wasserstein radius and the results show that the calibrated dr-SAGHP approaches reduce mean operational cost by approximately $2.6\%$ and the Conditional Value at Risk $\mathrm{CVaR}_{90}$ by approximately $8\%$ relative to the stochastic SAGHP benchmark, while avoiding the excessive conservatism observed in a classical robust optimization benchmark.

papers.title: Weak representability of actions of non-associative algebras
papers.abstract: We study the categorical-algebraic condition that internal actions are weakly representable (WRA) in the context of varieties of (non-associative) algebras over a field. Our first aim is to give a complete characterization of action accessible, operadic quadratic varieties of non-associative algebras which satisfy an identity of degree two and to study the representability of actions for them. Here we prove that the varieties of two-step nilpotent (anti-)commutative algebras are weakly action representable, and we explain that the condition (WRA) is closely connected to the existence of a so-called strong amalgam. Our second aim is to work towards the construction, still within the context of algebras over a field, of a weakly representing object $\mathcal{E}(X)$ for the actions on (or split extensions of) an object $X$. We actually obtain a partial algebra $\mathcal{E}(X)$, which we call external weak actor of $X$, together with a monomorphism of functors ${\mathrm{SplExt}(-,X) \rightarrowtail \mathrm{Hom}(U(-),\mathcal{E}(X))}$, which we study in detail in the case of quadratic varieties. Furthermore, the relations between the construction of the universal strict general actor $USGA(X)$ and that of $\mathcal{E}(X)$ are described in detail. We end with some open questions. This version is preceded by a corrigendum. Theorem 2.11 of the published article, which states that the variety of commutative associative algebras is weakly action representable, is false: we exhibit a $16$-dimensional algebra $X$ with zero multiplication for which the functor $\mathrm{SplExt}(-,X)$ admits no weak representation. Hence this variety is action accessible but not weakly action representable. The corrigendum amends the statements affected by this error, corrects Proposition 2.8, whose "if" part needs a strong amalgam, updates the definition of partial algebra, and lists some further minor corrections.

papers.title: Analysing Multiscale Clusterings with Persistent Homology
papers.abstract: In data clustering, it is often desirable to find not just a single partition into clusters but a sequence of partitions that describes the data at different scales (or levels of coarseness). A natural problem then is to analyse and compare, as a whole, the (not necessarily hierarchical) sequences of partitions that underpin such multiscale descriptions. Using tools from topological data analysis, we introduce here the Multiscale Clustering Filtration (MCF), a filtration of abstract simplicial complexes that encodes arbitrary cluster assignments in a sequence of partitions across scales of increasing coarseness. We prove the stability of the MCF with respect to small changes in the sequence of partitions, and establish that its persistence diagram (PD) provides an interpretable representation of the multiscale clustering: at dimension 0, it captures violations of the refinement order, and at higher dimensions, it tracks the emergence and resolution of higher-order inconsistencies between cluster assignments. We also introduce an equivalent construction of the MCF via a nerve complex filtration, and show that this nerve-based MCF has computational advantages in certain settings, aiding scalability. Further, we show that in the hierarchical case, the MCF reduces to a Vietoris-Rips filtration of an ultrametric space, and we establish that pairwise measures, such as conditional entropy or zigzag persistence, are fully determined by a graph representation of the Sankey diagram and thus fail to describe the higher-order inconsistencies across scales that MCF captures. Using synthetic and real-world data from stochastic block models, single-cell transcriptomics and temporal social interactions, we illustrate how the MCF PD serves to characterise and compare multiscale clusterings beyond pairwise or hierarchical baseline methods.

papers.title: On the representation functions of certain numeration systems
papers.abstract: Let $β>1$ be fixed. We consider the $(\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D})$-numeration system, where the base sequence $\mathbf{b}=(b_k)_{k\geq 0}$ consists of positive real numbers satisfying $\lim_{k\rightarrow \infty}b_{k+1}/b_k=β$, and the digit set $\mathcal{D}\ni 0$ is a finite set of nonnegative real numbers containing at least two elements. Let $r_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(λ)$ denote the number of representations of a given $λ\in\mathbb{R}$ in the form $\sum_{k\ge 0}δ_kb_k$ with digits $δ_k\in \mathcal{D}$. We establish upper bounds for $r_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(λ)$ as well as asymptotic formulas for its arbitrary moments. Furthermore, we prove that the associated Dirichlet series $ζ_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(s):=\sum_{λ>0}r_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(λ)λ^{-s}$ admits a meromorphic continuation to the entire complex plane when $b_k=β^{k}$, and to the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s)>\log_β\mathcal{D}-γ$ when $b_k=β^{k}+O(β^{(1-γ)k})$ for any fixed $γ\in(0,1]$. Within the regions of continuation, we determine all candidate poles, compute their corresponding residues, and locate the trivial zeros of $ζ_{\mathbf{b},\mathcal{D}}(s)$. As an application, we resolve several problems posed by Chow and Slattery concerning partitions into distinct terms of certain integer sequences.

papers.title: Tree embeddings and nonuniqueness in site percolation
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be an infinite connected simple graph of minimum degree at least seven. Suppose $G$ is embedded in the plane so that every compact set meets only finitely many vertices and edges. We prove that $p_c^{\mathrm{site}}(G)<1/2$ and that, for every $p_c^{\mathrm{site}}(G)<p<1-p_c^{\mathrm{site}}(G)$, Bernoulli$(p)$ site percolation almost surely has infinitely many infinite open clusters. We also construct a subtree of $G$ with critical site percolation probability $\sqrt{2}-1$. We prove a general stability theorem for infinite connected locally finite graphs $G\subseteq H$ on the same vertex set. Suppose that, at parameter $a\in(0,1)$, the probability that a deterministic finite set meets an infinite open cluster in $G$ tends uniformly to one as its size grows. Then, for each fixed $b\in(a,1]$, under the standard monotone coupling, almost surely every infinite open cluster in $H$ at parameter $b$ contains an infinite open cluster in $G$ at parameter $a$. No planarity, transitivity, or uniform degree bound is required. Finally, we obtain a lower bound on two-point connectivity under uniqueness for arbitrary infinite locally finite graphs, yielding a general criterion for nonuniqueness.

papers.title: The Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: The Weyl symbolic calculus of operators leads to the construction, if one takes for symbol a certain distribution decomposing over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, of an operator with the following property: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the validity of a collection of estimates involving this operator. Pseudodifferential arithmetic, a novel chapter of pseudodifferential operator theory, makes it possible to make the operator under study fully explicit. This leads to a proof of the conjecture.

papers.title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function
papers.abstract: We use an elementary arithmetic argument, going back to Blom and Fr{ö}berg, to obtain upper and lower bounds for the denumerant function of Sylvester for arbitrary positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_k$. The bounds hold along the multiples of $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_k)$, share the leading term of the denumerant, and yield its asymptotic behaviour with an explicit error term; for large $n$ and under a mild condition, a polynomial refinement of the lower bound improves on the lower bound of Agnarsson.

papers.title: Embeddings of $k$-complexes in $2k$-manifolds and minimum rank of partial symmetric matrices
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a $k$-dimensional simplicial complex having $n$ faces of dimension $k$, and $M$ a closed $(k-1)$-connected PL $2k$-dimensional manifold. We prove that for $k\ge3$ odd $K$ embeds into $M$ if and only if there are $\bullet$ a skew-symmetric $n\times n$-matrix $A$ with integer entries, whose rank over $\mathbb Q$ does not exceed $rk H_k(M;\mathbb Z)$, $\bullet$ a general position PL map $f:K\to\mathbb R^{2k}$, and $\bullet$ orientations on $k$-faces of $K$ \newline such that for any nonadjacent $k$-faces $σ,τ$ of $K$ the entry $A_{σ,τ}$ equals to the algebraic intersection of $fσ$ and $fτ$. We prove some analogues of this result (for any parity of $k$), including those for $\mathbb Z_2$- and $\mathbb Z$-embeddability. Our results generalize the Bikeev-Fulek-Kyn\v cl criteria for the $\mathbb Z_2$- and $\mathbb Z$-embeddability of graphs to surfaces, and are related to the Harris-Krushkal-Johnson-Paták-Tancer criteria for the embeddability of $k$-complexes into $2k$-manifolds. The main novelty of this paper is passing from the cohomology condition of Paták-Tancer to the simpler extendability of some intersection function to a low-rank matrix (defined in the paper using the idea of Fulek-Kyn\v cl).

papers.title: Uniqueness of the critical and supercritical Liouville quantum gravity metrics
papers.abstract: We show that for each ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in [1,25)$, there is a unique metric associated with Liouville quantum gravity (LQG) with matter central charge ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M}$. An earlier series of works by Ding-Dubédat-Dunlap-Falconet, Gwynne-Miller, and others showed that such a metric exists and is unique in the subcritical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$, which corresponds to coupling constant $γ\in (0,2)$. The critical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} = 1$ corresponds to $γ=2$ and the supercritical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in (1,25)$ corresponds to $γ\in \mathbb C$ with $|γ| = 2$. Our metric is constructed as the limit of an approximation procedure called Liouville first passage percolation, which was previously shown to be tight for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in [1,25)$ by Ding and Gwynne (2020). In this paper, we show that the subsequential limit is uniquely characterized by a natural list of axioms. This extends the characterization of the LQG metric proven by Gwynne and Miller (2019) for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$ to the full parameter range $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,25)$. Our argument is substantially different from the proof of the characterization of the LQG metric for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$. In particular, the core part of the argument is simpler and does not use confluence of geodesics.

papers.title: Characterization of Fréchet Spaces and Application to Hausdorff MNC
papers.abstract: We study the Hausdorff measure of noncompactness associated with compatible metrics on Fréchet spaces, with the aim of extending its Banach-space properties. After recalling the characterization by complete translation-invariant metrics with convex balls, we calculate the scalar Hausdorff measure for a standard weighted fractional metric. For bounded nonprecompact sets its value is the unique root of an equation involving a finite seminorm gauge determined by the covering radius. This yields an actual Hausdorff-condensing criterion for compact perturbations of maps having separate contraction constants at the seminorm levels. On countable products of Banach spaces we obtain an exact coordinate formula and a sharp scalar contraction bound on bounded domains, without requiring a uniform gap between the coordinate constants and one for strict condensation. For closed subspaces, an exact finite-projection formula retains the compatibility constraints on covering centers. Explicit examples show why separately computed seminorm measures cannot generally be substituted into the metric formula. Applications to spaces of real sequence-valued continuous functions give an explicit oscillation formula and exhibit the compatibility obstruction on an unbounded interval. Classical fixed-point consequences are recorded briefly.

papers.title: Some ordering properties of highest and lowest order statistics with exponentiated Gumble type-II distributed components
papers.abstract: This paper studies stochastic comparisons of the highest and lowest order statistics arising from independent Exponentiated Gumbel Type-II distributed random variables. First, using vector majorization, we establish a comprehensive set of stochastic orderings for the lowest and highest order statistics with respect to the outer and inner shape parameters. In particular, for the lowest order statistic, we derive results on the usual stochastic order and likelihood ratio order, which further imply failure rate, mean residual life, and increasing convex orderings. Second, we show that the lowest order statistics satisfy a proportional failure rate structure. In addition, we also establish star and dispersive orderings. For the highest order statistic, we obtain results in the reversed failure rate order, and we show that, in general, a proportional failure rate structure does not hold. Moreover, unlike several classical exponentiated models, the highest order statistics are not necessarily comparable in the usual stochastic order under heterogeneity of the inner shape parameters. Finally, we extend the analysis using multivariate chain majorization to study the effect of simultaneous variation in scale and outer shape parameters. Under this framework, we establish usual stochastic ordering results for both the lowest and highest order statistics. It provides more general reliability comparisons under joint parameter heterogeneity.

papers.title: Scl in graphs of groups
papers.abstract: Let G be a group acting on a tree with cyclic edge and vertex stabilizers. Then stable commutator length (scl) is rational in G. Furthermore, scl varies predictably and converges to rational limits in so-called "surgery" families. This is a homological analog of the phenomenon of geometric convergence in hyperbolic Dehn surgery.

papers.title: Dense semigroups of triangular matrices
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ be the semigroup of $n\times n$ lower triangular matrices with entries in $\mathbb{K}$. We show that $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ has dense subsemigroups generated by $n+1$ matrices, and that $n+1$ is the least possible number of generators; the same holds for dense subgroups of the group of invertible lower triangular matrices. The generators can be written down explicitly: $n$ of them are diagonal and one is a diagonal matrix plus a nilpotent perturbation. More precisely, let $D_0,\dots,D_m$ be diagonal matrices generating a dense subsemigroup of the diagonal matrices, where the diagonal entries of $D_0$ have strictly monotone moduli, and let $A$ be a lower triangular matrix with the same diagonal as $D_0$. We prove that the semigroup generated by $A,D_1,\dots,D_m$ is dense in $T_n(\mathbb{K})$ if and only if every subdiagonal entry of $A$ is nonzero.

papers.title: Nonlinear PDEs with modulated dispersion II: Korteweg-de Vries equation
papers.abstract: (Due to the limit on the number of characters for an abstract set by arXiv, the full abstract can not be displayed here. See the abstract in the paper.) We study dispersive equations with a time non-homogeneous modulation acting on the linear dispersion term. As primary models, we consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) and related equations such as the Benjamin-Ono equation (BO) and the intermediate long wave equation (ILW), imposing certain irregularity conditions on the time non-homogeneous modulation. In this work, we establish phenomena called regularization by noise in three-folds: (i) When the modulation is sufficiently irregular, we show that the modulated KdV on both the circle and the real line is locally well-posed in the regime where the (unmodulated) KdV equation is known to be ill-posed. In particular, given any $s \in \mathbb R$, we show that the modulated KdV on the circle with a sufficiently irregular modulation is locally well-posed in $H^s(\mathbb T)$. Moreover, by adapting the $I$-method to the current modulated setting, we prove global well-posedness of the modulated KdV in negative Sobolev spaces. (ii) It is known that certain (semilinear) dispersive equations such as BO and ILW exhibit quasilinear nature. We show that sufficiently irregular modulations make the modulated versions of these equations semilinear by establishing their local well-posedness by a contraction argument, providing local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map. (iii) We also prove nonlinear smoothing for these modulated equations, where we show that a gain of regularity of the nonlinear part becomes (arbitrarily) larger for more irregular modulations. As applications of our approach, we also include further examples.

papers.title: Maximally transitive semigroups of $n\times n$ matrices (revised and extended version)
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. We prove that for every $n\ge 1$ there is a pair of $n\times n$ matrices with entries in $\mathbb{K}$ that generates a dense subsemigroup of the space $M_n(\mathbb{K})$ of all $n\times n$ matrices. Since the powers of a single matrix are never dense, two generators is optimal. Equivalently, there is a $2$-generator semigroup of linear maps whose action on $(\mathbb{K}^n)^n$ is topologically transitive, whereas no semigroup of linear maps acts topologically transitively on $(\mathbb{K}^n)^{n+1}$. In fact, for such a semigroup every orbit closure in $(\mathbb{K}^n)^k$, for every $k\ge1$, is as large as linear algebra allows. Along the way we give a short self-contained proof of the density of explicit $2$-generator subsemigroups of $GL_2^+(\mathbb{R})$ and of $M_2(\mathbb{R})$, based on a simple criterion for closed subsemigroups of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$.

papers.title: Dense 2-generator subsemigroups of $2\times 2$ matrices (revised and extended version)
papers.abstract: We show that the semigroup of real linear fractional transformations of a proper subinterval of the real line does not contain a dense subsemigroup generated by two elements, while it does contain dense subsemigroups generated by three elements. For the semigroup generated by the two maps $x\mapsto 1+a/x$ and $x\mapsto x/b$ (the only pair not excluded by elementary arguments) we compute the closure exactly, and we describe all of its orbit closures in the plane. Consequently the semigroup of $2\times2$ matrices with nonnegative entries has no dense $2$-generator subsemigroup but has dense $3$-generator ones. In contrast, we prove a general density criterion for subsemigroups of $M_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $M_2(\mathbb{C})$ generated by three explicit matrices, and use a word identity of length seven to produce, for both $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{C}$, uncountable families of pairs of matrices that generate dense subsemigroups; a fully explicit rational example is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1/2\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\0&-8/3\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Thus the minimal number of generators of a dense subsemigroup is $3$ for the nonnegative cone and $2$ for $M_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $M_2(\mathbb{C})$.

papers.title: A Collatz-type conjecture on the set of rational numbers (revised and extended version)
papers.abstract: Let $θ(x)=(x-1)/3$ if $x\ge1$ and $θ(x)=2x/(1-x)$ if $0\le x<1$. We conjecture that the $θ$-orbit of every nonnegative rational number ends in $0$. A weaker conjecture asserts that no map in the semigroup generated by $3x+1$ and $x/(x+2)$, other than the generators' powers, has a positive rational fixed point; equivalently, the only matrices in the semigroup generated by $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}3&1\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\1&2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with an integer eigenvalue are their pure powers. We prove sharp two-sided bounds for the smallest eigenvalue of every word in the more general semigroups attached to the maps $\varphi_{a,b}$, which explain why the pair $\{2,3\}$ is distinguished: it is the only pair with $(a-1)(b-1)=2$. Combining these bounds with congruences for the trace, we determine the possible integer eigenvalues of words, and we prove that $θ$ has no rational $1$-circuits, no rational $2$-circuits and no even rational circuits. We show that, for each $k$, a random $k$-syllable word with exponents at most $M$ has an integer eigenvalue with probability at most $2k(k+\log_2 2k)/M$. Finally, we verify by computer that $θ$ has no positive rational cycle of length at most $36$.

papers.title: Semigroups of matrices with dense orbits (revised version)
papers.abstract: For $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and every $n\ge 1$ we construct two $n\times n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ such that the orbit of every vector $p\in\mathbb{K}^n$ with $p_1\ne 0$ under the semigroup generated by $A$ and $B$ is dense in $\mathbb{K}^n$; the remaining vectors lie in an invariant hyperplane, so the set of vectors with dense orbit is exactly the complement of a hyperplane. Thus two generators always suffice for a hypercyclic semigroup of matrices, in contrast with the commutative case, where $n+1$ generators are needed on $\mathbb{C}^n$. We give a transparent reformulation of the hypotheses, a criterion for the density of $\{a^mb^n\}$ that makes them checkable, and explicit examples with complete proofs. As applications we obtain affine pairs on $\mathbb{K}^n$ all of whose orbits are dense, and, for every $n$, a pair of real matrices with an orbit that is somewhere dense but not dense in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

papers.title: Nonconstant Congruence Speeds of Integer Tetration in Non-Squarefree Radices
papers.abstract: We further develop the theory of congruence speed for integer tetration in non-squarefree numeral systems, building on Appendix B of [M. Ripà and G. Di Pietro (2026), A compact notation for peculiar properties characterizing integer tetration, Notes on Number Theory and Discrete Mathematics, 32(3), 477-496]. For bases coprime to the radix, we establish an eventual floor-difference representation and determine the exact spectrum of attainable least periods. We construct explicit arithmetic progressions containing infinitely many prime bases with nonconstant congruence speed for every non-squarefree radix, thereby proving the coprime-infinitude conjecture posed in Appendix B. We also derive a uniform quadratic bound for the least coprime base with nonconstant congruence speed and establish exact natural densities of nonstabilizing bases, both among integers coprime to the radix and among those not divisible by its radical, together with the corresponding relative density among primes. Finally, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for the perfect-power congruence-speed identity (Equation (2.12) of the cited paper) to hold in arbitrary radices, determine the exact least eventual period when stabilization fails, and establish a separate criterion for the boundary case of the original parameter restriction.

papers.title: Excluding 54 of the 76 Nontrivial Factorization Patterns of the Cuboid Polynomial $P_{a,b,u}(t)$
papers.abstract: Let $P_{a,b,u}(t)$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$12$ third cuboid polynomial, with positive pairwise distinct rational parameters. We prove a uniform normal form for its complete factorization over $\mathbb{Q}$. Every factorization consists of at most two even quadratic factors, even irreducible factors of higher degree, and pairs of irreducible factors exchanged by $t\mapsto-t$. After dividing all degrees by the contribution of this symmetry, the normal form satisfies one degree equation, one sign equation, and an obligatory-factor alternative: an even irreducible factor of degree at least six, or an even irreducible quartic with positive rational-square constant term. The arithmetic input is a uniform construction over $\mathbb{Q}_2$, using Newton polygons, Hensel lifting, and a norm obstruction from $\mathbb{Q}_2(i)$. Valuations at all finite primes constrain rational factor constants to signed squares, while the real root equation gives exactly two simple negative roots of the auxiliary sextic. The normal form leaves exactly $22$ of the $76$ nontrivial partitions of $12$, thereby excluding $54$ complete irreducible degree patterns by one argument. Of these exclusions, $37$ follow from evenness alone and $17$ from the additional arithmetic restrictions. All local cases are proved explicitly, and an exact verification script accompanies the algebraic identities and exhaustive partition enumeration. The remaining patterns are necessary possibilities; their realization is not asserted, and full irreducibility remains open.

papers.title: Topological and measurewise amenability for locally compact groupoids
papers.abstract: We prove the equivalence of topological and measurewise amenability for $σ$-compact locally compact groupoids with a Hausdorff unit space and a continuous Haar system. This in particular includes the second countable locally compact Hausdorff case. Our proof averages arbitrary Radon probability measures along strictly positive densities to obtain quasi-invariant measures. We overcome the lack of absolute continuity of the original measure with respect to its quasi-invariant substitute by also averaging the Reiter functions along the same density.

papers.title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension six
papers.abstract: We summarize a coordinate-free classification of six-dimensional real Lie algebras up to isomorphism. Instead of solving the overdetermined Jacobi system of 120 quadratic equations on 90 structure constants modulo $\mathrm{GL}(6,\mathbb{R})$, the method uses the Levi--Malcev decomposition, Mostow's nilradical constraints, and the Skjelbred--Sund cohomological central extension technique. In the semisimple sector, the four real forms of $A_1\oplus A_1$ are classified by Killing signature invariants, with explicit matrix representatives for $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})_{\mathbb{R}}\cong\mathfrak{so}(3,1)$. For non-solvable algebras with three-dimensional radical, representation-theoretic rigidity shows that $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ cannot couple indecomposably with non-abelian radicals, yielding exactly three indecomposable classes governed by $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$. In the solvable category, Mostow's theorem restricts the nilradical dimension to $\{3,4,5,6\}$. The nilpotent sector in dimension six has twenty-four indecomposable isomorphism classes plus decomposable counterparts. Solvable non-nilpotent algebras are classified by nilradical codimension, with explicit real Jordan matrix representations for codimension one and two that resolve continuous moduli under gauge actions. The work also computes the minimal faithful representation dimension $μ(\mathfrak{g})$ under Ado's theorem, relates the classification to invariant complex structures on nilmanifolds, and provides a deterministic, page-breakable identification algorithm.

papers.title: Cobordism maps and Atiyah-Floer isomorphisms for framed instanton homology I
papers.abstract: We prove that isomorphisms of the type constructed by Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy, between framed instanton homology and the Lagrangian Floer homology of a Heegaard splitting, intertwine the cobordism maps of Kronheimer and Mrowka with maps defined by holomorphic curves alone, over the field of two elements. This holds for every connected cobordism between connected three-manifolds carrying a framed arc between its ends and an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ bundle trivialized along the ends and the arc. The symplectic maps count holomorphic triangles in moduli spaces of flat connections on surfaces, with the correspondence of a compression body as boundary condition for one- and three-handles. Consequently these maps are independent of the handle decomposition and of the Heegaard data, and form a functor isomorphic to framed instanton homology; where both are defined, our isomorphisms agree with those of Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy modulo two. The proof rests on two analytic results for the mixed anti-self-duality and holomorphic curve equation: an adiabatic limit in which a compression body collapses next to a holomorphic strip and becomes the Lagrangian boundary condition of its flat connections, and an excision theorem along a torus.

papers.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring of Undirected Path, Chordal Bipartite, and Strongly Chordal Graphs
papers.abstract: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper coloring in which each nonisolated vertex has a neighbor whose color occurs exactly once in its open neighborhood. We prove that deciding whether the clique number of colors suffices is NP-complete on undirected path graphs, even with a supplied representation by paths in a star. One extra color suffices on every instance in the reduction. We also prove NP-completeness on chordal bipartite graphs for every fixed palette size $k\ge4$. For strongly chordal graphs, reverse simple elimination gives a constructive upper bound of one more than the clique number. We obtain exact polynomial-time algorithms under several conditions on the maximum cliques, including when they induce a connected subtree of a clique tree. For strictly chordal graphs we characterize the optimum and construct an optimal coloring in $O(n+m)$ time, where $n$ and $m$ count the vertices and edges. For strongly chordal graphs with clique-tree separators of size at most $s$, we give an exact algorithm in $n^{2^{O(s+1)}}$ time, with no bound on the clique number.

papers.title: Local cohomology over Steenrod algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q = p^s$ elements. Let $S = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} S_n$ be a non-negatively graded commutative, Noetherian $\mathbb{F}_q$-algebra. Assume $S$ has a structure of an unstable Steenrod algebra. Let $M$ be a finitely generated graded unstable $S$-module. Let $I$ be a homogeneous ideal in $S$. We prove that for $i \geq 0$ the local cohomology modules $H^i_I(M)$ has a structure of a Cartan $S$-module. As application we give a direct and considerably simpler proof of D. Bourguiba and S. Zarati's generalization of Landweber-Stong conjecture. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for $S$ to have $S_r$-property of Serre in terms of Dickson polynomials.

papers.title: On the Topology of the Set of Nonnegative Forms That Are Not Sums of Squares
papers.abstract: We study the topology of the normalized space of real nonnegative forms of degree $2d$ in $n$ variables that are not sums of squares. Whenever it is nonempty, we prove that it is path-connected but not acyclic, and in particular not contractible. We give explicit bounds on the degrees in which its reduced homology can be nonzero. In the two minimal nonempty cases, we show an embedding of an exterior algebra into the cohomology ring, and prove containment of the binary octahedral and binary icosahedral groups, respectively, in its fundamental group.

papers.title: $s$-quasi-transitive weakly distance-regular digraphs
papers.abstract: A digraph is $s$-quasi-transitive if, for every path $(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ of length $s$, either $(x_0,x_s)\in AΓ$ or $(x_s,x_0)\in AΓ$ (or both). In this paper, we give a characterization of $s$-quasi-transitive commutative weakly distance-regular digraphs, where $s=4$, or $s\geq 5$ and the cycle polar diameter is at least $s$.

papers.title: Non-migration for planar elastic flows
papers.abstract: We consider a closed planar curve evolving by the free or the length-preserving elastic flow. We prove that the scale-invariant bound $L\int k^2\,ds\le 4π^2+8/3$ at the initial time prevents the entire curve from crossing any line between two times. For the free flow, the proof combines a monotonicity estimate for the normalized bending energy with a barrier that compares centroid motion to an expanding energy radius. For the length-preserving flow, a quantitative gradient estimate controls the total centroid displacement.

papers.title: Exact penalties for maximum-edge bicliques in bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: Given a bipartite graph $G$, we denote by $g(G)$ the largest product $|A||B|$ over pairs of vertex sets $A$ and $B$, one on each side, with no edge between them. These pairs are the bicliques of the bipartite complement of $G$; hence, computing $g(G)$ is the maximum-edge biclique problem, which is NP-hard, as shown by Peeters in 2003. Gillis and Glineur characterized it by a continuous quadratic program, in which a large enough penalty on the edges of $G$ makes the global maximizers correspond to the maximum pairs and the local maximizers to the maximal ones. We propose a new threshold for the penalty, which depends only on $g(G)$. For any penalty at or above it, the global maximizers correspond exactly to the maximum pairs, and every local maximizer with positive value corresponds to a maximal pair. This threshold is never larger than theirs and is sharp up to an additive $1/2$. Spectral and semidefinite bounds give computable penalties; in experiments, a simple local ascent succeeds far more often with the semidefinite one than with the earlier thresholds, although on our graphs that bound already reveals $g(G)$. The penalty formulation, whose optimal value is $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$, is also a copositive formulation of $g(G)$. Strengthening a semidefinite bound of Laurent, Polak and Vargas with the completely positive cone gives exactly $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$, while the doubly nonnegative strengthening is already inexact on six vertices. Finally, Pólya's linear programming approximations of the copositive cone become finite at an explicit level and converge to $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$ without ever being exact.

papers.title: Measures of maximal entropy for monotone factors of smooth surface diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We prove that a transitive monotone factor of a smooth surface diffeomorphism has a unique measure of maximal entropy whenever its topological entropy is positive. Its entropy is the entropy of a single homoclinic class of the diffeomorphism, and the factor map is a measure-theoretic isomorphism on every ergodic measure with positive entropy of that class. The other homoclinic classes are mapped to periodic orbits. We give an application to the essential factor of a diffeomorphism isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov map ---possibly relative to a finite invariant set--- constructed by García-Sassi \& Tal: the essential factor has a unique measure of maximal entropy, which is Bernoulli and has full support.

papers.title: Extending a property of vector spaces to abelian groups
papers.abstract: In this note, we determine the finite abelian groups $G$ such that for every subgroup $H\leq G$ there exists an automorphism $f\in{\rm Aut}(G)$ with ${\rm Fix}(f)=H$. This provides a partial answer to a problem posed by Deaconescu and Walls. Two generalizations of this problem are also proposed.

papers.title: Neyman Orthogonalized Specification Tests for Conditional Tail Index Models
papers.abstract: We develop specification tests for parametric conditional tail index models of heavy-tailed distributions. The tests are based on a projected empirical process that removes the first-order effect of estimating the null parameter. Within the conditional Hall class, we identify conditions under which projection also eliminates the leading Pareto approximation bias in the test process, permitting lower thresholds while preserving asymptotically correct size. We establish the validity of the tests via multiplier bootstrap. For log-linear models, bootstrap validity extends to settings in which covariates among observations above a common threshold concentrate and the smallest eigenvalue of the information matrix tends to zero. We further propose a data-driven threshold selection rule based on an estimate of the Pareto approximation bias after projection. The rule allows lower thresholds to retain more observations for testing while limiting size distortions, with potential gains in power. The finite sample performance of the tests is examined through simulations and a real data application.

papers.title: A Complete Equational Theory for Quantum Circuits with Generalized Control
papers.abstract: Controlled subcircuits are commonplace in quantum algorithms as they represent the quantum analogue of branching statements (if then). We introduce a generalization of controlled subcircuits in the form of a binary operation which sends pairs of unitary quantum circuits to a generalized controlled operation, whose semantics are based on matrix exponentials and logarithms. The family of quantum circuits with generalized controlled operations and circuit exponentiation is denoted HQC for Hierarchical Quantum Circuits. We formalize HQC as a modified prop category using a novel category-theoretic construction, and provide a sound and complete equational theory for diagrammatic reasoning in HQC.

papers.title: On Packed Passenger Permutations
papers.abstract: An occupied seat in a binary row is called packed if both of its immediate neighbors are occupied. We give a self-contained combinatorial account of this statistic, equivalently the number of overlapping occurrences of 111. An occupied-block decomposition yields a coefficient formula at fixed occupancy and a direct proof of the sharp minimum max{0,3m-2n-2} for m passengers in n seats, including arrangements attaining the bound. The same decomposition gives a rational generating function, recurrences, expectations, and avoidance asymptotics. Full rows, in which every empty seat would become packed upon being filled, are related to independent sets of a path. A neighborhood-union expansion also gives exact counts on rectangular grids. The emphasis is a unified elementary presentation and explicit extremal constructions, rather than a new general enumeration method.

papers.title: Local Homological Mirror Symmetry
papers.abstract: Local mirror symmetry, originated from the work of Chiang-Klemm-Yau-Zaslow arXiv:9903053, indicated a potential relation between mirrors to a vector bundle and mirrors to its zero section. In this paper, we constructed a homological mirror to these local varieties and proved the corresponding Homological Mirror Symmetry statement. As an application, we constructed infinite families of exotic Weinstein sectors as mirrors to Hirzebruch surfaces.

papers.title: Multiplicity and least energy sign-changing normalized solutions for a Kirchhoff equation on bounded domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study sign-changing normalized solutions of the Kirchhoff problem \[ \begin{cases} -\left(a+b\displaystyle\int_Ω|\nabla u|^2\,dx\right)Δu =|u|^{p-2}u+μu &\text{in }Ω,\\ u=0 &\text{on }\partialΩ, \end{cases} \] subject to the constraint \[ \int_Ω|u|^2\,dx=c, \] where $a,b>0$, $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$ is a smooth bounded connected domain, $1\le N\le3$, $c>0$ is prescribed, and $μ\in\mathbb R$ is a Lagrange multiplier. We assume $2<p<\infty$ for $N=1,2$ and $2<p\le6$ for $N=3$. For every integer $k\ge1$, we obtain at least $k$ distinct pairs of sign-changing normalized solutions for sufficiently small $c>0$. We determine the small mass asymptotics of their energies, Lagrange multipliers, and rescaled profiles in terms of the distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues and their eigenspaces. When $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$, we obtain infinitely many such pairs for every prescribed mass $c>0$, with energies tending to $+\infty$. At $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$, this conclusion holds for every sufficiently small fixed mass. We also establish the existence of a least energy sign-changing normalized solution on general bounded domains for every prescribed mass when $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$. For sufficiently small mass, such a solution exists on general bounded domains when $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$ and on star-shaped domains when $p>2+\frac{8}{N}$. For any family of such least energy solutions, the rescaled profiles approach the $L^2$-unit sphere of the second Dirichlet eigenspace in $H_0^1(Ω)$ as $c\to0^+$. The finite multiplicity and least energy results include the Sobolev critical case $N=3$, $p=6$. The proofs combine a localized symmetric minimax construction, energy comparisons with one-signed critical points, and compactness arguments that preserve the sign-changing property.

papers.title: On the critical value of void percolation in high dimensions
papers.abstract: In the random Lorentz gas, a point tracer moves through spherical obstacles of (reduced) density $Φ$ centered on a Poisson point process in $d$-dimensional space, $\mathbb{R}^d$, and becomes localized once the vacant space stops percolating, at $Φ_{\rm p}(d)$. The dimensional scaling of this void percolation threshold has remained elusive. Prior bounds, conjectural ones included, ranged from $Ω(1)$ to $O(d\ln d)$, leaving even the scaling undetermined. We here prove that $Φ_{\rm p}(d)=Θ(d)$, and in particular that $\tfrac12\,d \le Φ_{\rm p}(d) \le 5\,d$ for all sufficiently large $d$. The upper bound counts hierarchical families of escape waypoints called tree embeddings; the lower bound is via a weighted second-moment estimate on an explicit ensemble of ballistic escape routes. A linear scaling of $Φ_{\rm p}(d)$ excludes the $d\ln d$ growth suggested by analogy with other systems in the random first-order transition universality class and is consistent with the numerical estimate $Φ_{\rm p}/d \to 3.40(5)$. Because the mean-field dynamical transition is likewise linear, $Φ_{\rm d}\simeq 2.40\,d$, our result fixes the activated window $[Φ_{\rm d},Φ_{\rm p}]$ as a bounded---rather than diverging---correction to mean-field dynamical arrest in sufficiently high $d$.

papers.title: Energy methods and optimal decay for time-fractional equations
papers.abstract: We study energy methods for the time-fractional equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0)-(a(t,x)u_x)_x+(F(t,x,u))_x=Q(t,x,u)$ on the real line, where $0<α<1$, the coefficient $a$ is measurable and bounded from above and from below by positive constants, $σ\partial_xF\ge0$, $σQ\le0$, and the data are in $L^1\cap L^\infty$. Using Yosida approximations of the kernel, an iteration on the $L^{2^m}$ norms gives the parabolic decay $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\le C\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-α/2}$. In $L^2$ it gives the rate $t^{-α/4}$, which, already for the linear equation, improves the rate $t^{-α/5}$ obtained before by the classical energy method. For the convection--diffusion equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0)-u_{xx}+(|u|^{q-1}u)_x=0$, $q>1$, the parabolic rate is optimal for $q\ge2$, and for $1<q<2$ the convection improves it. An $L^1$ time-regularity estimate of Bénilan--Crandall type gives the pointwise flux bound $|u|^{q-1}u-u_x=O(\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-α})$. This bound takes the place of the Oleĭnik estimate and yields the optimal rate $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim t^{-α/q}$ for $1<q<2$. For nonnegative data, matching lower bounds hold for the $L^p$ norms.

papers.title: Multiplayer Stopping Games with a Conditionally Atomless Filtration
