The sieve allows for an asymptotically significant reduction of the private key search space, and can be used to decrease the bounds for the polynomial roots. We also provide a square-root speed-up of the best currently known runtime bound for factoring semiprime $N=pq$ with small prime difference $q-p$.

papers.title: An equivalence principle for martingales
papers.abstract: We show that any discrete-time filtration can be embedded into a dyadic filtration, realized via a non-classical measure-preserving map. This embedding makes it possible to reduce certain problems involving vector-valued martingales to the case of Haar martingales. Some applications of this result will also be discussed.

papers.title: Quasinilpotency of commutators under a weakened Kleinecke--Shirokov condition
papers.abstract: Kramar and Kramar Fijavž proved that a commutator $Y=AB-BA$ of two complex square matrices is nilpotent whenever $Y$ commutes with an iterated commutator $δ_Y^{k}(A)$, where $δ_Y(T)=YT-TY$, and asked whether this result can be generalized to bounded operators on infinite-dimensional spaces. We show that for $k\geq 2$ such a commutator need not be quasinilpotent. On the other hand, for every $k$ it is quasinilpotent whenever it is compact, or more generally whenever it is a Riesz operator or $AY-YA$ is compact. Moreover, its Riesz projection at any non-zero isolated point of its spectrum always has infinite rank.

papers.title: Scopes arrangements and product formulas
papers.abstract: We develop normalized abacus combinatorics for affine type \(C\). We also give explicit product formulas for the number of Scopes classes at every level and every positive depth in affine types \(A\) and \(C\).

papers.title: On Partitions with Constant-Sum Gap Sequences
papers.abstract: We introduce and study \emph{constant-sum gap partitions}: for a fixed nonnegative integer $C$, these are partitions $λ=(λ_1,\ldots,λ_k)$ whose successive differences $d_i=λ_{i+1}-λ_i$ satisfy $d_i+d_{k-i}=C$ for all valid $i$. We derive the generating function for this family, treating partitions of odd and even length separately, and compute it explicitly for $C=0, 1,2,3,4$. We then construct explicit bijections between constant-sum gap partitions with $2m+1$, respectively $2m$, parts and partitions into odd, respectively even, parts in which parts below the largest part have bounded multiplicity, together with an exact weight relation between a partition and its image. Finally, we give a geometric characterization of constant-sum gap partitions in terms of their Ferrers diagrams: removing a prescribed, linearly growing number of cells from each row renders the diagram symmetric about its middle row, for both the odd- and even-length cases.

papers.title: Macroscopic return-time spectra and Hausdorff dimension transitions
papers.abstract: Can the complete macroscopic spectrum of return times determine the Hausdorff dimension of the corresponding set of initial points? We classify all common lower and upper macroscopic intermediate-dimension spectra of zero-density integer sets and realize every admissible spectrum on a full-dimensional family of zero-frequency orbits under logarithmic-power bounds on inverse-branch contraction. For first-return branches with stretched-exponential contraction $e^{-n^δ}$, $0<δ<1$, complete spectrum levels exhibit a sharp zero/full dimension transition at the counting endpoint $δ$. At the critical exponent, exact laws $N_y(t)\sim c_0t^δ(\log t)^β$ yield zero dimension for $β\le0$ and full dimension for $β>0$, even with the complete spectrum fixed. An explicit two-branch intermittent interval map realizes this transition through genuine first returns. Above the critical exponent, imposing an exact counting law and a complete spectrum does not reduce the dimension of an intrinsic mean-energy level in an affine return tower. For nonlinear branches, we obtain quantitative bounds and an exact conditional-pressure formula under thermodynamic regularity assumptions, verified for an explicit non-affine family.

papers.title: Definably isometric cuboids over Hensel minimal fields
papers.abstract: We show that, over a valued field $K$ with $1$-h-minimal theory $\operatorname{Th}(K)$, two Cartesian products of balls must be equal up to translation and coordinate permutation in order for there to exist a definable surjective isometry between them. For this purpose, we introduce a notion of relative dimension for cuboids in $K^n$ that is computed combinatorially and relates to the notion of dimension for definable sets in Hensel minimal theories when $K$ has infinite residue field.

papers.title: A volume-conserving ALE continuous Galerkin method with residual-based Dirichlet--Neumann fluxes for nonlinear free-surface waves
papers.abstract: We develop an arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian continuous Galerkin finite element method for two-dimensional fully nonlinear free-surface potential flow. An isoparametric finite element method computes the interior potential on the current fluid domain, while a residual-based Dirichlet--Neumann flux drives the surface evolution. The residual-based flux satisfies a global discrete balance inherited from the interior variational formulation. When combined with compatible mesh motion, surface projection, and quadrature, this balance yields conservation of the discrete fluid volume at the semi-discrete level. An optional volume-conserving sixth-order surface dissipation controls high-frequency oscillations, and the surface equations are advanced with fourth-order Runge--Kutta integration, updating the mesh and interior solution at every stage. Numerical experiments confirm the expected spatial convergence for linear free-surface waves and demonstrate reduced mesh sensitivity for nonlinear waves over flat and curved bottoms. A rotating-wavemaker example further illustrates the treatment of moving solid boundaries.

papers.title: Alexandrov's theorem in the anti-Gaussian space: A Reilly-formula approach
papers.abstract: We give an alternative proof of Alexandrov's theorem about constant weighted mean curvature hypersurfaces in the anti-Gaussian space, due to the authors and Johne-Silini independently, via a Reilly-type formula approach. Moreover, we establish a sharp Heintze-Karcher-type inequality for hypersurfaces in manifolds with a generalized substatic condition, together with its rigidity in Euclidean space with density.

papers.title: Endpoint Schatten class properties of commutators on quantum Euclidean spaces
papers.abstract: We study commutators $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$ involving fractional Laplacians on quantum Euclidean spaces associated with arbitrary real antisymmetric matrices $θ$. For $d\geq2$ and $-\frac d2<ε\neq 0<1$, we characterize critical weak Schatten class membership of $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$ for any $x$ as a tempered distribution by Sobolev spaces, with equivalent corresponding norms. We also establish precise asymptotics of singular values for $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$. For this purpose, we extend the Cwikel estimates and the required asymptotics of singular values to arbitrary real antisymmetric matrices, and we also establish a systematic approximation theory of tempered distributions on quantum Euclidean spaces.

papers.title: The optimal barrier parameter of the three-dimensional power cone
papers.abstract: We determine the optimal logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier parameter for the three-dimensional power cone. Although several self-concordant barriers for this cone have been constructed, its optimal barrier parameter had remained unknown. For a power cone with exponent $c\in(0,1)$, we prove that the optimal parameter is $\frac{3}{1+\min\{c,1-c\}}$. Except at $c=1/2$, this value is strictly smaller than the parameter $3-2\min\{c,1-c\}$ of Chares' conjectured barrier. At $c=1/2$, the optimal parameter equals $2$, in agreement with the optimal barrier parameter of the second-order cone. The proof combines a sharp lower bound for arbitrary logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barriers with an explicit barrier attaining the bound.

papers.title: Twofold Control: Simultaneous Optimization of Initial Conditions and Control Inputs
papers.abstract: The paper introduces a novel control notion, twofold controllability, which consists of the joint optimisation of the initial state and the distributed control input in a controlled dynamical system, with the aim of reaching a prescribed target state within a given time interval. We show that the resulting problem is well-posed, derive the corresponding optimality conditions, and provide an explicit formulation of its solution. The proposed approach ensures the reachability of any target state independently of the Kalman rank condition. We show that incorporating the additional control component enlarges the set of states reachable with a fixed control cost. At the same time, the average energy required to reach target vectors on the unit sphere decreases. Furthermore, we analyse the asymptotic behaviour as the cost of controlling the system through the initial state tends to infinity. Particular attention is paid to the case in which the controllability Gramian is singular and the classical notion of controllability does not hold. The theoretical results are illustrated by numerical examples, including ones arising from the semi-discretisation of the heat and wave equations with boundary control.

papers.title: On the proof of multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for hyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: In this article, we use Wu's method to prove Budur's multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for completeness.

papers.title: High-Degree Restricted Cohomology for $K(3;1)^{(1)}$ in Characteristics Five and Seven
papers.abstract: We determine the high-degree restricted first cohomology of the positive subalgebra of the rank-one contact algebra in characteristics five and seven, with parabolically induced coefficients. In degrees from twice the characteristic through four times the characteristic minus three, each characteristic has six nonzero homogeneous components, of total dimension thirteen. The constituents include Frobenius twists of the natural horizontal module, represented by Cartier cocycles. PBW duality converts the calculation into bounded-degree homology, where the coefficient action couples the natural and cubic relation coordinates. The resulting modules determine the high-degree part of the coefficient cohomology used in the Lyndon-Hochschild-Serre term $E_2^{0,1}$ for extensions of induced contact modules. In particular, extensions from the Steinberg induced modules vanish in these degrees.

papers.title: The Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators in divergence form
papers.abstract:
We establish the Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators $L = -\operatorname{div}^α(μ
abla^α\cdot)$ of order $2α\in (0,2)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, built from the Riesz fractional gradient and divergence, with bounded, measurable and uniformly elliptic complex coefficients $μ$. More precisely, we show that the domain of $L^{1/2}$ coincides with the distributional fractional Sobolev space $\mathrm{S}^{α,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and that $\|L^{1/2} u\|_{\mathrm{L}^2} \simeq \|
abla^αu\|_{\mathrm{L}^2}$, with constants that are locally uniform in $α$. As a consequence, we recover the Kato square root property for elliptic operators $-\operatorname{div}(μ
abla\cdot)$ in the limit $α	o 1$, and we obtain continuity of the square root with respect to the parameter $α$. The proof follows the second-order approach to the Kato problem. Its two new ingredients are nonlocal off-diagonal estimates of polynomial order for the resolvents of $L$, and a construction of $T(b)$-test functions that circumvents the nonlocality of $
abla^α$ by factorizing it through Riesz potentials.

papers.title: Lyapunov spectrum, Harder--Narasimhan filtration and thin monodromy
papers.abstract: We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. This gives a nonlattice-transversality alternative of the monodromy group. On the other hand, we generalize Filip's Assumptions A and B to give classes of polarized variation of Hodge structures that achieve the equality. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.

papers.title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
papers.abstract: We analyze the unusual microstructure resulting from the cubic to orthorhombic phase transformation in the shape-memory alloy ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$. This seems to represent an approximate experimental realization of a deformation having a finite number of incompatible deformation gradients, which has been known to exist only as a theoretical possibility. Because the middle eigenvalue $γ$ of the transformation strain is very close to 1, the phase transformation in this alloy takes place via nucleation of exact austenite-martensite interfaces rather than, as usual for other alloys, by classical austenite-martensite interfaces separating the austenite from a finely-twinned laminate of martensite. According to the moving mask approximation of Della Porta this leads to the question whether a microstructure can be formed from the set $H$ of the twelve matrices ${\mathbf V}_i$ on the martensite energy wells that are rank-one connected to the identity, even though these matrices are mutually incompatible. We show that when $γ=1$ and the transformation is volume preserving, such a microstructure is possible that does not deform the grain boundary. This is a consequence of $H$ forming a degenerate $T_{12}$ configuration in the sense of Kirchheim. In fact there are such microstructures supported on just 8 of the 12 matrices in $H$. However there is no deformation satisfying the same boundary condition whose gradient belongs to $H$ almost everywhere. An additional prediction, confirmed experimentally, is that the macroscopic deformation gradient equals the identity everywhere. We also analyse the approximate compatibility of the ${\mathbf V}_i$. Although mutually incompatible, they are nearly compatible, with some pairs much more nearly compatible than others, these pairs corresponding to interfaces that are more frequently observed.

papers.title: From hydrological laws to catchment models: A process-based model matches deep-learning accuracy on three continents
papers.abstract: Dooge asked whether hydrology has laws at the catchment scale. We ask whether a low-dimensional system built under physical laws can match the accuracy of neural networks that outperform process-based models on the same inputs. Three laws constrain a lumped catchment model. Conservation makes it a flux-connected storage network, dissipation fixes the sign of every flux and aggregation determines how the unresolved composition enters the fluxes, through effective laws over threshold distributions and a memory of the forcing. These laws admit four kinds of refinement. A parsimonious model under them, CaRT (11 parameters per catchment), is refined in a loop assisted by AI agents. Each refinement addresses an observed deficit through a hypothesis from the literature. The result, CaRT+, has fourteen states, 35 parameters per catchment and no daily neural network. Most refinements follow from aggregation over thresholds or from variables that carry no water but modulate fluxes. On 602 British and 593 US gauged catchments, single CaRT+ models reach median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiencies of 0.863 and 0.765 in held-out years. A stateful LSTM reaches 0.869 and 0.751 and an entity-aware LSTM 0.862 and 0.754, while three-seed LSTM ensembles remain ahead of the CaRT+ ensemble by 0.003-0.012 in median paired NSE. On 505 drier Australian gauged catchments unused in development, single CaRT+ models reach 0.778 against 0.762 and 0.753 for the two LSTMs. The results suggest that catchment-scale laws exist as laws of form, with the constitutive families shared and only their parameters learned.

papers.title: Exponential Deviations and Hölder Continuity for Moving-Law Mixed Cocycles
papers.abstract: We study mixed random-quasiperiodic cocycles whose one-step laws evolve along an ergodic environment. Under mixed-base ergodicity, bounded logarithmic growth, and stationary-value uniqueness, which we characterize by relative quasi-irreducibility, we prove exponential quenched deviations for finite-time directional growth. A renewal example shows that, in general ergodic environments, annealed exponential deviations can fail despite quenched exponential concentration. This obstruction motivates us to consider a fixed finite-state irreducible aperiodic Markov environment, where we establish annealed exponential deviation estimates uniform over a relative neighborhood of a reference sampling kernel in the bounded mixed-base-ergodic class at each fixed tolerance. These estimates yield local Hölder continuity of the maximal Lyapunov exponent near a stationary-value-unique kernel with a simple top exponent. Under common matrix and inverse bounds, the continuity applies to synchronized Wasserstein perturbations with fixed translation marginals and continuous matrix fields, or to ordinary Wasserstein perturbations with uniform Hölder regularity in the phase. As an application, suitable frequency-support and noise-nondegeneracy conditions yield Hölder energy dependence for moving-law Schrödinger cocycles with continuous potentials.

papers.title: Intersection Product Formulas and Integral Dependence
papers.abstract: We prove the intersection product formulas of Gaffney and Gassler for polar multiplicities and Segre numbers over arbitrary Noetherian local rings. For equidimensional and universally catenary rings, we give a geometric refinement of the Principle of Specialization of Integral Dependence, in which the maximal dimension of the images of exceptional components mapping into the hypersurface determines a precise Segre number that strictly increases.

papers.title: Inference for Realized Quadratic Covariation of $R$ and $R^2$ as a Measure of Return Asymmetry
papers.abstract: We propose a nonparametric test of return asymmetry based on the realized quadratic covariation between a cumulative return path and its square using high-frequency data. Our null hypothesis is that the volatility path is independent of the Brownian motion driving returns. Under this null and a martingale condition, the infill limit of the statistic is conditionally Gaussian given the volatility path, with a conditional variance determined by integrated variance. Studentization by a feasible variance estimator yields an asymptotically standard normal statistic without specifying a parametric model for volatility. Simulations under Heston and Bates dynamics show near-nominal per-window size, quantify power gains from independent-window aggregation, and assess sensitivity to jump removal and volatility-dependent drift. An application to 165 U.S. stocks over 1998--2025 finds that rejections concentrate in negative asymmetry, consistent with the leverage effect.

papers.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
papers.abstract: We provide an algorithm for enumerating ordinary K3 surfaces over a fixed finite field based on Taelman's theorem. We use this algorithm to prove that there exist no K3 surfaces without rational points over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q\geq 13$. For elliptic K3 surfaces, we give a geometric proof of this non-existence without computer assistance. On the other hand, we also provide explicit pointless K3 surfaces over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q\leq 11$.

papers.title: Four-colour counterexamples for monochromatic path partitions
papers.abstract: In 1989, Gyárfás conjectured that the vertex set of every $r$-edge-coloured complete graph can be partitioned into at most $r$ monochromatic paths. The case $r=2$ follows from a theorem of Gerencsér and Gyárfás, and Pokrovskiy proved the conjecture for $r=3$. Recently, Li and Wang disproved the conjecture for all sufficiently large $r$, leaving open the smallest number of colours for which it fails. We show that this number is four. For every integer $n\geq118$, we construct a four-edge-colouring of $K_n$ in which every monochromatic path partition contains at least five paths. We also construct, for every integer $n\geq60$, a four-edge-colouring of $K_{n,n}$ in which every monochromatic path partition contains at least eight paths, disproving Pokrovskiy's conjectured bound $2r-1$ for balanced complete bipartite graphs when $r=4$.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic limits of the asymmetric Brownian energy process and its dynamic generalization
papers.abstract: We prove that the hydrodynamic limit of the asymmetric Brownian energy process (ABEP) is the viscous Burgers equation. We also prove the hydrodynamic limit of the dynamic ABEP which leads to a nonlinear equation for the macroscopic tail-energy potential. Both processes are related to the Brownian energy process (BEP) through invertible, non-local transformations involving discrete tail energies, which can be thought of as the microscopic equivalent of a transformation of Cole-Hopf type. Our main tool is a general micro-to-macro result showing that, under suitable conditions, such microscopic tail transformations induce corresponding transformations of the limiting density profiles. Combining this result with the fact that the hydrodynamic limit of BEP is the heat equation, we obtain the limiting profiles of ABEP and dynamic ABEP as explicit nonlinear transformations of solutions of the heat equation.

papers.title: On the (in)finiteness of fixed characters in genus $3$
papers.abstract: We construct a counterexample to the Putman--Wieland conjecture in genus $3$ and discuss some of its consequences.

papers.title: A general Lê--Siersma formula
papers.abstract: We consider the comparison between a Milnor fibre of a function $f$ and its section by the zero locus of a second function $s$ in a general ambient variety $\mathcal{X}$. We give a formula that generalizes those of Lê and Siersma, expressing the difference of their Euler characteristics as a sum of local contributions associated with the critical points of the restriction of $s$. We provide an algebraic formula in the case that $\mathcal{X}$ is {smooth of pure dimension outside $f^{-1}(0)$}, and show some applications and examples.

papers.title: One-dimensional nodal solutions of the Lane--Emden problem in cylinders: asymptotic behaviour and energy stability
papers.abstract: We consider the Lane-Emden problem $-Δu=|u|^{p-1}u$, $p>1$, in bounded domains of a half-cylinder $ω\times(0,+\infty)$, with Dirichlet conditions on the relative boundary and Neumann conditions on the boundary of the cylinder. In flat cylinders $ω\times(0,L)$ this problem admits, for every $p>1$, one-dimensional solutions with any prescribed number $m$ of nodal regions. We study the stability of these domains, as critical points of a related energy functional, with respect to volume-preserving deformations of the domain. We prove that, for $p$ large, the flat cylinders are stable as soon as their height exceeds a threshold growing linearly in $p$, while, for $p$ close to $1$, both stability and instability occur, with explicit thresholds depending on $m$ and on the first nontrivial Neumann eigenvalue of $ω$. These results rely on a detailed analysis of the one-dimensional profiles: we describe their asymptotic behaviour, and that of the first eigenvalue of the associated linearized operator, as $p\to1^+$ and $p\to+\infty$, we obtain expansions of the amplitude with explicit constants, and we prove global comparison results with respect to $p$, some of which are new also for positive solutions.

papers.title: Representation embeddings and the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field $k$. We prove that for every infinite cardinal $κ$ there is an indecomposable $A$-module $M$ with $\dim_k M=κ$. Over algebraically closed fields, this settles Simson's conjecture, also called the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture, that every representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra has indecomposable modules of arbitrarily large cardinality. To construct these modules, we extend Bongartz's representation embedding from finite-dimensional Kronecker modules without a simple injective summand to such modules of arbitrary dimension. The extended functor commutes with direct sums and filtered colimits and preserves the dimension of infinite-dimensional modules. Applying it to the indecomposable Kronecker modules of every infinite dimension constructed by Göbel and Simson yields the required $A$-modules.

papers.title: Second critical exponent for a quasilinear Hardy--Hénon equation
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the parabolic Hardy--Hénon equation $\partial_tu=Δu^m+|x|^σu^p$ with slow diffusion $m>1$ and a potential which is singular at the origin, $-2<σ<0$, in dimension $N\ge3$. Above the Fujita exponent, global and blowing-up solutions coexist, and we show that the spatial decay of the initial data decides between them. The second critical exponent turns out to be the decay rate of an explicit singular steady state. Data decaying more slowly blow up in finite time, whatever their size, while faster decaying data which are small in a weighted supremum norm give rise to global solutions. At the critical decay, and in the range where the singular steady state exists, we construct bounded stationary barriers with exactly critical tail by gluing the singular steady state to regular steady states. We deduce that the critical amplitude separating global existence from blow-up lies between the amplitude of the singular steady state and an explicit constant. We also show that data lying below a proper fraction of the singular steady state produce global bounded solutions, and that the singular amplitude itself is attained by global solutions whenever a Joseph--Lundgren type condition fails. Conjectures and open problems complete the picture.

papers.title: Generalized principal eigenvalues for nonlocal operators with drift
papers.abstract: Nonlocal diffusion operators with a drift term naturally arise in models such as moving coordinate systems induced by climate change. This paper systematically studies several concepts of generalized principal eigenvalues (GPEs) for such operators. We allow the dispersal kernel to be heterogeneous and non-symmetric, and remove the standard global upper bound on the kernel (thereby covering the case of heavy-tailed dispersal kernels). To overcome the analytical difficulties brought by this more general setting, we establish a new Harnack-type inequality for non-compactly supported kernels, and apply homogenization and cut-off approximation techniques to derive two-sided bounds for the domain approximation limit of GPEs. Furthermore, under the almost periodic setting, we prove that the GPEs defined through different admissible test function spaces (e.g., \(C^1\) spaces with bounded derivatives and uniformly continuous function spaces in the viscosity sense) are completely coincident. This characterization reveals a fundamental unification: the limit result of principal eigenvalues under domain approximation by Coville and Hamel coincides exactly with the explicit variational formula by Du, Fang, and Ni, thereby bridging two previously independent theoretical results.

papers.title: Exact certification for conic optimization over quadratic modules: partitions of unity and recession directions
papers.abstract: We consider linear conic problems whose cone is a product of truncated quadratic modules, the sum-of-squares (SOS) side of the moment-SOS hierarchy. A floating-point solution is turned into an exact rational certificate in three steps: rounding, repair of each block residual by a constant, and absorption of the constants along a recession direction of the problem. The repair relies on strict partitions of unity in the quadratic modules. We characterize their existence, relate the canonical one to the analytic center of the dual pseudo-moment cone, Christoffel-Darboux polynomials and Pell equations, and we derive closed-form rational partitions for balls and boxes. The loss incurred by the certification is the optimal value of a recession problem, equal to a support function of the masses of the dual feasible pseudomoments. The method is illustrated on polynomial optimization, volume computation and positivity of polynomials along D-finite trajectories.

papers.title: Dolgopyat estimate for partially hyperbolic systems: limit theorems and exponential mixing
papers.abstract: We prove a Dolgopyat-type estimate for the twisted transfer operators of a class of two-dimensional partially hyperbolic endomorphisms of the torus, not necessarily skew-products. The twist satisfies a quantitative transversality condition on the cotangent dynamics of the associated three-dimensional extension which, in the skew-product case, is related to Tsujii's notions of transversality and partial captivity conditions. We use the main estimate to prove higher order expansions in the central and mixing local limit theorems for the two-dimensional base, including the case of several ergodic absolutely continuous invariant measures, and we prove exponential decay of correlations for the associated three-dimensional circle extensions, with a partially hyperbolic base.

papers.title: Normal form smoothing and spatial analyticity for the dispersion-generalized periodic KdV equation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the persistence of spatial analyticity for solutions to the dispersion-generalized periodic Korteweg-de Vries equation $$\partial_tu-\partial_x|D_x|^αu+u\partial_xu=0,\qquadα\ge2.$$ For real-valued initial data $u_0\in G^{σ_0,s}(\mathbb T)$, with $σ_0>0$ and $s\ge-α/4$, we prove that the corresponding global solution satisfies $$u\in C([-T,T];G^{σ(T),s}(\mathbb T)),\qquadσ(T)=\min\left\{σ_0,\frac cT\right\},$$ for every $T>0$. As a consequence, our result improves the lower bound for the radius of spatial analyticity established by Himonas, Kalisch, and Selberg (2017) for $2\leα<4$, including the classical periodic KdV equation, and establishes a unified $T^{-1}$ lower bound for the analyticity radius for every $α\ge2$. The main novelties are twofold. First, we introduce a normal form reduction at the level of the Gevrey energy, which reveals an additional cancellation in the cubic Gevrey commutator and separates it into a non-accumulating boundary correction and a quartic remainder. Second, we establish a global-in-time periodic $L_{t,x}^4$ estimate for the non-polynomial phase $k|k|^α$, valid for every real $α\ge2$. Together, these ingredients yield a refined almost conservation law and the $T^{-1}$ lower bound for the radius of spatial analyticity.

papers.title: A weak $λ$-set that is not a $λ$-set under $\frak{p} = \frak{c}$
papers.abstract: Under $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak c$, Cantor space contains a weak $λ$-set that is not a $λ$-set. This answers the consistency question of de Oliveira Rodrigues, dos Santos Ronchim, and Szeptycki. The hypothesis $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak c$ is compatible with the failure of the continuum hypothesis. The construction combines the finite-unions form of Hindman's theorem with Bell's characterization of $\mathfrak p$ in terms of $σ$-centered forcing. The increasing enumerations of the infinite members of the constructed space form an unbounded family under eventual domination. This makes the countable set of finite subsets of $ω$ a witness to the failure of the $λ$-property.

papers.title: Hamiltonicity and cycle factors in k-quasi-transitive digraphs of large diameter
papers.abstract: A digraph is $k$-quasi-transitive if the endpoints of every directed path of length $k$ are adjacent. In this paper, we prove that every strong non-bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian when $k\ge7$ is odd. Moreover, combined with the known even case, for $k\ge6$, we also prove that a strong bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian if and only if it has a cycle factor. These answer two problems posed by Alva-Samos and Hernández-Cruz affirmatively [Journal of Graph Theory \textbf{96} (2021) 310--325].

papers.title: Identities of Representation of Lie subalgebras of the first Weyl algebra
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a field. We study weak polynomial identities for pairs $(A,V)$ where $A$ is the first Weyl algebra over $F$ and $V$ is either a Lie subalgebra (under the usual Lie bracket) of $A$, or simply a vector subspace of $A$. Sometimes the weak identities of $(A,V)$, when $V$ is a Lie algebra, are called identities of representations of Lie algebras. Our starting point is the description of finite dimensional Lie algebras $L$ that can be embedded into the first Weyl algebra; this description was given by Rausch de Traubenberg, Slupinski and Tanasă in 2006. First we assume that $F$ is algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and describe a finite basis of the weak identities of the pair $(A,L)$ where $L=\mathfrak{sl}_2$. In order to obtain such a basis we invoke theorems by Razmyslov and by Trishin concerning the identities of infinite dimensional irreducible representations of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$. Afterwards we consider $L$ as a filiform Lie algebra together with its concrete realisation inside the first Weyl algebra. We produce a finite basis of weak identities of the pair $(A,L)$, assuming $F$ to be infinite. Finally we study the weakest form of identities for $(A,V)$ where $A$ is the $n$-th Weyl algebra and $V$ is just a vector space - its canonical generating vector subspace. We deduce a basis of the weak identities in this case as well, once again assuming $F$ to be an infinite field, with no restriction on its characteristic. The same result was recently obtained by Dotsenko and Lopatin in characteristic $0$ by different methods. Our methods are combinatorial, we also use the theory developed by Razmyslov, and the representations of the symmetric and the general linear groups and their duality. We employ the characteristic-free description of the invariants of the symplectic group given by De Concini and Procesi.

papers.title: An Engineering Reading of the Bounded Halting Problem and Observable Properties of a Universal Machine
papers.abstract: The halting problem asks whether a program eventually halts, with unrestricted resources. Engineering systems instead certify bounded halting: given a program, an input, and a step budget T, decide whether the program halts within T steps. This paper studies two of its uses. First, it defines an exact finite-budget problem, placing the simulated program and the checker on the same unit-cost timescale, so the checker can be embedded in an adversarial program. A diagonal argument with explicit additive overhead shows that no fixed deterministic checker decides every instance within any fixed fraction of T below one, for large T. In the nondeterministic case, T bounds the branch depth allowed for a stable observable decision. Second, bounded-halting instances give adversarial tests for finitary universality, since a universal model must support arbitrary finite computations as T grows. The tests check resource growth with T, the absence of a fixed deliberation bound, and later access to intermediate data. They separate a fixed model with extendable external resources, a model family that grows with T, and a larger system built around a fixed component. For machine-learning systems, this identifies the resource growth a universality claim assumes and whether it fails for deployed models.

papers.title: Multiple $q$-zeta values as polynomials in partition multiplicities
papers.abstract: Writing multiple $q$-zeta values as sums over partitions, a conjecture of Bachmann, proved by Hirose, Maesaka and Watanabe by means of a recursion, says that polynomials in the parts and multiplicities can be replaced by polynomials in the multiplicities alone. We make this replacement explicit, derive from it bounds on weight and depth that make Bachmann's conjecture effective, and provide a closed formula for the Drop1 operator of Hirose, Maesaka, Seki and Watanabe.

papers.title: Perfect Forms and Torsion Bounds in Algebraic $K$-Theory over Totally Real and CM Fields
papers.abstract: We extend the method of Van Woerden \cite{woerden} to totally real and CM number fields to obtain an upper bound for the number of $\GLo-$equivalence classes of perfect forms. Moreover, by considering appropriate barycentric subdivisions of the Voronoi tessellation, we extend these estimates to the number of $\GLo$-orbits of $k$-dimensional faces of the Voronoi tessellation. As a consequence, we improve the asymptotic order of the bounds for the torsion part of $K_m(\rint)$ obtained by Soulé \cite{soule_hermitian_bounds} and Houriet \cite{Juliet_PHD}. We emphasise the improvement of the general bound for $F=\mathbb Q$, unchanged since Soulé's work, and the independence of the discriminant exponent from the field degree for totally real and CM fields.

papers.title: Critical one-arm probabilities for metric-graph loop soups in dimensions $d\ge3$
papers.abstract: We study the critical Brownian loop soup on the metric graph $\widetilde{\mathbb Z}^d$. Using a new unified approach, we determine the one-arm probability up to multiplicative constants in all dimensions $d\ge3$. In particular, at the upper critical dimension $d_c=6$, we show that the one-arm probability is comparable to $r^{-2}(\log r)^{\frac12}$, and moreover, with high probability a box of radius $r$ contains on the order of $\log r$ macroscopic clusters, each with volume of order $r^4(\log r)^{-\frac12}$. For $d\ne6$, we recover the one-arm estimates of Cai and Ding, $r^{-(d-2)/2}$ for $d=3,4,5$ and $r^{-2}$ for $d>6$ (arXiv:2406.02397; Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2025), and the three-dimensional estimate of Drewitz, Prévost and Rodriguez (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2026). Our proof adapts the entropy method of Dewan and Muirhead (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2023) to the loop-soup setting. This yields a renormalization inequality for the one-arm probability, from which we derive the upper bounds. Independently, Rodriguez, Shi, and Zhang (arXiv:2611.05357) have recently used a closely related entropy approach to recover the one-arm estimates for $d>6$ and improve the upper bound for $d=6$. They also announce the same sharp one-arm estimate for $d=6$ in forthcoming work.

papers.title: Entire solutions of a special binomial differential equation
papers.abstract: We consider the binomial differential equation $$ ff'-a(f'')^2=be^{2c},$$ where $a(z)$, $b(z)$, $c(z)$ are polynomials such that $b(z)\not\equiv 0$ and $c(z)$ is non-constant. In this paper, we determine all entire solutions of this equation.

papers.title: Optimal stability estimates and preasymptotic error analysis of the CIP-FEM for the Helmholtz equation with uniaxial perfectly matched layers
papers.abstract: We study the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) problem for the Helmholtz equation in two and three dimensions and establish wavenumber-explicit stability estimates at high wavenumbers. For the full-space UPML problem, we prove the optimal stability estimate with the inf-sup constant satisfying $μ_\infty\eqsim k^{-1}$ for sufficiently large $k$ if the absorption function $σ\in W^{1,\infty}$ is a piecewise-power function of order at least one for which $\|σ'\|_{L^\infty(\{t:0<σ(t)\leqδ_*\})}\leq \varepsilon_*$, where $\varepsilon_*$ and $δ_*$ depend only on the PML parameters. Using this stability estimate, we obtain the optimal inf-sup estimate $μ_L\eqsim k^{-1}$ for the truncated UPML problem. These estimates further yield preasymptotic error estimates for a linear continuous interior penalty finite element method (CIP-FEM). Numerical simulations confirmed the theoretical predictions and demonstrated the effectiveness of CIP-FEM under high-wavenumber conditions.

papers.title: Uniqueness of the hexagonal lattice's universal optimality
papers.abstract: We build on a recent proof of the universal optimality of the planar hexagonal lattice. We extend this result to demonstrate that, up to Euclidean motion, the hexagonal lattice is the only periodic configuration with this property.

papers.title: Classification of radially symmetric solutions to a Hardy-H{é}non equation with sublinear absorption and applications
papers.abstract: Uniqueness of a non-negative radially symmetric solution with non-increasing profile to the Hardy-H{é}non elliptic equation with sublinear absorption \\ ____________ $Δ$v(x) + |x|\textsuperscript{$σ$}v(x) - v\textsuperscript{1/m}(x)=0, ______ x$\in$___\textsuperscript{N}, \\ is established in the range N$\ge$1, m>1 and $σ$$\in$(max{-2,-N},0). Consequences of this result are the uniqueness (up to scaling) of the non-negative extremal function to a Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality and the uniqueness of a non-negative radially symmetric self-similar solution with nonincreasing profile to a parabolic Hardy-H{é}non equation with quasilinear diffusion. The proof relies on ordinary differential equations techniques, which can be used thanks to the radially symmetric setting, and requires in particular a delicate analysis of the well-posedness and continuous dependence in view of the non-Lipschitz nonlinearity and the singularity of |x|\textsuperscript{$σ$} at the origin.

papers.title: On generalized $k$-token graphs with distinguishable tokens and a maximum capacity of $s$ tokens per vertex
papers.abstract: Supertoken graphs \(F^s_{k\times1}(G)\), also known as generalized token graphs, model configurations of \(k\) distinguishable tokens on a graph \(G\), with at most \(s\) tokens at each vertex. We study structural and metric properties of these graphs in terms of the base graph. For regular \(G\), we characterize when \(F^s_{k\times1}(G)\) is regular. We show that bipartiteness is inherited from \(G\) and characterize it for complete base graphs. For \(s\ge2\), we characterize connectedness and show that \(t\)-vertex-connectivity of \(G\) implies \(t\)-vertex-connectivity of the supertoken graph. We obtain exact diameter formulas in several regimes, including complete graphs and stars, and derive lower bounds and a conjectured formula for odd cycles. We also determine the clique number, give bounds and equality conditions for the chromatic number, and characterize planarity for complete base graphs.

papers.title: Small 5-chromatic unit-distance graphs in disks of radius 3/2, 5/4 and 23/20
papers.abstract: We give three explicit unit-distance graphs in the plane with chromatic number 5 whose vertices lie in small disks: a graph with 773 vertices inside an open disk of radius 3/2, one with 5713 vertices inside an open disk of radius 5/4, and one with 8168 vertices inside an open disk of radius 23/20. The smallest examples previously reported for these radii have 11725, 11725 and 31171 vertices. All coordinates are exact elements of Q(sqrt3, sqrt5, sqrt11). In each case 5-chromaticity is certified by an explicit 5-colouring and a DRAT proof that no 4-colouring exists. The 773-vertex graph is vertex-critical.

papers.title: Retrials in Loss Systems: Mean-Field Analysis, Erlang Bounds, and Power-of-$d$ Comparison
papers.abstract: We consider a system of $N$ parallel, homogeneous servers, each with finite capacity $C$. Jobs requiring one unit of capacity arrive according to a Poisson process with total rate $Nλ$ and have exponential service times with rate $μ$. We study a decentralized random--retrial policy with $d$ attempts: upon arrival, a job is assigned to a uniformly chosen server; if the server is full, the job is reassigned to another uniformly chosen server, for at most $d$ attempts; if all $d$ attempts fail, the job is rejected. In the mean-field limit, we prove that the stationary blocking probability is characterized by the unique solution of a fixed-point equation involving the Erlang-B loss function, and we establish global convergence of the fluid model to this equilibrium. We also compare the mean-field stationary blocking probability with the analogous quantity in the power-of-$d$ model under the same parameters $(C,λ,μ)$. For the same $d$, we show, via coupling techniques, that the blocking probability under power-of-$d$ is always less than or equal to the blocking under retrial-of-$d$; but if we consider $d$ and $\tilde d$ with $\tilde d>d$, then the retrial-of-$\tilde d$ policy achieves a strictly lower blocking than the power-of-$d$ policy when $ρ=λ/μ$ is sufficiently large. Moreover we show that for some specific cases, like $C=2$, $d=2$ and $\tilde d=3$, it occurs for all $ρ>0$, not only for $ρ$ sufficiently large. We complement the analysis with simulations that estimate the load level above which retrial-of-$\tilde d$ outperforms power-of-$d$ in terms of blocking.

papers.title: Homology and Topology of Partially Ordered Fields
papers.abstract: We develop a unified homology theory for directed partial orders (DPOs) and lattice-ordered positive cones on fields of characteristic zero. With the underlying field and its operations fixed, we define order?carrying spaces independently by topological conditions, establish a bijection with DPO positive cones, and characterize lattice orders by intersections of minimal open neighborhoods. A unified comparison theorem identifies graded Ext for region ideals with sheaf cohomology and multiplicative Tor with the reduced singular homology of truncated regions, giving a topological interpretation of the existence and preservation of reduced decompositions. We obtain canonical cohomological obstructions to lattice ordering, prove that a coefficient module for positive multiplication is flat if and only if the multiplier has a positive inverse, and show that every strict extension of positive cones on the same field produces a nonzero first Tor obstruction. Finally, we place the concrete lattice recently constructed by Bao-Zhang within this framework.

papers.title: From the quantum group $U_{q^{1/2}}( {\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}}_2 )$ to the Kronecker quantum cluster algebra
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal A_q$ be the Kronecker quantum cluster algebra with principal coefficients. We construct an explicit algebra homomorphism from the whole quantum group ${U_{q^{1/2}}}( {\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}_2}} )$ to $\mathcal A_q$, whose images together with either of the two frozen variables generate $\mathcal A_q$. As an application, we obtain algebra homomorphisms from the split $\imath$quantum groups of affine $\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}_2$ to $\mathcal A_q$. Moreover, we explicitly determine the images of the positive and negative real and imaginary root vectors of ${U_{q^{1/2}}}( {\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}_2}} )$ in terms of quantum cluster variables.

papers.title: Hopf-Galois Structures on Extensions Arising from Division Points on Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We provide a general construction of infinite Hopf-Galois extensions from a direct system of finite Hopf-Galois extensions. We then apply this framework to extensions generated by division points on elliptic curves. Specifically, for a number field $K$ and an elliptic curve $E/K$ of rank at least $1$ with $P\in E(K)$ of infinite order, we consider for each integer $n\geq 2$ the extension $L_n=K(Q_n)$, where $Q_n\in E(\overline{K})$ is such that $nQ_n=P$. We show that the finite-level extensions $L_n/K$ need not be Hopf-Galois, and we give sufficient conditions for them to be so. We then prove that the infinite extension $L_\infty=\bigcup_{n\geq 2}L_n$ of $K$ is potentially Hopf-Galois, meaning it becomes Hopf-Galois after a finite extension of the base field.

papers.title: Law-Dependent Poisson-Refresh Randomised Feedback Control for Stochastic Systems
papers.abstract: This paper studies a continuous-time probabilistic control problem for stochastic systems in which the feedback law assigns a probability distribution over control inputs. The control is modelled as a law-dependent Poisson-refresh process: it is held constant between refresh times and resampled at Poisson times from a feedback rule depending on the current state and state law. The closed-loop system is therefore formulated as a jump--diffusion for the joint state--control process. The objective is to design the sampling rule by comparing the realised closed-loop system with a prescribed reference description. The cost separates two local terms: a relative-entropy penalty for the instantaneous refresh kernel and a state-side drift-mismatch cost. The state-side term is evaluated at the realised control value and is motivated by a frozen-control Girsanov identity. Under global Lipschitz, moment, and uniform ellipticity assumptions, we prove well-posedness of the closed loop and a dynamic programming principle on the joint state--control law space. For linear data and admissible mean-dependent affine-Gaussian refresh rules, the full joint law need not remain Gaussian, but the first and second moments of the joint state--control process close exactly. This yields a deterministic reduced control problem on moment space, with an explicit running cost, a reduced Hamiltonian, and a verification theorem.

papers.title: A Polynomial Erdős-Pósa bound for Eulerian digraphs
papers.abstract: In [Combinatorica 1996], Reed, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas proved Younger's conjecture dating back to 1973 that states that directed cycles have the Erdős-Pósa property. Specifically, they showed that every directed graph $D$ contains either $k$ arc-disjoint cycles or a set of at most $f(k)$ arcs that intersect every directed cycle. The function $f$, depending only on $k$, is however notoriously large--in fact, not even elementary. The first improvement on this function was only very recently provided by Hatzel, Kreutzer, Milani, and Muzi [FOCS 2024] who showed that $f$ can be taken to be an exponential tower of height $8$. In this work, we improve this function to $O(k^4)$ in the case where the digraph is Eulerian. This also answers an open question by Wahlström [Springer Monographs in Mathematics 2018] who asked explicitly when Eulerian digraphs have a polynomial Erdős-Pósa property. The only other known result about Erdős-Pósa on Eulerian digraphs is a result from Seymour [Combinatorica 1996] who showed that $f(k)=k$ when the Eulerian digraph admits a linkless embedding in 3-space, and such an equality is not possible for general Eulerian digraphs. We also complement our positive result, by showing that the result of Seymour cannot be extended to give a linear bound ($O(k)$) on general Eulerian digraphs, by showing that even on Eulerian digraphs the lower bound for the Erdős-Pósa property is $Ω(k \log k)$.

papers.title: Existence of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow Singularities with Bounded Mean Curvature
papers.abstract: In every dimension $n \ge 3$, we show there exist Lagrangian mean curvature flows that develop neck pinch singularities such that the mean curvature remains uniformly bounded. This follows from a related result that, under a structural assumption on the singularity formation, the mean curvature at small scales near the singularity can be bounded by the Lagrangian angle at outer scales with suitable weights. Applying this result to a subset of the finite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed in the companion paper [arXiv:2607.03152] and the infinite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed by Tsai, Wood, and the second-named author [arXiv:2401.02228] then gives examples of both finite-time and infinite-time singularity formation with uniformly bounded mean curvature.

papers.title: Certified Collision Exclusion and an Unconditional Upper Bound $Λ<0.156821$ for the de Bruijn--Newman Constant
papers.abstract: The de Bruijn--Newman constant $Λ$ is the transition time beyond which all zeros of the heat-deformed Riemann $ξ$-function are real. We develop a computer-assisted collision-exclusion method and obtain the bound $Λ<156821/10^6=0.156821$, in the normalisation of Polymath. The proof combines the published finite-height verification and the starting inequality $Λ\leq1/5$ with a compact-interior continuation theorem, five stable prime-polynomial Gram sources, certified moving-index recovery, a balanced real-jet transfer and a uniform Euler-product barrier at infinity. The resulting closed time-band exclusion, together with uniform remote reality, forces strictness at the proposed endpoint. The finite certificate uses 664,505 structural Fourier coefficients, 44,182 closed torus boxes, 184 separator moments and 17,385 separator rectangles. We isolate a Cauchy--Schwarz obstruction intrinsic to the four-prime source family, explaining the narrow feasibility margin of the certified endpoint. We state the proof-to-certificate interface and distinguish the present unconditional logical claim from other recent, as yet unrefereed, computational bounds.

papers.title: From Continuum-Kinematics-Inspired Peridynamics to Simplicial Hyperelasticity
papers.abstract: We develop a variational and functional-analytic framework for continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamics with simultaneous nonlocal interactions among multiple points. We encode the finite-difference data of each interacting simplex in a simplicial deformation gradient. For nondegenerate simplices in three dimensions, the gradient, its cofactor, and its determinant encode the associated continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic line, area, and volume changes, respectively. This unified representation leads to a class of simplicial hyperelastic energies with general, possibly nonadditive, constitutive dependence on the affine deformation of an interacting simplex, thereby extending the original continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic framework. To describe interactions occurring at different scales and over different simplex geometries, we introduce radial- and shape-weighted nonlocal spaces. Their multipoint seminorms control two-point energies induced by the edge marginals of the interaction measure. This comparison yields nonlocal Poincaré inequalities and fractional Sobolev embeddings. We establish existence of equilibrium configurations by two complementary mechanisms. Particle-wise averaged convexity yields weak lower semicontinuity of the associated energy functionals. Under stronger assumptions on the edge marginals, fractional compactness gives existence for nonconvex energy densities. These results provide a mathematical foundation for simplicial and continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic models.

papers.title: Sharp asymptotic stability of the IPM equation in $\mathbb{R}^2$ via isopycnal coordinates
papers.abstract: We study the incompressible porous media (IPM) equation, a model describing the motion of a fluid with variable density through a porous medium under the action of gravity. We prove that the stably stratified state, in which heavier fluid lies below lighter fluid, is nonlinearly stable: small perturbations decay over time and the fluid returns to equilibrium. Our result holds in the sharp Sobolev setting $H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ for every $s>2$: this threshold cannot be improved, since the equation is ill-posed in $H^2(\mathbb R^2)$. This result follows from a proof of global well-posedness at critical Besov regularity, with smallness required only in a norm invariant under the natural scaling of the equation. We also prove optimal decay rates for suitably localized initial data. The main difficulty is that the stabilizing effect of stratification acts only in some directions, while the nonlinear transport acts in all of them. Reaching the sharp regularity threshold requires two main novelties. First, we rewrite the equation in \emph{isopycnal coordinates}, which follow the level sets of the density: in these coordinates the transport becomes one-dimensional, and the anisotropic stabilizing mechanism can be exploited at minimal regularity. Second, we establish new \emph{anisotropic commutator estimates} which allow us to control the remaining nonlinear terms. Finally, we show that the estimates obtained in isopycnal coordinates can be transferred back to the original variables.

papers.title: Variational Splines and Generalized Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: Tikhonov regularization, kriging, and Gaussian-process regression share the same algorithm because, for a linear inverse problem with a Gaussian prior and Gaussian noise, the minimum-mean-square-error (MMSE) estimator is the solution of a regularized least-squares problem. We show that this equivalence survives the passage from vectors to generalized functions: the regularized least-squares estimators become generalized splines, and the Gaussian random vectors become generalized Gaussian processes (GGPs) on the dual of a nuclear space. A whitening operator $\mathrm{L}: \mathcal{S} \to L_2$ specifies both the native Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\mathrm{L} \subset \mathcal{S}'$ of the splines and a family of GGPs, which solve a stochastic differential equation subject to boundary conditions. We prove that the Gaussian spaces of these processes are congruent to the core $\mathrm{L}^\ast(L_2)$ of the native space, and that their MMSE estimators from finitely many linear measurements are generalized splines. Our framework extends the classical correspondences of Kimeldorf-Wahba, Parzen and Kailath in two respects: our estimators form a broader class that includes generalized functions, and we give a proper Bayesian treatment of the case where the null space of $\mathrm{L}$ is non-trivial. The framework gives a precise meaning to statements such as ``fractional splines are the optimal estimators of fractional Brownian motion,'' and it provides a rigorous Bayesian formulation of infinite-dimensional linear inverse problems.

papers.title: Calmness Modulus of Parameterized Convex Constraint Systems: Exact Closed-Form Formulas via Second-Order Admissibility
papers.abstract: We resolve the open problem of deriving an exact, closed-form algebraic formula for the calmness modulus of $\mathcal{C}^2$ convex constrained feasible set mappings $\mathcal{F}(b) := \{ x \in \mathbb{R}^n \colon f_t(x) \le b_t, \, \forall t \in T \}$ under right-hand side perturbations at a given pair of the graph $(\bar{b}, \bar{x})$. First, under the condition $0_n \in \mathrm{int}\left(\mathrm{conv}\left\{ \nabla f_t(\bar{x}) ,\; t \in T(\bar{x}) \right\}\right)$, we prove that the calmness modulus coincides with the inverse distance from the origin to the boundary of the nominal subdifferential. Second, for general $\mathcal{C}^2$ convex systems where the previously mentioned interior condition does not hold, we introduce a second-order admissibility filtering over the active indexes. We show that this filtered family, $\mathcal{D}^0_2(\bar{x})$, yields an exact characterization of the calmness modulus relying solely on nominal data.

papers.title: Random waves on sub-Riemannian $SU(2)$
papers.abstract: Random spherical eigenfunctions for the Lalplace-Beltrami operator are well understood and their local behavior, after renormalization, is described by Berry's random wave model. In this paper we construct a family of random fields on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$, identified with the group $SU(2)$, endowed with a sub-Riemannian structure. These fields are random eigenfunctions for the sub-Laplacian and they are constructed from matrix elements of unitary irreducible representations of $SU(2)$. We prove that the local behavior of such fields is the same as the Berry-Heisenberg random field on the Heisenberg group introduced in [10].

papers.title: Roughness of nets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the concepts of ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$τ$-convergence}' and ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$τ$-cluster point}' of a net in locally solid Riesz spaces. We also compare these concepts with key findings from the works of Lahiri $\&$ Das (2007/2008), Das (2012) and Aytar (2008), as follows: [(i):] The set of \emph{ideal-cluster points} of a sequence in a topological space is closed, [(ii):] The set of \emph{ideal-cluster points} of a net in a topological space is closed, [(iii):] The set of \emph{rough ideal-cluster points} of a sequence in a norm linear space is closed. We demonstrate that, generally, the set of ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$τ$-cluster points}' of a net in a locally solid Riesz space may not satisfy the aforementioned results, which implies that it may not be closed. This suggests that this set exhibits new characteristics, which we will discuss here. Ultimately, our characterization demonstrates that these new concepts can help identify an ideal that is maximal and effectively represent any closed $τ$-neighborhood of $θ$ within these spaces.

papers.title: Quasi-norms on $\mathbb{R}^d$: Characterization and Approximation by Conic Splines
papers.abstract: We first show that a regularizer on $\mathbb{R}^d$ that is continuous, symmetric, and amplitude-equivariant is of the form $g=q^γ$ with $γ>0$, where $q$ is continuous and absolutely homogeneous; we call the set of such $q$ the CH class, whose convex members are the seminorms. Within the CH class, we single out two configurations of interest for regularization: the quasi-norms, which are exactly the positive-definite members of the family, and the quasi-seminorms with null space control, which are the composition of a quasi-norm with a linear map that sets the null space. We then propose a universal parametrization of the class by conic splines, the continuous functions that are linear on each cone of a polyhedral fan. Specifically, we show that the polyhedral CH functionals are exactly the symmetric non-negative conic splines, and that these admit a stable nodal representation in a basis of conic B-splines. Finally, we determine the rates of approximation: the conic spline interpolant converges at the second-order rate $h^2\asymp n^{-2/(d-1)}$, in the $L_\infty$-norm on the hyper-sphere when the angular profile is twice differentiable, and in the $L_1$-norm when its spherical Hessian variation is bounded, which covers the polyhedral members of the class. The rate is sharp, already for the Euclidean norm. The planar case is worked out in full, with the trigonometric hat functions as basis and an $\ell_1$-norm of second differences as regularity index.

papers.title: Equilibrium webs and stability for arbitrary families of endomorphisms of projective spaces
papers.abstract: We consider arbitrary holomorphic families of endomorphisms of a complex projective space. We prove that the existence of an equilibrium web implies the holomorphic motion of all repelling cycles contained in the Julia set, i.e., the support of the unique measure of maximal entropy. Together with previous results of Berteloot, Bianchi, Brévard, Buff, and Dupont, this completes the extension of the stability-bifurcation theory to arbitrary families of holomorphic endomorphisms. The same conclusions also hold for holomorphic families of polynomial-like maps of large topological degree.

papers.title: Accessibility of collapsed Anosov flow
papers.abstract: We prove that every $C^1$ collapsed Anosov flow on a closed three-manifold with non-virtually-solvable fundamental group is accessible. No transitivity or nonwandering assumption is required, and the collapsing map need not satisfy the strong-collapse conditions. We also prove that every three-dimensional collapsed Anosov flow for which no positive iterate is a discretized Anosov flow is accessible.

papers.title: The Quantum Stochastic Limit for Non-Markovian Driving Processes
papers.abstract: We express the stochastic limit (weak-coupling limit) of a quantum system interacting with its environment as the limit of solutions to a parametrized family of quantum stochastic differential equations (QSDEs). We prove the convergence of such solutions in the case where the driving processes may be non-Markovian and the system may be infinite-dimensional with unbounded Hamiltonian. We achieve this by imposing a particular condition on the n-point functions of the driving process which we verify for annihilation, creation, and gauge operators on a bosonic Fock space with sufficient mixing. Additionally, we include not only the usual fast-evolving system Hamiltonian which is averaged out in the limit, but also a slow-evolving system Hamiltonian which survives the limit. We also relax the requirement for the fast-evolving Hamiltonian to have a purely discrete spectrum allowing accumulation points under some circumstances. Moreover, our convergence mode for the processes is convergence of all time-centered n-point functions which is stronger than the typical semigroup convergence for the stochastic limit.

papers.title: $C_2$-Cofiniteness of Permutation Orbifolds I: Relative $C_1$ Descent
papers.abstract: We establish a relative $C_1$-cofiniteness criterion for $C_2$-cofiniteness of finite group orbifolds. For permutation actions on a simple, self contragredient, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type, it suffices to check a single relation for a derivative of the conformal vector in the Virasoro vertex operator algebra. This reduces the problem to a calculation depending only on the central charge and tensor degree. An exact calculation then proves cofiniteness for a family of nonsolvable permutation orbifolds without restricting the central charge.

papers.title: Dispersion of Magnetic Coriolis Waves
papers.abstract: We consider the 3-D rotating magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equations. The combination of rotation and background magnetic field leads to the occurrence of dispersive magneto-Coriolis waves in the linearized equations. We establish a t ^{-1} decay estimate for waves with dispersion relation $σ$($ξ$) = $ξ$ \_3 h(|$ξ$|) under suitable assumptions on h, and show that this includes magneto-Coriolis waves. Then we apply these dispersive estimates to the nonlinear rotating MHD equations and obtain an improved lower bound on the lifespan of solutions.

papers.title: Constructing Cospectral Hypergraphs Using Adjacency Preserving Permutations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use permutations of the vertices of hypergraphs that preserve their adjacency matrices defined in banerjee 2021. These permutations form a group which lies between the automorphism group and the full symmetric group $S_n$ where $n$ is the number of vertices. Using elements from that group which are not automorphisms, we construct cospectral non-isomorphic hypergraphs. We use hypergraph structure coming from finite projective planes to show existence of infinitely many families of such hypergraphs. Also this method is very specific to uniform hypergraphs with uniformity greater than or equal to 3, i.e not applicable to graphs.

papers.title: Rational Torsion and Ramification Constraints on Odd Superelliptic Jacobians
papers.abstract: Let C: y^d = f(x) be a smooth projective superelliptic curve over Q, where d >= 3 is odd, f(x) in Q[x] is separable of degree n >= 3, and gcd(d,n) = 1. Let J = Jac(C) be its Jacobian. We study the rational torsion subgroup J(Q)_tors through the interaction of ramification geometry, Galois actions, reduction at primes of good reduction, and the geometry of divisors. First, we describe the subgroup R_d contained in J[d] generated by the ramification-point differences and determine its Galois-invariant subgroup explicitly in terms of the sizes of the Galois orbits of the roots of f. This yields a precise description of the rational d-torsion classes arising from ramification, without assuming that they account for all of J(Q)[d]. Second, we establish criteria based on the orders of reduced Jacobians that can prove the vanishing of the full rational torsion subgroup. Finally, we derive geometric constraints on divisor classes represented by effective divisors of degree smaller than the genus, including a restriction arising when distinct effective divisors represent the same class. Explicit examples illustrate how the Galois-theoretic and reduction-theoretic methods can be combined to study rational torsion on odd superelliptic Jacobians.

papers.title: Linear maps of $C^*$-algebras preserving norm parallelism
papers.abstract: Two elements $a,b$ in a normed space are parallel if $\|a+γb\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$ for some $|γ|=1$; they form a triangle equality attaining (TEA) pair if $\|a+b\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$. For finite-dimensional complex $C^*$-algebras other than $\mathbf M_2(\mathbb C)$ and $\mathbb C\oplus_\infty\mathbb C$, bijective linear maps on these algebras preserving parallel or TEA pairs are scalar multiples of isometries. For unital abelian algebras with spectra containing at least three points, preservation in both directions gives the same conclusion. We obtain corresponding results for type I factors, simple type I $C^*$-algebras, and unitarily invariant operator spaces under additional continuity and finite-rank hypotheses. All results for $C(X)$ and $B(H,K)$ hold over both real and complex fields.

papers.title: Improving Hydrofoil Efficiency Through Simulation-Driven Design Optimization
papers.abstract: Foil windsurfing is a sport in which competitors fine-tune their setup to optimize performance under varying environmental conditions. However, such adjustments are typically guided by intuition. This paper presents a methodology for improving hydrofoil design using computational fluid dynamics. First, structured light scanning was used to obtain the geometry of a conventional hydrofoil. Subsequently, five derived designs have been explored, inspired by advancements in airplane wing design. Following this, a preliminary design was selected, and a design of experiments approach was implemented. Generated simulation data were used to train a machine learning surrogate, which is ultimately used in the multi-objective design optimization. While the surrogate-based approach yielded promising results, it was limited to exploring a restricted set of design parameters. To overcome this constraint, additional improvements were attained through adjoint optimization, demonstrating that comparable performance can be achieved with a distinctly different hydrofoil design. Finally, the conventional design was refined through adjoint optimization. Notably, adjoint optimization yielded a 15% increase in efficiency. The results suggest that both proposed approaches can produce novel hydrofoil designs capable of outperforming the original configuration under specific conditions; however, due to its inherent flexibility, the adjoint approach with realistic constraints offers more freedom in the design exploration process.

papers.title: A Galois-type Springer theorem for hermitian and generalized quadratic forms
papers.abstract: We prove that anisotropy of nonsingular hermitian and skew-hermitian forms over central simple algebras with involution is preserved under scalar extension to every finite Galois extension of odd degree coprime to the index of the algebra. In characteristic two, the same conclusion holds for generalized quadratic forms over algebras with involution of the first kind, with no nonsingularity assumption on their polar forms. The main tool is an isometry-level descent theorem. For a cyclic extension of odd prime degree, every anisotropic nonsingular form over a division algebra with involution, of rank smaller than the extension degree and with Galois-invariant isometry class, descends to an anisotropic form over the base field. Unlike descent results for Witt classes, this theorem descends the form itself. A bounded-rank reduction, based on injectivity of the Witt-group restriction map, derives the cyclic anisotropy theorem from this descent result; a regularization argument removes the nonsingularity assumption on polar forms in characteristic two, and the Feit-Thompson theorem extends the result to arbitrary finite Galois extensions of odd degree.

papers.title: Optimal Error Estimates With Polynomial Dependence on $ε^{-1}$ for Mixed Finite Element Methods of the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes System
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze a first-order convex-splitting mixed finite element scheme for the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system, tracking explicitly how the error constants depend on the interface width $ε$. Due to the strong nonlinear coupling inherent in the CHNS system and the singular dependence of the Cahn--Hilliard equation on $ε$, conventional energy-based analyzes often lead to severe dependence of the error constants on $ε^{-1}$, and may even result in exponential growth. Such dependence significantly limits the applicability of the resulting error estimates in the small-interfacial-thickness regime. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a robust parameter error analysis framework with respect to interfacial thickness $ε$. In particular, by introducing $H^{-1}$ approximation properties for the Ritz projection and the Ritz and Stokes quasi-projection operators, together with spectral-type estimates for the discrete perturbed Cahn--Hilliard operator, we effectively control the singular terms arising from the interfacial thickness parameter in the error analysis. Compared with the classical results, which address only the Allen-Cahn or Cahn-Hilliard equation, we adopt a three-term discrete Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality analysis technique and achieve a substantial reduction in the degree of polynomial dependence for the coupled system. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical results and to demonstrate the robustness of the method for different parameters of interfacial thickness.

papers.title: Koszul duality and homotopy algebras for operads over quivers
papers.abstract: For a quiver $Q$, we introduce and study $Q$-operads (or operads over $Q$), defined as a special sort of $\mathbf{fc}$-multicategories or virtual double categories, in which the directions of the arrows of $Q$ encode the permitted input orderings. In this higher operadic framework, we construct the bar--cobar adjunction and develop a theory of Koszul duality and homotopy algebras, together with compatibility results under changes of quiver. We treat dg categories and their left modules, right modules, and bimodules as algebras over quiver-operads. We prove that these operads are Koszul and that their resolutions govern the corresponding $A_\infty$ categories and modules. We also categorify Sagave's notion of derived $A_\infty$ algebras and introduce modules over derived $A_\infty$ algebras and categories. Finally, we explain that restriction along a folding of quivers constructs diagonal $A_\infty$ bimodules, while extension along an inclusion of quivers realizes two-sided bar models of derived tensor products.

papers.title: Flux-Matched Poisson Iteration for Generated Jacobian Equations: Local Convergence and Spectral Galerkin Approximation
papers.abstract: We develop a flux-matched Poisson iteration for solving generated Jacobian equations with second boundary conditions. In each step, it solves a fixed shifted Poisson problem with a Neumann-type boundary condition. Near a smooth regular solution with positive $C^{1,1}$ densities, we prove that the iteration has local geometric convergence in $C^{2,α}$ on smooth connected Riemannian domains. The iteration is then discretized using a spectral Galerkin method, with local convergence proved for the Fourier-Jacobi scheme on spherical caps. Optical numerical experiments support these estimates and demonstrate useful imaging performance beyond the local convergence theory.

papers.title: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) can reconstruct fine-scale Earth-observation fields from coarse observations, but reconstruction accuracy alone does not provide a calibrated rule for identifying reliable spatial regions. Conformal Mask Calibration (CMC), built on conformal risk control, converts a spatial uncertainty score into a trust mask and controls the expected worst-case local distortion under exchangeability. However, its fixed threshold can become miscalibrated in Earth-observation streams affected by seasonality and episodic events. We propose $\textit{CARM}$ (Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking), a statistical framework for adaptive spatial risk control under temporal distribution shift. CARM maintains experts with heterogeneous update rates and aggregates their threshold proposals online using an asymmetric surrogate loss, balancing rapid adaptation to distribution changes against stability during relatively stationary periods. All updates are causal and use only mature feedback available after a fixed delay, allowing CARM to operate with any SR model that provides a spatial uncertainty score. We prove that the time-averaged mask-conditioned risk converges to at most $α$ at an $O(1/T)$ rate, without distributional assumptions and for any choice of aggregation weights across experts. On a daily South China Sea chlorophyll-$\textit{a}$ SR stream, CARM reduces the empirical violation rate from $43.49\%$ to $9.38\%$ and the moving-average exceedance frequency from $47.29\%$ to $1.22\%$ at $α=0.10$, while retaining a non-trivial trusted region. Experiments on ERA5 wind and OSTIA sea-surface temperature further show consistent relative improvements across multiple SR backbones.

papers.title: Hadamard configurations and sharp cubic-period bounds for stealth in dimensions 10, 11, and 12
papers.abstract: We construct explicit, nonlattice periodic point configurations in dimensions $10$, $11$ and $12$ with stealth center density $1/24$ and unit-density stealth radius $2\cdot24^{-1/n}$. These values exceed those of duals of the current record lattice packings, without claiming to exceed all possible lattices. The construction uses the $24$ sign rows of an order-$12$ Hadamard matrix and their antipodes, projected onto $n$ coordinates. For an arbitrary, not necessarily binary, equally weighted motif with marked period $2\mathbb{Z}^n$, we prove a sharp $2n$-point lower bound for a raw stealth radius at least one and classify equality by antipodal Hadamard configurations. We deduce bounded-complexity optimality, sharp optimality among binary motifs in dimensions $10$--$12$, and local maximality under simultaneous perturbations of the motif and the marked period shape. A divisibility argument excludes ordinary equally weighted periodic formal duals. Statements are confined to their indicated classes; no global optimality among arbitrary-period configurations is asserted.

papers.title: Highly connected uniquely $k$-linked digraphs
papers.abstract: Extending a result of Thomassen, we prove that for every choice of positive integers $K\geq k$ there exist a $K$-strong digraph which has two disjoint sets $S,T$ each of size $k$ so that the only linkage from $S$ to $T$ in $D$ is the one whose existence follows from Menger's theorem.

papers.title: A Viscous Cascade Construction of Nonunique Leray--Hopf Solutions to the Unforced 3D Navier--Stokes Equations
